Abu Salih related from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The qintar is twelve thousand ounces." [13] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/363.]]
On the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, he said: I, Thabit and some people with us entered upon Anas ibn Malik and said to him: "O Abu Hamzah, what did the Prophet ﷺ used to say about the night prayer?" Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites fifty verses in a night is not recorded among the heedless; whoever recites a hundred verses is given the reward of a full night's prayer; whoever recites two hundred verses with the Qur'an has fulfilled its right; whoever recites five hundred verses up to a thousand verses is like one who gave a qintar in charity before morning." It was said: "And what is the qintar?" He said: "A thousand dinars."
Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: The qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces, and this is the saying of Ibn 'Umar and similar.
Zirr ibn Hubaysh related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The qintar is one thousand ounces and two hundred ounces." [14] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30.]]
'Atiyyah related from Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar on the authority of al-Hakam on the authority of al-Dahhak: "The qintar is one thousand two hundred mithqals."
Similarly Yunus related from al-Hasan from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as a mursal report.
Hamzah related on the authority of Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The qintar is one thousand dinars." [15] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/10.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ikrimah: it is a hundred thousand, and a hundred [ratls], a hundred mithqals, and a hundred dirhams. Islam came, on the day it came, when [in Mecca] [[As in the manuscript; perhaps the original reads: "and the qanatir"]] there were a hundred men.

[On the authority of Sufyan from] Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: The qintar is a hundred ratls. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/273.]]

Al-Hakam said: The qintar is as much wealth as lies between the heaven and the earth.

Abu Nadhra: the hide of a bull filled with gold or silver.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Qatadah: eighty thousand.

Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: The qintar is seventy thousand.

Shurayk: forty thousand mithqals.

Al-Hasan: The qintar is the blood-money (diyah) of one of you.

Similarly, al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas, and Juwaybir from al-Dahhak, who said: twelve thousand dirhams or a thousand dinars, the blood-money of one of you.

From Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: In the language of Ifriqiya and al-Andalus, the qintar is eight thousand jarwals of gold or silver.

Al-Thumali narrated from al-Suddi, who said: four thousand mithqals.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some books that the qanatir [derive from binding a thing and making it firm], and its root is from firmness. It is said: "I qanantara al-shay'" (I made the thing firm) when one makes it firm, and from this the bridge is called al-qantarah al-muqantarah. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30, attributing it to al-Zajjaj.]]

Al-Dahhak said: al-Muqantarah: the fortified and secured.

Qatadah: it is the abundant, piled one, some of it upon others, as if it were buried. It is said: qantara when it increased.

Al-Suddi: the stored and minted, until they became dirhams and dinars.

Al-Farra' said: the multiplied, as if the qintar is three and the muqantarah is nine.

Abu Ubaydah: it is mufa'lalah from the qintar, like your saying "alf mu'allaf" (a thousand compiled).

﴿Of gold and silver﴾: it is said gold (dhahab) was so named because it goes away (yadhhabu) and does not remain, and silver (fiddah) because it is scattered (tanfadu), that is, dispersed.

﴿And horses branded﴾: "khayl" (horses) is a plural that has no singular from its own form; its singular is "faras," like "qawm" (people), "nisa'" (women), "rahT" (group), "jaysh" (army), and the like. The scholars differed over the meaning of "al-musawwamah" (branded). Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Rabi' said: it is the grazing one (al-ra'iyah).

Similarly, Atiyyah narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan: it is the pasture-grazing one (al-mar'iyyah). It is said: sāmat al-khayl yasūmu sawman, so it is sa'imah; and I made them graze (asamtuha) when I left them for that purpose, so they are musamamah; and I branded them (sawwamtuha taswiman), so they are musawwamah. God said: ﴿In which you pasture [them]﴾. [[Surat al-Nahl: 10.]]

In this there is the verse of al-Akhtal:
Like Ibn Bazi'ah, or like another such one... Be well, son of the grazing of the appointed times. [[Al-Aghani: 8/319 (Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyyah), where it reads: "like Ibn al-Bazi'ah."]]
He means: the son of the camels.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit and Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid: al-Mutahhamah: the handsome ones. Layth, on the authority of them: al-Musawwarah (the well-formed). And from Ikrimah: their taswim is their beauty. [[Fath al-Qadir: 1/324.]]

Al-Suddi: it is the one that is kept (al-ra'iyah), and all of these have one meaning.

Abu Ubaydah, al-Hasan, al-Akhfash, and al-Qutaybi: the marked/taught one (al-mu'allamah). Similarly, al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Qatadah: their white markings and their colors. Al-Mu'arrij: the branded with a brand (al-makwiyyah). Al-Mubarrad: the known in the lands.

Ibn Kaysan: al-yahlaq... and all of these have been established, and its root is from the sawmah, and al-musayyamah, which is the mark. It is said: "sawwamtu al-khayl taswiman" when I marked the horses. God the Exalted said: ﴿with five thousand angels marked﴾. [[Surat Al 'Imran: 125.]]

Al-Nabighah said describing horses:
With spears like arrows, branded ones, upon them a company resembling jinn.

Al-A'sha said:
And the horsemen of the guards at every frontier, leading the branded noble steeds.

Ibn Zayd and Aban ibn Tha'labah said: al-musawwamah: prepared for war and jihad.

Labid said:
By my life, Kulayb has indeed perished, every generation branded for battle.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some tafsirs that it is the hamalikh (the thoroughbred ones).

Section on horses.
"Their creation's description"
Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated from his father Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When God wished to create creation, He said to the south wind: 'I am creating from you a creature. I will make it a might for My friends, a humiliation for My enemies, and a beauty for the people of My obedience.' The wind said: 'Create.' So He took a handful from it and created a horse from it.

He said to it: 'I created you Arab, and I made good tied to your forelock, and spoils gathered on your back. I bent your companion toward you, and I made you fly without wings: you are for pursuit and you are for flight. I will place on your back men who will glorify Me, praise Me, declare Me one, and magnify Me. You will glorify when they glorify, you will declare Me one when they declare Me one, and you will magnify when they magnify.'"

And the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no glorification, praise, exaltation, or magnification that its doer utters and that goes beyond it, except that it is answered with its like." [16] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/195.]]

Then he said: "When the angels heard the description of the horse, they reproached its Creator, saying: 'Lord, we are Your angels; we glorify You and praise You, so what is for us?' So God created for them horses with necks like the necks of Bactrian camels." He said: "When the horse was sent to the earth and its feet settled on the earth, it neighed. It was said: 'Blessed are you, animal, by whose neighing the polytheists are humbled, by which their necks are made low, by which their ears are filled, and by which their hearts are terrified.'

When God presented to Adam from every creature, He said: 'Choose from My creation what you wish.' He chose the horse. He said to him: 'You have chosen your might and the might of your offspring, eternal while they are eternal, and remaining while they remain. [It will mate and produce offspring from you until the end of time.] My blessing upon you and upon it: I have not created a creature more beloved to Me than you and it.'" [17] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/465, no. 11382; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/195, and 4/111.]]

Its virtue:
Abu Salih narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection." [18] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/49.]]

And from Sa'id ibn Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: Nothing was more beloved to the Messenger of God ﷺ after women than horses.

And from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no Arabian horse except that it is given permission with every dawn to call out two supplications, saying: 'O God, You have made me subject to whoever You have made subject to me among the children of Adam, and You have made me for him; so make me the most beloved of his wealth and his family to him,' or 'of those most beloved to him in wealth and family.'" [19] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/170.]]

Its condition:
From Abu Wahb al-Husayni, who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Tie up horses, wipe their forelocks and their rumps, put collars on them, and do not put on them bowstrings. You should have every bay with a white blaze (aghurr) [[al-Aghurr: one that has a white mark on its forehead the size of a dirham.]] and white socks, or a chestnut with white socks, or a black with a blaze and white socks." [20] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/218.]]

Abu Zur'ah narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet used to dislike the shikal [[al-Shikal: whiteness in the two forelegs, or only in the right foreleg and the right hind leg; it is said the reverse is in the left.]] among horses.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman said: The shikal among horses is that it has three legs with white socks and one plain, or three plain legs and one with a white sock; and the shikal is only in the hind leg.

Sufyan narrated from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Ill omen is in three: the woman, the horse, and the house." [21] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/136.]]

Its aspects:
Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Tammar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Horses are for three: for a man a reward, for a man a covering, and for a man a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tied it in the way of God, and extended its tether in a meadow or garden, so whatever it grazed of meadow or garden within its tether is good deeds for him; and if it broke its tether and leapt a height or two heights, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him; and if it passed by a river and drank from it, when he did not intend to water it, that is good deeds for him. So it is for that a reward. And a man who tied it out of self-restraint and chastity, and did not forget God's right concerning its necks and backs, so it is for that a covering. And a man who tied it out of pride and show-off and enmity toward the people of Islam, so it is for that a burden."" [22] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/15.]]

And from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Horses are three: a horse for the Merciful, a horse for the human, and a horse for the Devil. As for the horse of the Merciful, it is what is raised in the way of God and upon which God's enemies are slain. As for the horse of the human, it is what is kept for himself and carried upon. As for the horse of the Devil, it is what is wagered upon, gambled over, and raced for stakes." [23] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/260.]]

﴿And the cattle﴾: plural of na'am, and they are camels, cows, and sheep, a plural that has no singular from its own form.

﴿And the tilth﴾: meaning the crops.

﴿That﴾: that which I mentioned.

﴿Is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾: not the provision of the Hereafter and the final end.

﴿And with God is the best return﴾: that is, the place of return, from maf'al from "aba," "ya'ubu awban," like "al-mata'."

Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn al-Arqam say to 'Umar (may God be pleased with him): "O Commander of the Faithful, we have some adornment of leather hides, and vessels of gold and silver; what is your opinion of them?" 'Umar said: "When you see me free, come to me." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you are free today." He said: "Then let us go with him." The wealth was brought. He said: "Spread it out in pieces." It was spread out. Then that wealth was brought and poured over it, and he said: "O God, You mentioned this wealth and said: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: of women, sons, heaped-up hoards of gold and silver﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 14.]] then You said: ﴿So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult in what He has given you﴾ [[Surat al-Hadid: 23.]] O God, we cannot help but exult in what You have given us. O God, spend it in what is right, and I seek refuge in You from it." He said: Then his son was brought to him, carried, named 'Abd al-Rahman, and he said: "O father, give me a ring." He said: "Go to your mother; she will give you sawiq (a sweet drink) to drink." So he gave him nothing.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 8–14 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾: meaning, and those firm in knowledge say, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord..."﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 191.]], meaning they say: ﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate﴾, do not incline them away from the truth and guidance, as the hearts of the Jews and Christians deviated, and ﴿those in whose hearts is deviation﴾.
It is said: zaagha - yazeegh - izaagha, when it inclines.
And zaagha - tazeegh - zaygan - wa-zuyoogan - wa-zaygaanan, when it departs.
﴿After You have guided us﴾: grant us success in Your religion, and faith in the muhkam and the mutashabih of Your Book.
﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾: and give us from Yourself mercy, success and steadfastness in the guidance and faith in which we are.
al-Dahhak said: "Pardon and forgiveness, true ... [.....] [[An illegible word.]] according to the condition of the Sunnah."
﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾: You give. In the verse is a refutation of the Qadariyya.
It is narrated from Asma' bint Yazid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say in his supplication: "O Allah, O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion" [8] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/302.]].
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, do hearts really turn?" He said: "Yes. There is no son of Adam whom Allah created except that his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He makes it deviate, and if He wills, He keeps it upright upon the truth. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, not to let our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us from Himself mercy; indeed He is the Bestower." [[To here is the hadith in Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/356.]]
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you not teach me a supplication to make for myself?"
He said: "Yes, say: 'O Allah, Lord of Muhammad the Prophet, forgive my sin, remove the anger of my heart, and protect me from the misleading trials as long as You keep me alive.'" [9] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/302.]]
And on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, he said: "The likeness of the heart is only the likeness of a feather in a desert of the earth." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/8.]]
Khalid ibn Ma'dan on the authority of Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The heart of the son of Adam is like a sparrow, it turns over seven times in a day." [[Ibid.]]
﴿Our Lord, indeed You are the gatherer of mankind for a Day﴾: [of resurrection for the Day of Judgment] [[From Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 2/13.]] and it is said: the lam means "in" (fi), i.e., on whatever day.
﴿About which there is no doubt﴾: there is no doubt about it, and it is the Day of Resurrection [ ... ] [[Two illegible words.]] when he recited the verse [ ... ] [[Two illegible words.]] and therefore he turned from the address to the report.
﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in the promise﴾: al-mi'ad is mif'al from the wa'd (promise).
﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will never avail them﴾: al-Sulami read (yughni) with the initial ya' and the intervening element [al-ha'il] between the noun and the verb.
And al-Hasan read (lan yughni) with ya' and the final ya' sukun, as in the poet's saying:
"Enough is despair from Asma' as a sufficer, / and there is no cure for its sickness when it lengthens."
Its original form should have been kafiyan, but he dropped the ya' (sent the ya'), and al-Farra' recited in a similar manner:
"As if their hands in the qaraq plain / are hands of maidens reaching for leaves."
al-Qarq and al-Qarqa are two dialects for "plain." [[From Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/22.]]
The meaning of His saying (lan yughni) is: it will not benefit, nor will it ward off. Wealth is called ghina only because it benefits people and wards off from them poverty and calamities.
﴿Their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all﴾.
Al-Kisa'i said, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is "from Allah" as "'inda Allah" (before Allah), min being in the sense of ḥāl (state).
﴿Those are the fuel of the Fire. Like the custom of the family of Pharaoh﴾: the construction of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will never avail them, nor their children﴾ at the arrival of vengeance and punishment, like the family of Pharaoh, and the disbelievers of past nations whom We punished, so ﴿their wealth nor their children will avail them﴾.
As for the meaning of ka-da'b: Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Abu Rawq, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: "like the example of the family of Pharaoh [with Moses]." Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "like the disbelief of the family of Pharaoh," ﴿and those before them﴾.
al-Rabi', al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "like the custom of the family of Pharaoh." al-Akhfash said: "like the affair of the family of Pharaoh."
Imru' al-Qays said:
"Like your custom with Umm al-Huwayrith before her, / and her neighbour Umm al-Rabab at Ma'sal."
[[Fath al-Qadir: 1/321.]]
This is the original root of the word. It is said: da'iba fi al-amr, or da'aba da'aban and da'iban [and yad'a, and da'ubanan] when one persists in the work and is diligent in it.
And ad'aba al-sayr, ad'aban, its meaning returns to the customary practice, the habit and the usage.
The poet said [[It is Zuhayr; see Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/244. The meaning: "unless the birth of a child prevents me."]]:
"I will surely depart at dawn, then I will persist."
Sibawayh said: the position of the kaf is nominative, because the kaf of comparison stands in place of a noun, and its estimate is: their custom is like the custom of the family of Pharaoh and those before them, like the custom of the past nations ﴿they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them﴾:
so He punished them.
﴿for their sins﴾: its parallel is His saying: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [[Surat al-'Ankabut: 40.]].
﴿And Allah is severe in punishment. Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered"﴾: Ishaq, Thabit, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and a group read both with ya'; the rest read both with ta'. Whoever reads both with ya' does so as a report about them, that they will be gathered and overturned; whoever reads both with ta' does so as address, i.e., say to them: "You will be overcome and gathered." Both readings are [sound], because it was not revealed to them, and when the one addressed is absent, and the address in speech is in ta' as second-person address, and in ya' as third-person report and information, as you say: "Say to other than Allah: 'He shall surely strike' and 'you shall surely strike.'"
The commentators differed about who is meant in this verse. Muqatil said: they are the polytheists of Mecca, and the meaning of the verse: it was said to the disbelievers of Mecca: ﴿You will be overcome﴾ at Badr, ﴿and gathered﴾ in the Hijrah.
When this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said to the disbelievers on the day of Badr: "Indeed Allah will overcome you and gather you to Hell."
The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and bitter﴾ [[Surat al-Qamar: 45-46.]].
Others said: the verse is meant for the Jews.
al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ defeated the polytheists at Badr, the Jews of Medina said: "This, by Allah, is the unlettered Prophet whom Moses gave us glad tidings of, and we find his description and attributes in our Book, and that his banner will not be turned back." They wanted to affirm him and follow him. Then some of them said to others: "Do not hasten until you see another stand." When it was the day of Uhud and the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were afflicted, they doubted and said: "No, by Allah, he is not the one," and wretchedness overcame them, and they did not embrace Islam. There had been between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a covenant for a term that had not yet ended, so they broke that covenant on account of it.
Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf set out with sixty riders to the people of Mecca, Abu Sufyan and his companions; they met them and agreed on a plan against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that their word would be one. Then they returned to Medina, and Allah revealed this verse concerning them.
Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of his narrators: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck the Quraysh at Badr and came to Medina, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa' and said: "O assembly of Jews, beware of Allah lest there befall you the like of what befell Quraysh on the day of Badr, and embrace Islam before there befalls you what befell them. You know that I am a sent Prophet; you find that in your Book and in the covenant Allah made with you."
They said: "O Muhammad, do not let it deceive you that you met a people who were inexperienced and had no knowledge of war, and you gained an opportunity against them. By Allah, if we fought you, you would know what manliness we have." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 12.]]: meaning the Jews, ﴿You will be overcome﴾ and defeated, ﴿and gathered to Hell﴾ in the Hereafter. This is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas.
He said: The people of lexicography say that the derivation of Jahannam is from al-jahnam, which is a well of great depth.
﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, meaning the Fire. ﴿There has been for you a sign﴾: he said "kana" and did not say "kanat" because the feminine of "ayah" is not real. It is also said: it refers back to the bayan (clarification), i.e., there has been for you a clarification; he went to the meaning and left the wording, like the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
"A tender, slender, soft one, / like the shoot of the branch that is detached."
He did not say "al-munfatira" because he meant the twig. al-Farra' said: he masculinized it because he separated them by an attribute, and when the attribute came between the verb and the feminine noun, he masculinized the verb and made it feminine:
"Indeed a man whom his unfamiliarity deceived, / after me and after you in the world, is deceived."
Whatever comes in the Qur'an of this kind, this is its explanation. So the meaning of the verse ﴿there has been for you a sign﴾: that is, a lesson and an indication of the truth of what I tell you: ﴿You will be overcome﴾.
﴿In two hosts﴾: two groups and two companies; the original sense in war is that some of them remain behind to others.
﴿Which met﴾ at Badr.
﴿One fighting in the way of Allah﴾: in obedience to Allah, and they were the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions,
and they were three hundred and thirteen men, equal to the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer: seventy-seven men from the Emigrants and two hundred and thirty-six men from the Helpers.
The bearer of the banner of the Prophet ﷺ and the champion was 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and the bearer of the banner of the Helpers was Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah. The camels in the army of the Prophet ﷺ were seventy camels, and the horses were two horses: a horse for al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, and a horse for Marthad ibn Abi Fahd al-'Anazi [[Perhaps: Ibn Abi Marthad.]]. With them were the arms: six coats of mail and eight swords. All the Muslims who were martyred at Badr were fourteen men from the Emigrants and eight from the Helpers.
﴿And another, disbelieving﴾: they were the polytheists of Mecca, and their head was 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn 'Abd Shams. They were nine hundred and fifty fighting men, and their horses were one hundred horses. The battle of Badr was a scene which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ witnessed, and the cause of that was A'yun ibn Sufyan. The readers differed on this verse. Among them, Fi'atun was read with the nominative, meaning "one of them, a group, or one of the two is a group."
al-Zuhri read it in the genitive as a substitution for "the two hosts."
Ibn al-Sumay'a read: fa-ma!, in the sense of praise.
Mujahid read yuqatilu with ya', referring it to the people; there are two possibilities, according to its wording. The rest read with ta'.
﴿They see them as twice their number﴾: Abu Raja', Abu al-Harith, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi', Ya'qub and Ayyub read with ta' and it was preferred by Abu Hatim; the rest read with ya'. Those who read with ta' mean by it: "You see, O assembly of Jews and disbelievers of Mecca, twice the number of the Muslims."
As for those who read with ya', they differed about its meaning. Some made the address to the Muslims, and then it has two interpretations, the first of which:
the Muslims saw the polytheists as their equals in number; then the small number prevailed over the large number by five times, and that is the verse. If it is said that it is so, may he say "mithlayhim" when they were three times their number? The answer is: he says: "This is a likeness, and you have a servant in need of you and of his like; he needed twice him, so you need three." And he says: "I have a thousand, and I need twice that," so you need three thousand. When you intend that the thousand is included in the likeness, the likeness and the two become three.
So said al-Farra'. The other interpretation is that its meaning is: the Muslims saw the polytheists as twice the number of themselves. Allah made them appear few in their eyes until they saw them as six hundred and twenty-six, and they were three times them, nine hundred and fifty. Then He made them appear few in their eyes in another state until they saw them as equal to their own number.
Ibn Mas'ud said: "Regarding this verse: we looked at the polytheists and saw them multiplying against us; then we looked at them and did not see them increase over us even by one; then Allah made them appear few in our eyes until they seemed to us a small number, fewer than ourselves."
Ibn Mas'ud also said: "They were made to appear few in our eyes on the day of Badr, until I said to a man beside me: 'Do you see them as seventy?' He said: 'I see them as a hundred.' Then we took a man of theirs prisoner and said: 'How many were you?' He said: 'A thousand.'"
Some said: the seeing is the seeing of the polytheists, i.e., the polytheists see the believers as twice their number; Allah made them appear few to them before the fighting, i.e., in the eyes of the polytheists, so that they would be emboldened against them and not withdraw; then when they began fighting, He made them appear many to them so they would be cowardly, and made them appear few in the eyes of the believers so that they would be bold. That is His saying: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met, few in your eyes﴾ [[Surat al-Anfal: 44.]] and so on.
Muhammad Abi al-Furat on the authority of Sa'id ibn Abi Awus regarding His saying ﴿They see them as twice their number, with the sight of the eye﴾ said: The polytheists used to see the Muslims as twice their number. When they took them prisoner, the polytheists asked them: "How many were you?" They said: "Three hundred and some ten." They said: "We did not see you except as doubling against us." He said: "And that is among what the Muslims were given victory by."
al-Sulami read yuraunahum with a ḍamma on the ya', in the passive voice without naming the agent; and if you wish, it is in the sense of "thinking" (zann).
ra'ya al-'ayn: that is, in the sight of the eye, an accusative with the particle of attribute removed; and if you wish, it is as a verbal noun, i.e., you see them with the sight of the eye, meaning in the view of the eye. It is said: ra'aytu al-shay' ra'yan wa-ru'yatan wa-ru'ya, three verbal nouns, except that ru'ya is used most often in dreams; to make clear that ra'y al-'ayn means the looking, when it is mentioned.
al-A'sha said:
"When he saw that they had a moment of opinion / of what they saw and what they hid."
﴿And Allah strengthens with His help whom He wills﴾: He strengthens by His victory whom He wills. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ which was mentioned ﴿is a lesson for those of vision﴾: for those of intellect; and it is said: for whoever sees the two hosts.
﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires﴾: plural of shahwah, which is an inclination of the soul toward it. The ha' in the plural was vowelled to make a distinction between the plural of the noun and the plural of the adjective, since the adjective is not vowelled, as in: ḍakhmah, ḍakhmāt; and ḥablah, ḥablāt; while the noun is vowelled, like: tamrah, tamarāt; nafaqat al-jīl, nafaqāt. When the second letter of the noun is a tā' or wāw, most Arabs make it sukūn, [due to the heaviness] of vowelling the yā' and wāw, as you say: bayḍah, bayḍāt; jawzah, jawzāt.
On the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire is surrounded by desires." [12] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/153.]]
﴿Of women﴾: he began with them because they are the nets of Satan and closest to temptation.
﴿And children﴾:
On the authority of al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Ash'ath ibn Qays: "Do you have a daughter of Hamzah among your offspring?" He said: "Yes, I have a boy from her, and I would love to have for him a bowl of food to feed those left of the Banu Hayyah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "If you say that, indeed they are the fruit of the hearts, the coolness of the eyes, and yet they are cowardly, stingy, and grief-causing." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30.]]
﴿And heaped-up hoards of gold and silver﴾: much wealth piled one upon another.
Ibn Kaysan: great wealth. Abu 'Ubaydah: the Arabs say it is that which has no limit.
The rest said: then it is unlimited; then they differed about it:
Abu Salih related from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The qintar is twelve thousand ounces." [13] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/363.]]
On the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, he said: I, Thabit and some people with us entered upon Anas ibn Malik and said to him: "O Abu Hamzah, what did the Prophet ﷺ used to say about the night prayer?" Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites fifty verses in a night is not recorded among the heedless; whoever recites a hundred verses is given the reward of a full night's prayer; whoever recites two hundred verses with the Qur'an has fulfilled its right; whoever recites five hundred verses up to a thousand verses is like one who gave a qintar in charity before morning." It was said: "And what is the qintar?" He said: "A thousand dinars."
Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: The qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces, and this is the saying of Ibn 'Umar and similar.
Zirr ibn Hubaysh related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The qintar is one thousand ounces and two hundred ounces." [14] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30.]]
'Atiyyah related from Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar on the authority of al-Hakam on the authority of al-Dahhak: "The qintar is one thousand two hundred mithqals."
Similarly Yunus related from al-Hasan from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as a mursal report.
Hamzah related on the authority of Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The qintar is one thousand dinars." [15] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/10.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ikrimah: it is a hundred thousand, and a hundred [ratls], a hundred mithqals, and a hundred dirhams. Islam came, on the day it came, when [in Mecca] [[As in the manuscript; perhaps the original reads: "and the qanatir"]] there were a hundred men.

[On the authority of Sufyan from] Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: The qintar is a hundred ratls. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/273.]]

Al-Hakam said: The qintar is as much wealth as lies between the heaven and the earth.

Abu Nadhra: the hide of a bull filled with gold or silver.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Qatadah: eighty thousand.

Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: The qintar is seventy thousand.

Shurayk: forty thousand mithqals.

Al-Hasan: The qintar is the blood-money (diyah) of one of you.

Similarly, al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas, and Juwaybir from al-Dahhak, who said: twelve thousand dirhams or a thousand dinars, the blood-money of one of you.

From Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: In the language of Ifriqiya and al-Andalus, the qintar is eight thousand jarwals of gold or silver.

Al-Thumali narrated from al-Suddi, who said: four thousand mithqals.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some books that the qanatir [derive from binding a thing and making it firm], and its root is from firmness. It is said: "I qanantara al-shay'" (I made the thing firm) when one makes it firm, and from this the bridge is called al-qantarah al-muqantarah. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30, attributing it to al-Zajjaj.]]

Al-Dahhak said: al-Muqantarah: the fortified and secured.

Qatadah: it is the abundant, piled one, some of it upon others, as if it were buried. It is said: qantara when it increased.

Al-Suddi: the stored and minted, until they became dirhams and dinars.

Al-Farra' said: the multiplied, as if the qintar is three and the muqantarah is nine.

Abu Ubaydah: it is mufa'lalah from the qintar, like your saying "alf mu'allaf" (a thousand compiled).

﴿Of gold and silver﴾: it is said gold (dhahab) was so named because it goes away (yadhhabu) and does not remain, and silver (fiddah) because it is scattered (tanfadu), that is, dispersed.

﴿And horses branded﴾: "khayl" (horses) is a plural that has no singular from its own form; its singular is "faras," like "qawm" (people), "nisa'" (women), "rahT" (group), "jaysh" (army), and the like. The scholars differed over the meaning of "al-musawwamah" (branded). Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Rabi' said: it is the grazing one (al-ra'iyah).

Similarly, Atiyyah narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan: it is the pasture-grazing one (al-mar'iyyah). It is said: sāmat al-khayl yasūmu sawman, so it is sa'imah; and I made them graze (asamtuha) when I left them for that purpose, so they are musamamah; and I branded them (sawwamtuha taswiman), so they are musawwamah. God said: ﴿In which you pasture [them]﴾. [[Surat al-Nahl: 10.]]

In this there is the verse of al-Akhtal:
Like Ibn Bazi'ah, or like another such one... Be well, son of the grazing of the appointed times. [[Al-Aghani: 8/319 (Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyyah), where it reads: "like Ibn al-Bazi'ah."]]
He means: the son of the camels.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit and Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid: al-Mutahhamah: the handsome ones. Layth, on the authority of them: al-Musawwarah (the well-formed). And from Ikrimah: their taswim is their beauty. [[Fath al-Qadir: 1/324.]]

Al-Suddi: it is the one that is kept (al-ra'iyah), and all of these have one meaning.

Abu Ubaydah, al-Hasan, al-Akhfash, and al-Qutaybi: the marked/taught one (al-mu'allamah). Similarly, al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Qatadah: their white markings and their colors. Al-Mu'arrij: the branded with a brand (al-makwiyyah). Al-Mubarrad: the known in the lands.

Ibn Kaysan: al-yahlaq... and all of these have been established, and its root is from the sawmah, and al-musayyamah, which is the mark. It is said: "sawwamtu al-khayl taswiman" when I marked the horses. God the Exalted said: ﴿with five thousand angels marked﴾. [[Surat Al 'Imran: 125.]]

Al-Nabighah said describing horses:
With spears like arrows, branded ones, upon them a company resembling jinn.

Al-A'sha said:
And the horsemen of the guards at every frontier, leading the branded noble steeds.

Ibn Zayd and Aban ibn Tha'labah said: al-musawwamah: prepared for war and jihad.

Labid said:
By my life, Kulayb has indeed perished, every generation branded for battle.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some tafsirs that it is the hamalikh (the thoroughbred ones).

Section on horses.
"Their creation's description"
Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated from his father Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When God wished to create creation, He said to the south wind: 'I am creating from you a creature. I will make it a might for My friends, a humiliation for My enemies, and a beauty for the people of My obedience.' The wind said: 'Create.' So He took a handful from it and created a horse from it.

He said to it: 'I created you Arab, and I made good tied to your forelock, and spoils gathered on your back. I bent your companion toward you, and I made you fly without wings: you are for pursuit and you are for flight. I will place on your back men who will glorify Me, praise Me, declare Me one, and magnify Me. You will glorify when they glorify, you will declare Me one when they declare Me one, and you will magnify when they magnify.'"

And the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no glorification, praise, exaltation, or magnification that its doer utters and that goes beyond it, except that it is answered with its like." [16] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/195.]]

Then he said: "When the angels heard the description of the horse, they reproached its Creator, saying: 'Lord, we are Your angels; we glorify You and praise You, so what is for us?' So God created for them horses with necks like the necks of Bactrian camels." He said: "When the horse was sent to the earth and its feet settled on the earth, it neighed. It was said: 'Blessed are you, animal, by whose neighing the polytheists are humbled, by which their necks are made low, by which their ears are filled, and by which their hearts are terrified.'

When God presented to Adam from every creature, He said: 'Choose from My creation what you wish.' He chose the horse. He said to him: 'You have chosen your might and the might of your offspring, eternal while they are eternal, and remaining while they remain. [It will mate and produce offspring from you until the end of time.] My blessing upon you and upon it: I have not created a creature more beloved to Me than you and it.'" [17] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/465, no. 11382; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/195, and 4/111.]]

Its virtue:
Abu Salih narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection." [18] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/49.]]

And from Sa'id ibn Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: Nothing was more beloved to the Messenger of God ﷺ after women than horses.

And from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no Arabian horse except that it is given permission with every dawn to call out two supplications, saying: 'O God, You have made me subject to whoever You have made subject to me among the children of Adam, and You have made me for him; so make me the most beloved of his wealth and his family to him,' or 'of those most beloved to him in wealth and family.'" [19] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/170.]]

Its condition:
From Abu Wahb al-Husayni, who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Tie up horses, wipe their forelocks and their rumps, put collars on them, and do not put on them bowstrings. You should have every bay with a white blaze (aghurr) [[al-Aghurr: one that has a white mark on its forehead the size of a dirham.]] and white socks, or a chestnut with white socks, or a black with a blaze and white socks." [20] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/218.]]

Abu Zur'ah narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet used to dislike the shikal [[al-Shikal: whiteness in the two forelegs, or only in the right foreleg and the right hind leg; it is said the reverse is in the left.]] among horses.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman said: The shikal among horses is that it has three legs with white socks and one plain, or three plain legs and one with a white sock; and the shikal is only in the hind leg.

Sufyan narrated from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Ill omen is in three: the woman, the horse, and the house." [21] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/136.]]

Its aspects:
Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Tammar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Horses are for three: for a man a reward, for a man a covering, and for a man a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tied it in the way of God, and extended its tether in a meadow or garden, so whatever it grazed of meadow or garden within its tether is good deeds for him; and if it broke its tether and leapt a height or two heights, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him; and if it passed by a river and drank from it, when he did not intend to water it, that is good deeds for him. So it is for that a reward. And a man who tied it out of self-restraint and chastity, and did not forget God's right concerning its necks and backs, so it is for that a covering. And a man who tied it out of pride and show-off and enmity toward the people of Islam, so it is for that a burden."" [22] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/15.]]

And from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Horses are three: a horse for the Merciful, a horse for the human, and a horse for the Devil. As for the horse of the Merciful, it is what is raised in the way of God and upon which God's enemies are slain. As for the horse of the human, it is what is kept for himself and carried upon. As for the horse of the Devil, it is what is wagered upon, gambled over, and raced for stakes." [23] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/260.]]

﴿And the cattle﴾: plural of na'am, and they are camels, cows, and sheep, a plural that has no singular from its own form.

﴿And the tilth﴾: meaning the crops.

﴿That﴾: that which I mentioned.

﴿Is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾: not the provision of the Hereafter and the final end.

﴿And with God is the best return﴾: that is, the place of return, from maf'al from "aba," "ya'ubu awban," like "al-mata'."

Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn al-Arqam say to 'Umar (may God be pleased with him): "O Commander of the Faithful, we have some adornment of leather hides, and vessels of gold and silver; what is your opinion of them?" 'Umar said: "When you see me free, come to me." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you are free today." He said: "Then let us go with him." The wealth was brought. He said: "Spread it out in pieces." It was spread out. Then that wealth was brought and poured over it, and he said: "O God, You mentioned this wealth and said: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: of women, sons, heaped-up hoards of gold and silver﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 14.]] then You said: ﴿So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult in what He has given you﴾ [[Surat al-Hadid: 23.]] O God, we cannot help but exult in what You have given us. O God, spend it in what is right, and I seek refuge in You from it." He said: Then his son was brought to him, carried, named 'Abd al-Rahman, and he said: "O father, give me a ring." He said: "Go to your mother; she will give you sawiq (a sweet drink) to drink." So he gave him nothing.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 8–14 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾: meaning, and those firm in knowledge say, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord..."﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 191.]], meaning they say: ﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate﴾, do not incline them away from the truth and guidance, as the hearts of the Jews and Christians deviated, and ﴿those in whose hearts is deviation﴾.
It is said: zaagha - yazeegh - izaagha, when it inclines.
And zaagha - tazeegh - zaygan - wa-zuyoogan - wa-zaygaanan, when it departs.
﴿After You have guided us﴾: grant us success in Your religion, and faith in the muhkam and the mutashabih of Your Book.
﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾: and give us from Yourself mercy, success and steadfastness in the guidance and faith in which we are.
al-Dahhak said: "Pardon and forgiveness, true ... [.....] [[An illegible word.]] according to the condition of the Sunnah."
﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾: You give. In the verse is a refutation of the Qadariyya.
It is narrated from Asma' bint Yazid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say in his supplication: "O Allah, O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion" [8] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/302.]].
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, do hearts really turn?" He said: "Yes. There is no son of Adam whom Allah created except that his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He makes it deviate, and if He wills, He keeps it upright upon the truth. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, not to let our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us from Himself mercy; indeed He is the Bestower." [[To here is the hadith in Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/356.]]
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you not teach me a supplication to make for myself?"
He said: "Yes, say: 'O Allah, Lord of Muhammad the Prophet, forgive my sin, remove the anger of my heart, and protect me from the misleading trials as long as You keep me alive.'" [9] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/302.]]
And on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, he said: "The likeness of the heart is only the likeness of a feather in a desert of the earth." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/8.]]
Khalid ibn Ma'dan on the authority of Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The heart of the son of Adam is like a sparrow, it turns over seven times in a day." [[Ibid.]]
﴿Our Lord, indeed You are the gatherer of mankind for a Day﴾: [of resurrection for the Day of Judgment] [[From Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 2/13.]] and it is said: the lam means "in" (fi), i.e., on whatever day.
﴿About which there is no doubt﴾: there is no doubt about it, and it is the Day of Resurrection [ ... ] [[Two illegible words.]] when he recited the verse [ ... ] [[Two illegible words.]] and therefore he turned from the address to the report.
﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in the promise﴾: al-mi'ad is mif'al from the wa'd (promise).
﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will never avail them﴾: al-Sulami read (yughni) with the initial ya' and the intervening element [al-ha'il] between the noun and the verb.
And al-Hasan read (lan yughni) with ya' and the final ya' sukun, as in the poet's saying:
"Enough is despair from Asma' as a sufficer, / and there is no cure for its sickness when it lengthens."
Its original form should have been kafiyan, but he dropped the ya' (sent the ya'), and al-Farra' recited in a similar manner:
"As if their hands in the qaraq plain / are hands of maidens reaching for leaves."
al-Qarq and al-Qarqa are two dialects for "plain." [[From Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/22.]]
The meaning of His saying (lan yughni) is: it will not benefit, nor will it ward off. Wealth is called ghina only because it benefits people and wards off from them poverty and calamities.
﴿Their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all﴾.
Al-Kisa'i said, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is "from Allah" as "'inda Allah" (before Allah), min being in the sense of ḥāl (state).
﴿Those are the fuel of the Fire. Like the custom of the family of Pharaoh﴾: the construction of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will never avail them, nor their children﴾ at the arrival of vengeance and punishment, like the family of Pharaoh, and the disbelievers of past nations whom We punished, so ﴿their wealth nor their children will avail them﴾.
As for the meaning of ka-da'b: Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Abu Rawq, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: "like the example of the family of Pharaoh [with Moses]." Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "like the disbelief of the family of Pharaoh," ﴿and those before them﴾.
al-Rabi', al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "like the custom of the family of Pharaoh." al-Akhfash said: "like the affair of the family of Pharaoh."
Imru' al-Qays said:
"Like your custom with Umm al-Huwayrith before her, / and her neighbour Umm al-Rabab at Ma'sal."
[[Fath al-Qadir: 1/321.]]
This is the original root of the word. It is said: da'iba fi al-amr, or da'aba da'aban and da'iban [and yad'a, and da'ubanan] when one persists in the work and is diligent in it.
And ad'aba al-sayr, ad'aban, its meaning returns to the customary practice, the habit and the usage.
The poet said [[It is Zuhayr; see Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/244. The meaning: "unless the birth of a child prevents me."]]:
"I will surely depart at dawn, then I will persist."
Sibawayh said: the position of the kaf is nominative, because the kaf of comparison stands in place of a noun, and its estimate is: their custom is like the custom of the family of Pharaoh and those before them, like the custom of the past nations ﴿they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them﴾:
so He punished them.
﴿for their sins﴾: its parallel is His saying: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [[Surat al-'Ankabut: 40.]].
﴿And Allah is severe in punishment. Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered"﴾: Ishaq, Thabit, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and a group read both with ya'; the rest read both with ta'. Whoever reads both with ya' does so as a report about them, that they will be gathered and overturned; whoever reads both with ta' does so as address, i.e., say to them: "You will be overcome and gathered." Both readings are [sound], because it was not revealed to them, and when the one addressed is absent, and the address in speech is in ta' as second-person address, and in ya' as third-person report and information, as you say: "Say to other than Allah: 'He shall surely strike' and 'you shall surely strike.'"
The commentators differed about who is meant in this verse. Muqatil said: they are the polytheists of Mecca, and the meaning of the verse: it was said to the disbelievers of Mecca: ﴿You will be overcome﴾ at Badr, ﴿and gathered﴾ in the Hijrah.
When this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said to the disbelievers on the day of Badr: "Indeed Allah will overcome you and gather you to Hell."
The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and bitter﴾ [[Surat al-Qamar: 45-46.]].
Others said: the verse is meant for the Jews.
al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ defeated the polytheists at Badr, the Jews of Medina said: "This, by Allah, is the unlettered Prophet whom Moses gave us glad tidings of, and we find his description and attributes in our Book, and that his banner will not be turned back." They wanted to affirm him and follow him. Then some of them said to others: "Do not hasten until you see another stand." When it was the day of Uhud and the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were afflicted, they doubted and said: "No, by Allah, he is not the one," and wretchedness overcame them, and they did not embrace Islam. There had been between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a covenant for a term that had not yet ended, so they broke that covenant on account of it.
Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf set out with sixty riders to the people of Mecca, Abu Sufyan and his companions; they met them and agreed on a plan against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that their word would be one. Then they returned to Medina, and Allah revealed this verse concerning them.
Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of his narrators: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck the Quraysh at Badr and came to Medina, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa' and said: "O assembly of Jews, beware of Allah lest there befall you the like of what befell Quraysh on the day of Badr, and embrace Islam before there befalls you what befell them. You know that I am a sent Prophet; you find that in your Book and in the covenant Allah made with you."
They said: "O Muhammad, do not let it deceive you that you met a people who were inexperienced and had no knowledge of war, and you gained an opportunity against them. By Allah, if we fought you, you would know what manliness we have." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 12.]]: meaning the Jews, ﴿You will be overcome﴾ and defeated, ﴿and gathered to Hell﴾ in the Hereafter. This is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas.
He said: The people of lexicography say that the derivation of Jahannam is from al-jahnam, which is a well of great depth.
﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, meaning the Fire. ﴿There has been for you a sign﴾: he said "kana" and did not say "kanat" because the feminine of "ayah" is not real. It is also said: it refers back to the bayan (clarification), i.e., there has been for you a clarification; he went to the meaning and left the wording, like the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
"A tender, slender, soft one, / like the shoot of the branch that is detached."
He did not say "al-munfatira" because he meant the twig. al-Farra' said: he masculinized it because he separated them by an attribute, and when the attribute came between the verb and the feminine noun, he masculinized the verb and made it feminine:
"Indeed a man whom his unfamiliarity deceived, / after me and after you in the world, is deceived."
Whatever comes in the Qur'an of this kind, this is its explanation. So the meaning of the verse ﴿there has been for you a sign﴾: that is, a lesson and an indication of the truth of what I tell you: ﴿You will be overcome﴾.
﴿In two hosts﴾: two groups and two companies; the original sense in war is that some of them remain behind to others.
﴿Which met﴾ at Badr.
﴿One fighting in the way of Allah﴾: in obedience to Allah, and they were the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions,
and they were three hundred and thirteen men, equal to the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer: seventy-seven men from the Emigrants and two hundred and thirty-six men from the Helpers.
The bearer of the banner of the Prophet ﷺ and the champion was 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and the bearer of the banner of the Helpers was Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah. The camels in the army of the Prophet ﷺ were seventy camels, and the horses were two horses: a horse for al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, and a horse for Marthad ibn Abi Fahd al-'Anazi [[Perhaps: Ibn Abi Marthad.]]. With them were the arms: six coats of mail and eight swords. All the Muslims who were martyred at Badr were fourteen men from the Emigrants and eight from the Helpers.
﴿And another, disbelieving﴾: they were the polytheists of Mecca, and their head was 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn 'Abd Shams. They were nine hundred and fifty fighting men, and their horses were one hundred horses. The battle of Badr was a scene which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ witnessed, and the cause of that was A'yun ibn Sufyan. The readers differed on this verse. Among them, Fi'atun was read with the nominative, meaning "one of them, a group, or one of the two is a group."
al-Zuhri read it in the genitive as a substitution for "the two hosts."
Ibn al-Sumay'a read: fa-ma!, in the sense of praise.
Mujahid read yuqatilu with ya', referring it to the people; there are two possibilities, according to its wording. The rest read with ta'.
﴿They see them as twice their number﴾: Abu Raja', Abu al-Harith, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi', Ya'qub and Ayyub read with ta' and it was preferred by Abu Hatim; the rest read with ya'. Those who read with ta' mean by it: "You see, O assembly of Jews and disbelievers of Mecca, twice the number of the Muslims."
As for those who read with ya', they differed about its meaning. Some made the address to the Muslims, and then it has two interpretations, the first of which:
the Muslims saw the polytheists as their equals in number; then the small number prevailed over the large number by five times, and that is the verse. If it is said that it is so, may he say "mithlayhim" when they were three times their number? The answer is: he says: "This is a likeness, and you have a servant in need of you and of his like; he needed twice him, so you need three." And he says: "I have a thousand, and I need twice that," so you need three thousand. When you intend that the thousand is included in the likeness, the likeness and the two become three.
So said al-Farra'. The other interpretation is that its meaning is: the Muslims saw the polytheists as twice the number of themselves. Allah made them appear few in their eyes until they saw them as six hundred and twenty-six, and they were three times them, nine hundred and fifty. Then He made them appear few in their eyes in another state until they saw them as equal to their own number.
Ibn Mas'ud said: "Regarding this verse: we looked at the polytheists and saw them multiplying against us; then we looked at them and did not see them increase over us even by one; then Allah made them appear few in our eyes until they seemed to us a small number, fewer than ourselves."
Ibn Mas'ud also said: "They were made to appear few in our eyes on the day of Badr, until I said to a man beside me: 'Do you see them as seventy?' He said: 'I see them as a hundred.' Then we took a man of theirs prisoner and said: 'How many were you?' He said: 'A thousand.'"
Some said: the seeing is the seeing of the polytheists, i.e., the polytheists see the believers as twice their number; Allah made them appear few to them before the fighting, i.e., in the eyes of the polytheists, so that they would be emboldened against them and not withdraw; then when they began fighting, He made them appear many to them so they would be cowardly, and made them appear few in the eyes of the believers so that they would be bold. That is His saying: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met, few in your eyes﴾ [[Surat al-Anfal: 44.]] and so on.
Muhammad Abi al-Furat on the authority of Sa'id ibn Abi Awus regarding His saying ﴿They see them as twice their number, with the sight of the eye﴾ said: The polytheists used to see the Muslims as twice their number. When they took them prisoner, the polytheists asked them: "How many were you?" They said: "Three hundred and some ten." They said: "We did not see you except as doubling against us." He said: "And that is among what the Muslims were given victory by."
al-Sulami read yuraunahum with a ḍamma on the ya', in the passive voice without naming the agent; and if you wish, it is in the sense of "thinking" (zann).
ra'ya al-'ayn: that is, in the sight of the eye, an accusative with the particle of attribute removed; and if you wish, it is as a verbal noun, i.e., you see them with the sight of the eye, meaning in the view of the eye. It is said: ra'aytu al-shay' ra'yan wa-ru'yatan wa-ru'ya, three verbal nouns, except that ru'ya is used most often in dreams; to make clear that ra'y al-'ayn means the looking, when it is mentioned.
al-A'sha said:
"When he saw that they had a moment of opinion / of what they saw and what they hid."
﴿And Allah strengthens with His help whom He wills﴾: He strengthens by His victory whom He wills. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ which was mentioned ﴿is a lesson for those of vision﴾: for those of intellect; and it is said: for whoever sees the two hosts.
﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires﴾: plural of shahwah, which is an inclination of the soul toward it. The ha' in the plural was vowelled to make a distinction between the plural of the noun and the plural of the adjective, since the adjective is not vowelled, as in: ḍakhmah, ḍakhmāt; and ḥablah, ḥablāt; while the noun is vowelled, like: tamrah, tamarāt; nafaqat al-jīl, nafaqāt. When the second letter of the noun is a tā' or wāw, most Arabs make it sukūn, [due to the heaviness] of vowelling the yā' and wāw, as you say: bayḍah, bayḍāt; jawzah, jawzāt.
On the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire is surrounded by desires." [12] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/153.]]
﴿Of women﴾: he began with them because they are the nets of Satan and closest to temptation.
﴿And children﴾:
On the authority of al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Ash'ath ibn Qays: "Do you have a daughter of Hamzah among your offspring?" He said: "Yes, I have a boy from her, and I would love to have for him a bowl of food to feed those left of the Banu Hayyah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "If you say that, indeed they are the fruit of the hearts, the coolness of the eyes, and yet they are cowardly, stingy, and grief-causing." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30.]]
﴿And heaped-up hoards of gold and silver﴾: much wealth piled one upon another.
Ibn Kaysan: great wealth. Abu 'Ubaydah: the Arabs say it is that which has no limit.
The rest said: then it is unlimited; then they differed about it:
Abu Salih related from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The qintar is twelve thousand ounces." [13] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/363.]]
On the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, he said: I, Thabit and some people with us entered upon Anas ibn Malik and said to him: "O Abu Hamzah, what did the Prophet ﷺ used to say about the night prayer?" Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites fifty verses in a night is not recorded among the heedless; whoever recites a hundred verses is given the reward of a full night's prayer; whoever recites two hundred verses with the Qur'an has fulfilled its right; whoever recites five hundred verses up to a thousand verses is like one who gave a qintar in charity before morning." It was said: "And what is the qintar?" He said: "A thousand dinars."
Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: The qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces, and this is the saying of Ibn 'Umar and similar.
Zirr ibn Hubaysh related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The qintar is one thousand ounces and two hundred ounces." [14] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30.]]
'Atiyyah related from Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar on the authority of al-Hakam on the authority of al-Dahhak: "The qintar is one thousand two hundred mithqals."
Similarly Yunus related from al-Hasan from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as a mursal report.
Hamzah related on the authority of Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The qintar is one thousand dinars." [15] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/10.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ikrimah: it is a hundred thousand, and a hundred [ratls], a hundred mithqals, and a hundred dirhams. Islam came, on the day it came, when [in Mecca] [[As in the manuscript; perhaps the original reads: "and the qanatir"]] there were a hundred men.

[On the authority of Sufyan from] Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: The qintar is a hundred ratls. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/273.]]

Al-Hakam said: The qintar is as much wealth as lies between the heaven and the earth.

Abu Nadhra: the hide of a bull filled with gold or silver.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Qatadah: eighty thousand.

Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: The qintar is seventy thousand.

Shurayk: forty thousand mithqals.

Al-Hasan: The qintar is the blood-money (diyah) of one of you.

Similarly, al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas, and Juwaybir from al-Dahhak, who said: twelve thousand dirhams or a thousand dinars, the blood-money of one of you.

From Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: In the language of Ifriqiya and al-Andalus, the qintar is eight thousand jarwals of gold or silver.

Al-Thumali narrated from al-Suddi, who said: four thousand mithqals.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some books that the qanatir [derive from binding a thing and making it firm], and its root is from firmness. It is said: "I qanantara al-shay'" (I made the thing firm) when one makes it firm, and from this the bridge is called al-qantarah al-muqantarah. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/30, attributing it to al-Zajjaj.]]

Al-Dahhak said: al-Muqantarah: the fortified and secured.

Qatadah: it is the abundant, piled one, some of it upon others, as if it were buried. It is said: qantara when it increased.

Al-Suddi: the stored and minted, until they became dirhams and dinars.

Al-Farra' said: the multiplied, as if the qintar is three and the muqantarah is nine.

Abu Ubaydah: it is mufa'lalah from the qintar, like your saying "alf mu'allaf" (a thousand compiled).

﴿Of gold and silver﴾: it is said gold (dhahab) was so named because it goes away (yadhhabu) and does not remain, and silver (fiddah) because it is scattered (tanfadu), that is, dispersed.

﴿And horses branded﴾: "khayl" (horses) is a plural that has no singular from its own form; its singular is "faras," like "qawm" (people), "nisa'" (women), "rahT" (group), "jaysh" (army), and the like. The scholars differed over the meaning of "al-musawwamah" (branded). Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Rabi' said: it is the grazing one (al-ra'iyah).

Similarly, Atiyyah narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan: it is the pasture-grazing one (al-mar'iyyah). It is said: sāmat al-khayl yasūmu sawman, so it is sa'imah; and I made them graze (asamtuha) when I left them for that purpose, so they are musamamah; and I branded them (sawwamtuha taswiman), so they are musawwamah. God said: ﴿In which you pasture [them]﴾. [[Surat al-Nahl: 10.]]

In this there is the verse of al-Akhtal:
Like Ibn Bazi'ah, or like another such one... Be well, son of the grazing of the appointed times. [[Al-Aghani: 8/319 (Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyyah), where it reads: "like Ibn al-Bazi'ah."]]
He means: the son of the camels.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit and Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid: al-Mutahhamah: the handsome ones. Layth, on the authority of them: al-Musawwarah (the well-formed). And from Ikrimah: their taswim is their beauty. [[Fath al-Qadir: 1/324.]]

Al-Suddi: it is the one that is kept (al-ra'iyah), and all of these have one meaning.

Abu Ubaydah, al-Hasan, al-Akhfash, and al-Qutaybi: the marked/taught one (al-mu'allamah). Similarly, al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Qatadah: their white markings and their colors. Al-Mu'arrij: the branded with a brand (al-makwiyyah). Al-Mubarrad: the known in the lands.

Ibn Kaysan: al-yahlaq... and all of these have been established, and its root is from the sawmah, and al-musayyamah, which is the mark. It is said: "sawwamtu al-khayl taswiman" when I marked the horses. God the Exalted said: ﴿with five thousand angels marked﴾. [[Surat Al 'Imran: 125.]]

Al-Nabighah said describing horses:
With spears like arrows, branded ones, upon them a company resembling jinn.

Al-A'sha said:
And the horsemen of the guards at every frontier, leading the branded noble steeds.

Ibn Zayd and Aban ibn Tha'labah said: al-musawwamah: prepared for war and jihad.

Labid said:
By my life, Kulayb has indeed perished, every generation branded for battle.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some tafsirs that it is the hamalikh (the thoroughbred ones).

Section on horses.
"Their creation's description"
Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated from his father Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When God wished to create creation, He said to the south wind: 'I am creating from you a creature. I will make it a might for My friends, a humiliation for My enemies, and a beauty for the people of My obedience.' The wind said: 'Create.' So He took a handful from it and created a horse from it.

He said to it: 'I created you Arab, and I made good tied to your forelock, and spoils gathered on your back. I bent your companion toward you, and I made you fly without wings: you are for pursuit and you are for flight. I will place on your back men who will glorify Me, praise Me, declare Me one, and magnify Me. You will glorify when they glorify, you will declare Me one when they declare Me one, and you will magnify when they magnify.'"

And the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no glorification, praise, exaltation, or magnification that its doer utters and that goes beyond it, except that it is answered with its like." [16] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/195.]]

Then he said: "When the angels heard the description of the horse, they reproached its Creator, saying: 'Lord, we are Your angels; we glorify You and praise You, so what is for us?' So God created for them horses with necks like the necks of Bactrian camels." He said: "When the horse was sent to the earth and its feet settled on the earth, it neighed. It was said: 'Blessed are you, animal, by whose neighing the polytheists are humbled, by which their necks are made low, by which their ears are filled, and by which their hearts are terrified.'

When God presented to Adam from every creature, He said: 'Choose from My creation what you wish.' He chose the horse. He said to him: 'You have chosen your might and the might of your offspring, eternal while they are eternal, and remaining while they remain. [It will mate and produce offspring from you until the end of time.] My blessing upon you and upon it: I have not created a creature more beloved to Me than you and it.'" [17] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/465, no. 11382; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/195, and 4/111.]]

Its virtue:
Abu Salih narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection." [18] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/49.]]

And from Sa'id ibn Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: Nothing was more beloved to the Messenger of God ﷺ after women than horses.

And from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no Arabian horse except that it is given permission with every dawn to call out two supplications, saying: 'O God, You have made me subject to whoever You have made subject to me among the children of Adam, and You have made me for him; so make me the most beloved of his wealth and his family to him,' or 'of those most beloved to him in wealth and family.'" [19] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/170.]]

Its condition:
From Abu Wahb al-Husayni, who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Tie up horses, wipe their forelocks and their rumps, put collars on them, and do not put on them bowstrings. You should have every bay with a white blaze (aghurr) [[al-Aghurr: one that has a white mark on its forehead the size of a dirham.]] and white socks, or a chestnut with white socks, or a black with a blaze and white socks." [20] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/218.]]

Abu Zur'ah narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet used to dislike the shikal [[al-Shikal: whiteness in the two forelegs, or only in the right foreleg and the right hind leg; it is said the reverse is in the left.]] among horses.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman said: The shikal among horses is that it has three legs with white socks and one plain, or three plain legs and one with a white sock; and the shikal is only in the hind leg.

Sufyan narrated from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Ill omen is in three: the woman, the horse, and the house." [21] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/136.]]

Its aspects:
Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Tammar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Horses are for three: for a man a reward, for a man a covering, and for a man a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tied it in the way of God, and extended its tether in a meadow or garden, so whatever it grazed of meadow or garden within its tether is good deeds for him; and if it broke its tether and leapt a height or two heights, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him; and if it passed by a river and drank from it, when he did not intend to water it, that is good deeds for him. So it is for that a reward. And a man who tied it out of self-restraint and chastity, and did not forget God's right concerning its necks and backs, so it is for that a covering. And a man who tied it out of pride and show-off and enmity toward the people of Islam, so it is for that a burden."" [22] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/15.]]

And from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Horses are three: a horse for the Merciful, a horse for the human, and a horse for the Devil. As for the horse of the Merciful, it is what is raised in the way of God and upon which God's enemies are slain. As for the horse of the human, it is what is kept for himself and carried upon. As for the horse of the Devil, it is what is wagered upon, gambled over, and raced for stakes." [23] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/260.]]

﴿And the cattle﴾: plural of na'am, and they are camels, cows, and sheep, a plural that has no singular from its own form.

﴿And the tilth﴾: meaning the crops.

﴿That﴾: that which I mentioned.

﴿Is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾: not the provision of the Hereafter and the final end.

﴿And with God is the best return﴾: that is, the place of return, from maf'al from "aba," "ya'ubu awban," like "al-mata'."

Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn al-Arqam say to 'Umar (may God be pleased with him): "O Commander of the Faithful, we have some adornment of leather hides, and vessels of gold and silver; what is your opinion of them?" 'Umar said: "When you see me free, come to me." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you are free today." He said: "Then let us go with him." The wealth was brought. He said: "Spread it out in pieces." It was spread out. Then that wealth was brought and poured over it, and he said: "O God, You mentioned this wealth and said: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: of women, sons, heaped-up hoards of gold and silver﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 14.]] then You said: ﴿So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult in what He has given you﴾ [[Surat al-Hadid: 23.]] O God, we cannot help but exult in what You have given us. O God, spend it in what is right, and I seek refuge in You from it." He said: Then his son was brought to him, carried, named 'Abd al-Rahman, and he said: "O father, give me a ring." He said: "Go to your mother; she will give you sawiq (a sweet drink) to drink." So he gave him nothing.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 8–14 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾: meaning, and those firm in knowledge say, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord..."﴾ [[Surat Al 'Imran: 191.]], meaning they say: ﴿Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate﴾, do not incline them away from the truth and guidance, as the hearts of the Jews and Christians deviated, and ﴿those in whose hearts is deviation﴾.
It is said: zaagha - yazeegh - izaagha, when it inclines.
And zaagha - tazeegh - zaygan - wa-zuyoogan - wa-zaygaanan, when it departs.
﴿After You have guided us﴾: grant us success in Your religion, and faith in the muhkam and the mutashabih of Your Book.
﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾: and give us from Yourself mercy, success and steadfastness in the guidance and faith in which we are.
al-Dahhak said: "Pardon and forgiveness, true ... [.....] [[An illegible word.]] according to the condition of the Sunnah."
﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾: You give. In the verse is a refutation of the Qadariyya.
It is narrated from Asma' bint Yazid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say in his supplication: "O Allah, O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion" [8] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/302.]].
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, do hearts really turn?" He said: "Yes. There is no son of Adam whom Allah created except that his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He makes it deviate, and if He wills, He keeps it upright upon the truth. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, not to let our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us from Himself mercy; indeed He is the Bestower." [[To here is the hadith in Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/356.]]
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you not teach me a supplication to make for myself?"
He said: "Yes, say: 'O Allah, Lord of Muhammad the Prophet, forgive my sin, remove the anger of my heart, and protect me from the misleading trials as long as You keep me alive.'" [9] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/302.]]
And on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, he said: "The likeness of the heart is only the likeness of a feather in a desert of the earth." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/8.]]
Khalid ibn Ma'dan on the authority of Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The heart of the son of Adam is like a sparrow, it turns over seven times in a day." [[Ibid.]]
﴿Our Lord, indeed You are the gatherer of mankind for a Day﴾: [of resurrection for the Day of Judgment] [[From Tafsir al-Tha'alabi: 2/13.]] and it is said: the lam means "in" (fi), i.e., on whatever day.
﴿About which there is no doubt﴾: there is no doubt about it, and it is the Day of Resurrection [ ... ] [[Two illegible words.]] when he recited the verse [ ... ] [[Two illegible words.]] and therefore he turned from the address to the report.
﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in the promise﴾: al-mi'ad is mif'al from the wa'd (promise).
﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will never avail them﴾: al-Sulami read (yughni) with the initial ya' and the intervening element [al-ha'il] between the noun and the verb.
And al-Hasan read (lan yughni) with ya' and the final ya' sukun, as in the poet's saying:
"Enough is despair from Asma' as a sufficer, / and there is no cure for its sickness when it lengthens."
Its original form should have been kafiyan, but he dropped the ya' (sent the ya'), and al-Farra' recited in a similar manner:
"As if their hands in the qaraq plain / are hands of maidens reaching for leaves."
al-Qarq and al-Qarqa are two dialects for "plain." [[From Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/22.]]
The meaning of His saying (lan yughni) is: it will not benefit, nor will it ward off. Wealth is called ghina only because it benefits people and wards off from them poverty and calamities.
﴿Their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all﴾.
Al-Kisa'i said, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is "from Allah" as "'inda Allah" (before Allah), min being in the sense of ḥāl (state).
﴿Those are the fuel of the Fire. Like the custom of the family of Pharaoh﴾: the construction of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will never avail them, nor their children﴾ at the arrival of vengeance and punishment, like the family of Pharaoh, and the disbelievers of past nations whom We punished, so ﴿their wealth nor their children will avail them﴾.
