[36] [[Fath al-Bari: 12/150; note that the phrase "the two Jews" is not mentioned in the hadith.]] Then the Messenger of God commanded that the two Jews be stoned. The Jews became exceedingly angry at that and dispersed. So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

**"Have you not considered those who were given a share of the Book"**: a portion of the Torah.

**"They are called to the Book of God so that it may judge between them, then a party of them turns away"**: He had informed them that it is in the Torah.

**"And they are turning away. That is because they said: 'The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days,' and their fabrications have deceived them in their religion. So how will it be when We gather them"**: that is, how will they act for **"a Day about which there is no doubt"**: which is the Day of Resurrection.

**"And every soul will be paid in full"**: righteous or wicked.

**"for what it earned"**: that is, the recompense of what it did, of good or evil.

**"And they will not be wronged"**: their good deeds will not be diminished, nor will their evil deeds be increased.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first banner raised for the people of the gathering on that Day is the banner of the disbelievers, the banner of the Jews. God will humiliate them before the witnesses, then He will command that they be taken to the Fire."

**"Say: O God, Owner of Sovereignty"**:

Al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God wished to send down the Opening of the Book, and the Verse of the Throne, and 'God bears witness,' and 'Say: O God, Owner of Sovereignty...'
...to 'without reckoning,' they hung from the Throne, and there was no veil between them and God, and they said: 'O Lord, will You cast us down into the abode of sins, and to one who disobeys You, while we are attached to the birds and the Throne?' He, exalted is He, said: 'By My might and My majesty, there is no servant who recites you at the end of every obligatory prayer except that I will settle him in the enclosure of holiness with what he had in it, and I will look upon him with My eye seventy times every day, and I will fulfil for him seventy needs every day, the least of which is forgiveness, and I will protect him from every enemy and grant him victory over it, and nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except associating partners with Me.'"

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "I was detained from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) one day, and I did not pray the Friday prayer with him. He said: 'O Mu'adh, what prevented you from the Friday prayer?' I said: 'O Messenger of God, the Jew Yuhanna had an ounce [of gold] owed to him by me, and he was watching me at my door, and I feared that he would detain me away from you.' He said: 'Would you like, O Mu'adh, that God pay off your debt?' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Say: "O God, Owner of Sovereignty..." to His saying "without reckoning," and say: "O Compassionate of this world and the Hereafter and its Merciful, You give from it what You will and withhold from it what You will, settle my debt for me." For if you had owed the earth filled with gold, God would settle it for you.'" [37] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/52; Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 3/320, no. 2398.]]

Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his Lord to make the kingdom of Persia and Rome belong to his community, so God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Abbas and Anas ibn Malik said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered Mecca and promised his community the kingdom of Persia and Rome, the hypocrites and the Jews said: "Far-fetched, far-fetched! From where would Muhammad have the kingdom of Persia? They are more powerful and stronger than that. Was it not enough for Muhammad to have Mecca and Medina, that he should aspire to the kingdom of Persia and Rome?" So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Awf narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) dug the trench in the year of the Confederates. Then he marked off forty cubits, ten for each group. He said: The Emigrants and the Helpers disputed concerning Salman al-Farisi, who was a strong man. The Emigrants said: "Salman is one of us." The Helpers said: "Salman is one of us."
The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." [38]

Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfa, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani, and six men from the Helpers were in forty cubits. We dug until we reached the hard ground, and God brought forth from the belly of the trench a hard white rock which broke our iron and was difficult for us. We said: "O Salman, go to the Messenger of God and inform him of the matter of this rock, for either we will turn away from it, for turning away is close, or he will command us regarding it with a command, for we do not wish to go beyond his line."

He said: So Salman climbed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who had a Turkish dome pitched over him. He said: "O Messenger of God, a white hard rock has emerged from the belly of the trench, and it has broken our iron and has been difficult for us, so that nothing, little or much, can be taken from it. So command us regarding it with your command, for we do not wish to go beyond your line." He said: So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) descended with Salman into the trench, and we nine remained on the edge of the trench. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck it a blow which split it, and from it a flash shone which lit up what was between its two lava fields (meaning Medina), until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." Then he (ﷺ) struck it and broke it, and from it a flash shone which lit up what was between its two lava fields, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar" with him. Then he took Salman by the hand and climbed up.

Salman said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God! I have seen something the like of which I have never seen before!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God [may our fathers and mothers be your ransom; we saw you strike and a flash came out like a wave, and we saw you say takbir so we said takbir, and we saw nothing other than that]."

He said: "I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw, the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra were illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs, and Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw, the palaces of Busra in the land of Rome were illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs, and Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. [Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw, the palaces of San'a were illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs, and Jibril informed me that my community will prevail over them.] [[Not found in Tafsir al-Tabari.]] So rejoice!" The Muslims rejoiced and said:
"Praise be to God, a true promise, that He promised us victory after siege."
[Then the confederates advanced, and the Muslims said:
"This is what God and His Messenger promised us" [[Surat al-Ahzab: 22.]] to the end of the verse.]

The hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel? He promises you and makes you hope for falsehood, and informs you that from Yathrib he sees the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be conquered for you, while you are only digging the trench out of fear, unable to come out!" He said: So the Qur'an was revealed: **"And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say: 'God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion'"** [[Surat al-Ahzab: 12.]] and God revealed in this story His saying, exalted is He: **"Say: O God, Owner of Sovereignty..."** [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 21/163.]]

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for the addition of the mim to this name, whose origin is (Allah), and concerning its case-ending (naṣb).

Some of them said: The mim was added at the end as a substitute for the vocative particle that was deleted from its beginning, because its origin is (ya Allah). So they deleted the vocative particle and added the mim in its place, as a replacement for it.

Just as they said: fam (mouth), dam (blood), and zarqam (blue-eyed), the original of which has been dropped, and sitham (a kind of bad tree), and what is similar to that of the nouns and adjectives from which a letter is dropped. [[There is a blank in the manuscript which we have corrected from Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/299.]]

They argued that such nouns and adjectives, when a letter is dropped from them, have a mim put in its place. Since the dropped part of this name was two letters, the substitution was two mims, so one of them was assimilated into the other, and hence the shadda (doubling). In its sister forms it is unstressed, because only one letter was dropped; then it takes the naṣb for the sake of the doubling.

Others rejected this view and said: We have heard the Arabs add the mim to it with the vocative ya. And al-Farra' recited:
"What is upon you if you say, whenever
you glorify or proclaim the oneness of God: 'O Allahumma!'
Return to us our old shaykh, a Muslim,
for we shall not be deprived of his goodness."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/53.]]

They said: We see that its origin is Allah in supplication, meaning (ya Allah), to which amma was added and the vocative particle deleted. It is intended as (ya Allah, give us good), i.e., direct it toward us. Then it was used in speech until it became mixed with it. The hamza was deleted for lightness, as in their saying: halumma ilayna, the original being hal lumma ilayna, meaning: aim or hasten. Then this word became so common that they said: lahumma, meaning allahumma, and sometimes they also put a kasra on its mim. And God knows best.

Abu Raja' al-Utaridi said: This mim in His saying "Allahumma" gathers seventy of His names, exalted and mighty is He: Owner of Sovereignty. God said in some books: "I am God, Owner of kings and Owner of sovereignty. The hearts of kings and their forelocks are in My hand. When servants obey Me, I make mercy upon them, and when servants disobey Me, I make punishment upon them. So do not busy yourselves with cursing kings, but repent to Me, and I will turn them toward you in compassion."

**"You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means the sovereignty of prophethood. Al-Kalbi: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: Muhammad and his companions, **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Abu Jahl and the chieftains of Quraysh.

Mu'tasim said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: the Arabs. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: the Romans, the non-Arabs, and all the other nations.

Al-Suddi: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: God gave the prophets and commanded the servants to obey them. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: He took it from the tyrants and commanded the servants to oppose them.

It was said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: Adam and his offspring, **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Iblis and his hosts.

It was said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: David. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Goliath.

It was said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: Sakhr. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Solomon (peace be upon him). He used to feed the bread to the slave-girls and eat barley bread, and he wore the patched garment, and he did not look at the sky for forty years, out of humility before God.
He used to enter the mosque, seeking out a poor man to sit beside him, and he would say: "A poor man sitting with a poor man."
**"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: the sovereignty of the self, until his desire overcomes him and he takes it as a god, as God, mighty and majestic, said: **"Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?"** [[Surat al-Jathiya: 23.]]

A poet said:
"I possessed my self, and that is a kingdom,
there is no kingdom like it among mankind.
So I became free by the kingdom of my self,
and no creature has sovereignty over me."

Another:
"Whoever possesses his self is free, [and the slave is he whom his desire possesses]."

It was said: It is the sovereignty of well-being. God, exalted is He, said: **"And He made you kings"** [[Surat al-Ma'ida: 20.]]

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you wakes up secure in his dwelling, healthy in his body, and has his daily food, it is as if the world were gathered for him in its entirety."

[39] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/5.]]

It was said: It is contentment.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The kings of my community are those content with each day as it comes. Whoever is given that and does not accept it with acceptance, and does not patiently bear it with gratitude, his deed is shortened and his intellect diminished." [40]

Ibn al-Mubarak said: I entered upon Sufyan al-Thawri in Mecca and found him ill, taking medicine, and he had great grief. I greeted him and said: "What is wrong with you, O servant of God?" He said: "I am ill, taking medicine, and I have great grief." I said: "Do you have a sprig of basil?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Bring it to me," and he brought it to me. I crushed it and said: "Smell it," and he smelled it, and at that moment he sneezed and said: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds," and his ailment was relieved. He said to me: "O son of al-Mubarak, you are a jurist and a physician," or he said: "a scholar and a physician." I said to him: "Tested, O Abu Abd Allah." He said: When I saw him, his ailment had subsided and his soul was content. I said: "I want to ask you a question." He said: "Ask whatever you wish."

I said: "Tell me, who are the people?" He said: "The jurists." I said: "Then who are the kings?" He said: "The ascetics." I said: "Then who are the nobles?" He said: "The pious." I said: "Then who are the riffraff?" He said: "Those who write down hadith in order to eat the wealth of people with it." I said to him: "Tell me, may God have mercy on you: who are the lowly?" He said: "The oppressors." Then I bade him farewell and left his presence.

He said: "O Ibn al-Mubarak, hold on to this report, for it is present and cheap, before it becomes expensive and cannot be found for any price."

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: meaning dominion over the self and the subjugation of Satan. As the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Satan runs through the children of Adam like blood flows." [41] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/156.]]

And He, exalted is He, said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: meaning the sovereignty of knowledge, as He gave it to the magicians, **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**, as He took it from Iblis and Balaam.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: meaning the sovereignty of Paradise, as He gave it to the believers. God, exalted is He, said: **"And a great sovereignty"** [[Surat al-Insan: 20.]], **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: as He took it from the disbelievers and the people of the Fire.

Abu Uthman: By "sovereignty" he meant: the success in faith and obedience.

Al-Ustadh Abu Sa'id al-Wa'iz related that he heard some ascetics of Yemen say: It is standing in prayer at night.

Al-Shibli: Being independent of the two worlds through the One who brought them into being.

Al-Wasiti: Kings boast of sovereignty, so God, exalted is He, informed them that sovereignty is [transient] [[An unreadable word; the likely reading is what we have given.]] among them, by His saying: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will."**

The wise said concerning this verse: This is an announcement of the perfection of power, and that He who is perfectly capable is capable of a thing and its opposite. So He informed that He is able to give sovereignty to whom He wills and to take sovereignty from whom He wills.

﴿You honour whom You will and You abase whom You will.﴾ Ata said: "You honour whom You will" refers to the Emigrants and the Helpers, and "You abase whom You will" refers to Persia and Rome.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" refers to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions when they entered Makkah with ten thousand men overcoming it, and "You abase whom You will" refers to Abu Jahl and his companions when their heads were cut off and they were thrown into the well.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through faith and knowledge, and "You abase whom You will" means through forsaking and deprivation.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through granting possession and empowerment, and "You abase whom You will" means through stripping away dominion and giving His enemy power over it.

Al-Warraq said: "You honour whom You will" means through subduing the self and opposing desire, and "You abase whom You will" means through following desire.

Al-Kiyani said: "You honour whom You will" means through His subduing of Satan, and "You abase whom You will" means through Satan's subduing of us.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through contentment and satisfaction, and "You abase whom You will" means through disgrace and greed.

Al-Tha'labi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Abd Allah ibn Ali say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Fadl say: I heard al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Wahid say: I heard Banan al-Hammal say: "The free man is a slave as long as he is greedy, and the slave is free as long as he is content."

Wahb said: Wealth and honour went out wandering, then they met contentment and settled with it. [Tarikh Dimashq 11/278, where it reads "wealth and poetry" instead of "wealth and honour".]

Isa (peace be upon him) said to his companions: "You are richer than kings."
They said: "How so, O Spirit of Allah, when we possess nothing?"
He said: "You have nothing and you do not desire it, while they have things and those things do not suffice them."

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
"Ah, O soul, if you are content with sustenance,
you will always be honoured and self-sufficient.
Leave aside greed and wishful longings,
for many a wish has brought about a death."
[Rawdat al-Wa'izin by al-Fattal al-Nishapuri: 457.]

Another poet said:
"Contentment has granted me every honour;
and what honour is more honourable than contentment?
So make it the capital for yourself,
and make it, with piety, your merchandise."
[Kashf al-Khafa': 2/102. In the source: "and where is wealth more honourable than contentment?"]

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through sincerity, and "You abase whom You will" means through showing off.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: "You honour whom You will" means through Paradise and vision, and "You abase whom You will" means through Hell and veiling.

﴿In Your hand is the good.﴾ That is, good and evil; but mention is made only of the good, because it is the more excellent and the more frequent, as in His saying ﴿...garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:81], meaning heat and cold. ﴿Indeed You are over all things competent.﴾

﴿You cause the night to enter the day﴾: [That is, You make what is lost from one of them enter the other], until the day becomes fifteen hours [which is its longest], and the night nine hours [which is its shortest]. [Words between brackets are additions from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/56.]

﴿And You cause the day to enter the night﴾: until the night becomes fifteen [hours] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/303] and the day nine hours; whatever is lost from this is added to the other, like His saying ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [Surah al-Zumar 39:5].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: [It is] a day and a night, a day and a night, from the creation of the heavens and the earth until the Hour is established. Then he recited: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night.﴾

﴿You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim, al-Suddi, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It means bringing the animal out of the drop of semen, which is dead, and bringing the drop of semen out of the animal.

Ikrimah and al-Kalbi said: "You bring the living out of the dead" means the chick out of the egg, and bringing the egg out of the bird.

Abu Malik said: It means bringing the palm tree out of the date stone, and bringing the date stone out of the palm tree, and bringing the ear of grain out of the seed and the seed out of the ear of grain.

Al-Hasan said: It means bringing the believer out of the disbeliever, and bringing the disbeliever out of the believer. The believer is a servant whose heart is alive, and the disbeliever is a servant whose heart is dead, as indicated by His saying ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life...﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:122].

Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon one of his wives, and there was a woman of good appearance. He said: "Who is this?" She said: "One of your maternal aunts." He said: "My maternal aunts in this land are many; which of my aunts is this?" She said: "This is Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth." He said: "Glory be to Allah who brings the living out of the dead." [42]
She was a righteous woman, and her father had died a disbeliever. [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 9/264; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 3/306.]

Al-Farra' said: It means bringing the good out of the bad and the bad out of the good.

The people of allusion (ahl al-ishara) said: It means bringing wisdom out of the heart of the wicked person, so that it does not settle in him, and bringing a slip out of the tongue of the knower.

﴿And You provide for whom You will without account.﴾

﴿The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Al-Hajjaj ibn Amr, Ibn Abi al-Huqayq and Qays ibn Zayd overpowered a group of the Helpers in order to turn them away from their religion. Rifa'ah ibn al-Mundhir, Abd Allah ibn Jubayr and Sa'd ibn Juhaymah said to those people: "Avoid these Jews, and beware of keeping company with them, speaking with them and remaining with them." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them.

The two Muqatils said: It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and others, who used to show affection to the disbelievers of Makkah, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade them from that.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions. They used to take the Jews and the polytheists as allies and bring them news, hoping that victory over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be theirs. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and forbade the believers from acting like them.

Yusuf ibn Dawud al-Dabbi narrated from some of them, saying: "Do not take the believers" with the nominative ("la yattakhidhu al-mu'minun") as a predicate for them, and it carries the sense of prohibition, like His saying ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:2].

Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: It was revealed concerning Ubadah ibn al-Samit al-Ansari, who was a man of Badr and pious, and who had Jewish allies. When the Prophet (ﷺ) went out on the day of the Confederates, Ubadah said: "O Prophet of Allah, I have with me five hundred men from the Jews, and I think they should go out with me, so that I may gain their support against the enemy." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies...﴾, the verse.
[Surah al-Mudhkur (the same surah): 3:28.]

﴿And whoever does that﴾, that is, allying with the disbelievers by transmitting news to them and revealing to them the numbers of the Muslims, ﴿then there is nothing of Allah in him﴾: there is an ellipsis here, meaning there is nothing of the religion of Allah in him.

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: He has nothing of allegiance, for Allah has disassociated Himself from him. Then He made an exception, saying:
﴿Except that you fear from them a fear﴾, meaning: except that you fear them with a fear.

Abu al-Aliyah, from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Abu Rajah, Jabir ibn Zayd and Humayd ibn Mujahid recited taqiyyah (with the form of nAqiyyah). Abu Hatim disagreed with them, saying: "They wrote it with a yā' like ḥaṣāh and nawāh, except with an alif."

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read "taqiyyah" (the usual form with a yā') [in this reading] the yā' is a feature of the reading. [In the sense of a qira'a: a variant recitation.]

The rest read "tuqatan" (with the ḍammah). This was chosen by Abu Ubaydah.

Al-Akhfash read "tuqa'ah," like "takah" and "yu'dah" and the like, and it is a verbal noun from "ittaqa." The pattern of "tuqyah" is "tuqah," "taqiyyah," "taqi," and "tuqwa." When you say "ittaqantu," its verbal noun is "al-ittiqa'," and the verb in "tattaqu" is from "al-ittiqa'" (the root of piety). Then He said "tuqatan" and did not say "ittiqa'," because the Arabs, when two words share one root but differ in form, give the verbal noun of one form to the other, saying: "I met so-and-so with a fine meeting" (laqitu falanan liqa'an hasanan).

Al-Qutami said, describing rain:
"It has prevailed beside the two mountains... a heap that digs up the soil in digging."
He did not say "hafran" [the verbal noun of the standard form], as God the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾ [Surah Nuh 71:17], and He said: ﴿And devote yourself to Him with devotion﴾ [Surah al-Muzzammil 73:8].

As for the meaning of the verse, the commentators said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade the believers from being affable with the disbelievers, allying with them, flattering them and trading with them, except when the disbelievers are dominant and victorious, or when the believer is among disbelieving people with none of his own kind, and fears them and treats them with tact in speech while his heart is at peace in faith, to protect himself without shedding unlawful blood or taking unlawful property, or revealing the weaknesses of the believers to the disbelievers. The one who fears (muttaqi) only does so when there is fear of being killed and good intention is present, like the action of Ammar ibn Yasir.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Ibn al-Musayyib, said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah and said: "I think I am nothing but ruined." He said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "Quraysh have tortured me." I said: "What did they say?" [The man said:] "How was your heart?" He said: "At peace." He said: "If they return to you, then return to them the same," and he said it three times.

Al-Musayyib ibn Ubaydah, from Ibrahim, said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Mix with people, be sociable with them, and shake hands with them in what they desire, but let your religion not be a cause of doubt."

Sa'sa'ah ibn Suhan said to Usamah ibn Zayd: "I was dearer to your father than you are, and you are dearer to me than my father." [In Tarikh Dimashq: "to me is my son."] Therefore I advise you with two qualities: be sincere to the believer and oppose the disbeliever, for the disbeliever will be satisfied from you with good character, and it is your duty to be sincere to the believer. [Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 3/1017. In Tarikh Dimashq (24/98): "oppose" is "khalif" instead of "khaliq".]

It is narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq that he said: Taqiyyah (dissimulation under threat) is obligatory, and indeed I hear a man in the mosque insulting me, so I hide behind the pillar from him so that he does not see me.
He also said: Showing off in front of a believer is polytheism, and in front of a hypocrite in his house it is worship.

Some people denied taqiyyah today.
Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from Mujahid, said: Taqiyyah existed at the dawn of Islam before the religion was firmly established and the Muslims became strong. But today Allah the Mighty and Majestic has honoured Islam, so the people of Islam should not guard themselves against their enemy.

Yahya al-Bakka' said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr in the days of al-Hajjaj: "Al-Hasan used to tell you: 'Taqiyyah is with the tongue, while the heart is at peace in faith.'" Sa'id said: "There is no taqiyyah in Islam; taqiyyah is only among the people of war."

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾: that is, Allah makes you fear, for taking disbelievers as allies and committing what is forbidden and opposing what is commanded, Him [i.e., His punishment] from Himself.
The commentators said: from His punishment, His chastisement and His seizing.
The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is "and Allah warns you of Him," because "thing," "self," "essence" and "name" are all expressions for existence, and the self of a thing is the thing itself, as in His saying ﴿Kill yourselves﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:66], meaning: let some of you kill others.

Al-A'sha said:
"One day, the most generous of gifts from him, when
the self of the miser frowns at its request."
He meant: when the miser frowns at his request.

﴿And to Allah is the destination.﴾
﴿Say: If you conceal what is in your breasts﴾: your hearts, of affection for the disbelievers; ﴿or reveal it﴾: of allying with them by word and deed; ﴿Allah knows it﴾: Al-Kalbi said: that is, they hide what is in their hearts against the Messenger of Allah of denial, and they show hostility; and He said: ﴿Allah knows it and preserves it against you until He fights you with it and punishes you for it.﴾ Then He said: ﴿And He knows﴾, which is in the nominative as a new clause, like their saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them, and will heal the breasts of a believing people and remove the rage of their hearts, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:14–15], in the nominative.

And His saying: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal over your heart and Allah would erase falsehood﴾ [Surah al-Shura 42:24], then He said: ﴿and establish the truth.﴾ How could your allegiance to the disbelievers and your inclination toward them be hidden from Him? The affection of the heart means help with the heart and with action.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾
﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present﴾: the word "yawm" (day) is in the accusative, with the preposition removed, meaning "on the day." It was also said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: remember and fear the Day when every soul finds what it has done of good present, complete, nothing of it diminished. The reading of the general readers is with fatḥah on the ḍād as an object, and this is confirmed by His saying: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:49]. Ubayd, from Umayr, read muḥḍiran with kasrah on the ḍād, meaning that his deed will bring him into Paradise, hastening with it, from "ḥuḍūr" or "ḥaḍr."

﴿And what it has done of evil﴾: some grammarians made it a predicate in the accusative position, with "wujūd" (finding) governing it, and made "'amilat" a relative clause, meaning "and its deed is found." Others made it a new predicate, and in that case "tawaddu" may be read with a nominative or a jussive. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Abd Allah: "and what it has done of evil, it wishes" (wa ma 'amilat min su'in tawaddu).

﴿Wishes that between it﴾: between the soul ﴿and between that﴾: meaning between the evil ﴿a distance far off.﴾ The amad (distance) is the term and the limit to which something ends. Allah said: ﴿Does my Lord set for it a term?﴾ [Surah al-Jinn 72:25], and He said: ﴿So the term became long for them﴾ [Surah al-Hadid 57:16].

Al-Nabighah said:
"Ah, for one like you, or one who is ahead of you,
in the lead of the horse when they are level at the goal."

Al-Suddi said: "a distance far off" means a far-off place.
Muqatil said: as far as between the east and the west.
Al-Hasan said: It is not that one of them does not meet his deed forever, nor that he would wish to know it.

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Compassionate to the servants﴾: that is, to the believers among them.

﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you...﴾, the verse.
Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), some people claimed that they loved Allah, and they said: "O Muhammad, we love our Lord." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse, and made following His Prophet a sign of His love.

Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) stood before the Quraysh while they were in the Sacred Mosque, and they had set up their idols, hung ostrich eggs on them, put swords in their ears, and were prostrating to them. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah you have opposed the creed of your father Abraham and Ishmael, and indeed they were upon Islam." Quraysh said to him: "O Muhammad, we worship them out of love for Allah, ﴿so that they may bring us near to Allah in position﴾." Then Allah the Exalted said: "Say, O Muhammad: ﴿If you love Allah and worship the idols so that they may bring you near to Him, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾, and I am His Messenger to you and His proof against you, and I am more deserving of veneration than the idols."

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, narrated: When the Jews said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:18], Allah revealed this verse. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) presented it to the Jews, but they refused to accept it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-Zubayr, who said: It was revealed concerning the Christians of Najran, because they said: "We magnify the Messiah and worship him out of love for Allah, the Glorified, and to magnify Him." So Allah said: "Say, O Muhammad: ﴿If you love Allah﴾, and your great saying about Jesus is out of love for Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and magnification of Him, ﴿then follow me; Allah will love you﴾", that is, follow my law and my practice, and Allah will love you. The love of the believers for Allah is their following His command, and their intention to obey Him and seek His pleasure, and the love of the Mighty and Majestic for the believers is a favour upon them, His reward for them, and His pardon for them; and that is His saying: ﴿and forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Al-Tha'labi said: Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, saying: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Surimi recited to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad recited to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim al-Bajali recited to me, for Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak:
"You disobey God while you show His love;
by my life, that is ugly in deeds.
If your love were true, you would obey Him,
for the one who loves is obedient to the one he loves."
[Tahdhib al-Kamal: 6/360; Tarikh Dimashq: 32/469.]

Narrated by 'Urwa from 'Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is lighter than the crawling of an ant on a smooth rock in a dark night. Its least degree is that you love something out of injustice, or hate something out of justice. And is religion anything other than loving for the sake of Allah and hating for the sake of Allah?" Allah said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [[Al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti: 2/85, no. 4935.]] [43].

When this verse was revealed, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said to his companions: "Muhammad makes his obedience like the obedience of Allah, and commands us to love him as the Christians loved 'Isa ibn Maryam." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away﴾, meaning: they turn away from obeying them both. ﴿Then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He does not approve of their deeds, nor of anything they have, and He will not forgive them. [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 1/319.]]

Waki' narrated from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever obeys the imam has obeyed me. Whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys the imam has disobeyed me." [44] [[Al-Musannaf of al-Kufi (Ibn Abi Shayba): 7/566.]]

The commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 23–32 (part 1 of 3):

**"a share of the Book"**: that is, a portion and a lot of the Book. It means: the Jews are called to the Book of God.

They differed concerning this Book to which God, exalted is He, informed that they were called and from which they turned away. Some said: it is the Qur'an.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse, that he said: God, mighty and majestic, made the Qur'an a judge between them and the Messenger of God, so the Qur'an ruled against the Jews and Christians that they were not upon the religion of guidance, so they turned away from it.

Qatada said: They are the enemies of God, the Jews. They were called to the judgment of the Qur'an and to following Muhammad (ﷺ), so they turned away, while they find it written in their books.

Al-Suddi: The Prophet (ﷺ) invited the Jews to Islam, and al-Nu'man ibn Abi Awfa said to him: "Come, O Muhammad, let us dispute with you before the rabbis." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "Rather, to the Book of God." He said: "Rather, to the rabbis."
So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Others said: it is the Torah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrima narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) upon a group of Jews, and he invited them to God, mighty and majestic.
Nu'aym ibn Amr and Ibn al-Harith ibn Fahd said to him: "Upon what religion are you, O Muhammad?" He said: "Upon the religion of Abraham." They said: "Abraham was a Jew." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "Then submit to the Torah, for it is between us and you." They refused, so God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: A man and a woman from the people of Khaybar committed fornication, and they were of nobility among them, and in their Book was stoning. They disliked stoning them because of their status and nobility, and they hoped that the Messenger of God would have mercy in their matter. So they referred it to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he ruled that they should be stoned. Al-Nu'man ibn Abi Awfa and Nakhri ibn Amr said to him: "O Muhammad, you have been unjust to us. There is no stoning for them." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "Between me and you is the Torah, for in it is stoning." They said: "You have been fair with us." He said: "Then who is most knowledgeable among you?"
They said: "A blind man who lives in Fadak, called Ibn Suriya. So send for him." He came to Medina, and Jibril (peace be upon him) had described him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Messenger of God said to him: "Are you Ibn Suriya?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Are you the most knowledgeable of the Jews?" He said: "So they claim." He said: "Then the Messenger of God called for some of the Torah, in which stoning was written. He said to him: 'Read.' When he reached the verse of stoning, he placed his palm upon it and read what came after it." Ibn Salam said: "O Messenger of God, he has passed over it, and he has placed his palm upon it." Ibn Salam rose to Ibn Suriya and lifted his palm from it, then he read to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The two married Jews, if they commit adultery and there is evidence against them, they shall be stoned; and if the woman is pregnant, she shall wait until she gives birth to what is in her womb." [36] [[Fath al-Bari: 12/150; note that the phrase "the two Jews" is not mentioned in the hadith.]] Then the Messenger of God commanded that the two Jews be stoned. The Jews became exceedingly angry at that and dispersed. So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

**"Have you not considered those who were given a share of the Book"**: a portion of the Torah.

**"They are called to the Book of God so that it may judge between them, then a party of them turns away"**: He had informed them that it is in the Torah.

**"And they are turning away. That is because they said: 'The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days,' and their fabrications have deceived them in their religion. So how will it be when We gather them"**: that is, how will they act for **"a Day about which there is no doubt"**: which is the Day of Resurrection.

**"And every soul will be paid in full"**: righteous or wicked.

**"for what it earned"**: that is, the recompense of what it did, of good or evil.

**"And they will not be wronged"**: their good deeds will not be diminished, nor will their evil deeds be increased.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first banner raised for the people of the gathering on that Day is the banner of the disbelievers, the banner of the Jews. God will humiliate them before the witnesses, then He will command that they be taken to the Fire."

**"Say: O God, Owner of Sovereignty"**:

Al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God wished to send down the Opening of the Book, and the Verse of the Throne, and 'God bears witness,' and 'Say: O God, Owner of Sovereignty...'
...to 'without reckoning,' they hung from the Throne, and there was no veil between them and God, and they said: 'O Lord, will You cast us down into the abode of sins, and to one who disobeys You, while we are attached to the birds and the Throne?' He, exalted is He, said: 'By My might and My majesty, there is no servant who recites you at the end of every obligatory prayer except that I will settle him in the enclosure of holiness with what he had in it, and I will look upon him with My eye seventy times every day, and I will fulfil for him seventy needs every day, the least of which is forgiveness, and I will protect him from every enemy and grant him victory over it, and nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except associating partners with Me.'"

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "I was detained from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) one day, and I did not pray the Friday prayer with him. He said: 'O Mu'adh, what prevented you from the Friday prayer?' I said: 'O Messenger of God, the Jew Yuhanna had an ounce [of gold] owed to him by me, and he was watching me at my door, and I feared that he would detain me away from you.' He said: 'Would you like, O Mu'adh, that God pay off your debt?' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Say: "O God, Owner of Sovereignty..." to His saying "without reckoning," and say: "O Compassionate of this world and the Hereafter and its Merciful, You give from it what You will and withhold from it what You will, settle my debt for me." For if you had owed the earth filled with gold, God would settle it for you.'" [37] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/52; Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 3/320, no. 2398.]]

Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his Lord to make the kingdom of Persia and Rome belong to his community, so God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Abbas and Anas ibn Malik said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered Mecca and promised his community the kingdom of Persia and Rome, the hypocrites and the Jews said: "Far-fetched, far-fetched! From where would Muhammad have the kingdom of Persia? They are more powerful and stronger than that. Was it not enough for Muhammad to have Mecca and Medina, that he should aspire to the kingdom of Persia and Rome?" So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Awf narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) dug the trench in the year of the Confederates. Then he marked off forty cubits, ten for each group. He said: The Emigrants and the Helpers disputed concerning Salman al-Farisi, who was a strong man. The Emigrants said: "Salman is one of us." The Helpers said: "Salman is one of us."
The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." [38]

Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfa, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani, and six men from the Helpers were in forty cubits. We dug until we reached the hard ground, and God brought forth from the belly of the trench a hard white rock which broke our iron and was difficult for us. We said: "O Salman, go to the Messenger of God and inform him of the matter of this rock, for either we will turn away from it, for turning away is close, or he will command us regarding it with a command, for we do not wish to go beyond his line."

He said: So Salman climbed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who had a Turkish dome pitched over him. He said: "O Messenger of God, a white hard rock has emerged from the belly of the trench, and it has broken our iron and has been difficult for us, so that nothing, little or much, can be taken from it. So command us regarding it with your command, for we do not wish to go beyond your line." He said: So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) descended with Salman into the trench, and we nine remained on the edge of the trench. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck it a blow which split it, and from it a flash shone which lit up what was between its two lava fields (meaning Medina), until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." Then he (ﷺ) struck it and broke it, and from it a flash shone which lit up what was between its two lava fields, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar" in the takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar" with him. Then he took Salman by the hand and climbed up.

Salman said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God! I have seen something the like of which I have never seen before!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God [may our fathers and mothers be your ransom; we saw you strike and a flash came out like a wave, and we saw you say takbir so we said takbir, and we saw nothing other than that]."

He said: "I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw, the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra were illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs, and Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw, the palaces of Busra in the land of Rome were illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs, and Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that my community will prevail over them. [Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw, the palaces of San'a were illuminated for me from it, as if they were the fangs of dogs, and Jibril informed me that my community will prevail over them.] [[Not found in Tafsir al-Tabari.]] So rejoice!" The Muslims rejoiced and said:
"Praise be to God, a true promise, that He promised us victory after siege."
[Then the confederates advanced, and the Muslims said:
"This is what God and His Messenger promised us" [[Surat al-Ahzab: 22.]] to the end of the verse.]

The hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel? He promises you and makes you hope for falsehood, and informs you that from Yathrib he sees the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be conquered for you, while you are only digging the trench out of fear, unable to come out!" He said: So the Qur'an was revealed: **"And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say: 'God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion'"** [[Surat al-Ahzab: 12.]] and God revealed in this story His saying, exalted is He: **"Say: O God, Owner of Sovereignty..."** [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 21/163.]]

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for the addition of the mim to this name, whose origin is (Allah), and concerning its case-ending (naṣb).

Some of them said: The mim was added at the end as a substitute for the vocative particle that was deleted from its beginning, because its origin is (ya Allah). So they deleted the vocative particle and added the mim in its place, as a replacement for it.

Just as they said: fam (mouth), dam (blood), and zarqam (blue-eyed), the original of which has been dropped, and sitham (a kind of bad tree), and what is similar to that of the nouns and adjectives from which a letter is dropped. [[There is a blank in the manuscript which we have corrected from Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/299.]]

They argued that such nouns and adjectives, when a letter is dropped from them, have a mim put in its place. Since the dropped part of this name was two letters, the substitution was two mims, so one of them was assimilated into the other, and hence the shadda (doubling). In its sister forms it is unstressed, because only one letter was dropped; then it takes the naṣb for the sake of the doubling.

Others rejected this view and said: We have heard the Arabs add the mim to it with the vocative ya. And al-Farra' recited:
"What is upon you if you say, whenever
you glorify or proclaim the oneness of God: 'O Allahumma!'
Return to us our old shaykh, a Muslim,
for we shall not be deprived of his goodness."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/53.]]

They said: We see that its origin is Allah in supplication, meaning (ya Allah), to which amma was added and the vocative particle deleted. It is intended as (ya Allah, give us good), i.e., direct it toward us. Then it was used in speech until it became mixed with it. The hamza was deleted for lightness, as in their saying: halumma ilayna, the original being hal lumma ilayna, meaning: aim or hasten. Then this word became so common that they said: lahumma, meaning allahumma, and sometimes they also put a kasra on its mim. And God knows best.

Abu Raja' al-Utaridi said: This mim in His saying "Allahumma" gathers seventy of His names, exalted and mighty is He: Owner of Sovereignty. God said in some books: "I am God, Owner of kings and Owner of sovereignty. The hearts of kings and their forelocks are in My hand. When servants obey Me, I make mercy upon them, and when servants disobey Me, I make punishment upon them. So do not busy yourselves with cursing kings, but repent to Me, and I will turn them toward you in compassion."

**"You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means the sovereignty of prophethood. Al-Kalbi: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: Muhammad and his companions, **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Abu Jahl and the chieftains of Quraysh.

Mu'tasim said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: the Arabs. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: the Romans, the non-Arabs, and all the other nations.

Al-Suddi: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: God gave the prophets and commanded the servants to obey them. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: He took it from the tyrants and commanded the servants to oppose them.

It was said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: Adam and his offspring, **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Iblis and his hosts.

It was said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: David. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Goliath.

It was said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: Sakhr. **"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: Solomon (peace be upon him). He used to feed the bread to the slave-girls and eat barley bread, and he wore the patched garment, and he did not look at the sky for forty years, out of humility before God.
He used to enter the mosque, seeking out a poor man to sit beside him, and he would say: "A poor man sitting with a poor man."
**"And You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: the sovereignty of the self, until his desire overcomes him and he takes it as a god, as God, mighty and majestic, said: **"Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?"** [[Surat al-Jathiya: 23.]]

A poet said:
"I possessed my self, and that is a kingdom,
there is no kingdom like it among mankind.
So I became free by the kingdom of my self,
and no creature has sovereignty over me."

Another:
"Whoever possesses his self is free, [and the slave is he whom his desire possesses]."

It was said: It is the sovereignty of well-being. God, exalted is He, said: **"And He made you kings"** [[Surat al-Ma'ida: 20.]]

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you wakes up secure in his dwelling, healthy in his body, and has his daily food, it is as if the world were gathered for him in its entirety."

[39] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/5.]]

It was said: It is contentment.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The kings of my community are those content with each day as it comes. Whoever is given that and does not accept it with acceptance, and does not patiently bear it with gratitude, his deed is shortened and his intellect diminished." [40]

Ibn al-Mubarak said: I entered upon Sufyan al-Thawri in Mecca and found him ill, taking medicine, and he had great grief. I greeted him and said: "What is wrong with you, O servant of God?" He said: "I am ill, taking medicine, and I have great grief." I said: "Do you have a sprig of basil?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Bring it to me," and he brought it to me. I crushed it and said: "Smell it," and he smelled it, and at that moment he sneezed and said: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds," and his ailment was relieved. He said to me: "O son of al-Mubarak, you are a jurist and a physician," or he said: "a scholar and a physician." I said to him: "Tested, O Abu Abd Allah." He said: When I saw him, his ailment had subsided and his soul was content. I said: "I want to ask you a question." He said: "Ask whatever you wish."

I said: "Tell me, who are the people?" He said: "The jurists." I said: "Then who are the kings?" He said: "The ascetics." I said: "Then who are the nobles?" He said: "The pious." I said: "Then who are the riffraff?" He said: "Those who write down hadith in order to eat the wealth of people with it." I said to him: "Tell me, may God have mercy on you: who are the lowly?" He said: "The oppressors." Then I bade him farewell and left his presence.

He said: "O Ibn al-Mubarak, hold on to this report, for it is present and cheap, before it becomes expensive and cannot be found for any price."

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: meaning dominion over the self and the subjugation of Satan. As the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Satan runs through the children of Adam like blood flows." [41] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/156.]]

And He, exalted is He, said: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: meaning the sovereignty of knowledge, as He gave it to the magicians, **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**, as He took it from Iblis and Balaam.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will"**: meaning the sovereignty of Paradise, as He gave it to the believers. God, exalted is He, said: **"And a great sovereignty"** [[Surat al-Insan: 20.]], **"and You take sovereignty from whom You will"**: as He took it from the disbelievers and the people of the Fire.

Abu Uthman: By "sovereignty" he meant: the success in faith and obedience.

Al-Ustadh Abu Sa'id al-Wa'iz related that he heard some ascetics of Yemen say: It is standing in prayer at night.

Al-Shibli: Being independent of the two worlds through the One who brought them into being.

Al-Wasiti: Kings boast of sovereignty, so God, exalted is He, informed them that sovereignty is [transient] [[An unreadable word; the likely reading is what we have given.]] among them, by His saying: **"You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will."**

The wise said concerning this verse: This is an announcement of the perfection of power, and that He who is perfectly capable is capable of a thing and its opposite. So He informed that He is able to give sovereignty to whom He wills and to take sovereignty from whom He wills.

﴿You honour whom You will and You abase whom You will.﴾ Ata said: "You honour whom You will" refers to the Emigrants and the Helpers, and "You abase whom You will" refers to Persia and Rome.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" refers to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions when they entered Makkah with ten thousand men overcoming it, and "You abase whom You will" refers to Abu Jahl and his companions when their heads were cut off and they were thrown into the well.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through faith and knowledge, and "You abase whom You will" means through forsaking and deprivation.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through granting possession and empowerment, and "You abase whom You will" means through stripping away dominion and giving His enemy power over it.

Al-Warraq said: "You honour whom You will" means through subduing the self and opposing desire, and "You abase whom You will" means through following desire.

Al-Kiyani said: "You honour whom You will" means through His subduing of Satan, and "You abase whom You will" means through Satan's subduing of us.

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through contentment and satisfaction, and "You abase whom You will" means through disgrace and greed.

Al-Tha'labi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Abd Allah ibn Ali say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Fadl say: I heard al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Wahid say: I heard Banan al-Hammal say: "The free man is a slave as long as he is greedy, and the slave is free as long as he is content."

Wahb said: Wealth and honour went out wandering, then they met contentment and settled with it. [Tarikh Dimashq 11/278, where it reads "wealth and poetry" instead of "wealth and honour".]

Isa (peace be upon him) said to his companions: "You are richer than kings."
They said: "How so, O Spirit of Allah, when we possess nothing?"
He said: "You have nothing and you do not desire it, while they have things and those things do not suffice them."

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
"Ah, O soul, if you are content with sustenance,
you will always be honoured and self-sufficient.
Leave aside greed and wishful longings,
for many a wish has brought about a death."
[Rawdat al-Wa'izin by al-Fattal al-Nishapuri: 457.]

Another poet said:
"Contentment has granted me every honour;
and what honour is more honourable than contentment?
So make it the capital for yourself,
and make it, with piety, your merchandise."
[Kashf al-Khafa': 2/102. In the source: "and where is wealth more honourable than contentment?"]

It was also said: "You honour whom You will" means through sincerity, and "You abase whom You will" means through showing off.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: "You honour whom You will" means through Paradise and vision, and "You abase whom You will" means through Hell and veiling.

﴿In Your hand is the good.﴾ That is, good and evil; but mention is made only of the good, because it is the more excellent and the more frequent, as in His saying ﴿...garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:81], meaning heat and cold. ﴿Indeed You are over all things competent.﴾

﴿You cause the night to enter the day﴾: [That is, You make what is lost from one of them enter the other], until the day becomes fifteen hours [which is its longest], and the night nine hours [which is its shortest]. [Words between brackets are additions from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/56.]

﴿And You cause the day to enter the night﴾: until the night becomes fifteen [hours] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/303] and the day nine hours; whatever is lost from this is added to the other, like His saying ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [Surah al-Zumar 39:5].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: [It is] a day and a night, a day and a night, from the creation of the heavens and the earth until the Hour is established. Then he recited: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night.﴾

﴿You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim, al-Suddi, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It means bringing the animal out of the drop of semen, which is dead, and bringing the drop of semen out of the animal.

Ikrimah and al-Kalbi said: "You bring the living out of the dead" means the chick out of the egg, and bringing the egg out of the bird.

Abu Malik said: It means bringing the palm tree out of the date stone, and bringing the date stone out of the palm tree, and bringing the ear of grain out of the seed and the seed out of the ear of grain.

Al-Hasan said: It means bringing the believer out of the disbeliever, and bringing the disbeliever out of the believer. The believer is a servant whose heart is alive, and the disbeliever is a servant whose heart is dead, as indicated by His saying ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life...﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:122].

Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon one of his wives, and there was a woman of good appearance. He said: "Who is this?" She said: "One of your maternal aunts." He said: "My maternal aunts in this land are many; which of my aunts is this?" She said: "This is Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth." He said: "Glory be to Allah who brings the living out of the dead." [42]
She was a righteous woman, and her father had died a disbeliever. [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 9/264; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 3/306.]

Al-Farra' said: It means bringing the good out of the bad and the bad out of the good.

The people of allusion (ahl al-ishara) said: It means bringing wisdom out of the heart of the wicked person, so that it does not settle in him, and bringing a slip out of the tongue of the knower.

﴿And You provide for whom You will without account.﴾

﴿The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Al-Hajjaj ibn Amr, Ibn Abi al-Huqayq and Qays ibn Zayd overpowered a group of the Helpers in order to turn them away from their religion. Rifa'ah ibn al-Mundhir, Abd Allah ibn Jubayr and Sa'd ibn Juhaymah said to those people: "Avoid these Jews, and beware of keeping company with them, speaking with them and remaining with them." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them.

The two Muqatils said: It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and others, who used to show affection to the disbelievers of Makkah, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade them from that.

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions. They used to take the Jews and the polytheists as allies and bring them news, hoping that victory over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be theirs. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and forbade the believers from acting like them.

Yusuf ibn Dawud al-Dabbi narrated from some of them, saying: "Do not take the believers" with the nominative ("la yattakhidhu al-mu'minun") as a predicate for them, and it carries the sense of prohibition, like His saying ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:2].

Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: It was revealed concerning Ubadah ibn al-Samit al-Ansari, who was a man of Badr and pious, and who had Jewish allies. When the Prophet (ﷺ) went out on the day of the Confederates, Ubadah said: "O Prophet of Allah, I have with me five hundred men from the Jews, and I think they should go out with me, so that I may gain their support against the enemy." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies...﴾, the verse.
[Surah al-Mudhkur (the same surah): 3:28.]

﴿And whoever does that﴾, that is, allying with the disbelievers by transmitting news to them and revealing to them the numbers of the Muslims, ﴿then there is nothing of Allah in him﴾: there is an ellipsis here, meaning there is nothing of the religion of Allah in him.

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: He has nothing of allegiance, for Allah has disassociated Himself from him. Then He made an exception, saying:
﴿Except that you fear from them a fear﴾, meaning: except that you fear them with a fear.

Abu al-Aliyah, from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Abu Rajah, Jabir ibn Zayd and Humayd ibn Mujahid recited taqiyyah (with the form of nAqiyyah). Abu Hatim disagreed with them, saying: "They wrote it with a yā' like ḥaṣāh and nawāh, except with an alif."

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read "taqiyyah" (the usual form with a yā') [in this reading] the yā' is a feature of the reading. [In the sense of a qira'a: a variant recitation.]

The rest read "tuqatan" (with the ḍammah). This was chosen by Abu Ubaydah.

Al-Akhfash read "tuqa'ah," like "takah" and "yu'dah" and the like, and it is a verbal noun from "ittaqa." The pattern of "tuqyah" is "tuqah," "taqiyyah," "taqi," and "tuqwa." When you say "ittaqantu," its verbal noun is "al-ittiqa'," and the verb in "tattaqu" is from "al-ittiqa'" (the root of piety). Then He said "tuqatan" and did not say "ittiqa'," because the Arabs, when two words share one root but differ in form, give the verbal noun of one form to the other, saying: "I met so-and-so with a fine meeting" (laqitu falanan liqa'an hasanan).

Al-Qutami said, describing rain:
"It has prevailed beside the two mountains... a heap that digs up the soil in digging."
He did not say "hafran" [the verbal noun of the standard form], as God the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾ [Surah Nuh 71:17], and He said: ﴿And devote yourself to Him with devotion﴾ [Surah al-Muzzammil 73:8].

As for the meaning of the verse, the commentators said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade the believers from being affable with the disbelievers, allying with them, flattering them and trading with them, except when the disbelievers are dominant and victorious, or when the believer is among disbelieving people with none of his own kind, and fears them and treats them with tact in speech while his heart is at peace in faith, to protect himself without shedding unlawful blood or taking unlawful property, or revealing the weaknesses of the believers to the disbelievers. The one who fears (muttaqi) only does so when there is fear of being killed and good intention is present, like the action of Ammar ibn Yasir.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Ibn al-Musayyib, said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah and said: "I think I am nothing but ruined." He said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "Quraysh have tortured me." I said: "What did they say?" [The man said:] "How was your heart?" He said: "At peace." He said: "If they return to you, then return to them the same," and he said it three times.

Al-Musayyib ibn Ubaydah, from Ibrahim, said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Mix with people, be sociable with them, and shake hands with them in what they desire, but let your religion not be a cause of doubt."

Sa'sa'ah ibn Suhan said to Usamah ibn Zayd: "I was dearer to your father than you are, and you are dearer to me than my father." [In Tarikh Dimashq: "to me is my son."] Therefore I advise you with two qualities: be sincere to the believer and oppose the disbeliever, for the disbeliever will be satisfied from you with good character, and it is your duty to be sincere to the believer. [Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 3/1017. In Tarikh Dimashq (24/98): "oppose" is "khalif" instead of "khaliq".]

It is narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq that he said: Taqiyyah (dissimulation under threat) is obligatory, and indeed I hear a man in the mosque insulting me, so I hide behind the pillar from him so that he does not see me.
He also said: Showing off in front of a believer is polytheism, and in front of a hypocrite in his house it is worship.

Some people denied taqiyyah today.
Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from Mujahid, said: Taqiyyah existed at the dawn of Islam before the religion was firmly established and the Muslims became strong. But today Allah the Mighty and Majestic has honoured Islam, so the people of Islam should not guard themselves against their enemy.

Yahya al-Bakka' said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr in the days of al-Hajjaj: "Al-Hasan used to tell you: 'Taqiyyah is with the tongue, while the heart is at peace in faith.'" Sa'id said: "There is no taqiyyah in Islam; taqiyyah is only among the people of war."

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾: that is, Allah makes you fear, for taking disbelievers as allies and committing what is forbidden and opposing what is commanded, Him [i.e., His punishment] from Himself.
The commentators said: from His punishment, His chastisement and His seizing.
The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is "and Allah warns you of Him," because "thing," "self," "essence" and "name" are all expressions for existence, and the self of a thing is the thing itself, as in His saying ﴿Kill yourselves﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:66], meaning: let some of you kill others.

Al-A'sha said:
"One day, the most generous of gifts from him, when
the self of the miser frowns at its request."
He meant: when the miser frowns at his request.

﴿And to Allah is the destination.﴾
﴿Say: If you conceal what is in your breasts﴾: your hearts, of affection for the disbelievers; ﴿or reveal it﴾: of allying with them by word and deed; ﴿Allah knows it﴾: Al-Kalbi said: that is, they hide what is in their hearts against the Messenger of Allah of denial, and they show hostility; and He said: ﴿Allah knows it and preserves it against you until He fights you with it and punishes you for it.﴾ Then He said: ﴿And He knows﴾, which is in the nominative as a new clause, like their saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them, and will heal the breasts of a believing people and remove the rage of their hearts, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:14–15], in the nominative.

And His saying: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal over your heart and Allah would erase falsehood﴾ [Surah al-Shura 42:24], then He said: ﴿and establish the truth.﴾ How could your allegiance to the disbelievers and your inclination toward them be hidden from Him? The affection of the heart means help with the heart and with action.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾
﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present﴾: the word "yawm" (day) is in the accusative, with the preposition removed, meaning "on the day." It was also said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: remember and fear the Day when every soul finds what it has done of good present, complete, nothing of it diminished. The reading of the general readers is with fatḥah on the ḍād as an object, and this is confirmed by His saying: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:49]. Ubayd, from Umayr, read muḥḍiran with kasrah on the ḍād, meaning that his deed will bring him into Paradise, hastening with it, from "ḥuḍūr" or "ḥaḍr."

﴿And what it has done of evil﴾: some grammarians made it a predicate in the accusative position, with "wujūd" (finding) governing it, and made "'amilat" a relative clause, meaning "and its deed is found." Others made it a new predicate, and in that case "tawaddu" may be read with a nominative or a jussive. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Abd Allah: "and what it has done of evil, it wishes" (wa ma 'amilat min su'in tawaddu).

﴿Wishes that between it﴾: between the soul ﴿and between that﴾: meaning between the evil ﴿a distance far off.﴾ The amad (distance) is the term and the limit to which something ends. Allah said: ﴿Does my Lord set for it a term?﴾ [Surah al-Jinn 72:25], and He said: ﴿So the term became long for them﴾ [Surah al-Hadid 57:16].

Al-Nabighah said:
"Ah, for one like you, or one who is ahead of you,
in the lead of the horse when they are level at the goal."

Al-Suddi said: "a distance far off" means a far-off place.
Muqatil said: as far as between the east and the west.
Al-Hasan said: It is not that one of them does not meet his deed forever, nor that he would wish to know it.

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Compassionate to the servants﴾: that is, to the believers among them.

﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you...﴾, the verse.
Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), some people claimed that they loved Allah, and they said: "O Muhammad, we love our Lord." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse, and made following His Prophet a sign of His love.

Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) stood before the Quraysh while they were in the Sacred Mosque, and they had set up their idols, hung ostrich eggs on them, put swords in their ears, and were prostrating to them. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah you have opposed the creed of your father Abraham and Ishmael, and indeed they were upon Islam." Quraysh said to him: "O Muhammad, we worship them out of love for Allah, ﴿so that they may bring us near to Allah in position﴾." Then Allah the Exalted said: "Say, O Muhammad: ﴿If you love Allah and worship the idols so that they may bring you near to Him, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾, and I am His Messenger to you and His proof against you, and I am more deserving of veneration than the idols."

Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, narrated: When the Jews said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:18], Allah revealed this verse. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) presented it to the Jews, but they refused to accept it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-Zubayr, who said: It was revealed concerning the Christians of Najran, because they said: "We magnify the Messiah and worship him out of love for Allah, the Glorified, and to magnify Him." So Allah said: "Say, O Muhammad: ﴿If you love Allah﴾, and your great saying about Jesus is out of love for Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and magnification of Him, ﴿then follow me; Allah will love you﴾", that is, follow my law and my practice, and Allah will love you. The love of the believers for Allah is their following His command, and their intention to obey Him and seek His pleasure, and the love of the Mighty and Majestic for the believers is a favour upon them, His reward for them, and His pardon for them; and that is His saying: ﴿and forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Al-Tha'labi said: Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, saying: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Surimi recited to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad recited to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim al-Bajali recited to me, for Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak:
"You disobey God while you show His love;
by my life, that is ugly in deeds.
If your love were true, you would obey Him,
for the one who loves is obedient to the one he loves."
[Tahdhib al-Kamal: 6/360; Tarikh Dimashq: 32/469.]

Narrated by 'Urwa from 'Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is lighter than the crawling of an ant on a smooth rock in a dark night. Its least degree is that you love something out of injustice, or hate something out of justice. And is religion anything other than loving for the sake of Allah and hating for the sake of Allah?" Allah said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [[Al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti: 2/85, no. 4935.]] [43].

When this verse was revealed, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said to his companions: "Muhammad makes his obedience like the obedience of Allah, and commands us to love him as the Christians loved 'Isa ibn Maryam." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away﴾, meaning: they turn away from obeying them both. ﴿Then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He does not approve of their deeds, nor of anything they have, and He will not forgive them. [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 1/319.]]

Waki' narrated from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever obeys the imam has obeyed me. Whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys the imam has disobeyed me." [44] [[Al-Musannaf of al-Kufi (Ibn Abi Shayba): 7/566.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 33–43 (part 1 of 3):

Indeed, God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Jews said, "We are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and we follow their religion and way," so God Most High revealed this verse. Meaning: God chose these people who professed Islam, while you are not upon the religion of Islam. *Iṣṭafā* (chose) is of the form *iftaʿala*, from *al-ṣafwa*, which is the purest part of anything. Meaning: they chose and selected Adam, the father of mankind, and Noah, the elder of the messengers, and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran.

Some said: By "the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran" he meant Abraham and ʿImran themselves, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind﴾ [2:248], meaning Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them.

A poet said:
"Do not weep for a dead man after a dead man whom I loved, ʿAli and ʿAbbas and the family of Abu Bakr."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/63.]]
Meaning: Abu Bakr.

Others said: "The family of Abraham" means Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is from the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran.

Muqatil said: It is ʿImran ibn Yaṣhar ibn Fahath [[Another report reads: Qahath. See Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/400.]] ibn Lawi ibn Yaʿqub, and his family is Moses and Aaron.

Al-Hasan and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It is ʿImran ibn Ashham ibn Amun, from the descendants of Solomon son of David, and his family is Mary and Jesus.

It was also said: It is ʿImran ibn Matan [[In al-Qurtubi 4/63 it is attributed to al-Suhayli.]], and his wife Hannah [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/63, the saying is from al-Suhayli.]]. He was singled out from among the prophets because the prophets and messengers, the majority and the minority of them, are from his offspring. *ʿAla al-ʿalamin dhurriyyatan* (over the worlds, as offspring): it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), said al-Akhfash.
Al-Farrāʾ said it is in the accusative as a detached qualifier (qaṭʿ), because *dhurriyya* is indefinite while "the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran" are definite.
