Some scholars of meanings and most exegetes said: his tongue was bound from speech as a punishment for him, because he asked for the sign after the angels had questioned him. So he did not speak for three days except by gesture (ramz), meaning a sign.

Al-Farra said: the gesture (ramz) may be made with the tongue without clear articulation; it is a hidden sound, like a whisper.

Al-Aʿmash read ﴿ramazan﴾ with a fatha on the mim, and it means prayer, as if it were a request made by it.

ʿAta said: it meant fasting for three days, because when they fasted they would not speak except by gesture.

﴿And when the angels said﴾ — meaning Jibril alone —

﴿"O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you"﴾ through the birth of ʿIsa without a father,

﴿"and purified you"﴾ from the touch of a man. (Tafsir al-Jalalayn: 72.) Al-Suddi said: Maryam did not menstruate.

﴿"and chosen you"﴾ through her dedication in the mosque, ﴿"above the women of the worlds"﴾, the worlds of her time, and no one else was dedicated in this way.

﴿"O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow."﴾ Be obedient and prolong the prayer; ﴿to your Lord﴾: the angels spoke this to her directly, face to face.

Al-Awza'i said: when the angels said that to her, she stood in prayer until her feet swelled and they oozed blood and pus. (Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/84.)

﴿And prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 33–43 (part 1 of 3):

Indeed, God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Jews said, "We are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and we follow their religion and way," so God Most High revealed this verse. Meaning: God chose these people who professed Islam, while you are not upon the religion of Islam. *Iṣṭafā* (chose) is of the form *iftaʿala*, from *al-ṣafwa*, which is the purest part of anything. Meaning: they chose and selected Adam, the father of mankind, and Noah, the elder of the messengers, and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran.

Some said: By "the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran" he meant Abraham and ʿImran themselves, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind﴾ [2:248], meaning Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them.

A poet said:
"Do not weep for a dead man after a dead man whom I loved, ʿAli and ʿAbbas and the family of Abu Bakr."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/63.]]
Meaning: Abu Bakr.

Others said: "The family of Abraham" means Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is from the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran.

Muqatil said: It is ʿImran ibn Yaṣhar ibn Fahath [[Another report reads: Qahath. See Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/400.]] ibn Lawi ibn Yaʿqub, and his family is Moses and Aaron.

Al-Hasan and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It is ʿImran ibn Ashham ibn Amun, from the descendants of Solomon son of David, and his family is Mary and Jesus.

It was also said: It is ʿImran ibn Matan [[In al-Qurtubi 4/63 it is attributed to al-Suhayli.]], and his wife Hannah [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/63, the saying is from al-Suhayli.]]. He was singled out from among the prophets because the prophets and messengers, the majority and the minority of them, are from his offspring. *ʿAla al-ʿalamin dhurriyyatan* (over the worlds, as offspring): it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), said al-Akhfash.
Al-Farrāʾ said it is in the accusative as a detached qualifier (qaṭʿ), because *dhurriyya* is indefinite while "the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran" are definite.
Al-Zajjaj said: it is in the accusative as an apposition (badal). It was also said: it is in the accusative as an indefinite (nakira), meaning He chose offspring, some of whom are from others. It was also said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause, meaning some of them are descendants of others. Abu Rawq said: some of them follow the religion of others.
[[Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 5/84.]]

*Wallahu samiʿun ʿalim* (And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing): al-Harawi said: When al-Hasan al-Basri died, and his death was on the evening of Friday, when people had prayed Friday prayer and carried him, in the Grand Mosque of Basra there was no prayer left since Islam began except on the day of al-Hasan's death, for the people followed his funeral and no one remained praying the ʿAsr prayer in the mosque.
Al-Jazairi said: I heard a caller calling: "Indeed God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds," and God chose al-Hasan al-Basri over the people of his time.

Al-Aʿmash reported from Abu Wa'il, who said: I read in the *muṣḥaf* (codex) of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: "Indeed God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran." Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil said: It is ʿImran ibn Mayan, not ʿImran the father of Moses, and between them there were one thousand three hundred years. The sons of Mayan [[Another report reads: Matan, Masan.]] were the chiefs of the Children of Israel, their rabbis and their kings.

Ibn Ishaq said [[In Tarikh al-Tabari (1/418): ʿImran ibn Yashhum ibn Amun ibn Minsha ibn Hizqiya ibn Ihziq ibn Yuthām ibn ʿAzariya ibn Amasiya ibn Yawash ibn Ahziyahu ibn Yarim ibn Yahshafat ibn Asa ibn Abiya ibn Rahaʿam ibn Solomon.
In Tarikh Dimashq: Mary ibn ʿImran ibn Hathan ibn al-Maʿadhir ibn al-Yud ibn Ajbun ibn Sadouq ibn ʿAyazur ibn al-Yaqim ibn Ayboud ibn Zarbabil ibn Shaltan ibn Yuhinna ibn Lirshitya ibn Amun ibn Misha ibn Hizqiya ibn Ajaz ibn Yuthām ibn ʿAzariya ibn Burām ibn Yusafat ibn Asa ibn Iyba ibn Rada'am ibn Solomon. I say: the disagreement is mostly due to differences in the readings of the manuscripts.]]: He is ʿImran ibn Ashham ibn Amun ibn Mitha ibn Hawqata ibn Ihrin ibn Yunam ibn ʿAwariya ibn Imdiya ibn Yawas ibn Jarbahwa ibn Yarim ibn Sif Shat ibn Lamsayin ibn Yaʿmur ibn Solomon ibn David (peace be upon him).

*Inni nadhartu laka ma fi baṭni muḥarraran* (Indeed I have vowed to You what is in my womb as dedicated): meaning, I have made what is in my womb dedicated, as a vow from me to You. A *nadhr* (vow) is what a person makes obligatory upon himself, whether with a condition or without a condition.
God said: ﴿Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾ [19:26], meaning: I have made it obligatory.
The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows to obey God, let him obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey God, let him not disobey Him."
[45]
Al-Aʿsha said:
"I visited Layla by night among the curtains, and I sought her, and I vowed vows."
[[Tarikh Dimashq: 20/140, ed. Dar al-Fikr; Diwan al-Aʿsha: 88, ed. Beirut.]]
From this is the saying: "So-and-so vowed the blood of so-and-so," meaning he made it obligatory upon himself to kill him.
Jamil said:
"Would that men who vowed my blood regarding you, and protected my meeting with you, were..."

*Muḥarraran* (dedicated): meaning free, purely devoted to God, serving the church, confined to it, devoted to the worship of God and the service of the church, not occupied by anything of this world. Whatever is purified is *muḥarrar*. It is said: "I freed the slave" when I manumitted him; "I *ḥarrartu* the writing" when I purified it and it no longer needed correction; a *ḥurr* (free) man is one who belongs to himself, with no one holding a claim over him; and *al-ṭīn al-ḥurr* is clay that is cleared of sand, pebbles and defects.
*Muḥarraran* is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause.
Al-Kalbi, Ibn Ishaq and others said: The *ḥurr* is a man who is freed and placed in the church, serving it and sweeping it and serving it, and he does not leave it until he reaches maturity. Then he is given the choice: if he wishes to remain there he remains, and if he wishes to leave he goes wherever he wishes. If he wants to leave after the choice, that is not allowed for him. No one among the [prophets] and scholars was not from the offspring of one who was dedicated at Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). Only boys were dedicated, and a girl was not required to do this nor was she suited to it, because of menstruation and harm that befalls her. So the mother of Mary dedicated what was in her womb.

The story behind this is that Zakariya and ʿImran married two sisters. Ishaʿ [[Lisan al-ʿArab: 12/151.]] daughter of Faqud, the mother of Yahya, was with Zakariya, and Hannah daughter of Faqud, the mother of Mary, was with ʿImran. Hannah had been kept from having a child until she despaired and became unable. They were a family that held a high position with God. Once, while she was in the shade of a tree, she saw a bird feeding its chick, and her desire for a child was stirred. She called upon God to grant her a child and said: "O God, to You is my vow: if You grant me a child, I will give him in charity to Jerusalem, so that he will be among its guardians and servants, as a vow and an act of thanks." So she conceived Mary and dedicated what was in her womb, not knowing what it was. Her husband said to her: "Woe to you, what have you done! What if what is in your womb is a female [and a female is a shame] and is not suited for this?" So both of them fell into anxiety about this, and ʿImran died while Hannah was pregnant with Mary.

*Falamma waḍaʿatha* (And when she gave birth to her): meaning she bore her, and behold, it was a girl. The pronoun in His saying *waḍaʿatha* refers to the vowed child, that is, Mary, from Hannah. For this reason it is feminine.
*Qalat* (She said): in regret, for she had hoped it would be a boy, and for that reason she had dedicated it.
*Rabbi inni waḍaʿtuha unthā* (My Lord, I have given birth to her, a female): an apology to God, Mighty and Majestic.
*Wallahu aʿlamu bi-mā waḍaʿat* (And God knows best what she bore): [what she had thought] [[See Zad al-Masir: 1/322.]], from al-Suddi. The common reading is with the tā' unvowelled [*waḍaʿat*]. ʿAli, Abu Maytham al-Najafi, Ibn ʿAmir, Abu Bakr and Yaʿqub read *wuḍaʿat* with a *ḍamma* on the tā', taking it as the words of Mary's mother [[See Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 2/280, and Fath al-Qadir: 1/334, which adds: Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a *kasra* on the tā'.]].

*Wa-laysa al-dhakaru ka-l-unthā* (And the male is not like the female): in service of the church and the worshippers in it, because of her weakness, and what befalls her of menstruation, postnatal bleeding and harm.

*Wa-innī sammaytuhā Maryam* (And indeed I named her Mary): in their language it means [the servant and the worshipper, and she was the most beautiful of women of her time and the best of them].
[[Qisas al-Anbiya' of al-Tha'labi: 371–374.]]

Abu Zurʿa reported from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Four are enough for you among the women of the worlds: Mary daughter of ʿImran, Asiya the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima daughter of Muhammad."
[46]
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/326; Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/19; see the verse.]]

*Wa-innī uʿīdhuhā bika* (And indeed I seek refuge for her in You): I entrust her and place her under Your protection. *Wa-dhurriyyatahā* (and her offspring): and her children.
*Min al-shayṭān al-rajīm* (from the accursed Satan): the cast-out, accursed one, struck with meteors.

Ibn al-Musayyab reported from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no child born but that Satan touches him when he is born, so he cries out loudly from the touch of Satan, except Mary and her son."
[47]
Then Abu Hurayra said: Recite if you wish: ﴿And indeed I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from Satan the accursed﴾.
[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/275; and both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) reported it in the Sahihayn.]]

Saʿid reported from Qatada, who said: "Every son of Adam was pricked by Satan in his side when he was born, except Jesus son of Mary, and his mother. A veil was placed between them, so the prick struck the veil and nothing from it reached her."
[48]
He said: It was also mentioned to us that the two of them did not commit sins as the rest of the children of Adam do.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "When Jesus (peace be upon him) was born, the devils came to Iblis and said: 'The idols have been overturned this morning.' He said: 'This is because of a new event that has happened.' He said: 'Stay here,' and he flew until he reached the two ends of the earth, but found nothing. Then he went to the seas and found nothing. Then he flew again and found that Jesus had been born, and the angels had surrounded him, so Iblis could not reach him, and he returned to them and said: 'A prophet has been born last night. No female has ever conceived or given birth without my being present at her side, except this one. So despair of the worship of idols after this night, but go to the children of Adam through levity and haste.'"
[[Qisas al-Anbiya': 372.]]

*Fa-taqabbalahā* (So her Lord accepted her): meaning God accepted Mary from Hannah and was pleased with her in place of the dedicated child. It is said: "qabila" and "wa-la-a" when a thing pleases him, he accepts it, *qubūlan* with a *fatḥa*, a verbal noun like *al-zāriʿ* and *al-zurūʿ* and *al-qabūl*. These three are the only forms; the analogical form would be with a *ḍamma*, like *al-dukhūl* and *al-khurūj*, said Abu ʿAmr, al-Kisa'i and the imams. Some said: the meaning of *al-taqabbul* (acceptance) is taking responsibility for her upbringing and attending to her affairs.
Al-Hasan said: His accepting her means that He did not punish her for even an hour of day or night.
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/69.]]

*Rabbuhā bi-qabūlin ḥasan* (Her Lord with a goodly acceptance): and He did not say *bi-taqabbul* (with acceptance). This type is called the verbal noun of a different verb (al-maṣdar ʿalā ghayr al-maṣdar).
Al-Farra' said: like your saying "I spoke a speech" (*takallamtu kalāman*).
Al-Fitami said: "The best of matters is what you are firmly established in, and not that you follow it by following."
Another said: "And if you walk, we will visit you as visitors," and he did not say "you visit."

*Wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan* (And He made her grow with a goodly growth): and He did not say *inbātan* (growth).
Juwaybir reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas: *Fa-taqabbalahā rabbuhā bi-qabūlin ḥasan* means: He led her on the path of the blessed. *Wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan* means: He perfected her creation without excess or deficiency. She would grow in a day as much as a child grows in a year.
Ibn Jurayj: Her Lord made her grow in her nourishment and provision, *nabātan ḥasanan*, until she became a fully grown adult woman.

*Wa-kaffalahā Zakariyya* (And Zakariya took charge of her): The commentators said: Her mother took her when she gave birth to her, wrapped her in a cloth and carried her to the mosque, and placed her before the rabbis, the sons of Aaron, who at that time were in Jerusalem, in the part that serves the custody of the Kaʿba. She said to them: "Take this vowed child." The rabbis competed for her, because she was the daughter of their leader and the custodian of their offerings. Zakariya said to them: "I am more entitled to her than you, because her aunt is with me."
The rabbis said to him: "Do not do that, for if she were left to the people's right over her, she would be left with her mother who bore her. But we will draw lots for her, and she will be with whoever's arrow comes out." So they went out, and they were twenty-nine [[In al-Qasas of al-Tha'labi: ten.]] men, to a flowing river.
Al-Suddi said: It was the Jordan river. They threw their pens into the water, and Zakariya's pen rose above the water, while theirs sank into the river. This was reported by Ibn Ishaq and a group.
Al-Suddi and a group said: Rather, Zakariya's pen stayed firm and stood above the water as if it were in mud, and their pens drifted with the flow of the water, so the water carried them off. Thus Zakariya was chosen and won the lot. He was the chief of the rabbis and their prophet. This is God's saying, Most High: *Wa-kaffalahā Zakariyya*, meaning he took her to himself and took charge of her affairs.

Ibn Ishaq said: When Zakariya took charge of her, he placed her with her aunt, the mother of Yahya, and found a wet nurse for her. When she grew up and reached the age of womanhood, he built for her a *miḥrāb* (a chamber in the mosque), that is, a room in the mosque, and made its door in its middle, so that no one could climb up to it except by a ladder, like the door of the Kaʿba, so that no one else could climb up to it. He would bring her food, drink and oil every day.

*Kullamā dakhala ʿalayhā Zakariyya al-miḥrāb wajada ʿindahā rizqan* (Whenever Zakariya entered upon her in the chamber, he found provision with her): meaning Zakariya found with her fruit out of its season, summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, fresh and tender.
*Qāla yā Maryam anna laki hādhā* (He said: "O Mary, from where is this for you?"): for whenever God granted her something and she was asked about it, she said: *Huwa min ʿindi Allāh, inna Allāha yarzuqu man yashāʾ bi-ghayri ḥisāb* (It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning).
[The gap is recorded from the author himself in his book Qisas al-Anbiya': 372–373.]
[Ibn Hamid reported to us with his chain from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stayed for days without eating any food, until it grieved him. He went around the houses of his wives but found nothing in the house of any of them. So he came to Fatima (may God be pleased with her) and said: "O my daughter, do you have anything to eat, for I am hungry?" She said: "No, by God, may my father and mother be your ransom." When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) left her, a neighbour of hers sent her two loaves and a piece of meat. She took them from her, put them in a bowl, covered it, and said: "I will prefer the Messenger of God (ﷺ) over myself and those with me." They were all in need of a fill of food. So she sent al-Hasan and al-Husayn to their grandfather, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he returned to her. She said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God, God has brought us something, and I have saved it for you." He said: "Then bring it." It was brought, and she uncovered the bowl, and behold, it was full of bread and meat. When he looked at it he was amazed, and knew that it was from the blessing of God. He praised God and invoked blessings upon His Prophet. He (peace be upon him) said: "From where is this for you, my daughter?" She said: *Huwa min ʿindi Allāh, inna Allāha yarzuqu man yashāʾ bi-ghayri ḥisāb*. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) praised God and said: "Praise be to God who has made you like the mistress of the women of the Children of Israel, for she was given provision by God, a goodly provision, and when she was asked about it she said: *Huwa min ʿindi Allāh, inna Allāha yarzuqu man yashāʾ bi-ghayri ḥisāb*."]
[[The manuscript has a lacuna and an obscured passage, which we have restored from the author in Qisas al-Anbiya': 374, 373, chapter on the birth of Mary (peace be upon her).]]

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent for ʿAli (may God be pleased with him). Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ), ʿAli, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, all the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and all his household ate until they were satisfied.
Fatima said: The bowl remained as it was, and I gave generously from it to all my neighbours, and God placed in it blessing and good.
[49]

The people of tafsir said: When Zakariya saw that, he said: "The One who is able to bring Mary fruit out of its season, without any cause or any person's action, is able to set right my wife and grant me a son in old age." So he longed for a child, because his family had died out, and Zakariya had grown old and despaired of having children.

God, Most High, said: ﴿There Zakariya called upon his Lord﴾: meaning, at that point. *Hunālika* (there) indicates a far point, just as *hādhihi* (this) indicates what is present. The *kāf* is the sign of the addressee, and the *lām* is kasra'd because two sakins meet.
Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama said: *Hunālika* is mostly used of time, and *hunāka* of place, but here one has been used in place of the other.

*Daʿā Zakariyya rabbahu* (Zakariya called upon his Lord): so he entered the chamber, closed the doors, and privately communed with his Lord.
*Qāla Rabbi* (He said: "My Lord"): meaning: O Lord. The vocative particle was deleted from its beginning and the *yāʾ* from its end, and the kasra on the *bāʾ* is used instead of the *yāʾ*.
*Hab lī* (Grant me): give me,
*min ladunka* (from Yourself): from Your presence. *Ladun* has four dialects: *ladun*, with a fatḥa on the lām, a ḍamma on the dāl, and a sukun on the nūn, which is the most eloquent; *lad*, with a fatḥa on the lām, a ḍamma on the dāl, and the nūn deleted; *ladan*, with a fatḥa on the lām, a sukun on the dāl, and a fatḥa on the nūn; and *ladun*, with a ḍamma on the lām, a sukun on the dāl, and a fatḥa on the nūn.
[[See Lisan al-ʿArab: 13/385.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 33–43 (part 2 of 3):

Al-Farra' said: "It is made specific by the genitive construction (idafa), and it may be put in the nominative according to the view of madhhab (Taj al-Arus: 9/332-333). And he recited the verse of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in both readings:

ما زال مهري مزجر الكلب منهم ... لدن غدوة حتى دنت لغروب

(Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/24.)

ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً: a blessed, pure, righteous, pleasing offspring. Dhurriyya (offspring) may be singular or plural, masculine or feminine, and here it is singular, as indicated by His words: ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾ (Maryam 19:5). He did not say "heirs" (awliya'). He made tayyiba feminine only because the word dhurriyya is feminine in form.

As the poet said:

أبوك خليفة ولدته أخرى ... وأنت خليفة ذاك الكمال

(Al-Sihah: 4/1356.)

He made waladathu feminine because the word khalifa is feminine in form. Likewise another said:

فما تزدري من حية جبلية سكات ... إذا ما غض ليس بأدردا

(Al-Sihah: 1/253.)

He made jabaliyya feminine because the word hayya is feminine in form, and then he returned to the meaning, saying ghadd (agreeing with the masculine), because he meant a male snake, and hayya applies to both male and female. This license applies only to words such as dabba (beast), dhurriyya (offspring) and khalifa (successor), which are used for both genders. When a man is named by one of these, which in meaning is "two men," it is not permissible to make his verb or adjective feminine. So one does not say "hadathana Mughayyar al-Dabbi" (feminine form), nor "hadathatna Mughayyara al-Dabbiyya."

إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعاءِ: that is, the One who hears it; and it is said, the One who answers it, as in His words: ﴿Indeed I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me﴾ (Ya Sin 36:25), meaning: so answer me. And the saying "Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) means: Allah answered him.

And he recited:

دعوت الله حتى خفت ألا ... يكون الله يسمع ما أقول

(Al-Fa'iq fi Gharib al-Hadith: 2/158.)

That is: I wept.

Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies and leaves behind a righteous offspring, Allah will grant him the like of the reward of their deeds, without diminishing anything of their rewards." [50] (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/72.)

فَنادَتْهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ: Yahya, Thabit, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited فناداه (fa-nadahu) with the ya'; Abu 'Imara and Abu 'Ubayda, and the rest recited فنادته (fa-nadathu) with the ta'. Abu Hatim preferred this. When the verb precedes its subject, one has the choice: if you wish, make it feminine; if you wish, make it masculine. However, whoever recites with the ta' does so because of the feminine form of "al-malaika" (the angels) and because it is plural; and when the subject of the verb is masculine but plural, feminine marking is better and more eloquent, as in His words: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed"﴾ (al-Hujurat 49:14). Whoever uses the masculine follows this pattern.

Al-Qasim ibn Sallam related from Jarir, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) used to make al-malaika masculine in the Qur'an." Abu 'Ubayda said: "He thought that Allah chose that, in opposition to the polytheists in their saying 'the angels are the daughters of Allah.' So by using the masculine here He refutes them."

Al-Sha'bi related that Ibn Mas'ud said: "If you disagree about the ya' and the ta', make it ya', and make the Qur'an masculine." [Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 7/202, where it reads: "The Qur'an is masculine, so make it masculine." Al-Sha'bi related it from 'Alqama from 'Abdullah.]

'Amr ibn Dinar related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "If a letter in the Qur'an has both ta' and ya', make it ya'." He meant by "the angels" here only Jibril (Gabriel) alone. That is because Zakariyya was the great rabbi who was in charge of the offerings and opened the door of the sanctuary; they did not enter until he gave them permission to enter. While he was standing in the mosque by the altar, praying, and the people were waiting for him to permit them to enter, suddenly there was a young man in white garments. He was frightened by him, and he called him, and it was Jibril: "O Zakariyya, indeed Allah gives you good news of Yahya." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿the angels called him﴾, meaning Jibril alone. Its parallel is His words in this surah: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Maryam..."﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:42), meaning Jibril alone; and His words in al-Nahl: ﴿He sends down the angels﴾ (al-Nahl 16:2), meaning Jibril, who brings the revelation, because the messenger to all the prophets was Jibril (peace be upon him). This is consistent with the saying of Ibn Mas'ud.

فناداه جبريل وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ: This is permissible in Arabic, to report about one using a plural form, as in the saying "So-and-so rode in ships," when he rode only one ship; "he went out on postal mules," when he was on only one mule; and "I heard this news from people," when he heard it from one person. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Those to whom the people said﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:173), meaning Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud; ﴿Indeed the people have gathered against you﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:173), meaning Abu Sufyan, and similar cases of plurality.

Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama said: If the speaker is a leader, it is permissible to report about him in the plural, because his companions are with him. Since Jibril is the leader of the angels, and every time he is sent there is a group of them with him, it is on this basis.

وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ: meaning in the mosque. Its parallel is His words: ﴿So he came out to his people from the mihrab﴾ (Maryam 19:11), meaning the mosque; and His words: ﴿when they climbed over the wall into the mihrab﴾ (Sad 38:21), meaning the mosque. It is a mif'al form from harb (war). It was said that it was so named because Satan fights (yuhariba) in it, just as the racecourse (midmar) is called so because horses are trained (tudmar) in it. Ibn 'Amir inclined the alif of al-mihrab throughout the Qur'an, while the others pronounce it with full emphasis (tafkhim).

أَنَّ اللَّهَ: Ibn 'Amir, 'Isa ibn 'Amr, al-A'mash and Hamza recited it with a kasra on the alif, on the assumption of an implied verb of saying, its meaning being: "the angels called him and said: Indeed Allah..." because calling is a form of speech.

The rest recited it with a fatha, making the call govern it, as if he said: "the angels called him that Allah gives you good news."

'Abdullah recited: وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ يا زكريا إن الله يبشرك.

Al-Farra' differed concerning the future form of this verb (yubashshiru), and counted its occurrences in the Qur'an as ten: two here; in al-Tawba, يُبَشِّرُهُمْ (9:21); in Maryam; in al-Hijr, إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ (15:53); and فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ (15:54); in al-Isra' and al-Kahf, وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (2:223 and 9:112); in Maryam, two places: يا زَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ and ولِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ; and in Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf: ذلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبادَهُ (42:21, 23). These are ten places. They agreed that one of them, فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ, is doubled (shaddah); and they differed about the other nine. Hamza recited all of them with a fatha on the ba', a sukun on the ya', a damma on the shin, and lightened (without shaddah).

Yahya ibn Ri'ab and al-Kisa'i recited five of them lightened: the two here, and those in al-Isra' and al-Kahf and 'Ayn Sin Qaf.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr lightened one of them, namely in Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf: ذلِكَ النبي الَّذِي يَبْشُرُ اللَّهُ عِبادَهُ.

Humayd ibn Qays recited all of them with a damma on the ya', a sukun on the ba', a kasra on the shin, and lightened.

The rest recited with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the ba', a kasra on the shin, and doubled.

Whoever lightens the shin with a damma on the ba' is taking it from abshara yubshiru, as the poet said:

يا أمّ عمرو أبشري بالبشرى ... موت ذريع وجراد عظلي

(Al-Jarad al-'Adhla: that which does not depart. By "Umm 'Amr" he means Umm 'Amir, a euphemism for the hyena. See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/75; the verse is also in Kitab al-'Ayn: 2/85.)

Whoever recites with the shin lightened and the ba' with a fatha takes it from bashara yubshiru, which is the dialect of Tihama and the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The poet said:

نشرت عوالي إذا رأيت حيفة ... ماسك من الحجّاج تعلى كتابها

Al-Farra' said:

وإذا رأيت الباهشين إلى العلى ... غبرا أكفهم بقاع ممحل
فأعنهم وأبشر بما بشروا به ... وإذا هم نزلوا بضنك فأنزل

(Lisan al-'Arab: 4/62.)

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad related from Mu'adh al-Kufi, who said: Whoever recites يُبَشِّرُهُمْ (yubashshiruhum) doubled, it is from bushra (glad tidings); and whoever recites yubshiruhum lightened with a fatha on the ya', it is from surur (joy), gladdening them. (Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/342.) The confirmation of this reading is what Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam related from his father: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to a man: "Allah gives you good news of a boy," and his wife bore a boy.

As for whoever recites with the doubled form, from bashshara yubashshiru, meaning bashir, this is the most eloquent and the most chaste of the dialects. Jarir said:

يا بشر حق لوجهك التبشير ... هلا غضبت لنا وأنت أمير

(Sharh Shafiyat Ibn al-Hajib: 4/328.)

The proof for the doubled form is that everything in the Qur'an of this type, whether in the obligatory past or the imperative, is with the doubled form, as in His words: ﴿So give good news to My servants who...﴾ (al-Muzzammil 73:17–18); ﴿And We gave him good news of Ishaq﴾ (al-Saffat 37:112); ﴿They said, "We give you good news of the truth"﴾ (al-Hijr 15:55).

بِيَحْيى: this is a name that is not inflected (la yajri) because it is a proper name, and the extra letter at its beginning, as in yazid, ya'mur and yashkur, is the prefix. Some people inclined it because of the ya', and others emphasized it. Its plural is "Yahyun," like Musawn and 'Isawn. They differed as to why he was named "Yahya."

Ibn 'Abbas said: because Allah revived through him the barrenness of his mother's womb. Qatada said: because Allah revived his heart with faith. Some said: because Allah revived his heart with prophethood. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: because Allah revived him through obedience, so that he never disobeyed nor intended a sin.

What is related from Ibn 'Abbas: he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one who will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who has not intended a sin he has committed, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he did not intend it nor commit it."

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard the teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: he was named that because he was martyred, and the martyrs are "alive with their Lord, receiving provision" (Al 'Imran 3:169).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Among the contempt of the world before Allah is that Yahya ibn Zakariyya was killed by a woman." [51] (Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/383, no. 2502.)

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Mansur [al-Jamshadhi] say, from 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Maqdisi: Allah revealed to Ibrahim the Friend: "Say to Sarah" – and that was her name – "I will bring forth from you two a servant who will not die through My disobedience; his name is Hayy. So give him a letter from your name." She gave him the first letter of her name, and he became Yahya, and Ibrahim's wife became Sarah.

مُصَدِّقاً بِكَلِمَةٍ: accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). مِنَ اللَّهِ: meaning 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called a "word" because Allah said to him "Be" without a father, and he was. The name "word" fell upon him because he came about by it. Yahya was the first to believe in 'Isa and confirm him. Yahya was six months older than 'Isa, and they were two maternal cousins. Then Yahya was killed before 'Isa was raised (peace be upon them both).

Abu 'Ubayda and 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ means "and His signs," and one says: "recite to me the word of so-and-so," meaning his poem.

وَسَيِّداً: from the form fay'al, like sada yasudu; its origin is yasud. It is the leader who is followed and to whom one turns for his word.

Al-Mufaddal said: He meant "a master (sayyid) in religion."

Sharik, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, said: "The sayyid is one of good character."

Sharik also related with his isnad from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The sayyid is the one who obeys his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: the sayyid is the jurist, the learned. Qatada: a master in knowledge and fasting. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: the forbearing. Al-Dahhak: the pious. 'Ikrima: the one who does not become angry. Mujahid: the honored before Allah. Ibn Zayd: the noble, the great. Sufyan al-Thawri: the one who is not envied.

Yusuf ibn al-Husayn al-Razi related from Dhu'l-Nun al-Misri, who said: "The envious one is never a master."

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: one who is obeyed.

Al-Zajjaj: the one who intends good for all things, and wishes good for his peers.

Ahmad ibn 'Asim: the sayyid is the one content with what has been apportioned to him.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq: the one who is satisfied with Allah's decree.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi: the one who relies upon Allah.

Abu Zayd al-Bastami: the one whose resolve is great and whose rank is noble, who has not let his soul speak of the abode of this world. It was also said: he is the generous.

Ibn al-Zubayr related from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is your sayyid, O sons of Salama?" They said: "Jadd ibn Qays, but he is stingy and a coward." He said: "And what disease is worse than stinginess? Rather, your sayyid is 'Amr ibn Jamuh." [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/15, with variation.]

'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas related that he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when about ten men in travelling clothes came to him. They greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people, then said: "Who among you is the sayyid?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim." They recognized that he was the Messenger of Allah, and said: "Is there no sayyid in your community?" He said: "Yes, a man who has been given lawful wealth and provided with generosity, who draws near the poor and whose complaints are few." [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/197.]

It is related that Asad ibn 'Abdullah said to a man from Banu Shayban: "It has reached me that nobility (su'dud) is cheap among you." He said: "As for us, we do not make a man our sayyid unless he gives us his camel-saddle, spreads out his honor for us, and gives us his wealth." He said: "By God, nobility among you is indeed expensive."

وَحَصُوراً: its origin is from hasr, which is confinement. It is said: "I held the man back from his need" when I confined him; "I was restricted from such-and-such" when I refrained from it; "So-and-so was restricted in his recitation" when he refrained from reciting and was unable to do it; and from this is "ihsar" (siege) by the enemy. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made Jahannam a prison (hasir) for the disbelievers﴾ (al-Isra' 17:8), meaning a confinement. It is said of a man who keeps a secret and holds it back and does not divulge it: he is a hasur.

Jarir said:

ولقد تسقطني الوشاة فصادفوا ... حصرا بسرك يا أميم ضنينا

(Al-Sihah: 2/631.)

So al-hasur, according to Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Qatada, 'Ata', Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Hasan, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, is the one who does not come to women nor approach them. On this view it is a maf'ul in the sense of fa'il: he confines himself from desires.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Dahhak said: he is the impotent one who has no seed. The evidence for this interpretation is what Abu Salih related from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every son of Adam will meet Allah with a sin which he committed, and He will punish him for it or have mercy on him, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he was a sayyid and a hasur." [52]

وَنَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed with his hand toward a speck of dust from the earth, took it, and said: "His male organ was like this speck." [53] (Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/520, no. 32428; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/209.)

Al-Mubarrad said: al-hasur is one who does not take part in play, frivolity and vanities. Its origin is the Arabs' saying: "One who does not enter into gambling is a hasur." Al-Akhtal said:

وشارب مربح بالكأس نادمني ... لا بالحصور ولا فيها بسوار

(Lisan al-'Arab: 4/194.)

When the angels called Zakariyya with the good news, he said: رَبِّ, "O my lord" (sayyidi, my master), he said it to Jibril (peace be upon him). This is the view of al-Kalbi and most of the commentators.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: Zakariyya only said "O Lord" to Allah, not to Jibril.

أَنَّى يَكُونُ: from where will it be? لِي غُلامٌ: a son. وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ: Abu Hamza, al-Farra' and al-Mu'arrikh ibn al-Mufaddal said: this is an inverted (maqlub) construction: meaning "I have reached old age," just as one says "hunger has reached me," meaning "I am in hardship." He says this statement "will not cut me off," meaning it will not reach what he wants it to cut off. Al-Mufaddal recited:

كانت فريضة ما زعمت ... كما كانت الزناء فريضة الرجم

(Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/111; Zad al-Masir: 5/24; Lisan al-'Arab: 14/359; the verse is by al-Ju'di, with "ma taqul kama".)

It was also said that its meaning is: old age has overtaken me, reached me, taken from me and weakened me.

Al-Kalbi said: On the day he was given the good news of a child, he was ninety-two years old. It was also said: ninety-nine years old (or ninety-eight, according to another report; and other figures are also mentioned). That is His words: وَامْرَأَتِي عاقِرٌ, meaning barren, unable to bear. One says "a man 'aqir and a woman 'aqir," and "qad 'aqira" (with a damma on the qaf), ya'qaru 'aqran and 'aqara. It was also said: "takallama hatta u'qira" (with a kasra on the qaf), ya'qaru 'aqran, when one is left unable to speak.

'Amir ibn al-Tufayl said:

ولبئس الفتى إن كنت أعور عاقرا ... جبانا فما عذري لدى كل محضر

(Fath al-Bari: 6/337.)

The ha' was dropped only because this form is restricted to females, and al-Khalil at times said so.

Sibawayh said: it is for attribution, meaning "possessing barrenness," just as one says "imra'a mursi'" meaning "possessing a suckling child"; and every [... ] (lacuna in the original manuscript) "imra'ati" means "'aqir," and a person may be "'aqir."

'Ubayd said: "'aqir" is like "dhat rahim" (possessing a womb), or "khanim" like "man [yanhab]."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 33–43 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Thus does Allah do what He wills.﴾ It may be asked: why did Zakariyya deny this and ask for a sign after the angels had given him the good news? Was that doubt about their truthfulness, or was it a denial of his Lord's power? (Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/350.) This is not something that people of faith may be described as having, so how much less the prophets (peace be upon them)?

The answer to this is what ʿIkrima and al-Suddi related: when Zakariyya heard the call of the angels, Satan came to him and said, "O Zakariyya, the voice you heard is not from Allah. It is only from Satan, mocking you. If it were from Allah, He would have revealed it to you secretly, just as He called you secretly and as He reveals to you in all other matters." He said this to repel the whispering.

The second answer: he did not doubt the child, but doubted how it would come about and the manner in which the child would be produced. So he said: ﴿How can I have a boy?﴾ That is, how will there be a child for me? Will You make me and my wife young again? Or will You grant us a child in our old age? Or will You grant me a child from my wife or from other women? He said this as a question, not as a denial. This is the view of al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan.

﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾ A sign by which I may know the time of my wife's conception, so that I may increase my worship in gratitude to You.

﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to people﴾ — you will refrain from speech — ﴿for three days except by gestures."﴾ You will devote your words to my worship and obedience. It does not mean that his tongue was restrained from speech in general; rather, it was a prohibition on that, as shown by His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning.﴾

Some scholars of meanings and most exegetes said: his tongue was bound from speech as a punishment for him, because he asked for the sign after the angels had questioned him. So he did not speak for three days except by gesture (ramz), meaning a sign.

Al-Farra said: the gesture (ramz) may be made with the tongue without clear articulation; it is a hidden sound, like a whisper.

Al-Aʿmash read ﴿ramazan﴾ with a fatha on the mim, and it means prayer, as if it were a request made by it.

ʿAta said: it meant fasting for three days, because when they fasted they would not speak except by gesture.

﴿And when the angels said﴾ — meaning Jibril alone —

﴿"O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you"﴾ through the birth of ʿIsa without a father,

﴿"and purified you"﴾ from the touch of a man. (Tafsir al-Jalalayn: 72.) Al-Suddi said: Maryam did not menstruate.

﴿"and chosen you"﴾ through her dedication in the mosque, ﴿"above the women of the worlds"﴾, the worlds of her time, and no one else was dedicated in this way.

﴿"O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow."﴾ Be obedient and prolong the prayer; ﴿to your Lord﴾: the angels spoke this to her directly, face to face.

Al-Awza'i said: when the angels said that to her, she stood in prayer until her feet swelled and they oozed blood and pus. (Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/84.)

﴿And prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 33–43 (part 1 of 3):

Indeed, God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Jews said, "We are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and we follow their religion and way," so God Most High revealed this verse. Meaning: God chose these people who professed Islam, while you are not upon the religion of Islam. *Iṣṭafā* (chose) is of the form *iftaʿala*, from *al-ṣafwa*, which is the purest part of anything. Meaning: they chose and selected Adam, the father of mankind, and Noah, the elder of the messengers, and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran.

Some said: By "the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran" he meant Abraham and ʿImran themselves, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind﴾ [2:248], meaning Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them.

A poet said:
"Do not weep for a dead man after a dead man whom I loved, ʿAli and ʿAbbas and the family of Abu Bakr."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/63.]]
Meaning: Abu Bakr.

Others said: "The family of Abraham" means Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is from the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran.

Muqatil said: It is ʿImran ibn Yaṣhar ibn Fahath [[Another report reads: Qahath. See Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/400.]] ibn Lawi ibn Yaʿqub, and his family is Moses and Aaron.

Al-Hasan and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It is ʿImran ibn Ashham ibn Amun, from the descendants of Solomon son of David, and his family is Mary and Jesus.

It was also said: It is ʿImran ibn Matan [[In al-Qurtubi 4/63 it is attributed to al-Suhayli.]], and his wife Hannah [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/63, the saying is from al-Suhayli.]]. He was singled out from among the prophets because the prophets and messengers, the majority and the minority of them, are from his offspring. *ʿAla al-ʿalamin dhurriyyatan* (over the worlds, as offspring): it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), said al-Akhfash.
Al-Farrāʾ said it is in the accusative as a detached qualifier (qaṭʿ), because *dhurriyya* is indefinite while "the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran" are definite.
Al-Zajjaj said: it is in the accusative as an apposition (badal). It was also said: it is in the accusative as an indefinite (nakira), meaning He chose offspring, some of whom are from others. It was also said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause, meaning some of them are descendants of others. Abu Rawq said: some of them follow the religion of others.
[[Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 5/84.]]

*Wallahu samiʿun ʿalim* (And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing): al-Harawi said: When al-Hasan al-Basri died, and his death was on the evening of Friday, when people had prayed Friday prayer and carried him, in the Grand Mosque of Basra there was no prayer left since Islam began except on the day of al-Hasan's death, for the people followed his funeral and no one remained praying the ʿAsr prayer in the mosque.
Al-Jazairi said: I heard a caller calling: "Indeed God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds," and God chose al-Hasan al-Basri over the people of his time.

Al-Aʿmash reported from Abu Wa'il, who said: I read in the *muṣḥaf* (codex) of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: "Indeed God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran." Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil said: It is ʿImran ibn Mayan, not ʿImran the father of Moses, and between them there were one thousand three hundred years. The sons of Mayan [[Another report reads: Matan, Masan.]] were the chiefs of the Children of Israel, their rabbis and their kings.

Ibn Ishaq said [[In Tarikh al-Tabari (1/418): ʿImran ibn Yashhum ibn Amun ibn Minsha ibn Hizqiya ibn Ihziq ibn Yuthām ibn ʿAzariya ibn Amasiya ibn Yawash ibn Ahziyahu ibn Yarim ibn Yahshafat ibn Asa ibn Abiya ibn Rahaʿam ibn Solomon.
In Tarikh Dimashq: Mary ibn ʿImran ibn Hathan ibn al-Maʿadhir ibn al-Yud ibn Ajbun ibn Sadouq ibn ʿAyazur ibn al-Yaqim ibn Ayboud ibn Zarbabil ibn Shaltan ibn Yuhinna ibn Lirshitya ibn Amun ibn Misha ibn Hizqiya ibn Ajaz ibn Yuthām ibn ʿAzariya ibn Burām ibn Yusafat ibn Asa ibn Iyba ibn Rada'am ibn Solomon. I say: the disagreement is mostly due to differences in the readings of the manuscripts.]]: He is ʿImran ibn Ashham ibn Amun ibn Mitha ibn Hawqata ibn Ihrin ibn Yunam ibn ʿAwariya ibn Imdiya ibn Yawas ibn Jarbahwa ibn Yarim ibn Sif Shat ibn Lamsayin ibn Yaʿmur ibn Solomon ibn David (peace be upon him).

*Inni nadhartu laka ma fi baṭni muḥarraran* (Indeed I have vowed to You what is in my womb as dedicated): meaning, I have made what is in my womb dedicated, as a vow from me to You. A *nadhr* (vow) is what a person makes obligatory upon himself, whether with a condition or without a condition.
God said: ﴿Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾ [19:26], meaning: I have made it obligatory.
The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows to obey God, let him obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey God, let him not disobey Him."
[45]
Al-Aʿsha said:
"I visited Layla by night among the curtains, and I sought her, and I vowed vows."
[[Tarikh Dimashq: 20/140, ed. Dar al-Fikr; Diwan al-Aʿsha: 88, ed. Beirut.]]
From this is the saying: "So-and-so vowed the blood of so-and-so," meaning he made it obligatory upon himself to kill him.
Jamil said:
"Would that men who vowed my blood regarding you, and protected my meeting with you, were..."

*Muḥarraran* (dedicated): meaning free, purely devoted to God, serving the church, confined to it, devoted to the worship of God and the service of the church, not occupied by anything of this world. Whatever is purified is *muḥarrar*. It is said: "I freed the slave" when I manumitted him; "I *ḥarrartu* the writing" when I purified it and it no longer needed correction; a *ḥurr* (free) man is one who belongs to himself, with no one holding a claim over him; and *al-ṭīn al-ḥurr* is clay that is cleared of sand, pebbles and defects.
*Muḥarraran* is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause.
Al-Kalbi, Ibn Ishaq and others said: The *ḥurr* is a man who is freed and placed in the church, serving it and sweeping it and serving it, and he does not leave it until he reaches maturity. Then he is given the choice: if he wishes to remain there he remains, and if he wishes to leave he goes wherever he wishes. If he wants to leave after the choice, that is not allowed for him. No one among the [prophets] and scholars was not from the offspring of one who was dedicated at Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). Only boys were dedicated, and a girl was not required to do this nor was she suited to it, because of menstruation and harm that befalls her. So the mother of Mary dedicated what was in her womb.

The story behind this is that Zakariya and ʿImran married two sisters. Ishaʿ [[Lisan al-ʿArab: 12/151.]] daughter of Faqud, the mother of Yahya, was with Zakariya, and Hannah daughter of Faqud, the mother of Mary, was with ʿImran. Hannah had been kept from having a child until she despaired and became unable. They were a family that held a high position with God. Once, while she was in the shade of a tree, she saw a bird feeding its chick, and her desire for a child was stirred. She called upon God to grant her a child and said: "O God, to You is my vow: if You grant me a child, I will give him in charity to Jerusalem, so that he will be among its guardians and servants, as a vow and an act of thanks." So she conceived Mary and dedicated what was in her womb, not knowing what it was. Her husband said to her: "Woe to you, what have you done! What if what is in your womb is a female [and a female is a shame] and is not suited for this?" So both of them fell into anxiety about this, and ʿImran died while Hannah was pregnant with Mary.

*Falamma waḍaʿatha* (And when she gave birth to her): meaning she bore her, and behold, it was a girl. The pronoun in His saying *waḍaʿatha* refers to the vowed child, that is, Mary, from Hannah. For this reason it is feminine.
*Qalat* (She said): in regret, for she had hoped it would be a boy, and for that reason she had dedicated it.
*Rabbi inni waḍaʿtuha unthā* (My Lord, I have given birth to her, a female): an apology to God, Mighty and Majestic.
*Wallahu aʿlamu bi-mā waḍaʿat* (And God knows best what she bore): [what she had thought] [[See Zad al-Masir: 1/322.]], from al-Suddi. The common reading is with the tā' unvowelled [*waḍaʿat*]. ʿAli, Abu Maytham al-Najafi, Ibn ʿAmir, Abu Bakr and Yaʿqub read *wuḍaʿat* with a *ḍamma* on the tā', taking it as the words of Mary's mother [[See Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 2/280, and Fath al-Qadir: 1/334, which adds: Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a *kasra* on the tā'.]].

*Wa-laysa al-dhakaru ka-l-unthā* (And the male is not like the female): in service of the church and the worshippers in it, because of her weakness, and what befalls her of menstruation, postnatal bleeding and harm.

*Wa-innī sammaytuhā Maryam* (And indeed I named her Mary): in their language it means [the servant and the worshipper, and she was the most beautiful of women of her time and the best of them].
[[Qisas al-Anbiya' of al-Tha'labi: 371–374.]]

Abu Zurʿa reported from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Four are enough for you among the women of the worlds: Mary daughter of ʿImran, Asiya the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima daughter of Muhammad."
[46]
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/326; Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/19; see the verse.]]

*Wa-innī uʿīdhuhā bika* (And indeed I seek refuge for her in You): I entrust her and place her under Your protection. *Wa-dhurriyyatahā* (and her offspring): and her children.
*Min al-shayṭān al-rajīm* (from the accursed Satan): the cast-out, accursed one, struck with meteors.

Ibn al-Musayyab reported from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no child born but that Satan touches him when he is born, so he cries out loudly from the touch of Satan, except Mary and her son."
[47]
Then Abu Hurayra said: Recite if you wish: ﴿And indeed I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from Satan the accursed﴾.
[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/275; and both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) reported it in the Sahihayn.]]

Saʿid reported from Qatada, who said: "Every son of Adam was pricked by Satan in his side when he was born, except Jesus son of Mary, and his mother. A veil was placed between them, so the prick struck the veil and nothing from it reached her."
[48]
He said: It was also mentioned to us that the two of them did not commit sins as the rest of the children of Adam do.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "When Jesus (peace be upon him) was born, the devils came to Iblis and said: 'The idols have been overturned this morning.' He said: 'This is because of a new event that has happened.' He said: 'Stay here,' and he flew until he reached the two ends of the earth, but found nothing. Then he went to the seas and found nothing. Then he flew again and found that Jesus had been born, and the angels had surrounded him, so Iblis could not reach him, and he returned to them and said: 'A prophet has been born last night. No female has ever conceived or given birth without my being present at her side, except this one. So despair of the worship of idols after this night, but go to the children of Adam through levity and haste.'"
[[Qisas al-Anbiya': 372.]]

*Fa-taqabbalahā* (So her Lord accepted her): meaning God accepted Mary from Hannah and was pleased with her in place of the dedicated child. It is said: "qabila" and "wa-la-a" when a thing pleases him, he accepts it, *qubūlan* with a *fatḥa*, a verbal noun like *al-zāriʿ* and *al-zurūʿ* and *al-qabūl*. These three are the only forms; the analogical form would be with a *ḍamma*, like *al-dukhūl* and *al-khurūj*, said Abu ʿAmr, al-Kisa'i and the imams. Some said: the meaning of *al-taqabbul* (acceptance) is taking responsibility for her upbringing and attending to her affairs.
Al-Hasan said: His accepting her means that He did not punish her for even an hour of day or night.
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/69.]]

*Rabbuhā bi-qabūlin ḥasan* (Her Lord with a goodly acceptance): and He did not say *bi-taqabbul* (with acceptance). This type is called the verbal noun of a different verb (al-maṣdar ʿalā ghayr al-maṣdar).
Al-Farra' said: like your saying "I spoke a speech" (*takallamtu kalāman*).
Al-Fitami said: "The best of matters is what you are firmly established in, and not that you follow it by following."
Another said: "And if you walk, we will visit you as visitors," and he did not say "you visit."

*Wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan* (And He made her grow with a goodly growth): and He did not say *inbātan* (growth).
Juwaybir reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas: *Fa-taqabbalahā rabbuhā bi-qabūlin ḥasan* means: He led her on the path of the blessed. *Wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan* means: He perfected her creation without excess or deficiency. She would grow in a day as much as a child grows in a year.
Ibn Jurayj: Her Lord made her grow in her nourishment and provision, *nabātan ḥasanan*, until she became a fully grown adult woman.

*Wa-kaffalahā Zakariyya* (And Zakariya took charge of her): The commentators said: Her mother took her when she gave birth to her, wrapped her in a cloth and carried her to the mosque, and placed her before the rabbis, the sons of Aaron, who at that time were in Jerusalem, in the part that serves the custody of the Kaʿba. She said to them: "Take this vowed child." The rabbis competed for her, because she was the daughter of their leader and the custodian of their offerings. Zakariya said to them: "I am more entitled to her than you, because her aunt is with me."
The rabbis said to him: "Do not do that, for if she were left to the people's right over her, she would be left with her mother who bore her. But we will draw lots for her, and she will be with whoever's arrow comes out." So they went out, and they were twenty-nine [[In al-Qasas of al-Tha'labi: ten.]] men, to a flowing river.
Al-Suddi said: It was the Jordan river. They threw their pens into the water, and Zakariya's pen rose above the water, while theirs sank into the river. This was reported by Ibn Ishaq and a group.
Al-Suddi and a group said: Rather, Zakariya's pen stayed firm and stood above the water as if it were in mud, and their pens drifted with the flow of the water, so the water carried them off. Thus Zakariya was chosen and won the lot. He was the chief of the rabbis and their prophet. This is God's saying, Most High: *Wa-kaffalahā Zakariyya*, meaning he took her to himself and took charge of her affairs.

Ibn Ishaq said: When Zakariya took charge of her, he placed her with her aunt, the mother of Yahya, and found a wet nurse for her. When she grew up and reached the age of womanhood, he built for her a *miḥrāb* (a chamber in the mosque), that is, a room in the mosque, and made its door in its middle, so that no one could climb up to it except by a ladder, like the door of the Kaʿba, so that no one else could climb up to it. He would bring her food, drink and oil every day.

*Kullamā dakhala ʿalayhā Zakariyya al-miḥrāb wajada ʿindahā rizqan* (Whenever Zakariya entered upon her in the chamber, he found provision with her): meaning Zakariya found with her fruit out of its season, summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, fresh and tender.
*Qāla yā Maryam anna laki hādhā* (He said: "O Mary, from where is this for you?"): for whenever God granted her something and she was asked about it, she said: *Huwa min ʿindi Allāh, inna Allāha yarzuqu man yashāʾ bi-ghayri ḥisāb* (It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning).
[The gap is recorded from the author himself in his book Qisas al-Anbiya': 372–373.]
[Ibn Hamid reported to us with his chain from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stayed for days without eating any food, until it grieved him. He went around the houses of his wives but found nothing in the house of any of them. So he came to Fatima (may God be pleased with her) and said: "O my daughter, do you have anything to eat, for I am hungry?" She said: "No, by God, may my father and mother be your ransom." When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) left her, a neighbour of hers sent her two loaves and a piece of meat. She took them from her, put them in a bowl, covered it, and said: "I will prefer the Messenger of God (ﷺ) over myself and those with me." They were all in need of a fill of food. So she sent al-Hasan and al-Husayn to their grandfather, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he returned to her. She said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God, God has brought us something, and I have saved it for you." He said: "Then bring it." It was brought, and she uncovered the bowl, and behold, it was full of bread and meat. When he looked at it he was amazed, and knew that it was from the blessing of God. He praised God and invoked blessings upon His Prophet. He (peace be upon him) said: "From where is this for you, my daughter?" She said: *Huwa min ʿindi Allāh, inna Allāha yarzuqu man yashāʾ bi-ghayri ḥisāb*. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) praised God and said: "Praise be to God who has made you like the mistress of the women of the Children of Israel, for she was given provision by God, a goodly provision, and when she was asked about it she said: *Huwa min ʿindi Allāh, inna Allāha yarzuqu man yashāʾ bi-ghayri ḥisāb*."]
[[The manuscript has a lacuna and an obscured passage, which we have restored from the author in Qisas al-Anbiya': 374, 373, chapter on the birth of Mary (peace be upon her).]]

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent for ʿAli (may God be pleased with him). Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ), ʿAli, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, all the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and all his household ate until they were satisfied.
Fatima said: The bowl remained as it was, and I gave generously from it to all my neighbours, and God placed in it blessing and good.
[49]
[[In full in Qisas al-Anbiya' of al-Tha'labi: 373–374; Tafsir Ibn Kathir with its chain: 1/368; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/20; Subul al-Huda wa-l-Rashad by al-Shami: 9/483 and 11/47; al-Bidaya wa-l-Nihaya of Ibn Kathir: 6/122.]]

The people of tafsir said: When Zakariya saw that, he said: "The One who is able to bring Mary fruit out of its season, without any cause or any person's action, is able to set right my wife and grant me a son in old age." So he longed for a child, because his family had died out, and Zakariya had grown old and despaired of having children.

God, Most High, said: ﴿There Zakariya called upon his Lord﴾: meaning, at that point. *Hunālika* (there) indicates a far point, just as *hādhihi* (this) indicates what is present. The *kāf* is the sign of the addressee, and the *lām* is kasra'd because two sakins meet.
Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama said: *Hunālika* is mostly used of time, and *hunāka* of place, but here one has been used in place of the other.

*Daʿā Zakariyya rabbahu* (Zakariya called upon his Lord): so he entered the chamber, closed the doors, and privately communed with his Lord.
*Qāla Rabbi* (He said: "My Lord"): meaning: O Lord. The vocative particle was deleted from its beginning and the *yāʾ* from its end, and the kasra on the *bāʾ* is used instead of the *yāʾ*.
*Hab lī* (Grant me): give me,
*min ladunka* (from Yourself): from Your presence. *Ladun* has four dialects: *ladun*, with a fatḥa on the lām, a ḍamma on the dāl, and a sukun on the nūn, which is the most eloquent; *lad*, with a fatḥa on the lām, a ḍamma on the dāl, and the nūn deleted; *ladan*, with a fatḥa on the lām, a sukun on the dāl, and a fatḥa on the nūn; and *ladun*, with a ḍamma on the lām, a sukun on the dāl, and a fatḥa on the nūn.
[[See Lisan al-ʿArab: 13/385.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 33–43 (part 2 of 3):

Al-Farra' said: "It is made specific by the genitive construction (idafa), and it may be put in the nominative according to the view of madhhab (Taj al-Arus: 9/332-333). And he recited the verse of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in both readings:

ما زال مهري مزجر الكلب منهم ... لدن غدوة حتى دنت لغروب

(Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/24.)

ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً: a blessed, pure, righteous, pleasing offspring. Dhurriyya (offspring) may be singular or plural, masculine or feminine, and here it is singular, as indicated by His words: ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾ (Maryam 19:5). He did not say "heirs" (awliya'). He made tayyiba feminine only because the word dhurriyya is feminine in form.

As the poet said:

أبوك خليفة ولدته أخرى ... وأنت خليفة ذاك الكمال

(Al-Sihah: 4/1356.)

He made waladathu feminine because the word khalifa is feminine in form. Likewise another said:

فما تزدري من حية جبلية سكات ... إذا ما غض ليس بأدردا

(Al-Sihah: 1/253.)

He made jabaliyya feminine because the word hayya is feminine in form, and then he returned to the meaning, saying ghadd (agreeing with the masculine), because he meant a male snake, and hayya applies to both male and female. This license applies only to words such as dabba (beast), dhurriyya (offspring) and khalifa (successor), which are used for both genders. When a man is named by one of these, which in meaning is "two men," it is not permissible to make his verb or adjective feminine. So one does not say "hadathana Mughayyar al-Dabbi" (feminine form), nor "hadathatna Mughayyara al-Dabbiyya."

إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعاءِ: that is, the One who hears it; and it is said, the One who answers it, as in His words: ﴿Indeed I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me﴾ (Ya Sin 36:25), meaning: so answer me. And the saying "Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) means: Allah answered him.

And he recited:

دعوت الله حتى خفت ألا ... يكون الله يسمع ما أقول

(Al-Fa'iq fi Gharib al-Hadith: 2/158.)

That is: I wept.

Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies and leaves behind a righteous offspring, Allah will grant him the like of the reward of their deeds, without diminishing anything of their rewards." [50] (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/72.)

فَنادَتْهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ: Yahya, Thabit, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited فناداه (fa-nadahu) with the ya'; Abu 'Imara and Abu 'Ubayda, and the rest recited فنادته (fa-nadathu) with the ta'. Abu Hatim preferred this. When the verb precedes its subject, one has the choice: if you wish, make it feminine; if you wish, make it masculine. However, whoever recites with the ta' does so because of the feminine form of "al-malaika" (the angels) and because it is plural; and when the subject of the verb is masculine but plural, feminine marking is better and more eloquent, as in His words: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed"﴾ (al-Hujurat 49:14). Whoever uses the masculine follows this pattern.

Al-Qasim ibn Sallam related from Jarir, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) used to make al-malaika masculine in the Qur'an." Abu 'Ubayda said: "He thought that Allah chose that, in opposition to the polytheists in their saying 'the angels are the daughters of Allah.' So by using the masculine here He refutes them."

Al-Sha'bi related that Ibn Mas'ud said: "If you disagree about the ya' and the ta', make it ya', and make the Qur'an masculine." [Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 7/202, where it reads: "The Qur'an is masculine, so make it masculine." Al-Sha'bi related it from 'Alqama from 'Abdullah.]

'Amr ibn Dinar related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "If a letter in the Qur'an has both ta' and ya', make it ya'." He meant by "the angels" here only Jibril (Gabriel) alone. That is because Zakariyya was the great rabbi who was in charge of the offerings and opened the door of the sanctuary; they did not enter until he gave them permission to enter. While he was standing in the mosque by the altar, praying, and the people were waiting for him to permit them to enter, suddenly there was a young man in white garments. He was frightened by him, and he called him, and it was Jibril: "O Zakariyya, indeed Allah gives you good news of Yahya." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿the angels called him﴾, meaning Jibril alone. Its parallel is His words in this surah: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Maryam..."﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:42), meaning Jibril alone; and His words in al-Nahl: ﴿He sends down the angels﴾ (al-Nahl 16:2), meaning Jibril, who brings the revelation, because the messenger to all the prophets was Jibril (peace be upon him). This is consistent with the saying of Ibn Mas'ud.

فناداه جبريل وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ: This is permissible in Arabic, to report about one using a plural form, as in the saying "So-and-so rode in ships," when he rode only one ship; "he went out on postal mules," when he was on only one mule; and "I heard this news from people," when he heard it from one person. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Those to whom the people said﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:173), meaning Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud; ﴿Indeed the people have gathered against you﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:173), meaning Abu Sufyan, and similar cases of plurality.

Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama said: If the speaker is a leader, it is permissible to report about him in the plural, because his companions are with him. Since Jibril is the leader of the angels, and every time he is sent there is a group of them with him, it is on this basis.

وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ: meaning in the mosque. Its parallel is His words: ﴿So he came out to his people from the mihrab﴾ (Maryam 19:11), meaning the mosque; and His words: ﴿when they climbed over the wall into the mihrab﴾ (Sad 38:21), meaning the mosque. It is a mif'al form from harb (war). It was said that it was so named because Satan fights (yuhariba) in it, just as the racecourse (midmar) is called so because horses are trained (tudmar) in it. Ibn 'Amir inclined the alif of al-mihrab throughout the Qur'an, while the others pronounce it with full emphasis (tafkhim).

أَنَّ اللَّهَ: Ibn 'Amir, 'Isa ibn 'Amr, al-A'mash and Hamza recited it with a kasra on the alif, on the assumption of an implied verb of saying, its meaning being: "the angels called him and said: Indeed Allah..." because calling is a form of speech.

The rest recited it with a fatha, making the call govern it, as if he said: "the angels called him that Allah gives you good news."

'Abdullah recited: وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ يا زكريا إن الله يبشرك.

Al-Farra' differed concerning the future form of this verb (yubashshiru), and counted its occurrences in the Qur'an as ten: two here; in al-Tawba, يُبَشِّرُهُمْ (9:21); in Maryam; in al-Hijr, إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ (15:53); and فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ (15:54); in al-Isra' and al-Kahf, وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (2:223 and 9:112); in Maryam, two places: يا زَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ and ولِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ; and in Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf: ذلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبادَهُ (42:21, 23). These are ten places. They agreed that one of them, فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ, is doubled (shaddah); and they differed about the other nine. Hamza recited all of them with a fatha on the ba', a sukun on the ya', a damma on the shin, and lightened (without shaddah).

Yahya ibn Ri'ab and al-Kisa'i recited five of them lightened: the two here, and those in al-Isra' and al-Kahf and 'Ayn Sin Qaf.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr lightened one of them, namely in Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf: ذلِكَ النبي الَّذِي يَبْشُرُ اللَّهُ عِبادَهُ.

Humayd ibn Qays recited all of them with a damma on the ya', a sukun on the ba', a kasra on the shin, and lightened.

The rest recited with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the ba', a kasra on the shin, and doubled.

Whoever lightens the shin with a damma on the ba' is taking it from abshara yubshiru, as the poet said:

يا أمّ عمرو أبشري بالبشرى ... موت ذريع وجراد عظلي

(Al-Jarad al-'Adhla: that which does not depart. By "Umm 'Amr" he means Umm 'Amir, a euphemism for the hyena. See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/75; the verse is also in Kitab al-'Ayn: 2/85.)

Whoever recites with the shin lightened and the ba' with a fatha takes it from bashara yubshiru, which is the dialect of Tihama and the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The poet said:

نشرت عوالي إذا رأيت حيفة ... ماسك من الحجّاج تعلى كتابها

Al-Farra' said:

وإذا رأيت الباهشين إلى العلى ... غبرا أكفهم بقاع ممحل
فأعنهم وأبشر بما بشروا به ... وإذا هم نزلوا بضنك فأنزل

(Lisan al-'Arab: 4/62.)

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad related from Mu'adh al-Kufi, who said: Whoever recites يُبَشِّرُهُمْ (yubashshiruhum) doubled, it is from bushra (glad tidings); and whoever recites yubshiruhum lightened with a fatha on the ya', it is from surur (joy), gladdening them. (Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/342.) The confirmation of this reading is what Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam related from his father: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to a man: "Allah gives you good news of a boy," and his wife bore a boy.

As for whoever recites with the doubled form, from bashshara yubashshiru, meaning bashir, this is the most eloquent and the most chaste of the dialects. Jarir said:

يا بشر حق لوجهك التبشير ... هلا غضبت لنا وأنت أمير

(Sharh Shafiyat Ibn al-Hajib: 4/328.)

The proof for the doubled form is that everything in the Qur'an of this type, whether in the obligatory past or the imperative, is with the doubled form, as in His words: ﴿So give good news to My servants who...﴾ (al-Muzzammil 73:17–18); ﴿And We gave him good news of Ishaq﴾ (al-Saffat 37:112); ﴿They said, "We give you good news of the truth"﴾ (al-Hijr 15:55).

بِيَحْيى: this is a name that is not inflected (la yajri) because it is a proper name, and the extra letter at its beginning, as in yazid, ya'mur and yashkur, is the prefix. Some people inclined it because of the ya', and others emphasized it. Its plural is "Yahyun," like Musawn and 'Isawn. They differed as to why he was named "Yahya."

Ibn 'Abbas said: because Allah revived through him the barrenness of his mother's womb. Qatada said: because Allah revived his heart with faith. Some said: because Allah revived his heart with prophethood. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: because Allah revived him through obedience, so that he never disobeyed nor intended a sin.

What is related from Ibn 'Abbas: he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one who will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who has not intended a sin he has committed, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he did not intend it nor commit it."

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard the teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: he was named that because he was martyred, and the martyrs are "alive with their Lord, receiving provision" (Al 'Imran 3:169).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Among the contempt of the world before Allah is that Yahya ibn Zakariyya was killed by a woman." [51] (Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/383, no. 2502.)

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Mansur [al-Jamshadhi] say, from 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Maqdisi: Allah revealed to Ibrahim the Friend: "Say to Sarah" – and that was her name – "I will bring forth from you two a servant who will not die through My disobedience; his name is Hayy. So give him a letter from your name." She gave him the first letter of her name, and he became Yahya, and Ibrahim's wife became Sarah.

مُصَدِّقاً بِكَلِمَةٍ: accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). مِنَ اللَّهِ: meaning 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called a "word" because Allah said to him "Be" without a father, and he was. The name "word" fell upon him because he came about by it. Yahya was the first to believe in 'Isa and confirm him. Yahya was six months older than 'Isa, and they were two maternal cousins. Then Yahya was killed before 'Isa was raised (peace be upon them both).

Abu 'Ubayda and 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ means "and His signs," and one says: "recite to me the word of so-and-so," meaning his poem.

وَسَيِّداً: from the form fay'al, like sada yasudu; its origin is yasud. It is the leader who is followed and to whom one turns for his word.

Al-Mufaddal said: He meant "a master (sayyid) in religion."

Sharik, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, said: "The sayyid is one of good character."

Sharik also related with his isnad from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The sayyid is the one who obeys his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: the sayyid is the jurist, the learned. Qatada: a master in knowledge and fasting. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: the forbearing. Al-Dahhak: the pious. 'Ikrima: the one who does not become angry. Mujahid: the honored before Allah. Ibn Zayd: the noble, the great. Sufyan al-Thawri: the one who is not envied.

Yusuf ibn al-Husayn al-Razi related from Dhu'l-Nun al-Misri, who said: "The envious one is never a master."

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: one who is obeyed.

Al-Zajjaj: the one who intends good for all things, and wishes good for his peers.

Ahmad ibn 'Asim: the sayyid is the one content with what has been apportioned to him.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq: the one who is satisfied with Allah's decree.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi: the one who relies upon Allah.

Abu Zayd al-Bastami: the one whose resolve is great and whose rank is noble, who has not let his soul speak of the abode of this world. It was also said: he is the generous.

Ibn al-Zubayr related from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is your sayyid, O sons of Salama?" They said: "Jadd ibn Qays, but he is stingy and a coward." He said: "And what disease is worse than stinginess? Rather, your sayyid is 'Amr ibn Jamuh." [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/15, with variation.]

'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas related that he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when about ten men in travelling clothes came to him. They greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people, then said: "Who among you is the sayyid?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim." They recognized that he was the Messenger of Allah, and said: "Is there no sayyid in your community?" He said: "Yes, a man who has been given lawful wealth and provided with generosity, who draws near the poor and whose complaints are few." [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/197.]

It is related that Asad ibn 'Abdullah said to a man from Banu Shayban: "It has reached me that nobility (su'dud) is cheap among you." He said: "As for us, we do not make a man our sayyid unless he gives us his camel-saddle, spreads out his honor for us, and gives us his wealth." He said: "By God, nobility among you is indeed expensive."

وَحَصُوراً: its origin is from hasr, which is confinement. It is said: "I held the man back from his need" when I confined him; "I was restricted from such-and-such" when I refrained from it; "So-and-so was restricted in his recitation" when he refrained from reciting and was unable to do it; and from this is "ihsar" (siege) by the enemy. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made Jahannam a prison (hasir) for the disbelievers﴾ (al-Isra' 17:8), meaning a confinement. It is said of a man who keeps a secret and holds it back and does not divulge it: he is a hasur.

Jarir said:

ولقد تسقطني الوشاة فصادفوا ... حصرا بسرك يا أميم ضنينا

(Al-Sihah: 2/631.)

So al-hasur, according to Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Qatada, 'Ata', Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Hasan, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, is the one who does not come to women nor approach them. On this view it is a maf'ul in the sense of fa'il: he confines himself from desires.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Dahhak said: he is the impotent one who has no seed. The evidence for this interpretation is what Abu Salih related from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every son of Adam will meet Allah with a sin which he committed, and He will punish him for it or have mercy on him, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he was a sayyid and a hasur." [52]

وَنَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed with his hand toward a speck of dust from the earth, took it, and said: "His male organ was like this speck." [53] (Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/520, no. 32428; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/209.)

Al-Mubarrad said: al-hasur is one who does not take part in play, frivolity and vanities. Its origin is the Arabs' saying: "One who does not enter into gambling is a hasur." Al-Akhtal said:

وشارب مربح بالكأس نادمني ... لا بالحصور ولا فيها بسوار

(Lisan al-'Arab: 4/194.)

When the angels called Zakariyya with the good news, he said: رَبِّ, "O my lord" (sayyidi, my master), he said it to Jibril (peace be upon him). This is the view of al-Kalbi and most of the commentators.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: Zakariyya only said "O Lord" to Allah, not to Jibril.

أَنَّى يَكُونُ: from where will it be? لِي غُلامٌ: a son. وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ: Abu Hamza, al-Farra' and al-Mu'arrikh ibn al-Mufaddal said: this is an inverted (maqlub) construction: meaning "I have reached old age," just as one says "hunger has reached me," meaning "I am in hardship." He says this statement "will not cut me off," meaning it will not reach what he wants it to cut off. Al-Mufaddal recited:
