[59] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/263; Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/6; Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/384, no. 10035.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 55–64:**

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in death and raise you to Me."﴾ The commentators differ over the meaning of *tawaffi* (taking in full, causing to die, or taking up) here. Ka'b, al-Hasan, al-Kalbi, Mutarr al-Warraq [[He is Abu Bakr al-Warraq.]], Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is "I will take you (qabid)."

﴿And raise you﴾: from this world.

﴿To Me﴾: without death. This is indicated by His words, ﴿When You took me up (tawaffaytani)﴾, meaning, "You took me up to the heavens while I was alive," because his people became Christians only after his being raised, not after his death. On this view, *tawaffi* has two interpretations:

The first: "I will raise you to Me complete, so that they cannot harm you," from the expression "I took such-and-such in full (tawaffaytu kadha wa-istawfaytuhu)," meaning, I took it entire.

The second: "I will hand you over (musallimuk)," from the expression "I took my due from him (tawaffaytu minhu kadha)," meaning, I received it in full, or "I handed it over (sallamtuhu)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: its meaning is "I will put you to sleep (munimuk) and raise you to Me away from your people." This is supported by His words, ﴿It is He who takes you in death by night﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 60.]], meaning, He puts you to sleep, because sleep is the brother of death, and by His words, ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [[Surat al-Zumar: 42.]].

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "I will cause you to die," supported by His words, ﴿Say: The angel of death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [[Surat al-Sajda: 11.]], and His words, ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you (natawaffayannaka)﴾ [[Surat Yunus: 46.]]. On this view there are two interpretations:

The first is what Wahb said: Allah caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then brought him back to life and raised him.

The second is what al-Dahhak and a group of the scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: there is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the speech, and its meaning is "I will raise you to Me..."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: "and cause you to die after I bring you down from the heavens," like His words, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a term appointed﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 129.]].

A poet said:

"Oh palm tree of Dhat 'Irq, upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Meaning: "Upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Another said:

"You have combined defamation, arrogance and slander, three traits that do not befit one who should refrain."

Meaning: "You have combined arrogance, slander and defamation."

Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The prophets are half-brothers with different mothers, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will be a ruler over my community and its successor (khalifa). When you see him, recognize him: he is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair as though it were dripping though no water has touched it. He will be between two saffron-dyed garments. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizya (poll tax). He will surely go to al-Rawha, to perform Hajj or 'Umra or both together. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys all the religions in his time, and Allah will destroy in his time the false Messiah, the liar, the Dajjal. Safety will prevail on earth, so that lions graze with camels, panthers with cows, and wolves with sheep. Children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth for forty years." [56] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/242, with variations.]]

In the narration of Ka'b: "Twenty-four years. Then he will marry and have children, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him in the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ)." [57] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396, with variations.]]

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl was asked: "Do you find the descent of Jesus (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes."

His words ﴿and in maturity (kahlan)﴾: he did not reach maturity in this world; its meaning is "and in maturity after his descent from the heavens."

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim that Amir al-Mu'minin Abu Ja'far narrated to him about this verse, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can a community perish when I am at its beginning, Jesus is at its end, and the Mahdi from my family is in its middle?" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/269, no. 38682.]] [58]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Wasiti said: its meaning is "I will cause you to die to your desires and the drives of your soul," and he spoke well, because when Jesus was raised to heaven his state became like the state of the angels.

﴿And raise you to Me﴾: al-Bashali and al-Shaybani said: Jesus was on [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], then a wind blew, so Jesus (peace be upon him) hurried, and Allah raised him in his hurrying, while he wore a woolen garment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Moses wore only wool, and Jesus wore only hair until he was raised.

Ibn 'Umar said: "We saw the Prophet (ﷺ) smiling during the circumambulation, and he was asked about that. He said: 'Jesus met me during the circumambulation, accompanied by two angels.'"

It was also said: its meaning is "raising you in rank to Paradise and bringing you near to honor."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: that is, bringing you out from among them and delivering you from them.

﴿And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾: Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Islam who followed his religion and his way, from the community of Muhammad. By Allah, those who followed him in the sense of calling him "lord" did not follow him. ﴿Superior to those who disbelieve﴾: dominant, openly manifest in honor, strength, proof and argument.

al-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Aban said: it means the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) are superior to those who disbelieved. It was also said: they are the Romans.

Ibn Zayd said: "And He will make the Christians superior to the Jews." There is no land in which there are Christians but they are superior to the Jews, who are humiliated and subjugated. On these two views, "following" means claiming and loving, not following the religion and creed.

﴿Then to Me is your return﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿So I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ﴾: concerning the religion and the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him).

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾: by killing, captivity, humiliation and the jizya (poll tax); ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾: by the Fire.

﴿And they will have no helpers.﴾

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾: al-Hasan, Hafs and Yunus recited it with *ya* (yuwaffihim), and the rest with *nun* (nuwaffihim).

﴿And Allah does not love wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿That﴾: meaning, what I have mentioned.

﴿We recite it to you from the signs and the Wise Reminder.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the Qur'an."

It was also said: it is the Preserved Tablet, which is suspended from the Throne in a white pearl. "The Wise" means one who judges between truth and falsehood.

Muqatil said: "Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam..." The verse was revealed because the delegation of Najran said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you revile our companion?" He said: "What do I say?" They said: "You say he is a servant." He said: "Yes, he is a servant of Allah, His messenger, and His word that He cast to the virgin Mary." They became angry and said: "Have you ever seen a human being without a father? If you are truthful, show us the like of him!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah, in being created without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, in being created without a father or mother. He created him from dust﴾. The sentence is complete here.

﴿Then He said to him﴾: that is, to Jesus.

﴿"Be," and he was﴾: that is, so he was.

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾:

al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning "it is the truth," i.e., "this is the truth." Abu 'Ubayda said: it is a new sentence after the completion of the previous speech, and its predicate is in His words "from your Lord." It was also said: it is by supposing an implied verb, meaning "the state is the truth." If you wish, you may read it in the nominative with a *damma* and intend an inversion, its meaning being "from your Lord is the truth," as they say, "from you is your hand," even though it is a proverb.

﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾: the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is his community, because he was never forbidden about the matter of Jesus.

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾: disputes with you and debates with you, O Muhammad, concerning this matter.

﴿Concerning it﴾: concerning Jesus.

﴿After the knowledge has come to you﴾: that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger.

﴿Then say: "Come"﴾: al-Hasan, Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Abu al-Simmak al-'Adawi recited *ta'alu* with a *damma* on the *lam*, while the rest read it with a *fatha*. The original form is *ta'aliyu*, because it is *tafa'alu* from *al-'uluw* (height). The *damma* on the *ya* was heavy, so it was made quiescent, then deleted, and the *lam* remained in its place. The *damma* of the *lam* is because it transferred the vowel of the deleted *ya*, which is the final radical of the verb, to the *lam*.

al-Farra' said: the meaning of *ta'al* is as if he says, "Rise up."

﴿We will call﴾: jussive as the answer to the imperative, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the *waw*.

﴿Our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾: it was said: he meant their souls; it was said: he meant the wives.

﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾: we entreat in supplication. So said Ibn 'Abbas.

Muqatil said: we sincerely devote ourselves in supplication.

al-Kalbi said: we strive and exert ourselves in supplication. al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubayda said: we invoke a curse, saying, "May the curse of Allah be upon the liar among us." It is said: "Upon him be the curse of Allah (bahlatu Allah)," and *bahlatuhu* means "his curse."

Labid said, concerning the arrival of the chiefs:
"The age looked upon them and was struck with a curse (ibtahala)."

﴿Then let us lay the curse of Allah﴾: a verbal noun. ﴿Upon the liars﴾: among us and among you, concerning the matter of Jesus.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to the delegation of Najran and invited them to *mubahala* (mutual cursing, invocation of a curse upon the liar), they said: "Let us return and consider our affair, then we will come to you tomorrow." They withdrew among themselves, and they said to al-'Aqib, who was their man of judgment: "O 'Abd al-Masih, what do you think?" He said:

"By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you know that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the decisive word concerning your companion. By Allah, no people have ever cursed a prophet and then their elders have lived or their young have grown. If we were to do that, we would surely perish. So if you insist on keeping your religion and on remaining in what you say about your companion, then make peace with the man, and go back to your lands."

They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had gone out in the morning, embracing al-Husayn and holding the hand of al-Hasan, with Fatima walking behind him and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) behind her, and he was saying to them: "When I supplicate, say Amin."

The bishop (usquf) of Najran said: "O assembly of Christians, I see faces which, if they asked Allah to remove a mountain from its place, He would remove it. So do not invoke a curse, lest you perish and no Christian remain on the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection." They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you, and to leave you on your religion and remain on ours." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you refuse the mubahala, then embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have, and you will bear what they bear." They refused. He said: "Then I declare war upon you." They said: "We have no strength for war with the Arabs, but we will make peace with you on condition that you do not attack us, do not frighten us, and do not turn us back from our religion, on condition that we pay you every year two thousand *sikka* (coins): a thousand in Safar and a thousand in Rajab." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with them on that. And he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the punishment had already descended upon the people of Najran. Had they cursed one another, they would have been transformed into apes and swine, and the valley would have blazed with fire over them, and Allah would have uprooted Najran and its people, even the birds upon the trees, and the year would not have passed over all the Christians until they perished." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/39; al-Fusul al-Muhimma: 23–25.]]

Allah the Exalted said:

﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ ... to ﴿But if they turn away﴾: they turn away from faith.

﴿Then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters﴾: those who worship other than Allah and call people to worship other than Him.

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you"...﴾ [the verse].

The commentators said: the delegation of Najran came to Medina and met the Jews, and they disputed about Abraham. The Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and they said: "O Muhammad, we have disputed about Abraham and his religion. The Christians claim that he was a Christian, and that they are upon his religion and are the people most entitled to him. The Jews said: rather he was a Jew, and they are upon his religion and are most entitled to him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Both groups are innocent of Abraham and his religion. Rather, Abraham was a *hanif* (upright monotheist), and I am upon his religion, so follow his religion, which is Islam." The Jews said: "O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we take you as a lord, as the Christians took Jesus as a lord." The Christians said: "By Allah, O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we say about you what the Jews said about 'Uzayr."

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable (sawa') between us and you"﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it thus, and said: "He called to *al-sawa'*," meaning to the middle, and *sawa'* of everything is its middle. Allah said: ﴿So he saw him in the midst of the Hellfire (sawa' al-Jahim)﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 55.]]. The middle is called *sawa'* because the most just and the best of matters is the middle.

*Sawa'* is an attribute of *kalima* (word), except that it is a verbal noun, and verbal nouns are not dualized, pluralized, or feminized. If the *sin* is pronounced with a *fatha*, it is lengthened (sawa'), and if it is pronounced with a *kasra* or *damma*, it is shortened (sawan, sawan). Like His words: ﴿a place (makanan suwan)﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 58.]], meaning, a place level for it. Then He explained the word: ﴿That we worship none but Allah﴾. The position of *an* is in the nominative by implying "it is" (i.e., "it is that we do not worship but Allah").

al-Zajjaj said: its position is nominative, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is accusative, by removing the preposition, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is genitive, as a substitute for *kalima*, meaning "come to that we do not worship but Allah."

﴿And not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords besides Allah﴾: as the Jews and Christians did. Allah said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 31.]]. 'Ikrima said: this is the prostration of some of them to others.

It was also said: its meaning is "do not obey anyone in sin." In a report: "Whoever obeys a creature in disobedience to Allah, it is as if he prostrated to someone other than Him."

﴿And if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾: those sincere in monotheism.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote this verse to Caesar and the kings of Rome: "From Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great of ... Peace be upon him who follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you to Islam; embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of the Aryisiyyin (peasants). ﴿O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾ [the verse]." [59] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/263; Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/6; Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/384, no. 10035.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 55–64:**

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in death and raise you to Me."﴾ The commentators differ over the meaning of *tawaffi* (taking in full, causing to die, or taking up) here. Ka'b, al-Hasan, al-Kalbi, Mutarr al-Warraq [[He is Abu Bakr al-Warraq.]], Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is "I will take you (qabid)."

﴿And raise you﴾: from this world.

﴿To Me﴾: without death. This is indicated by His words, ﴿When You took me up (tawaffaytani)﴾, meaning, "You took me up to the heavens while I was alive," because his people became Christians only after his being raised, not after his death. On this view, *tawaffi* has two interpretations:

The first: "I will raise you to Me complete, so that they cannot harm you," from the expression "I took such-and-such in full (tawaffaytu kadha wa-istawfaytuhu)," meaning, I took it entire.

The second: "I will hand you over (musallimuk)," from the expression "I took my due from him (tawaffaytu minhu kadha)," meaning, I received it in full, or "I handed it over (sallamtuhu)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: its meaning is "I will put you to sleep (munimuk) and raise you to Me away from your people." This is supported by His words, ﴿It is He who takes you in death by night﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 60.]], meaning, He puts you to sleep, because sleep is the brother of death, and by His words, ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [[Surat al-Zumar: 42.]].

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "I will cause you to die," supported by His words, ﴿Say: The angel of death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [[Surat al-Sajda: 11.]], and His words, ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you (natawaffayannaka)﴾ [[Surat Yunus: 46.]]. On this view there are two interpretations:

The first is what Wahb said: Allah caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then brought him back to life and raised him.

The second is what al-Dahhak and a group of the scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: there is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the speech, and its meaning is "I will raise you to Me..."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: "and cause you to die after I bring you down from the heavens," like His words, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a term appointed﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 129.]].

A poet said:

"Oh palm tree of Dhat 'Irq, upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Meaning: "Upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Another said:

"You have combined defamation, arrogance and slander, three traits that do not befit one who should refrain."

Meaning: "You have combined arrogance, slander and defamation."

Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The prophets are half-brothers with different mothers, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will be a ruler over my community and its successor (khalifa). When you see him, recognize him: he is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair as though it were dripping though no water has touched it. He will be between two saffron-dyed garments. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizya (poll tax). He will surely go to al-Rawha, to perform Hajj or 'Umra or both together. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys all the religions in his time, and Allah will destroy in his time the false Messiah, the liar, the Dajjal. Safety will prevail on earth, so that lions graze with camels, panthers with cows, and wolves with sheep. Children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth for forty years." [56] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/242, with variations.]]

In the narration of Ka'b: "Twenty-four years. Then he will marry and have children, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him in the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ)." [57] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396, with variations.]]

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl was asked: "Do you find the descent of Jesus (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes."

His words ﴿and in maturity (kahlan)﴾: he did not reach maturity in this world; its meaning is "and in maturity after his descent from the heavens."

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim that Amir al-Mu'minin Abu Ja'far narrated to him about this verse, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can a community perish when I am at its beginning, Jesus is at its end, and the Mahdi from my family is in its middle?" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/269, no. 38682.]] [58]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Wasiti said: its meaning is "I will cause you to die to your desires and the drives of your soul," and he spoke well, because when Jesus was raised to heaven his state became like the state of the angels.

﴿And raise you to Me﴾: al-Bashali and al-Shaybani said: Jesus was on [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], then a wind blew, so Jesus (peace be upon him) hurried, and Allah raised him in his hurrying, while he wore a woolen garment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Moses wore only wool, and Jesus wore only hair until he was raised.

Ibn 'Umar said: "We saw the Prophet (ﷺ) smiling during the circumambulation, and he was asked about that. He said: 'Jesus met me during the circumambulation, accompanied by two angels.'"

It was also said: its meaning is "raising you in rank to Paradise and bringing you near to honor."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: that is, bringing you out from among them and delivering you from them.

﴿And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾: Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Islam who followed his religion and his way, from the community of Muhammad. By Allah, those who followed him in the sense of calling him "lord" did not follow him. ﴿Superior to those who disbelieve﴾: dominant, openly manifest in honor, strength, proof and argument.

al-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Aban said: it means the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) are superior to those who disbelieved. It was also said: they are the Romans.

Ibn Zayd said: "And He will make the Christians superior to the Jews." There is no land in which there are Christians but they are superior to the Jews, who are humiliated and subjugated. On these two views, "following" means claiming and loving, not following the religion and creed.

﴿Then to Me is your return﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿So I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ﴾: concerning the religion and the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him).

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾: by killing, captivity, humiliation and the jizya (poll tax); ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾: by the Fire.

﴿And they will have no helpers.﴾

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾: al-Hasan, Hafs and Yunus recited it with *ya* (yuwaffihim), and the rest with *nun* (nuwaffihim).

﴿And Allah does not love wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿That﴾: meaning, what I have mentioned.

﴿We recite it to you from the signs and the Wise Reminder.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the Qur'an."

It was also said: it is the Preserved Tablet, which is suspended from the Throne in a white pearl. "The Wise" means one who judges between truth and falsehood.

Muqatil said: "Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam..." The verse was revealed because the delegation of Najran said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you revile our companion?" He said: "What do I say?" They said: "You say he is a servant." He said: "Yes, he is a servant of Allah, His messenger, and His word that He cast to the virgin Mary." They became angry and said: "Have you ever seen a human being without a father? If you are truthful, show us the like of him!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah, in being created without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, in being created without a father or mother. He created him from dust﴾. The sentence is complete here.

﴿Then He said to him﴾: that is, to Jesus.

﴿"Be," and he was﴾: that is, so he was.

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾:

al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning "it is the truth," i.e., "this is the truth." Abu 'Ubayda said: it is a new sentence after the completion of the previous speech, and its predicate is in His words "from your Lord." It was also said: it is by supposing an implied verb, meaning "the state is the truth." If you wish, you may read it in the nominative with a *damma* and intend an inversion, its meaning being "from your Lord is the truth," as they say, "from you is your hand," even though it is a proverb.

﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾: the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is his community, because he was never forbidden about the matter of Jesus.

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾: disputes with you and debates with you, O Muhammad, concerning this matter.

﴿Concerning it﴾: concerning Jesus.

﴿After the knowledge has come to you﴾: that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger.

﴿Then say: "Come"﴾: al-Hasan, Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Abu al-Simmak al-'Adawi recited *ta'alu* with a *damma* on the *lam*, while the rest read it with a *fatha*. The original form is *ta'aliyu*, because it is *tafa'alu* from *al-'uluw* (height). The *damma* on the *ya* was heavy, so it was made quiescent, then deleted, and the *lam* remained in its place. The *damma* of the *lam* is because it transferred the vowel of the deleted *ya*, which is the final radical of the verb, to the *lam*.

al-Farra' said: the meaning of *ta'al* is as if he says, "Rise up."

﴿We will call﴾: jussive as the answer to the imperative, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the *waw*.

﴿Our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾: it was said: he meant their souls; it was said: he meant the wives.

﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾: we entreat in supplication. So said Ibn 'Abbas.

Muqatil said: we sincerely devote ourselves in supplication.

al-Kalbi said: we strive and exert ourselves in supplication. al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubayda said: we invoke a curse, saying, "May the curse of Allah be upon the liar among us." It is said: "Upon him be the curse of Allah (bahlatu Allah)," and *bahlatuhu* means "his curse."

Labid said, concerning the arrival of the chiefs:
"The age looked upon them and was struck with a curse (ibtahala)."

﴿Then let us lay the curse of Allah﴾: a verbal noun. ﴿Upon the liars﴾: among us and among you, concerning the matter of Jesus.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to the delegation of Najran and invited them to *mubahala* (mutual cursing, invocation of a curse upon the liar), they said: "Let us return and consider our affair, then we will come to you tomorrow." They withdrew among themselves, and they said to al-'Aqib, who was their man of judgment: "O 'Abd al-Masih, what do you think?" He said:

"By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you know that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the decisive word concerning your companion. By Allah, no people have ever cursed a prophet and then their elders have lived or their young have grown. If we were to do that, we would surely perish. So if you insist on keeping your religion and on remaining in what you say about your companion, then make peace with the man, and go back to your lands."

They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had gone out in the morning, embracing al-Husayn and holding the hand of al-Hasan, with Fatima walking behind him and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) behind her, and he was saying to them: "When I supplicate, say Amin."

The bishop (usquf) of Najran said: "O assembly of Christians, I see faces which, if they asked Allah to remove a mountain from its place, He would remove it. So do not invoke a curse, lest you perish and no Christian remain on the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection." They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you, and to leave you on your religion and remain on ours." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you refuse the mubahala, then embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have, and you will bear what they bear." They refused. He said: "Then I declare war upon you." They said: "We have no strength for war with the Arabs, but we will make peace with you on condition that you do not attack us, do not frighten us, and do not turn us back from our religion, on condition that we pay you every year two thousand *sikka* (coins): a thousand in Safar and a thousand in Rajab." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with them on that. And he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the punishment had already descended upon the people of Najran. Had they cursed one another, they would have been transformed into apes and swine, and the valley would have blazed with fire over them, and Allah would have uprooted Najran and its people, even the birds upon the trees, and the year would not have passed over all the Christians until they perished." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/39; al-Fusul al-Muhimma: 23–25.]]

Allah the Exalted said:

﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ ... to ﴿But if they turn away﴾: they turn away from faith.

﴿Then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters﴾: those who worship other than Allah and call people to worship other than Him.

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you"...﴾ [the verse].

The commentators said: the delegation of Najran came to Medina and met the Jews, and they disputed about Abraham. The Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and they said: "O Muhammad, we have disputed about Abraham and his religion. The Christians claim that he was a Christian, and that they are upon his religion and are the people most entitled to him. The Jews said: rather he was a Jew, and they are upon his religion and are most entitled to him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Both groups are innocent of Abraham and his religion. Rather, Abraham was a *hanif* (upright monotheist), and I am upon his religion, so follow his religion, which is Islam." The Jews said: "O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we take you as a lord, as the Christians took Jesus as a lord." The Christians said: "By Allah, O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we say about you what the Jews said about 'Uzayr."

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable (sawa') between us and you"﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it thus, and said: "He called to *al-sawa'*," meaning to the middle, and *sawa'* of everything is its middle. Allah said: ﴿So he saw him in the midst of the Hellfire (sawa' al-Jahim)﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 55.]]. The middle is called *sawa'* because the most just and the best of matters is the middle.

*Sawa'* is an attribute of *kalima* (word), except that it is a verbal noun, and verbal nouns are not dualized, pluralized, or feminized. If the *sin* is pronounced with a *fatha*, it is lengthened (sawa'), and if it is pronounced with a *kasra* or *damma*, it is shortened (sawan, sawan). Like His words: ﴿a place (makanan suwan)﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 58.]], meaning, a place level for it. Then He explained the word: ﴿That we worship none but Allah﴾. The position of *an* is in the nominative by implying "it is" (i.e., "it is that we do not worship but Allah").

al-Zajjaj said: its position is nominative, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is accusative, by removing the preposition, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is genitive, as a substitute for *kalima*, meaning "come to that we do not worship but Allah."

﴿And not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords besides Allah﴾: as the Jews and Christians did. Allah said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 31.]]. 'Ikrima said: this is the prostration of some of them to others.

It was also said: its meaning is "do not obey anyone in sin." In a report: "Whoever obeys a creature in disobedience to Allah, it is as if he prostrated to someone other than Him."

﴿And if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾: those sincere in monotheism.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote this verse to Caesar and the kings of Rome: "From Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great of ... Peace be upon him who follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you to Islam; embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of the Aryisiyyin (peasants). ﴿O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾ [the verse]." [59] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/263; Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/6; Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/384, no. 10035.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 55–64:**

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in death and raise you to Me."﴾ The commentators differ over the meaning of *tawaffi* (taking in full, causing to die, or taking up) here. Ka'b, al-Hasan, al-Kalbi, Mutarr al-Warraq [[He is Abu Bakr al-Warraq.]], Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is "I will take you (qabid)."

﴿And raise you﴾: from this world.

﴿To Me﴾: without death. This is indicated by His words, ﴿When You took me up (tawaffaytani)﴾, meaning, "You took me up to the heavens while I was alive," because his people became Christians only after his being raised, not after his death. On this view, *tawaffi* has two interpretations:

The first: "I will raise you to Me complete, so that they cannot harm you," from the expression "I took such-and-such in full (tawaffaytu kadha wa-istawfaytuhu)," meaning, I took it entire.

The second: "I will hand you over (musallimuk)," from the expression "I took my due from him (tawaffaytu minhu kadha)," meaning, I received it in full, or "I handed it over (sallamtuhu)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: its meaning is "I will put you to sleep (munimuk) and raise you to Me away from your people." This is supported by His words, ﴿It is He who takes you in death by night﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 60.]], meaning, He puts you to sleep, because sleep is the brother of death, and by His words, ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [[Surat al-Zumar: 42.]].

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "I will cause you to die," supported by His words, ﴿Say: The angel of death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [[Surat al-Sajda: 11.]], and His words, ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you (natawaffayannaka)﴾ [[Surat Yunus: 46.]]. On this view there are two interpretations:

The first is what Wahb said: Allah caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then brought him back to life and raised him.

The second is what al-Dahhak and a group of the scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: there is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the speech, and its meaning is "I will raise you to Me..."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: "and cause you to die after I bring you down from the heavens," like His words, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a term appointed﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 129.]].

A poet said:

"Oh palm tree of Dhat 'Irq, upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Meaning: "Upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Another said:

"You have combined defamation, arrogance and slander, three traits that do not befit one who should refrain."

Meaning: "You have combined arrogance, slander and defamation."

Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The prophets are half-brothers with different mothers, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will be a ruler over my community and its successor (khalifa). When you see him, recognize him: he is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair as though it were dripping though no water has touched it. He will be between two saffron-dyed garments. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizya (poll tax). He will surely go to al-Rawha, to perform Hajj or 'Umra or both together. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys all the religions in his time, and Allah will destroy in his time the false Messiah, the liar, the Dajjal. Safety will prevail on earth, so that lions graze with camels, panthers with cows, and wolves with sheep. Children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth for forty years." [56] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/242, with variations.]]

In the narration of Ka'b: "Twenty-four years. Then he will marry and have children, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him in the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ)." [57] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396, with variations.]]

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl was asked: "Do you find the descent of Jesus (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes."

His words ﴿and in maturity (kahlan)﴾: he did not reach maturity in this world; its meaning is "and in maturity after his descent from the heavens."

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim that Amir al-Mu'minin Abu Ja'far narrated to him about this verse, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can a community perish when I am at its beginning, Jesus is at its end, and the Mahdi from my family is in its middle?" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/269, no. 38682.]] [58]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Wasiti said: its meaning is "I will cause you to die to your desires and the drives of your soul," and he spoke well, because when Jesus was raised to heaven his state became like the state of the angels.

﴿And raise you to Me﴾: al-Bashali and al-Shaybani said: Jesus was on [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], then a wind blew, so Jesus (peace be upon him) hurried, and Allah raised him in his hurrying, while he wore a woolen garment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Moses wore only wool, and Jesus wore only hair until he was raised.

Ibn 'Umar said: "We saw the Prophet (ﷺ) smiling during the circumambulation, and he was asked about that. He said: 'Jesus met me during the circumambulation, accompanied by two angels.'"

It was also said: its meaning is "raising you in rank to Paradise and bringing you near to honor."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: that is, bringing you out from among them and delivering you from them.

﴿And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾: Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Islam who followed his religion and his way, from the community of Muhammad. By Allah, those who followed him in the sense of calling him "lord" did not follow him. ﴿Superior to those who disbelieve﴾: dominant, openly manifest in honor, strength, proof and argument.

al-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Aban said: it means the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) are superior to those who disbelieved. It was also said: they are the Romans.

Ibn Zayd said: "And He will make the Christians superior to the Jews." There is no land in which there are Christians but they are superior to the Jews, who are humiliated and subjugated. On these two views, "following" means claiming and loving, not following the religion and creed.

﴿Then to Me is your return﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿So I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ﴾: concerning the religion and the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him).

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾: by killing, captivity, humiliation and the jizya (poll tax); ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾: by the Fire.

﴿And they will have no helpers.﴾

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾: al-Hasan, Hafs and Yunus recited it with *ya* (yuwaffihim), and the rest with *nun* (nuwaffihim).

﴿And Allah does not love wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿That﴾: meaning, what I have mentioned.

﴿We recite it to you from the signs and the Wise Reminder.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the Qur'an."

It was also said: it is the Preserved Tablet, which is suspended from the Throne in a white pearl. "The Wise" means one who judges between truth and falsehood.

Muqatil said: "Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam..." The verse was revealed because the delegation of Najran said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you revile our companion?" He said: "What do I say?" They said: "You say he is a servant." He said: "Yes, he is a servant of Allah, His messenger, and His word that He cast to the virgin Mary." They became angry and said: "Have you ever seen a human being without a father? If you are truthful, show us the like of him!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah, in being created without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, in being created without a father or mother. He created him from dust﴾. The sentence is complete here.

﴿Then He said to him﴾: that is, to Jesus.

﴿"Be," and he was﴾: that is, so he was.

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾:

al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning "it is the truth," i.e., "this is the truth." Abu 'Ubayda said: it is a new sentence after the completion of the previous speech, and its predicate is in His words "from your Lord." It was also said: it is by supposing an implied verb, meaning "the state is the truth." If you wish, you may read it in the nominative with a *damma* and intend an inversion, its meaning being "from your Lord is the truth," as they say, "from you is your hand," even though it is a proverb.

﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾: the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is his community, because he was never forbidden about the matter of Jesus.

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾: disputes with you and debates with you, O Muhammad, concerning this matter.

﴿Concerning it﴾: concerning Jesus.

﴿After the knowledge has come to you﴾: that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger.

﴿Then say: "Come"﴾: al-Hasan, Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Abu al-Simmak al-'Adawi recited *ta'alu* with a *damma* on the *lam*, while the rest read it with a *fatha*. The original form is *ta'aliyu*, because it is *tafa'alu* from *al-'uluw* (height). The *damma* on the *ya* was heavy, so it was made quiescent, then deleted, and the *lam* remained in its place. The *damma* of the *lam* is because it transferred the vowel of the deleted *ya*, which is the final radical of the verb, to the *lam*.

al-Farra' said: the meaning of *ta'al* is as if he says, "Rise up."

﴿We will call﴾: jussive as the answer to the imperative, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the *waw*.

﴿Our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾: it was said: he meant their souls; it was said: he meant the wives.

﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾: we entreat in supplication. So said Ibn 'Abbas.

Muqatil said: we sincerely devote ourselves in supplication.

al-Kalbi said: we strive and exert ourselves in supplication. al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubayda said: we invoke a curse, saying, "May the curse of Allah be upon the liar among us." It is said: "Upon him be the curse of Allah (bahlatu Allah)," and *bahlatuhu* means "his curse."

Labid said, concerning the arrival of the chiefs:
"The age looked upon them and was struck with a curse (ibtahala)."

﴿Then let us lay the curse of Allah﴾: a verbal noun. ﴿Upon the liars﴾: among us and among you, concerning the matter of Jesus.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to the delegation of Najran and invited them to *mubahala* (mutual cursing, invocation of a curse upon the liar), they said: "Let us return and consider our affair, then we will come to you tomorrow." They withdrew among themselves, and they said to al-'Aqib, who was their man of judgment: "O 'Abd al-Masih, what do you think?" He said:

"By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you know that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the decisive word concerning your companion. By Allah, no people have ever cursed a prophet and then their elders have lived or their young have grown. If we were to do that, we would surely perish. So if you insist on keeping your religion and on remaining in what you say about your companion, then make peace with the man, and go back to your lands."

They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had gone out in the morning, embracing al-Husayn and holding the hand of al-Hasan, with Fatima walking behind him and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) behind her, and he was saying to them: "When I supplicate, say Amin."

The bishop (usquf) of Najran said: "O assembly of Christians, I see faces which, if they asked Allah to remove a mountain from its place, He would remove it. So do not invoke a curse, lest you perish and no Christian remain on the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection." They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you, and to leave you on your religion and remain on ours." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you refuse the mubahala, then embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have, and you will bear what they bear." They refused. He said: "Then I declare war upon you." They said: "We have no strength for war with the Arabs, but we will make peace with you on condition that you do not attack us, do not frighten us, and do not turn us back from our religion, on condition that we pay you every year two thousand *sikka* (coins): a thousand in Safar and a thousand in Rajab." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with them on that. And he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the punishment had already descended upon the people of Najran. Had they cursed one another, they would have been transformed into apes and swine, and the valley would have blazed with fire over them, and Allah would have uprooted Najran and its people, even the birds upon the trees, and the year would not have passed over all the Christians until they perished." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/39; al-Fusul al-Muhimma: 23–25.]]

Allah the Exalted said:

﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ ... to ﴿But if they turn away﴾: they turn away from faith.

﴿Then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters﴾: those who worship other than Allah and call people to worship other than Him.

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you"...﴾ [the verse].

The commentators said: the delegation of Najran came to Medina and met the Jews, and they disputed about Abraham. The Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and they said: "O Muhammad, we have disputed about Abraham and his religion. The Christians claim that he was a Christian, and that they are upon his religion and are the people most entitled to him. The Jews said: rather he was a Jew, and they are upon his religion and are most entitled to him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Both groups are innocent of Abraham and his religion. Rather, Abraham was a *hanif* (upright monotheist), and I am upon his religion, so follow his religion, which is Islam." The Jews said: "O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we take you as a lord, as the Christians took Jesus as a lord." The Christians said: "By Allah, O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we say about you what the Jews said about 'Uzayr."

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable (sawa') between us and you"﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it thus, and said: "He called to *al-sawa'*," meaning to the middle, and *sawa'* of everything is its middle. Allah said: ﴿So he saw him in the midst of the Hellfire (sawa' al-Jahim)﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 55.]]. The middle is called *sawa'* because the most just and the best of matters is the middle.

*Sawa'* is an attribute of *kalima* (word), except that it is a verbal noun, and verbal nouns are not dualized, pluralized, or feminized. If the *sin* is pronounced with a *fatha*, it is lengthened (sawa'), and if it is pronounced with a *kasra* or *damma*, it is shortened (sawan, sawan). Like His words: ﴿a place (makanan suwan)﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 58.]], meaning, a place level for it. Then He explained the word: ﴿That we worship none but Allah﴾. The position of *an* is in the nominative by implying "it is" (i.e., "it is that we do not worship but Allah").

al-Zajjaj said: its position is nominative, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is accusative, by removing the preposition, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is genitive, as a substitute for *kalima*, meaning "come to that we do not worship but Allah."

﴿And not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords besides Allah﴾: as the Jews and Christians did. Allah said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 31.]]. 'Ikrima said: this is the prostration of some of them to others.

It was also said: its meaning is "do not obey anyone in sin." In a report: "Whoever obeys a creature in disobedience to Allah, it is as if he prostrated to someone other than Him."

﴿And if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾: those sincere in monotheism.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote this verse to Caesar and the kings of Rome: "From Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great of ... Peace be upon him who follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you to Islam; embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of the Aryisiyyin (peasants). ﴿O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾ [the verse]." [59] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/263; Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/6; Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/384, no. 10035.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 55–64:**

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in death and raise you to Me."﴾ The commentators differ over the meaning of *tawaffi* (taking in full, causing to die, or taking up) here. Ka'b, al-Hasan, al-Kalbi, Mutarr al-Warraq [[He is Abu Bakr al-Warraq.]], Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is "I will take you (qabid)."

﴿And raise you﴾: from this world.

﴿To Me﴾: without death. This is indicated by His words, ﴿When You took me up (tawaffaytani)﴾, meaning, "You took me up to the heavens while I was alive," because his people became Christians only after his being raised, not after his death. On this view, *tawaffi* has two interpretations:

The first: "I will raise you to Me complete, so that they cannot harm you," from the expression "I took such-and-such in full (tawaffaytu kadha wa-istawfaytuhu)," meaning, I took it entire.

The second: "I will hand you over (musallimuk)," from the expression "I took my due from him (tawaffaytu minhu kadha)," meaning, I received it in full, or "I handed it over (sallamtuhu)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: its meaning is "I will put you to sleep (munimuk) and raise you to Me away from your people." This is supported by His words, ﴿It is He who takes you in death by night﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 60.]], meaning, He puts you to sleep, because sleep is the brother of death, and by His words, ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [[Surat al-Zumar: 42.]].

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "I will cause you to die," supported by His words, ﴿Say: The angel of death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [[Surat al-Sajda: 11.]], and His words, ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you (natawaffayannaka)﴾ [[Surat Yunus: 46.]]. On this view there are two interpretations:

The first is what Wahb said: Allah caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then brought him back to life and raised him.

The second is what al-Dahhak and a group of the scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: there is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the speech, and its meaning is "I will raise you to Me..."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: "and cause you to die after I bring you down from the heavens," like His words, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a term appointed﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 129.]].

A poet said:

"Oh palm tree of Dhat 'Irq, upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Meaning: "Upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Another said:

"You have combined defamation, arrogance and slander, three traits that do not befit one who should refrain."

Meaning: "You have combined arrogance, slander and defamation."

Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The prophets are half-brothers with different mothers, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will be a ruler over my community and its successor (khalifa). When you see him, recognize him: he is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair as though it were dripping though no water has touched it. He will be between two saffron-dyed garments. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizya (poll tax). He will surely go to al-Rawha, to perform Hajj or 'Umra or both together. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys all the religions in his time, and Allah will destroy in his time the false Messiah, the liar, the Dajjal. Safety will prevail on earth, so that lions graze with camels, panthers with cows, and wolves with sheep. Children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth for forty years." [56] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/242, with variations.]]

In the narration of Ka'b: "Twenty-four years. Then he will marry and have children, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him in the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ)." [57] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396, with variations.]]

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl was asked: "Do you find the descent of Jesus (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes."

His words ﴿and in maturity (kahlan)﴾: he did not reach maturity in this world; its meaning is "and in maturity after his descent from the heavens."

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim that Amir al-Mu'minin Abu Ja'far narrated to him about this verse, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can a community perish when I am at its beginning, Jesus is at its end, and the Mahdi from my family is in its middle?" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/269, no. 38682.]] [58]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Wasiti said: its meaning is "I will cause you to die to your desires and the drives of your soul," and he spoke well, because when Jesus was raised to heaven his state became like the state of the angels.

﴿And raise you to Me﴾: al-Bashali and al-Shaybani said: Jesus was on [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], then a wind blew, so Jesus (peace be upon him) hurried, and Allah raised him in his hurrying, while he wore a woolen garment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Moses wore only wool, and Jesus wore only hair until he was raised.

Ibn 'Umar said: "We saw the Prophet (ﷺ) smiling during the circumambulation, and he was asked about that. He said: 'Jesus met me during the circumambulation, accompanied by two angels.'"

It was also said: its meaning is "raising you in rank to Paradise and bringing you near to honor."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: that is, bringing you out from among them and delivering you from them.

﴿And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾: Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Islam who followed his religion and his way, from the community of Muhammad. By Allah, those who followed him in the sense of calling him "lord" did not follow him. ﴿Superior to those who disbelieve﴾: dominant, openly manifest in honor, strength, proof and argument.

al-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Aban said: it means the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) are superior to those who disbelieved. It was also said: they are the Romans.

Ibn Zayd said: "And He will make the Christians superior to the Jews." There is no land in which there are Christians but they are superior to the Jews, who are humiliated and subjugated. On these two views, "following" means claiming and loving, not following the religion and creed.

﴿Then to Me is your return﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿So I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ﴾: concerning the religion and the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him).

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾: by killing, captivity, humiliation and the jizya (poll tax); ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾: by the Fire.

﴿And they will have no helpers.﴾

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾: al-Hasan, Hafs and Yunus recited it with *ya* (yuwaffihim), and the rest with *nun* (nuwaffihim).

﴿And Allah does not love wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿That﴾: meaning, what I have mentioned.

﴿We recite it to you from the signs and the Wise Reminder.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the Qur'an."

It was also said: it is the Preserved Tablet, which is suspended from the Throne in a white pearl. "The Wise" means one who judges between truth and falsehood.

Muqatil said: "Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam..." The verse was revealed because the delegation of Najran said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you revile our companion?" He said: "What do I say?" They said: "You say he is a servant." He said: "Yes, he is a servant of Allah, His messenger, and His word that He cast to the virgin Mary." They became angry and said: "Have you ever seen a human being without a father? If you are truthful, show us the like of him!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah, in being created without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, in being created without a father or mother. He created him from dust﴾. The sentence is complete here.

﴿Then He said to him﴾: that is, to Jesus.

﴿"Be," and he was﴾: that is, so he was.

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾:

al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning "it is the truth," i.e., "this is the truth." Abu 'Ubayda said: it is a new sentence after the completion of the previous speech, and its predicate is in His words "from your Lord." It was also said: it is by supposing an implied verb, meaning "the state is the truth." If you wish, you may read it in the nominative with a *damma* and intend an inversion, its meaning being "from your Lord is the truth," as they say, "from you is your hand," even though it is a proverb.

﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾: the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is his community, because he was never forbidden about the matter of Jesus.

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾: disputes with you and debates with you, O Muhammad, concerning this matter.

﴿Concerning it﴾: concerning Jesus.

﴿After the knowledge has come to you﴾: that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger.

﴿Then say: "Come"﴾: al-Hasan, Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Abu al-Simmak al-'Adawi recited *ta'alu* with a *damma* on the *lam*, while the rest read it with a *fatha*. The original form is *ta'aliyu*, because it is *tafa'alu* from *al-'uluw* (height). The *damma* on the *ya* was heavy, so it was made quiescent, then deleted, and the *lam* remained in its place. The *damma* of the *lam* is because it transferred the vowel of the deleted *ya*, which is the final radical of the verb, to the *lam*.

al-Farra' said: the meaning of *ta'al* is as if he says, "Rise up."

﴿We will call﴾: jussive as the answer to the imperative, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the *waw*.

﴿Our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾: it was said: he meant their souls; it was said: he meant the wives.

﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾: we entreat in supplication. So said Ibn 'Abbas.

Muqatil said: we sincerely devote ourselves in supplication.

al-Kalbi said: we strive and exert ourselves in supplication. al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubayda said: we invoke a curse, saying, "May the curse of Allah be upon the liar among us." It is said: "Upon him be the curse of Allah (bahlatu Allah)," and *bahlatuhu* means "his curse."

Labid said, concerning the arrival of the chiefs:
"The age looked upon them and was struck with a curse (ibtahala)."

﴿Then let us lay the curse of Allah﴾: a verbal noun. ﴿Upon the liars﴾: among us and among you, concerning the matter of Jesus.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to the delegation of Najran and invited them to *mubahala* (mutual cursing, invocation of a curse upon the liar), they said: "Let us return and consider our affair, then we will come to you tomorrow." They withdrew among themselves, and they said to al-'Aqib, who was their man of judgment: "O 'Abd al-Masih, what do you think?" He said:

"By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you know that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the decisive word concerning your companion. By Allah, no people have ever cursed a prophet and then their elders have lived or their young have grown. If we were to do that, we would surely perish. So if you insist on keeping your religion and on remaining in what you say about your companion, then make peace with the man, and go back to your lands."

They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had gone out in the morning, embracing al-Husayn and holding the hand of al-Hasan, with Fatima walking behind him and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) behind her, and he was saying to them: "When I supplicate, say Amin."

The bishop (usquf) of Najran said: "O assembly of Christians, I see faces which, if they asked Allah to remove a mountain from its place, He would remove it. So do not invoke a curse, lest you perish and no Christian remain on the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection." They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you, and to leave you on your religion and remain on ours." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you refuse the mubahala, then embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have, and you will bear what they bear." They refused. He said: "Then I declare war upon you." They said: "We have no strength for war with the Arabs, but we will make peace with you on condition that you do not attack us, do not frighten us, and do not turn us back from our religion, on condition that we pay you every year two thousand *sikka* (coins): a thousand in Safar and a thousand in Rajab." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with them on that. And he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the punishment had already descended upon the people of Najran. Had they cursed one another, they would have been transformed into apes and swine, and the valley would have blazed with fire over them, and Allah would have uprooted Najran and its people, even the birds upon the trees, and the year would not have passed over all the Christians until they perished." [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/39; al-Fusul al-Muhimma: 23–25.]]

Allah the Exalted said:

﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ ... to ﴿But if they turn away﴾: they turn away from faith.

﴿Then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters﴾: those who worship other than Allah and call people to worship other than Him.

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you"...﴾ [the verse].

The commentators said: the delegation of Najran came to Medina and met the Jews, and they disputed about Abraham. The Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and they said: "O Muhammad, we have disputed about Abraham and his religion. The Christians claim that he was a Christian, and that they are upon his religion and are the people most entitled to him. The Jews said: rather he was a Jew, and they are upon his religion and are most entitled to him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Both groups are innocent of Abraham and his religion. Rather, Abraham was a *hanif* (upright monotheist), and I am upon his religion, so follow his religion, which is Islam." The Jews said: "O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we take you as a lord, as the Christians took Jesus as a lord." The Christians said: "By Allah, O Muhammad, you want nothing but that we say about you what the Jews said about 'Uzayr."

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable (sawa') between us and you"﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it thus, and said: "He called to *al-sawa'*," meaning to the middle, and *sawa'* of everything is its middle. Allah said: ﴿So he saw him in the midst of the Hellfire (sawa' al-Jahim)﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 55.]]. The middle is called *sawa'* because the most just and the best of matters is the middle.

*Sawa'* is an attribute of *kalima* (word), except that it is a verbal noun, and verbal nouns are not dualized, pluralized, or feminized. If the *sin* is pronounced with a *fatha*, it is lengthened (sawa'), and if it is pronounced with a *kasra* or *damma*, it is shortened (sawan, sawan). Like His words: ﴿a place (makanan suwan)﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 58.]], meaning, a place level for it. Then He explained the word: ﴿That we worship none but Allah﴾. The position of *an* is in the nominative by implying "it is" (i.e., "it is that we do not worship but Allah").

al-Zajjaj said: its position is nominative, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is accusative, by removing the preposition, meaning "that we do not worship but Allah." It was also said: its position is genitive, as a substitute for *kalima*, meaning "come to that we do not worship but Allah."

﴿And not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords besides Allah﴾: as the Jews and Christians did. Allah said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 31.]]. 'Ikrima said: this is the prostration of some of them to others.

It was also said: its meaning is "do not obey anyone in sin." In a report: "Whoever obeys a creature in disobedience to Allah, it is as if he prostrated to someone other than Him."

﴿And if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾: those sincere in monotheism.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote this verse to Caesar and the kings of Rome: "From Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great of ... Peace be upon him who follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you to Islam; embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of the Aryisiyyin (peasants). ﴿O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾ [the verse]." [59] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/263; Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/6; Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/384, no. 10035.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 55–64:**

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you in death and raise you to Me."﴾ The commentators differ over the meaning of *tawaffi* (taking in full, causing to die, or taking up) here. Ka'b, al-Hasan, al-Kalbi, Mutarr al-Warraq [[He is Abu Bakr al-Warraq.]], Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is "I will take you (qabid)."

﴿And raise you﴾: from this world.

﴿To Me﴾: without death. This is indicated by His words, ﴿When You took me up (tawaffaytani)﴾, meaning, "You took me up to the heavens while I was alive," because his people became Christians only after his being raised, not after his death. On this view, *tawaffi* has two interpretations:

The first: "I will raise you to Me complete, so that they cannot harm you," from the expression "I took such-and-such in full (tawaffaytu kadha wa-istawfaytuhu)," meaning, I took it entire.

The second: "I will hand you over (musallimuk)," from the expression "I took my due from him (tawaffaytu minhu kadha)," meaning, I received it in full, or "I handed it over (sallamtuhu)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: its meaning is "I will put you to sleep (munimuk) and raise you to Me away from your people." This is supported by His words, ﴿It is He who takes you in death by night﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 60.]], meaning, He puts you to sleep, because sleep is the brother of death, and by His words, ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [[Surat al-Zumar: 42.]].

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "I will cause you to die," supported by His words, ﴿Say: The angel of death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [[Surat al-Sajda: 11.]], and His words, ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you (natawaffayannaka)﴾ [[Surat Yunus: 46.]]. On this view there are two interpretations:

The first is what Wahb said: Allah caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then brought him back to life and raised him.

The second is what al-Dahhak and a group of the scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: there is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the speech, and its meaning is "I will raise you to Me..."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: "and cause you to die after I bring you down from the heavens," like His words, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a term appointed﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 129.]].

A poet said:

"Oh palm tree of Dhat 'Irq, upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Meaning: "Upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Another said:

"You have combined defamation, arrogance and slander, three traits that do not befit one who should refrain."

Meaning: "You have combined arrogance, slander and defamation."

Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The prophets are half-brothers with different mothers, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will be a ruler over my community and its successor (khalifa). When you see him, recognize him: he is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair as though it were dripping though no water has touched it. He will be between two saffron-dyed garments. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizya (poll tax). He will surely go to al-Rawha, to perform Hajj or 'Umra or both together. He will fight people for Islam until Allah destroys all the religions in his time, and Allah will destroy in his time the false Messiah, the liar, the Dajjal. Safety will prevail on earth, so that lions graze with camels, panthers with cows, and wolves with sheep. Children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth for forty years." [56] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/242, with variations.]]

In the narration of Ka'b: "Twenty-four years. Then he will marry and have children, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him in the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ)." [57] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/396, with variations.]]

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl was asked: "Do you find the descent of Jesus (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes."

His words ﴿and in maturity (kahlan)﴾: he did not reach maturity in this world; its meaning is "and in maturity after his descent from the heavens."

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim that Amir al-Mu'minin Abu Ja'far narrated to him about this verse, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can a community perish when I am at its beginning, Jesus is at its end, and the Mahdi from my family is in its middle?" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/269, no. 38682.]] [58]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Wasiti said: its meaning is "I will cause you to die to your desires and the drives of your soul," and he spoke well, because when Jesus was raised to heaven his state became like the state of the angels.

﴿And raise you to Me﴾: al-Bashali and al-Shaybani said: Jesus was on [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], then a wind blew, so Jesus (peace be upon him) hurried, and Allah raised him in his hurrying, while he wore a woolen garment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Moses wore only wool, and Jesus wore only hair until he was raised.

Ibn 'Umar said: "We saw the Prophet (ﷺ) smiling during the circumambulation, and he was asked about that. He said: 'Jesus met me during the circumambulation, accompanied by two angels.'"

It was also said: its meaning is "raising you in rank to Paradise and bringing you near to honor."

﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾: that is, bringing you out from among them and delivering you from them.

﴿And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾: Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Islam who followed his religion and his way, from the community of Muhammad. By Allah, those who followed him in the sense of calling him "lord" did not follow him. ﴿Superior to those who disbelieve﴾: dominant, openly manifest in honor, strength, proof and argument.

al-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Aban said: it means the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) are superior to those who disbelieved. It was also said: they are the Romans.

Ibn Zayd said: "And He will make the Christians superior to the Jews." There is no land in which there are Christians but they are superior to the Jews, who are humiliated and subjugated. On these two views, "following" means claiming and loving, not following the religion and creed.

﴿Then to Me is your return﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿So I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ﴾: concerning the religion and the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him).

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾: by killing, captivity, humiliation and the jizya (poll tax); ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾: by the Fire.

﴿And they will have no helpers.﴾

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾: al-Hasan, Hafs and Yunus recited it with *ya* (yuwaffihim), and the rest with *nun* (nuwaffihim).

﴿And Allah does not love wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿That﴾: meaning, what I have mentioned.

﴿We recite it to you from the signs and the Wise Reminder.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the Qur'an."

It was also said: it is the Preserved Tablet, which is suspended from the Throne in a white pearl. "The Wise" means one who judges between truth and falsehood.

Muqatil said: "Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam..." He said: "Yes, he is a servant of Allah, His messenger, and His word that He cast to the virgin Mary." They became angry and said: "Have you ever seen a human being without a father? If you are truthful, show us the like of him!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah, in being created without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, in being created without a father or mother. He created him from dust﴾. The sentence is complete here.

﴿Then He said to him﴾: that is, to Jesus.

﴿"Be," and he was﴾: that is, so he was.

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾:

al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning "it is the truth," i.e., "this is the truth." ﴿Concerning it﴾: concerning Jesus.

﴿After the knowledge has come to you﴾: that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger.

﴿Then say: "Come"﴾: al-Hasan, Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Abu al-Simmak al-'Adawi recited *ta'alu* with a *damma* on the *lam*, while the rest read it with a *fatha*. al-Farra' said: the meaning of *ta'al* is as if he says, "Rise up."

﴿Our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾: it was said: he meant their souls; it was said: he meant the wives.

﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾: we entreat in supplication. So said Ibn 'Abbas.

Muqatil said: we sincerely devote ourselves in supplication.

al-Kalbi said: we strive and exert ourselves in supplication. al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubayda said: we invoke a curse, saying, "May the curse of Allah be upon the liar among us." It is said: "Upon him be the curse of Allah (bahlatu Allah)," and *bahlatuhu* means "his curse."

"The age looked upon them and was struck with a curse (ibtahala)."

﴿Then let us lay the curse of Allah﴾: a verbal noun. ﴿Upon the liars﴾: among us and among you, concerning the matter of Jesus.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to the delegation of Najran and invited them to *mubahala* (mutual cursing, invocation of a curse upon the liar), they said: "Let us return and consider our affair, then we will come to you tomorrow."
