﴿And if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾: those sincere in monotheism.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote this verse to Caesar and the kings of Rome: "From Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great of ... Peace be upon him who follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you to Islam; embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of the Aryisiyyin (peasants). ﴿O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾ [the verse]." [59] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/263; Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/6; Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/384, no. 10035.]]

O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when you claim that he was upon your religion, Judaism and Christianity, while Judaism came into being after the revelation of the Torah and Christianity after the revelation of the Gospel?

﴿And the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him.﴾ That is, after the death of Abraham by a long time. There were a thousand years between Abraham and Moses, and two thousand years between Moses and Jesus.

﴿Will you not reason?﴾ That is, by presenting your argument and the falsehood of your claim.

﴿Ha antum﴾ (lo, you are): Ahl al-Madinah recited it without hamzah and without a prolonged vowel, except for the length needed for the silent alif. Ahl Makkah recited it with a hamzah and a short vowel, on the pattern of ﴿ha'antum﴾. Ahl al-Kufah recited it with both the prolongation (madd) and the hamzah. The rest recited it with the prolongation and without the hamzah.

The scholars differed about its origin. Some said: its origin is antum, and the ha is for alerting (tanbih). Al-Akhfash said: its origin is a'antum, and the first hamzah was changed to ha, as in their saying: harqat and araqat (I spilled).

﴿Haulaa'﴾ (these): it is indeclinable, built on kasrah, and its origin is ulaa'. The particle of alerting ha was prefixed to it. It has two forms: the short (qasr) and the long (madd). Some Arabs join it with the ya' (as in ﴿haa'ulaai﴾).

Abu Hazim recited:

By your life, we and our allies, these,
are in a trial whose infants have not been weaned.

(In the source: Hatim.) (Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/108, where it reads: "whose nails have not been trimmed.")

And ﴿haa haahuna﴾ (here) in the position of a vocative means: O these people.

﴿You argued about what you have knowledge of﴾: that is, about the matter of Muhammad, because they knew him from what they found of his description in their books, so they argued with it falsely.

﴿Why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of?﴾ That is, about the story of Abraham, for there is nothing in your books that he was a Jew or a Christian.

﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾ He exonerated Abraham (peace be upon him) and cleared him of their claim, and so He said:

﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim.﴾ The ḥanīf (upright monotheist) is one who affirms the oneness of God, performs the pilgrimage, sacrifices, is circumcised, and faces the qiblah. It is the easiest of religions and the most beloved to God, and its people are the most honored of creation before God.

﴿And he was not of the polytheists.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: The leaders of the Jews said: "By God, O Muhammad, you know that we are more entitled to the religion of Abraham than you or anyone else, and that he was a Jew. Nothing prevents you but envy of us." So God revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul, occasions of revelation, by al-Wahidi: 68.)

Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ); and Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, raising it (to the Prophet). The narration of some of them has entered into that of others. They said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, and what happened at Badr happened, the Quraysh gathered in the Dar al-Nadwah (the council house) and said: "We have a claim against those among Muhammad's Companions who are with al-Najashi, for those of you killed at Badr. So gather wealth and present it to al-Najashi, perhaps he will hand over to you those of your people who are with him. Let two men of your opinion be appointed for this."

So they sent Amr ibn al-As and Amarah ibn Abi Mu'it with gifts, leather and other things. They boarded the sea and reached Abyssinia. When they entered upon al-Najashi, they prostrated to him, greeted him, and said: "Our people are sincere advisers to you, grateful to you, and love your righteousness. They sent us to warn you about these people who came to you, for they are the people of a lying man who rose among us and claimed that he is the Messenger of God. No one followed him except fools. We had constricted their affairs and forced them into a mountain pass of our land where no one can enter to them or leave from them. Hunger and thirst have killed them. When the matter became severe for them, he sent to you a cousin of his to corrupt your religion, your kingdom, and your subjects. So beware of them and hand them over to us, so that we may deal with them for you." They said: "The sign of this is that when they enter upon you, they do not prostrate to you nor greet you with the greeting by which people greet you, out of aversion to your religion and your custom."

He (the narrator) said: Al-Najashi summoned them, and when they were present, Ja'far shouted at the door: "The party of God asks permission to enter upon you." Al-Najashi said: "Tell this caller to repeat his words." Ja'far did so. Al-Najashi said: "Yes, let them enter in the safety of God and His protection." Amr ibn al-As looked at his companion and said: "Do you not hear how they enter with 'the party of God', and what al-Najashi answered them?" That displeased them both. Then they entered upon him and did not prostrate to him.

Amr said: "Do you not see that they are arrogant, not prostrating to you?" So al-Najashi said to them: "What prevented you from prostrating to me and greeting me with the greeting with which those who come to me from the lands greet me?" They said: "We prostrate to God, who created you and gave you your kingdom." He said: "The greeting to kings was ours, and we were idolaters. Then God sent among us a truthful prophet, and commanded us with the greeting that God has approved for us, which is 'peace', the greeting of the people of Paradise." Al-Najashi recognized that this is true, as it is in the Torah and the Gospel. He said: "Which of you is the one who called out: 'The party of God asks permission to enter upon you'?" Ja'far said: "I am."

He said: "Speak." He said: "You are a king among the kings of the earth, and of the People of the Book. Excessive talk and injustice are not proper before you. I wish to answer on behalf of my companions, so let one of these two men speak while the other listens, that you may hear our discussion." Amr said to Ja'far: "Speak."

Ja'far said to al-Najashi: "Ask these two men: are we slaves or free? If we were slaves who had run away from our masters, return us to them." Al-Najashi said: "O Amr, are they slaves or free?" He said: "No, rather free and noble."

Al-Najashi said: "They are saved from slavery." Then Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have shed blood unjustly, so that we may be requited." Amr said: "No, not even a drop." Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have taken people's wealth unjustly, so that we must repay it."

Al-Najashi said: "Speak, O Amr, even if it were a qintar (a large weight of gold), I will pay it." He said: "No, not even a qirat." Al-Najashi said: "Then what do you seek from them?" Amr said: "We and they were upon one religion and one matter, the religion of our fathers. They abandoned that religion and followed another. We remained upon it. So we sent you their people, that you might hand them over to us."

Al-Najashi said: "What is this religion you were upon, and what is the religion you have followed?" Ja'far said: "As for the religion we were upon, we have abandoned it, and it is the religion of Satan and his affair. We used to disbelieve in God and worship stones. As for what we have turned to, it is the religion of Islam, which came to us from God through a Messenger and a Book like the Book of the son of Mary, confirming it."

Al-Najashi said: "O Ja'far, you have spoken a great matter; so take your time." Then al-Najashi commanded that the bell (naqus) be struck, and every priest and monk gathered to him. When they had assembled before him, al-Najashi said: "I adjure you by God who sent down the Gospel to Jesus: Do you find between Jesus and the Day of Resurrection any prophet sent?" They said: "Yes, by God. Jesus (peace be upon him) gave us good news of him, saying: 'Whoever believes in him has believed in me, and whoever disbelieves in him has disbelieved in me.'"

Al-Najashi said to Ja'far: "Heyh (speak) — that is, tell me: what does this man say to you, and what does he command you, and what does he forbid you?" They said: "He recites to us the Book of God, commands what is right, forbids what is wrong, commands good neighborliness and maintaining the ties of kinship, commands kindness to parents and orphans, and commands that we worship God alone, with no partner."

He said: "Recite to me something of what is recited to you." So Ja'far recited to them Surah al-'Ankabut and al-Rum. The eyes of al-Najashi and his companions overflowed with tears. They said: "O Ja'far, add more of this good speech." So he recited to them Surah al-Kahf. Amr wanted to anger al-Najashi.

He said: "They revile Jesus and his mother." Al-Najashi said: "What do you say about this?" Ja'far recited to them Surah Maryam. When he came to the mention of Mary and Jesus, al-Najashi raised himself from his seat as much as the (speck that) irritates the eye, and said: "The Messiah did not exceed what you say."

Then he turned to Ja'far and his companions and said: "Go, for you are safe (sayyum) in my land; whoever reviles you or harms you will pay a fine." Then he said: "Rejoice and do not fear, for there is no oppression today upon the party of Abraham (peace be upon him)." Amr said to al-Najashi: "And who is the party of Abraham?" He said: "These people, and their companion who came from him, and whoever follows him. But you are the polytheists."

Then al-Najashi returned to Amr and his companions the wealth they had brought, and said: "Your gifts were a bribe to me. Take them back, for God has made me king and did not take a bribe from me." Ja'far said: "So we departed, and we were in the best of homes and the most honorable of lands." And God revealed on that day, concerning their dispute, to His Messenger, while he was in Madinah: (Asbab al-nuzul, by al-Wahidi: 71.)

﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him﴾ — upon his likeness.

﴿And this Prophet﴾: meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And those who believe. And Allah is the Guardian of the believers.﴾

Masruq narrated from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every prophet has a close friend (wali) among the prophets, and my close friend among them is my father and the intimate friend of my Lord," and then he recited the verse: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him...﴾.

﴿Wadat﴾ means: wished, desired.

﴿A group of the People of the Scripture...﴾ (the verse). It was revealed concerning Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Ammar ibn Yasir, when the Jews invited them to their religion. This story has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah.

﴿Wadat﴾: wished. ﴿Ta'ifah﴾ (a group): a community of the People of the Scripture, meaning the Jews.

﴿Law yudillunakum﴾ (if they could lead you astray): they would make you slip from your religion and return you to disbelief. Ibn Jarir said: it means "they would destroy you," as in the saying of al-Akhtal satirizing Jarir ibn Atiyyah:

You were a speck of dust in a turbid, foaming sea,
which the flood cast up, and so it strayed into destruction.

That is, he perished a perishing.

﴿And they lead astray none but themselves, and they perceive not.﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture: meaning the Jews and the Christians. Why do you disbelieve in the signs of God﴾: meaning the Qur'an and the explanation of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿While you witness﴾: that his description is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you confuse (talbisun) the truth with falsehood﴾: you mix the truth, Islam, with Judaism and Christianity.

Ibn Zayd said: "The Torah which God sent down to Moses" with the falsehood which you altered, distorted, lost, and wrote with your own hands.

﴿And you conceal the truth while you know﴾: that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and his religion is true.

Abu Mijlaz recited: talabbisun (with the doubled ba'), and Hasan ibn Umayr recited: talbisu and taktumu without the nun, and there is no basis for this.

﴿And a group of the People of the Scripture said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day...﴾ (the verse).

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: Twelve rabbis of the Jews of Khaybar and Arab villages conspired together, and some of them said to others: "Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue only, without belief in the heart, and disbelieve at the end of the day, and say: 'We examined our books and consulted our scholars, and we found that Muhammad is not that, and his falsehood and the invalidity of his religion have become clear to us.' When you do this, his Companions will doubt their religion, and they will say: 'They are the People of the Book, and they know it better than us,' so they will return from their religion to yours."

Mujahid, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi said: This concerns the clarification of the qiblah, when it was turned toward the Ka'bah. That was hard on the Jews because they opposed it. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said to his companions: "Believe in what was revealed to Muhammad concerning the matter of the Ka'bah, and pray toward it at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve at the end of the day, and return to your qiblah, the Rock, so that they may say: 'The People of the Book are more knowing than us,' and they will return to our qiblah." So God warned His Prophet of the plotting of these people and informed him of their secret. So He revealed: ﴿And a group of the People of the Scripture said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day﴾: its first part. It is called "the face" (wajh) because it is the best of it, and the first thing that one faces and sees. It is also said that the first of white hair is called its face (wajh).

Rabi' ibn Ziyad said:

Whoever is glad at the killing of Malik,
let him come to our women with the face of the day.

(Lisan al-Arab: 13/556.)

﴿And disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will waver﴾: they will doubt. ﴿Return﴾: from their religion. ﴿And do not believe﴾: do not confirm.

﴿Except to him who follows your religion﴾: this is also from the speech of the Jews to one another. "And do not believe, and do not affirm, except one who follows your religion," that is, who agrees with your creed and prays toward your qiblah. The lam in His saying ﴿li-man﴾ is extra (silah). The meaning: "Do not believe except one who follows your religion, Judaism."

As in the saying of God Most High: ﴿Say: Perhaps some of what you are hastening after will be close behind you﴾ (Surah al-Naml: 72).

﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, that there be given to anyone the like of what you were given﴾ (the verse). The reciters and scholars differed concerning it. The common reading is: "an yu'ta" with a fatha on the alif and a short alif. The meaning of this reading: this statement is inserted between two statements, and it is a report from God Most High that the clarification and what indicates it, His saying ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, is connected to the first statement as a report of the speech of the Jews to one another. The meaning of the verse: "And do not believe except one who follows your religion," and: "Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given," of knowledge, wisdom, proof, the manna and the quails, the splitting of the sea, and other virtues and marvels. "And do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord, because you have a sounder religion than theirs." This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid and al-Akhfash.

Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayyab said: The Jews said to their common people: "Do not believe except one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the like of what you were given, and what superiority would you have over them if they knew what you know?" "And then they will argue with you before your Lord": they will say, "You know that our religion is true, so do not confirm them, lest they know the like of what you know, and argue with you before your Lord." It may be that on this view the lam is not a hidden (implied) particle, as in His saying: ﴿God makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 176). Its implied meaning would be: "And do not believe except one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the knowledge like what you were given, and lest they argue with you before your Lord."

Al-Hasan and al-A'mash recited: "in yu'ta" with a kasrah on the alif. The basis of this reading: all of this is the speech of God without interruption, and the speech of the Jews is complete at His saying ﴿except to one who follows your religion﴾. The meaning of the verse: "Say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God; that anyone is given what is given the like of what you were given, O community of Muhammad, or they argue with you" — that is, unless the Jews argue with you falsely, saying, "We are better than you." His saying "before your Lord" means "before the grace of your Lord toward you, that is what they have." "In" (an) on this reading means denial and negation.

This is the meaning of the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible that "aw" (or) means "until," as one says: "Hold on to him until he gives you your right," that is, until he gives you your right.

Imru' al-Qays said:

I said to him: "Do not let your eye weep, for we only seek a kingdom or we die, and so be excused."

That is, until we die.

The meaning: "No one is given the like of what you were given, O community of Muhammad, of religion and proof, until they argue with you before your Lord." (Kitab al-'Ayn, by al-Khalil: 8/438.)

Ibn Kathir recited: "an yu'ta" with a long alif, and in this case there is an optional (ikhtiyar) construction in the sentence. Its estimated sense: "that anyone be given the like of what you were given, O company of Jews, of the Book and wisdom; you envy them and do not believe in them." This is the saying of Qatadah and al-Rabi'.

﴿Illa﴾ here is a statement of God Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say to them, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, for He sent down a Book like your book and sent a prophet like your prophet, and you envied him and disbelieved in him.

﴿Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Hatim said: Its meaning is "now" (in), so the conditional lam is omitted for lightness, and its long vowel is changed, as in the reading of one who recited: "an kana dha mal" (if he was one with wealth), meaning "now he was."

As for His saying ﴿or they argue with you﴾, on this reading it returns to address the believers, and "aw" is used in the sense of "an" (if), since both are particles of doubt and condition, and one may be placed in the position of the other. The estimated sense of the verse: "And if they argue with you, O company of believers, before your Lord, then say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, and we are upon it."

It is possible that the whole is an address to the believers, and the arrangement of the verse would be: "That anyone be given the like of what you were given, O company of believers [so do not waver when the Jews confuse you], then say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God."

And if they argue with you, say: "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God."

These are the aspects of the verses according to the variations of the Qur'an. It is possible that the report about the Jews ends at His saying, "so that they may return," and that His saying, "And do not believe except those who follow your religion," through to the end of the verse, is part of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is because Allah, exalted is He, strengthens the hearts of the believers and sharpens their insight, so that they do not doubt when the Jews confuse and falsify matters concerning their religion. The meaning is: O company of believers, do not believe except those who follow your religion. Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given of religion and virtue, and do not believe that they will argue with you about your religion before your Lord and prevail over you. Indeed, "guidance is the guidance of God, and bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing." Thus the whole verse becomes an address from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the believers at the time the Jews confuse them, so that they do not slip or become doubtful, and Allah knows best.

This is supported by the statement of al-Dahhak, who said: "The Jews said, 'We argue before our Lord against those who oppose us in our religion.' So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that they are the ones who are refuted (al-mudhhadūn), meaning the defeated, and that the believers are the victorious."

The people of allusion (ahl al-ishara, the adherents of esoteric or allusive interpretation) said regarding this verse: "Do not keep company except with those who agree with you in your states and your path, for whoever does not agree with you will not accompany you."

"He singles out for His mercy": with His prophethood, His religion, and His blessing.

"Whom He wills, and God is Possessor of Great Bounty." Abu Hayyan said: "The general statement remains, along with the hope of the one who hopes and the fear of the one who fears."

I wish to answer on behalf of my companions, so let one of these two men speak while the other listens, that you may hear our discussion." Amr said to Ja'far: "Speak."

Ja'far said to al-Najashi: "Ask these two men: are we slaves or free? If we were slaves who had run away from our masters, return us to them." Al-Najashi said: "O Amr, are they slaves or free?" He said: "No, rather free and noble."

Al-Najashi said: "They are saved from slavery." Then Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have shed blood unjustly, so that we may be requited." Amr said: "No, not even a drop." Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have taken people's wealth unjustly, so that we must repay it."

Al-Najashi said: "Speak, O Amr, even if it were a qintar (a large weight of gold), I will pay it." He said: "No, not even a qirat." Al-Najashi said: "Then what do you seek from them?" Amr said: "We and they were upon one religion and one matter, the religion of our fathers. They abandoned that religion and followed another. We remained upon it. So we sent you their people, that you might hand them over to us."

Al-Najashi said: "What is this religion you were upon, and what is the religion you have followed?" Ja'far said: "As for the religion we were upon, we have abandoned it, and it is the religion of Satan and his affair. We used to disbelieve in God and worship stones. As for what we have turned to, it is the religion of Islam, which came to us from God through a Messenger and a Book like the Book of the son of Mary, confirming it."

Al-Najashi said: "O Ja'far, you have spoken a great matter; so take your time." Then al-Najashi commanded that the bell (naqus) be struck, and every priest and monk gathered to him. When they had assembled before him, al-Najashi said: "I adjure you by God who sent down the Gospel to Jesus: Do you find between Jesus and the Day of Resurrection any prophet sent?" They said: "Yes, by God. Jesus (peace be upon him) gave us good news of him, saying: 'Whoever believes in him has believed in me, and whoever disbelieves in him has disbelieved in me.'"

Al-Najashi said to Ja'far: "Heyh (speak) — that is, tell me: what does this man say to you, and what does he command you, and what does he forbid you?" They said: "He recites to us the Book of God, commands what is right, forbids what is wrong, commands good neighborliness and maintaining the ties of kinship, commands kindness to parents and orphans, and commands that we worship God alone, with no partner."

He said: "Recite to me something of what is recited to you." So Ja'far recited to them Surah al-'Ankabut and al-Rum. The eyes of al-Najashi and his companions overflowed with tears. They said: "O Ja'far, add more of this good speech." So he recited to them Surah al-Kahf. Amr wanted to anger al-Najashi.

He said: "They revile Jesus and his mother." Al-Najashi said: "What do you say about this?" Ja'far recited to them Surah Maryam. When he came to the mention of Mary and Jesus, al-Najashi raised himself from his seat as much as the (speck that) irritates the eye, and said: "The Messiah did not exceed what you say."

Then he turned to Ja'far and his companions and said: "Go, for you are safe (sayyum) in my land; whoever reviles you or harms you will pay a fine." Then he said: "Rejoice and do not fear, for there is no oppression today upon the party of Abraham (peace be upon him)." Amr said to al-Najashi: "And who is the party of Abraham?" He said: "These people, and their companion who came from him, and whoever follows him. But you are the polytheists."

Then al-Najashi returned to Amr and his companions the wealth they had brought, and said: "Your gifts were a bribe to me. Take them back, for God has made me king and did not take a bribe from me." Ja'far said: "So we departed, and we were in the best of homes and the most honorable of lands." And God revealed on that day, concerning their dispute, to His Messenger, while he was in Madinah: (Asbab al-nuzul, by al-Wahidi: 71.)

﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him﴾ — upon his likeness.

﴿And this Prophet﴾: meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And those who believe. And Allah is the Guardian of the believers.﴾

Masruq narrated from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every prophet has a close friend (wali) among the prophets, and my close friend among them is my father and the intimate friend of my Lord," and then he recited the verse: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him...﴾.

﴿Wadat﴾ means: wished, desired.

﴿A group of the People of the Scripture...﴾ (the verse). It was revealed concerning Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Ammar ibn Yasir, when the Jews invited them to their religion. This story has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah.

﴿Wadat﴾: wished. ﴿Ta'ifah﴾ (a group): a community of the People of the Scripture, meaning the Jews.

﴿Law yudillunakum﴾ (if they could lead you astray): they would make you slip from your religion and return you to disbelief. Ibn Jarir said: it means "they would destroy you," as in the saying of al-Akhtal satirizing Jarir ibn Atiyyah:

You were a speck of dust in a turbid, foaming sea,
which the flood cast up, and so it strayed into destruction.

That is, he perished a perishing.

﴿And they lead astray none but themselves, and they perceive not.﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture: meaning the Jews and the Christians. Why do you disbelieve in the signs of God﴾: meaning the Qur'an and the explanation of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿While you witness﴾: that his description is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you confuse (talbisun) the truth with falsehood﴾: you mix the truth, Islam, with Judaism and Christianity.

Ibn Zayd said: "The Torah which God sent down to Moses" with the falsehood which you altered, distorted, lost, and wrote with your own hands.

﴿And you conceal the truth while you know﴾: that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and his religion is true.

Abu Mijlaz recited: talabbisun (with the doubled ba'), and Hasan ibn Umayr recited: talbisu and taktumu without the nun, and there is no basis for this.

﴿And a group of the People of the Scripture said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day...﴾ (the verse).

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: Twelve rabbis of the Jews of Khaybar and Arab villages conspired together, and some of them said to others: "Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue only, without belief in the heart, and disbelieve at the end of the day, and say: 'We examined our books and consulted our scholars, and we found that Muhammad is not that, and his falsehood and the invalidity of his religion have become clear to us.' When you do this, his Companions will doubt their religion, and they will say: 'They are the People of the Book, and they know it better than us,' so they will return from their religion to yours."

Mujahid, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi said: This concerns the clarification of the qiblah, when it was turned toward the Ka'bah. That was hard on the Jews because they opposed it. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said to his companions: "Believe in what was revealed to Muhammad concerning the matter of the Ka'bah, and pray toward it at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve at the end of the day, and return to your qiblah, the Rock, so that they may say: 'The People of the Book are more knowing than us,' and they will return to our qiblah." So God warned His Prophet of the plotting of these people and informed him of their secret. So He revealed: ﴿And a group of the People of the Scripture said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day﴾: its first part. It is called "the face" (wajh) because it is the best of it, and the first thing that one faces and sees. It is also said that the first of white hair is called its face (wajh).

Rabi' ibn Ziyad said:

Whoever is glad at the killing of Malik,
let him come to our women with the face of the day.

(Lisan al-Arab: 13/556.)

﴿And disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will waver﴾: they will doubt. ﴿Return﴾: from their religion. ﴿And do not believe﴾: do not confirm.

﴿Except to him who follows your religion﴾: this is also from the speech of the Jews to one another. "And do not believe, and do not affirm, except one who follows your religion," that is, who agrees with your creed and prays toward your qiblah. The lam in His saying ﴿li-man﴾ is extra (silah). The meaning: "Do not believe except one who follows your religion, Judaism."

As in the saying of God Most High: ﴿Say: Perhaps some of what you are hastening after will be close behind you﴾ (Surah al-Naml: 72).

﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, that there be given to anyone the like of what you were given﴾ (the verse). The reciters and scholars differed concerning it. The common reading is: "an yu'ta" with a fatha on the alif and a short alif. The meaning of this reading: this statement is inserted between two statements, and it is a report from God Most High that the clarification and what indicates it, His saying ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, is connected to the first statement as a report of the speech of the Jews to one another. The meaning of the verse: "And do not believe except one who follows your religion," and: "Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given," of knowledge, wisdom, proof, the manna and the quails, the splitting of the sea, and other virtues and marvels. "And do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord, because you have a sounder religion than theirs." This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid and al-Akhfash.

Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayyab said: The Jews said to their common people: "Do not believe except one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the like of what you were given, and what superiority would you have over them if they knew what you know?" "And then they will argue with you before your Lord": they will say, "You know that our religion is true, so do not confirm them, lest they know the like of what you know, and argue with you before your Lord." It may be that on this view the lam is not a hidden (implied) particle, as in His saying: ﴿God makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 176). Its implied meaning would be: "And do not believe except one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the knowledge like what you were given, and lest they argue with you before your Lord."

Al-Hasan and al-A'mash recited: "in yu'ta" with a kasrah on the alif. The basis of this reading: all of this is the speech of God without interruption, and the speech of the Jews is complete at His saying ﴿except to one who follows your religion﴾. The meaning of the verse: "Say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God; that anyone is given what is given the like of what you were given, O community of Muhammad, or they argue with you" — that is, unless the Jews argue with you falsely, saying, "We are better than you." His saying "before your Lord" means "before the grace of your Lord toward you, that is what they have." "In" (an) on this reading means denial and negation.

This is the meaning of the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible that "aw" (or) means "until," as one says: "Hold on to him until he gives you your right," that is, until he gives you your right.

Imru' al-Qays said:

I said to him: "Do not let your eye weep, for we only seek a kingdom or we die, and so be excused."

That is, until we die.

The meaning: "No one is given the like of what you were given, O community of Muhammad, of religion and proof, until they argue with you before your Lord." (Kitab al-'Ayn, by al-Khalil: 8/438.)

Ibn Kathir recited: "an yu'ta" with a long alif, and in this case there is an optional (ikhtiyar) construction in the sentence. Its estimated sense: "that anyone be given the like of what you were given, O company of Jews, of the Book and wisdom; you envy them and do not believe in them." This is the saying of Qatadah and al-Rabi'.

﴿Illa﴾ here is a statement of God Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say to them, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, for He sent down a Book like your book and sent a prophet like your prophet, and you envied him and disbelieved in him.

﴿Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Hatim said: Its meaning is "now" (in), so the conditional lam is omitted for lightness, and its long vowel is changed, as in the reading of one who recited: "an kana dha mal" (if he was one with wealth), meaning "now he was."

As for His saying ﴿or they argue with you﴾, on this reading it returns to address the believers, and "aw" is used in the sense of "an" (if), since both are particles of doubt and condition, and one may be placed in the position of the other. The estimated sense of the verse: "And if they argue with you, O company of believers, before your Lord, then say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, and we are upon it."

It is possible that the whole is an address to the believers, and the arrangement of the verse would be: "That anyone be given the like of what you were given, O company of believers [so do not waver when the Jews confuse you], then say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God."

And if they argue with you, say: "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God."

These are the aspects of the verses according to the variations of the Qur'an. It is possible that the report about the Jews ends at His saying, "so that they may return," and that His saying, "And do not believe except those who follow your religion," through to the end of the verse, is part of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is because Allah, exalted is He, strengthens the hearts of the believers and sharpens their insight, so that they do not doubt when the Jews confuse and falsify matters concerning their religion. The meaning is: O company of believers, do not believe except those who follow your religion. Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given of religion and virtue, and do not believe that they will argue with you about your religion before your Lord and prevail over you. Indeed, "guidance is the guidance of God, and bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing." Thus the whole verse becomes an address from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the believers at the time the Jews confuse them, so that they do not slip or become doubtful, and Allah knows best.

This is supported by the statement of al-Dahhak, who said: "The Jews said, 'We argue before our Lord against those who oppose us in our religion.' So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that they are the ones who are refuted (al-mudhhadūn), meaning the defeated, and that the believers are the victorious."

The people of allusion (ahl al-ishara, the adherents of esoteric or allusive interpretation) said regarding this verse: "Do not keep company except with those who agree with you in your states and your path, for whoever does not agree with you will not accompany you."

"He singles out for His mercy": with His prophethood, His religion, and His blessing.

"Whom He wills, and God is Possessor of Great Bounty." Abu Hayyan said: "The general statement remains, along with the hope of the one who hopes and the fear of the one who fears."

O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when you claim that he was upon your religion, Judaism and Christianity, while Judaism came into being after the revelation of the Torah and Christianity after the revelation of the Gospel?

﴿And the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him.﴾ That is, after the death of Abraham by a long time. There were a thousand years between Abraham and Moses, and two thousand years between Moses and Jesus.

﴿Will you not reason?﴾ That is, by presenting your argument and the falsehood of your claim.

﴿Ha antum﴾ (lo, you are): Ahl al-Madinah recited it without hamzah and without a prolonged vowel, except for the length needed for the silent alif. Ahl Makkah recited it with a hamzah and a short vowel, on the pattern of ﴿ha'antum﴾. Ahl al-Kufah recited it with both the prolongation (madd) and the hamzah. The rest recited it with the prolongation and without the hamzah.

The scholars differed about its origin. Some said: its origin is antum, and the ha is for alerting (tanbih). Al-Akhfash said: its origin is a'antum, and the first hamzah was changed to ha, as in their saying: harqat and araqat (I spilled).

﴿Haulaa'﴾ (these): it is indeclinable, built on kasrah, and its origin is ulaa'. The particle of alerting ha was prefixed to it. It has two forms: the short (qasr) and the long (madd). Some Arabs join it with the ya' (as in ﴿haa'ulaai﴾).

Abu Hazim recited:

By your life, we and our allies, these,
are in a trial whose infants have not been weaned.

(In the source: Hatim.) (Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/108, where it reads: "whose nails have not been trimmed.")

And ﴿haa haahuna﴾ (here) in the position of a vocative means: O these people.

﴿You argued about what you have knowledge of﴾: that is, about the matter of Muhammad, because they knew him from what they found of his description in their books, so they argued with it falsely.

﴿Why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of?﴾ That is, about the story of Abraham, for there is nothing in your books that he was a Jew or a Christian.

﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾ He exonerated Abraham (peace be upon him) and cleared him of their claim, and so He said:

﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim.﴾ The ḥanīf (upright monotheist) is one who affirms the oneness of God, performs the pilgrimage, sacrifices, is circumcised, and faces the qiblah. It is the easiest of religions and the most beloved to God, and its people are the most honored of creation before God.

﴿And he was not of the polytheists.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: The leaders of the Jews said: "By God, O Muhammad, you know that we are more entitled to the religion of Abraham than you or anyone else, and that he was a Jew. Nothing prevents you but envy of us." So God revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul, occasions of revelation, by al-Wahidi: 68.)

Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ); and Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, raising it (to the Prophet). The narration of some of them has entered into that of others. They said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, and what happened at Badr happened, the Quraysh gathered in the Dar al-Nadwah (the council house) and said: "We have a claim against those among Muhammad's Companions who are with al-Najashi, for those of you killed at Badr. So gather wealth and present it to al-Najashi, perhaps he will hand over to you those of your people who are with him. Let two men of your opinion be appointed for this."

So they sent Amr ibn al-As and Amarah ibn Abi Mu'it with gifts, leather and other things. They boarded the sea and reached Abyssinia. When they entered upon al-Najashi, they prostrated to him, greeted him, and said: "Our people are sincere advisers to you, grateful to you, and love your righteousness. They sent us to warn you about these people who came to you, for they are the people of a lying man who rose among us and claimed that he is the Messenger of God. No one followed him except fools. We had constricted their affairs and forced them into a mountain pass of our land where no one can enter to them or leave from them. Hunger and thirst have killed them. When the matter became severe for them, he sent to you a cousin of his to corrupt your religion, your kingdom, and your subjects. So beware of them and hand them over to us, so that we may deal with them for you." They said: "The sign of this is that when they enter upon you, they do not prostrate to you nor greet you with the greeting by which people greet you, out of aversion to your religion and your custom."

He (the narrator) said: Al-Najashi summoned them, and when they were present, Ja'far shouted at the door: "The party of God asks permission to enter upon you." Al-Najashi said: "Tell this caller to repeat his words." Ja'far did so. Al-Najashi said: "Yes, let them enter in the safety of God and His protection." Amr ibn al-As looked at his companion and said: "Do you not hear how they enter with 'the party of God', and what al-Najashi answered them?" That displeased them both. Then they entered upon him and did not prostrate to him.

Amr said: "Do you not see that they are arrogant, not prostrating to you?" So al-Najashi said to them: "What prevented you from prostrating to me and greeting me with the greeting with which those who come to me from the lands greet me?" They said: "We prostrate to God, who created you and gave you your kingdom." He said: "The greeting to kings was ours, and we were idolaters. Then God sent among us a truthful prophet, and commanded us with the greeting that God has approved for us, which is 'peace', the greeting of the people of Paradise." Al-Najashi recognized that this is true, as it is in the Torah and the Gospel. He said: "Which of you is the one who called out: 'The party of God asks permission to enter upon you'?" Ja'far said: "I am."

He said: "Speak." He said: "You are a king among the kings of the earth, and of the People of the Book. Excessive talk and injustice are not proper before you. I wish to answer on behalf of my companions, so let one of these two men speak while the other listens, that you may hear our discussion." Amr said to Ja'far: "Speak."

Ja'far said to al-Najashi: "Ask these two men: are we slaves or free? If we were slaves who had run away from our masters, return us to them." Al-Najashi said: "O Amr, are they slaves or free?" He said: "No, rather free and noble."

Al-Najashi said: "They are saved from slavery." Then Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have shed blood unjustly, so that we may be requited." Amr said: "No, not even a drop." Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have taken people's wealth unjustly, so that we must repay it."

Al-Najashi said: "Speak, O Amr, even if it were a qintar (a large weight of gold), I will pay it." He said: "No, not even a qirat." Al-Najashi said: "Then what do you seek from them?" Amr said: "We and they were upon one religion and one matter, the religion of our fathers. They abandoned that religion and followed another. We remained upon it. So we sent you their people, that you might hand them over to us."

Al-Najashi said: "What is this religion you were upon, and what is the religion you have followed?" Ja'far said: "As for the religion we were upon, we have abandoned it, and it is the religion of Satan and his affair. We used to disbelieve in God and worship stones. As for what we have turned to, it is the religion of Islam, which came to us from God through a Messenger and a Book like the Book of the son of Mary, confirming it."

Al-Najashi said: "O Ja'far, you have spoken a great matter; so take your time." Then al-Najashi commanded that the bell (naqus) be struck, and every priest and monk gathered to him. When they had assembled before him, al-Najashi said: "I adjure you by God who sent down the Gospel to Jesus: Do you find between Jesus and the Day of Resurrection any prophet sent?" They said: "Yes, by God. Jesus (peace be upon him) gave us good news of him, saying: 'Whoever believes in him has believed in me, and whoever disbelieves in him has disbelieved in me.'"

Al-Najashi said to Ja'far: "Heyh (speak) — that is, tell me: what does this man say to you, and what does he command you, and what does he forbid you?" They said: "He recites to us the Book of God, commands what is right, forbids what is wrong, commands good neighborliness and maintaining the ties of kinship, commands kindness to parents and orphans, and commands that we worship God alone, with no partner."

He said: "Recite to me something of what is recited to you." So Ja'far recited to them Surah al-'Ankabut and al-Rum. The eyes of al-Najashi and his companions overflowed with tears. They said: "O Ja'far, add more of this good speech." So he recited to them Surah al-Kahf. Amr wanted to anger al-Najashi.

He said: "They revile Jesus and his mother." Al-Najashi said: "What do you say about this?" Ja'far recited to them Surah Maryam. When he came to the mention of Mary and Jesus, al-Najashi raised himself from his seat as much as the (speck that) irritates the eye, and said: "The Messiah did not exceed what you say."

Then he turned to Ja'far and his companions and said: "Go, for you are safe (sayyum) in my land; whoever reviles you or harms you will pay a fine." Then he said: "Rejoice and do not fear, for there is no oppression today upon the party of Abraham (peace be upon him)." Amr said to al-Najashi: "And who is the party of Abraham?" He said: "These people, and their companion who came from him, and whoever follows him. But you are the polytheists."

Then al-Najashi returned to Amr and his companions the wealth they had brought, and said: "Your gifts were a bribe to me. Take them back, for God has made me king and did not take a bribe from me." Ja'far said: "So we departed, and we were in the best of homes and the most honorable of lands." And God revealed on that day, concerning their dispute, to His Messenger, while he was in Madinah: (Asbab al-nuzul, by al-Wahidi: 71.)

Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said to his companions: "Believe in what was revealed to Muhammad concerning the matter of the Ka'bah, and pray toward it at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve at the end of the day, and return to your qiblah, the Rock, so that they may say: 'The People of the Book are more knowing than us,' and they will return to our qiblah." So God warned His Prophet of the plotting of these people and informed him of their secret. So He revealed: ﴿And a group of the People of the Scripture said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day﴾: its first part. It is called "the face" (wajh) because it is the best of it, and the first thing that one faces and sees. It is also said that the first of white hair is called its face (wajh).

Rabi' ibn Ziyad said:

Whoever is glad at the killing of Malik,
let him come to our women with the face of the day.

(Lisan al-Arab: 13/556.)

﴿And disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will waver﴾: they will doubt. ﴿Return﴾: from their religion. ﴿And do not believe﴾: do not confirm.

﴿Except to him who follows your religion﴾: this is also from the speech of the Jews to one another. "And do not believe, and do not affirm, except one who follows your religion," that is, who agrees with your creed and prays toward your qiblah. The lam in His saying ﴿li-man﴾ is extra (silah). The meaning: "Do not believe except one who follows your religion, Judaism."

As in the saying of God Most High: ﴿Say: Perhaps some of what you are hastening after will be close behind you﴾ (Surah al-Naml: 72).

﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, that there be given to anyone the like of what you were given﴾ (the verse). The reciters and scholars differed concerning it. The common reading is: "an yu'ta" with a fatha on the alif and a short alif. The meaning of this reading: this statement is inserted between two statements, and it is a report from God Most High that the clarification and what indicates it, His saying ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, is connected to the first statement as a report of the speech of the Jews to one another. The meaning of the verse: "And do not believe except one who follows your religion," and: "Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given," of knowledge, wisdom, proof, the manna and the quails, the splitting of the sea, and other virtues and marvels. "And do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord, because you have a sounder religion than theirs." This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid and al-Akhfash.

Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayyab said: The Jews said to their common people: "Do not believe except one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the like of what you were given, and what superiority would you have over them if they knew what you know?" "And then they will argue with you before your Lord": they will say, "You know that our religion is true, so do not confirm them, lest they know the like of what you know, and argue with you before your Lord." It may be that on this view the lam is not a hidden (implied) particle, as in His saying: ﴿God makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 176). Its implied meaning would be: "And do not believe except one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the knowledge like what you were given, and lest they argue with you before your Lord."

Al-Hasan and al-A'mash recited: "in yu'ta" with a kasrah on the alif. The basis of this reading: all of this is the speech of God without interruption, and the speech of the Jews is complete at His saying ﴿except to one who follows your religion﴾. The meaning of the verse: "Say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God; that anyone is given what is given the like of what you were given, O community of Muhammad, or they argue with you" — that is, unless the Jews argue with you falsely, saying, "We are better than you." His saying "before your Lord" means "before the grace of your Lord toward you, that is what they have." "In" (an) on this reading means denial and negation.

This is the meaning of the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible that "aw" (or) means "until," as one says: "Hold on to him until he gives you your right," that is, until he gives you your right.

Imru' al-Qays said:

I said to him: "Do not let your eye weep, for we only seek a kingdom or we die, and so be excused."

That is, until we die.

The meaning: "No one is given the like of what you were given, O community of Muhammad, of religion and proof, until they argue with you before your Lord." (Kitab al-'Ayn, by al-Khalil: 8/438.)

Ibn Kathir recited: "an yu'ta" with a long alif, and in this case there is an optional (ikhtiyar) construction in the sentence. Its estimated sense: "that anyone be given the like of what you were given, O company of Jews, of the Book and wisdom; you envy them and do not believe in them." This is the saying of Qatadah and al-Rabi'.

﴿Illa﴾ here is a statement of God Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say to them, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God﴾, for He sent down a Book like your book and sent a prophet like your prophet, and you envied him and disbelieved in him.

﴿Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Hatim said: Its meaning is "now" (in), so the conditional lam is omitted for lightness, and its long vowel is changed, as in the reading of one who recited: "an kana dha mal" (if he was one with wealth), meaning "now he was."

As for His saying ﴿or they argue with you﴾, on this reading it returns to address the believers, and "aw" is used in the sense of "an" (if), since both are particles of doubt and condition, and one may be placed in the position of the other. The estimated sense of the verse: "And if they argue with you, O company of believers, before your Lord, then say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, and we are upon it."

It is possible that the whole is an address to the believers, and the arrangement of the verse would be: "That anyone be given the like of what you were given, O company of believers [so do not waver when the Jews confuse you], then say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God."

And if they argue with you, say: "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God."

These are the aspects of the verses according to the variations of the Qur'an. It is possible that the report about the Jews ends at His saying, "so that they may return," and that His saying, "And do not believe except those who follow your religion," through to the end of the verse, is part of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is because Allah, exalted is He, strengthens the hearts of the believers and sharpens their insight, so that they do not doubt when the Jews confuse and falsify matters concerning their religion. The meaning is: O company of believers, do not believe except those who follow your religion. Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given of religion and virtue, and do not believe that they will argue with you about your religion before your Lord and prevail over you. Indeed, "guidance is the guidance of God, and bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing." Thus the whole verse becomes an address from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the believers at the time the Jews confuse them, so that they do not slip or become doubtful, and Allah knows best.

This is supported by the statement of al-Dahhak, who said: "The Jews said, 'We argue before our Lord against those who oppose us in our religion.' So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that they are the ones who are refuted (al-mudhhadūn), meaning the defeated, and that the believers are the victorious."

The people of allusion (ahl al-ishara, the adherents of esoteric or allusive interpretation) said regarding this verse: "Do not keep company except with those who agree with you in your states and your path, for whoever does not agree with you will not accompany you."

"He singles out for His mercy": with His prophethood, His religion, and His blessing.

"Whom He wills, and God is Possessor of Great Bounty." Abu Hayyan said: "The general statement remains, along with the hope of the one who hopes and the fear of the one who fears."

O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when you claim that he was upon your religion, Judaism and Christianity, while Judaism came into being after the revelation of the Torah and Christianity after the revelation of the Gospel?

﴿And the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him.﴾ That is, after the death of Abraham by a long time. There were a thousand years between Abraham and Moses, and two thousand years between Moses and Jesus.

﴿Will you not reason?﴾ That is, by presenting your argument and the falsehood of your claim.

﴿Ha antum﴾ (lo, you are): Ahl al-Madinah recited it without hamzah and without a prolonged vowel, except for the length needed for the silent alif. Ahl Makkah recited it with a hamzah and a short vowel, on the pattern of ﴿ha'antum﴾. Ahl al-Kufah recited it with both the prolongation (madd) and the hamzah. The rest recited it with the prolongation and without the hamzah.

The scholars differed about its origin. Some said: its origin is antum, and the ha is for alerting (tanbih). Al-Akhfash said: its origin is a'antum, and the first hamzah was changed to ha, as in their saying: harqat and araqat (I spilled).

﴿Haulaa'﴾ (these): it is indeclinable, built on kasrah, and its origin is ulaa'. The particle of alerting ha was prefixed to it. It has two forms: the short (qasr) and the long (madd). Some Arabs join it with the ya' (as in ﴿haa'ulaai﴾).

Abu Hazim recited:

By your life, we and our allies, these,
are in a trial whose infants have not been weaned.

(In the source: Hatim.) (Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/108, where it reads: "whose nails have not been trimmed.")

And ﴿haa haahuna﴾ (here) in the position of a vocative means: O these people.

﴿You argued about what you have knowledge of﴾: that is, about the matter of Muhammad, because they knew him from what they found of his description in their books, so they argued with it falsely.

﴿Why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of?﴾ That is, about the story of Abraham, for there is nothing in your books that he was a Jew or a Christian.

﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾ He exonerated Abraham (peace be upon him) and cleared him of their claim, and so He said:

﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim.﴾ The ḥanīf (upright monotheist) is one who affirms the oneness of God, performs the pilgrimage, sacrifices, is circumcised, and faces the qiblah. It is the easiest of religions and the most beloved to God, and its people are the most honored of creation before God.

﴿And he was not of the polytheists.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: The leaders of the Jews said: "By God, O Muhammad, you know that we are more entitled to the religion of Abraham than you or anyone else, and that he was a Jew. Nothing prevents you but envy of us." So God revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul, occasions of revelation, by al-Wahidi: 68.)

Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ); and Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, raising it (to the Prophet). The narration of some of them has entered into that of others. They said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, and what happened at Badr happened, the Quraysh gathered in the Dar al-Nadwah (the council house) and said: "We have a claim against those among Muhammad's Companions who are with al-Najashi, for those of you killed at Badr. So gather wealth and present it to al-Najashi, perhaps he will hand over to you those of your people who are with him. Let two men of your opinion be appointed for this."

So they sent Amr ibn al-As and Amarah ibn Abi Mu'it with gifts, leather and other things. They boarded the sea and reached Abyssinia. When they entered upon al-Najashi, they prostrated to him, greeted him, and said: "Our people are sincere advisers to you, grateful to you, and love your righteousness. They sent us to warn you about these people who came to you, for they are the people of a lying man who rose among us and claimed that he is the Messenger of God. No one followed him except fools. We had constricted their affairs and forced them into a mountain pass of our land where no one can enter to them or leave from them. Hunger and thirst have killed them. When the matter became severe for them, he sent to you a cousin of his to corrupt your religion, your kingdom, and your subjects. So beware of them and hand them over to us, so that we may deal with them for you." They said: "The sign of this is that when they enter upon you, they do not prostrate to you nor greet you with the greeting by which people greet you, out of aversion to your religion and your custom."

He (the narrator) said: Al-Najashi summoned them, and when they were present, Ja'far shouted at the door: "The party of God asks permission to enter upon you." Al-Najashi said: "Tell this caller to repeat his words." Ja'far did so. Al-Najashi said: "Yes, let them enter in the safety of God and His protection." Amr ibn al-As looked at his companion and said: "Do you not hear how they enter with 'the party of God', and what al-Najashi answered them?" That displeased them both. Then they entered upon him and did not prostrate to him.

Amr said: "Do you not see that they are arrogant, not prostrating to you?" So al-Najashi said to them: "What prevented you from prostrating to me and greeting me with the greeting with which those who come to me from the lands greet me?" They said: "We prostrate to God, who created you and gave you your kingdom." He said: "The greeting to kings was ours, and we were idolaters. Then God sent among us a truthful prophet, and commanded us with the greeting that God has approved for us, which is 'peace', the greeting of the people of Paradise." Al-Najashi recognized that this is true, as it is in the Torah and the Gospel. He said: "Which of you is the one who called out: 'The party of God asks permission to enter upon you'?" Ja'far said: "I am."

He said: "Speak." He said: "You are a king among the kings of the earth, and of the People of the Book. Excessive talk and injustice are not proper before you. I wish to answer on behalf of my companions, so let one of these two men speak while the other listens, that you may hear our discussion." Amr said to Ja'far: "Speak."

Ja'far said to al-Najashi: "Ask these two men: are we slaves or free? If we were slaves who had run away from our masters, return us to them." Al-Najashi said: "O Amr, are they slaves or free?" He said: "No, rather free and noble."

Al-Najashi said: "They are saved from slavery." Then Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have shed blood unjustly, so that we may be requited." Amr said: "No, not even a drop." Ja'far said: "Ask them whether we have taken people's wealth unjustly, so that we must repay it."

Al-Najashi said: "Speak, O Amr, even if it were a qintar (a large weight of gold), I will pay it." He said: "No, not even a qirat." Al-Najashi said: "Then what do you seek from them?" Amr said: "We and they were upon one religion and one matter, the religion of our fathers. They abandoned that religion and followed another. We remained upon it. So we sent you their people, that you might hand them over to us."

Al-Najashi said: "What is this religion you were upon, and what is the religion you have followed?" Ja'far said: "As for the religion we were upon, we have abandoned it, and it is the religion of Satan and his affair. We used to disbelieve in God and worship stones. As for what we have turned to, it is the religion of Islam, which came to us from God through a Messenger and a Book like the Book of the son of Mary, confirming it."

Al-Najashi said: "O Ja'far, you have spoken a great matter; so take your time." Then al-Najashi commanded that the bell (naqus) be struck, and every priest and monk gathered to him. When they had assembled before him, al-Najashi said: "I adjure you by God who sent down the Gospel to Jesus: Do you find between Jesus and the Day of Resurrection any prophet sent?" They said: "Yes, by God. Jesus (peace be upon him) gave us good news of him, saying: 'Whoever believes in him has believed in me, and whoever disbelieves in him has disbelieved in me.'"

Al-Najashi said to Ja'far: "Heyh (speak) — that is, tell me: what does this man say to you, and what does he command you, and what does he forbid you?" They said: "He recites to us the Book of God, commands what is right, forbids what is wrong, commands good neighborliness and maintaining the ties of kinship, commands kindness to parents and orphans, and commands that we worship God alone, with no partner."

He said: "Recite to me something of what is recited to you." So Ja'far recited to them Surah al-'Ankabut and al-Rum. The eyes of al-Najashi and his companions overflowed with tears. They said: "O Ja'far, add more of this good speech." So he recited to them Surah al-Kahf. Amr wanted to anger al-Najashi.

He said: "They revile Jesus and his mother." Al-Najashi said: "What do you say about this?" Ja'far recited to them Surah Maryam. When he came to the mention of Mary and Jesus, al-Najashi raised himself from his seat as much as the (speck that) irritates the eye, and said: "The Messiah did not exceed what you say."

Then he turned to Ja'far and his companions and said: "Go, for you are safe (sayyum) in my land; whoever reviles you or harms you will pay a fine." Then he said: "Rejoice and do not fear, for there is no oppression today upon the party of Abraham (peace be upon him)." Amr said to al-Najashi: "And who is the party of Abraham?" He said: "These people, and their companion who came from him, and whoever follows him. But you are the polytheists."

Then al-Najashi returned to Amr and his companions the wealth they had brought, and said: "Your gifts were a bribe to me. Take them back, for God has made me king and did not take a bribe from me." Ja'far said: "So we departed, and we were in the best of homes and the most honorable of lands." And God revealed on that day, concerning their dispute, to His Messenger, while he was in Madinah: (Asbab al-nuzul, by al-Wahidi: 71.)

﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him﴾ — upon his likeness.

﴿And this Prophet﴾: meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And those who believe. And Allah is the Guardian of the believers.﴾

Masruq narrated from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every prophet has a close friend (wali) among the prophets, and my close friend among them is my father and the intimate friend of my Lord," and then he recited the verse: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him...﴾.

﴿Wadat﴾ means: wished, desired.

﴿A group of the People of the Scripture...﴾ (the verse). It was revealed concerning Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Ammar ibn Yasir, when the Jews invited them to their religion. This story has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah.

﴿Wadat﴾: wished. ﴿Ta'ifah﴾ (a group): a community of the People of the Scripture, meaning the Jews.

You were a speck of dust in a turbid, foaming sea,
which the flood cast up, and so it strayed into destruction.

That is, he perished a perishing.

﴿And they lead astray none but themselves, and they perceive not.﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture: meaning the Jews and the Christians. Why do you disbelieve in the signs of God﴾: meaning the Qur'an and the explanation of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿While you witness﴾: that his description is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you confuse (talbisun) the truth with falsehood﴾: you mix the truth, Islam, with Judaism and Christianity.

Ibn Zayd said: "The Torah which God sent down to Moses" with the falsehood which you altered, distorted, lost, and wrote with your own hands.

﴿And you conceal the truth while you know﴾: that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and his religion is true.

Abu Mijlaz recited: talabbisun (with the doubled ba'), and Hasan ibn Umayr recited: talbisu and taktumu without the nun, and there is no basis for this.

﴿And a group of the People of the Scripture said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day...﴾ (the verse).

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: Twelve rabbis of the Jews of Khaybar and Arab villages conspired together, and some of them said to others: "Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue only, without belief in the heart, and disbelieve at the end of the day, and say: 'We examined our books and consulted our scholars, and we found that Muhammad is not that, and his falsehood and the invalidity of his religion have become clear to us.' When you do this, his Companions will doubt their religion, and they will say: 'They are the People of the Book, and they know it better than us,' so they will return from their religion to yours."
