So he returned his land to him and added to it a large amount from his own land, fearing that some of his right might remain in his hand; it became for that man's descendants after him.

Bādhān related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: it was revealed concerning Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis al-Kindi, against whom ʿAbdan ibn Ashraʿ sought a ruling. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) decided that he should take the oath. When he was about to swear, this verse was revealed. Imruʾ al-Qays refrained from swearing, admitted the right of ʿAbdan, and handed it over to him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "For you is Paradise because of it."

Mujahid and al-Shaʿbi said: a man displayed his merchandise early in the day. When it was late in the day, a man came and bargained with him. He swore: "By God, he has withheld it earlier in the day for such-and-such, and if not for the evening he would not have sold it for that." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God﴾, i.e., they exchange the covenant of God and the fulfilment of trusts ﴿and their oaths﴾, the false ones, ﴿for a small price﴾.

﴿Those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾: its bliss and its reward. ﴿And God will not speak to them﴾, speech that benefits them and gladdens them. This is what the exegetes said. Al-Mufaddal said: ﴿God will not speak to them﴾: by accepting an argument they could present.

﴿Nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾: meaning, He will not have mercy upon them, nor show compassion to them, nor do good to them, nor speak to them kindly. It is said: "so-and-so looked at so-and-so" and "looked upon him" when he showed mercy to him and did good to him.

The poet said:
So I said: look, how beautiful all the people are, to the sons of Ghullat Sadban, whom longing has wasted away.

From Abu ʿAmr al-Jawni, who said: God never looked upon a thing without having mercy on it. Even if He had decreed to look upon the people of the Fire, He would have had mercy on them; but He decreed that He would not look upon them.

ʿAbdullah ibn Kaʿb related from Abu Umama al-Khazzani that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever seizes the right of a Muslim man by his oath, God has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden Paradise to him." A man said: "Even if it is a small thing?" He said: "Even if it is a twig of arak."

Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Qurashi related from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Umama al-Khazzani, from ʿAbdullah ibn Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, and the perjurous oath (yamin al-ghamus). By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one swears an oath, even if it were on the weight of a mosquito's wing, except that it will be a stain in his heart until the Day of Resurrection."

﴿Nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾:
A man who withheld surplus water on the road, and so denied the traveler; a man who gave allegiance to a man, not giving allegiance except for worldly gain, so if he gave him what he wanted he would fulfil it, and if not he would not fulfil it; and a man who bargained over his merchandise after the afternoon prayer, then swore by God: "He has been given so much for it," and the other believed him and took it.

Al-Harith al-Aʿwar related from ʿAli (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the false oath, for it leaves the dwellings desolate of their people."

Maʿmar related regarding a man from the Banu Tamim, from Abu al-Aswad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The false oath makes the womb barren."

al-ʿAlaʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The false oath promotes the sale of goods and erases the profit."

﴿And indeed among them﴾: meaning, among the People of the Book who were mentioned before, and they are the Jews.

﴿A party﴾: a group. They are: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Abu Yasir, Huyayy, and Sabaʿa ibn ʿAmr the poet.

﴿Distorting﴾: the people of Medina read yulawwuna with the yaʾ dammed, the lam open, and the waw doubled, for intensity. Hamid read yalūna with one waw, on the intention of hamza, then he dropped the hamza and transferred its vowel to the lam. The rest read with two waws and a silent light lam. Their meanings are all the same: ﴿they twist﴾.

﴿Their tongues﴾: by distortion, deliberate and obstinate, which is what they changed of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the verse of stoning. It is said: "He twisted his tongue from such-and-such," meaning he altered it. And "he twisted the thing from what it was" when he changed it to something else. And "he twisted so-and-so from his opinion" when he turned him away from it. From this comes "procrastination by the debtor" (layy al-ghariym). The poet al-Nabigha al-Jaʿdi said:
God twisted the knowledge of the unseen away from its level, and knows what has passed and what came later.

Its parallel is His words: ﴿And if you twist or turn away...﴾, to the end of the verse.

﴿So that you may think﴾: so that you may suppose what they distorted ﴿from the Book﴾: which God sent down.

﴿And it is not from the Book﴾ ... ﴿And they speak falsely about God while they know﴾: that they are liars.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas: the verse was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians together, and those who distorted the Torah and the Gospel, and struck the Book of God, some of it against some, and attached to it what is not from it, so they dropped from it the Hanifite religion. So God the Exalted made their lie clear to the believers.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 75–85 (part 2 of 3):

﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Scripture and the wisdom and prophethood…﴾ (the verse).

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning ʿIsa (peace be upon him), ﴿that Allah should give him the Scripture﴾, meaning he should be given wisdom. It was revealed concerning the Christians of Najran.

Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAta said: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿that Allah should give him the Scripture﴾, meaning the Qur'an. The reason was that Abu Rafi al-Qurazi, from the Jews, and the chief of the Christians of Najran said: "O Muhammad, do you want us to worship you and take you as a lord?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in Allah from worshipping other than Allah, or from commanding the worship of other than Allah. It is not for this that I was sent, nor for this that I was commanded." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan said: It has reached me that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, we greet you as some of us greet one another. Shall we not prostrate to you?" He said: "It is not fitting that anyone be prostrated to besides Allah, but honour your Prophet and recognise the right of those who deserve it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning: it is not befitting for a human being, like His saying ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ [4:92], and His saying ﴿It is not for us to speak of this﴾ [24:16], meaning: it is not befitting.

The people of the meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: this lam is transposed (manqulah), and "an" carries the sense of lam, and the construction of the verse is: "It is not for a human being that he should say that." Similar to His saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾ [19:35], i.e., Allah would not take a son; and His saying ﴿It is not for a prophet to defraud﴾ [3:161], i.e., it is not for a prophet to defraud. "Al-bashar" is the entirety of the children of Adam, with no singular from its own form, like "qawm" (people) and "jaysh" (army); it is used both for the singular and the plural.

﴿that Allah should give him the Scripture and the wisdom and prophethood﴾: meaning understanding and knowledge. It is also said: the rulings from Allah, like His saying: ﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture and the wisdom and prophethood﴾ [6:89].

﴿then he should say to the people﴾: it is in the accusative as a conjunction; Mahbub related from Abu ʿAmr: "thumma yaqulu" with the nominative, as a new sentence.

﴿Be worshippers of me besides Allah﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: this is the dialect of Muzayna, who say "ʿabad" for "ʿabid" (servants).

﴿but rather be﴾: i.e., "but rather he would say: be," so the verb "say" is omitted.

﴿rabbaniyyin﴾ (godly/rabbis): they differed concerning it:
ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: be jurists and scholars.
Mujahid: jurists, but below the rabbis (ahbar). Abu Razin, Qatada and al-Suddi: wise scholars, and this is the narration of ʿAta from Ibn ʿAbbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from him: teaching jurists.
Marrah ibn Sharahil said: ʿAlqama was among the rabbaniyyin who teach people the Qur'an.
Al-Fadl ibn ʿIyad related from ʿAta ibn al-Sa'ib from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: wise and pious.
Ibn Zayd: the rulers of the people and their leaders, some of them devoted and sincere worshippers.
ʿAta: scholars, wise, appointed by Allah over His creation. Abu ʿUbayd: the Arabs did not know the word "rabbaniyyin."
Abu [ʿUbayd]: I heard a learned man say: the rabbani is the one who knows the lawful and the unlawful, the commanding and the forbidding,
and who knows the reports of the community and what was and what will be.
The historian: "Be rabbaniyyin" means: those who submit to their Lord, as if it were "fa'lani" derived from "rububiyya" (lordship).
Some of them said: it was originally "rabbi," then the alif was added for emphasis, as is the Syriac usage, then the nun was added because the alif is silent, as it is said: sanʿani, bahrani, darani.
Al-Mubarrad: the rabbaniyyin are masters of knowledge; its singular is "rabban," who inherits knowledge and trains people, i.e., teaches and reforms them and takes charge of their affairs. The alif and nun are for intensification, as they said: rayyan, ʿatshan, shabʿan, ghawthan, and nuʿsan from "nuʿas" (drowsiness), and wasnan; then the nisba ya was added to it, as is said. A poet said:
"Had I been held in the truth, the narration would have brought me down from it, and my rabbis (ahbari) would have raised me."

ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) gathered all these sayings together and said: he is the one whose knowledge is nurtured by his action.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said on the day Ibn ʿAbbas died: "The rabbani of this community has died."

﴿as you were﴾: its meaning is necessity, i.e., "because you are." Like His saying ﴿and my wife was barren﴾ [19:5], i.e., and my wife; and His saying ﴿how can we speak to one who is in the cradle as a child?﴾ [19:29], i.e., who is in the cradle a child.

﴿you teach the Scripture﴾: As-Sulami, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and the people of Kufa read "tuʿallimuna" with shadda, from "taʿlim" (teaching), and Abu ʿUbayda preferred it. The rest read "taʿlamuna" without shadda, from "ʿilm" (knowledge), and Abu Hatim preferred it. Abu ʿAmr said: its corroboration is ﴿and as you studied﴾ — he did not say "yadrusun." Al-Hasan read "tuʿallimuna" with ta and ʿayn and shadda on the lam, meaning "taʿlamuna." Abu ʿUbayda read "tudrisuna," from "adrasa yadrusu." Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tudarrisuna," from "tadris" (teaching). The rest: "yadrusuna," from "dars," i.e., they recite; its parallel is in Surat al-Aʿraf: ﴿and they studied what is in it﴾ [7:169].

Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no believer, male or female, free or slave, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has a binding right upon him: that he learn the Qur'an and gain understanding of it." Then he recited this verse: ﴿but rather be rabbaniyyin, as you were teaching the Scripture and as you were studying﴾.

﴿And he does not command you﴾: al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, ʿAsim and Hamza read "wa la yaʾmurakum" with fatha, as a conjunction to His saying "thumma yaqula."
It is also said: it is with the hidden "an," and on this reading it is linked back to "al-bashar." The rest read with damma, as a new sentence, cut off from the first speech; this is supported by the reading of ʿAbdullah and Talha: "wa lan yaʾmurakum." Then they differed about it: most read according to its meaning, "wa la yaʾmurakum" (Allah). Ibn Jurayj said: "wa la yaʾmurakum" (Muhammad, peace be upon him). It is also said: "wa la yaʾmurakum" (the human being).

﴿that you take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾: like the saying of Quraysh and Banu Mulayh when they said: the angels are the daughters of Allah; and the Jews and Christians, when they said about the Messiah and ʿUzayr what they said.

﴿Would he command you to disbelief after you have submitted?﴾: in the form of astonishment and denial, meaning: he would not do this.

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom…﴾: Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "lamma" with a shadda on the mim; Yahya ibn Ri'ab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read with the lam genitive and the mim without shadda.
As for the rest: with fatha on the lam and no shadda on the mim. As for one who reads the lam with fatha and the mim without shadda, al-Akhfash said: it is the lam of initiation, introduced upon "ma" which is the predicate, like the speaker's saying: "Certainly Zayd is better than you." "Ma ataytukum" and what follows it is its relative clause, and its response is in His saying ﴿you shall believe in him﴾. If you wish, make the predicate of "ma" to be "from the Book of Allah." You may say "min" is superfluous, meaning: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom." Then he began: "thumma" meaning: "then there comes to you…" And if you wish, you say: ﴿then, when there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾: the lam is the lam of oath, its sense being: "By Allah, you shall surely believe in him." So it was emphasised at the beginning of the speech with the lam of emphasis, and at the end with the lam of oath.

Al-Farra said: whoever reads with fatha on the lam makes it a superfluous lam, because of His saying: when the oath falls upon a sentence, it makes that conditional act into the form of an act, and makes its response like the response of the oath. The meaning: "Whatever Scripture I have given you, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him," for the lam in His saying "you shall surely believe in him."

Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj said: this is the lam of verification (lam al-tahqiq), introduced upon "ma" of condition, as it is introduced upon "an," and its meaning is: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him." The lam in His saying "you shall surely believe in him" is the response of the condition, like His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away﴾ [17:86], and similar.

Al-Kisa'i said: "la tu'minunna" is connected to the first speech, and the response of the condition is in His saying: ﴿Then whoever turns away after that﴾. Whoever reads with kasra on the lam, it is the lam of annexation (idafa), introduced upon "ma" meaning "that which": "that which I have given you," meaning: the covenant of the prophets was taken for the sake of what is before them of Scripture and wisdom; "then, when there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him," after the covenant, because the taking of the covenant is equivalent to making one swear. It is as we say in speech: "I took your pledge that you would do such and such," as if you had said: "I made you swear that you would do it."

The author of al-Nazm said: whoever reads with kasra on the lam, it has the meaning of "after" (baʿda), i.e., after what I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, like the saying of al-Nabigha:
"I thought the signs of her camp had been effaced, so I recognised them after six years, and this year is the seventh."
I.e., after six years. Whoever doubles the mim, its meaning is "when I gave you" (hina ataytukum), by His saying: ﴿ataytukum﴾.

The people of Kufa read "ataynakum" in the plural of majesty; the others read "ataytukum" in the singular, and this is the preferred reading for agreement with the script, like His saying: ﴿and I am with you﴾ [3:81]. The statement is coherent in the verse on the three modes of its construction: (And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets).

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of this verse. A group said: the covenant was taken from the prophets only that each should confirm the others, and that some should command belief in others; this is the meaning of "confirmation" in the verse, and this is the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Qatada, al-Hasan and al-Suddi, supported by the apparent sense of the verse.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Allah did not send any prophet, from Adam and onward, except that He took from him the covenant concerning Muhammad (ﷺ), and commanded him to take the covenant from his people: ﴿you shall surely believe in him, and surely support him﴾, and that if he were sent while they were alive, they would surely support him.

Others said: the covenant was taken from the People of the Book, among whom the prophets were sent; this is the saying of Mujahid and al-Rabi.

Mujahid said: this is a mixing from the Book, and it is from the reading of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book." They said: do you not see His saying: ﴿then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾? Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent only to the People of the Book, not to the prophets.

Some said: the covenant was taken from the prophets and their nations [that they would surely believe in him]; the prophets are singled out from mention of the nations, because taking the covenant from the leader is an indication that it was taken from the followers. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, and this is closer to the correct view.

Allah said: ﴿Do you acknowledge and accept My covenant on that terms?﴾ — meaning: and do you accept on that My covenant, like His saying: ﴿If you are given this, then take it﴾ [5:41], i.e., accept it; and His saying: ﴿no ransom will be accepted from it﴾, i.e., no ransom will be accepted; and His saying: ﴿He takes the charities﴾, i.e., He accepts them. ﴿They said: We acknowledge.﴾

Allah said: ﴿So bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses﴾ against you and against them.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "fa-ashhadu": meaning "then know." Al-Zajjaj said: "fa-ashhadu," i.e., then make clear, because the witness is the one who identifies the claim of the claimant; and Allah's witness to the prophets is the making clear of the matter of their prophethood through signs and miracles. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: Allah said to the angels: "bear witness against them," so it is a reference to something not mentioned.

﴿Whoever turns away after that﴾ — after the acknowledgment and the testimony — ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾: the sinners, who depart from faith.

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?…﴾ (the verse).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The People of the Book brought their disputes to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), each group claiming that it was closer to his religion. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Both groups are free from the religion of Ibrahim." They became angry and said: "By Allah, we will not accept your judgment nor follow your religion." So Allah revealed: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾

It is the reading of al-Hasan, Humayd, Ya'qub, Salam, Sahl and Safwan with the ya', because of His saying: ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. Abu ʿAmr read "yabghuna" with ya' and "turja'un" with ta', saying: because the first is specific and the second is general, so he differentiated between them for their difference in meaning. The rest read with ta' in both, in address, because of His saying: ﴿whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom﴾.

﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾: "aslama" means submitted and complied; "taw'an" is compliance and following with ease, from their saying: "a horse that is taw' al-'inan," i.e., obedient to the rein. "Karhan" is what is with hardship and the soul's refusal. "Karhan" with damma on the kaf; both are verbal nouns placed in the position of a circumstantial clause, as if He said: "And to Him submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, obedient and unwilling."

They differed concerning His saying "ta'an" and "karhan":
It was narrated that Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning His saying: ﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾, said: "The angels obeyed Him in the heavens, and the Ansar and ʿAbd al-Qays obeyed Him on the earth."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my companions, for my companions embraced Islam out of fear of Allah, and people embraced it out of fear of the sword."

Al-Hasan and al-Mufaddal said: "taw'" is for the people of the heavens specifically; as for the people of the earth, some embraced Islam willingly and some unwillingly.

Ibn ʿAbbas: their worship of Allah, all of them, willingly and unwillingly, and submission to Him.

Al-Rabi, from Abu al-ʿAliya, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾, said: Every child of Adam acknowledged against himself that Allah is my Lord and I am His servant; this is the Islam which, had he remained upon it, would have been [his]; but when he spoke it, it became a proof against him. Then he associated others in worship; this is the one who submitted unwillingly. And among them is one who testified that Allah is my Lord and I am His servant, then made his worship sincere; this is the one who submitted willingly. Al-Dahhak said: this is when the covenant was taken from them and they acknowledged it.

Mujahid: "taw'an" is the shade of the believer, and "karhan" is the shade of the disbeliever, supported by His saying: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ [13:15], and His saying: ﴿whose shadows turn from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah﴾ [16:48].

Al-Sha'bi: it is their seeking refuge in Him when they are in distress, supported by His saying: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [29:65].

Qatada: the believer submits willingly and the disbeliever unwillingly. As for the believer, he submits willingly, so that benefits him and it is accepted from him. As for the disbeliever, he submits unwillingly at the time of calamity and seeing [the punishment], so it is not accepted from him and does not benefit him, supported by His saying: ﴿Their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [40:85].

al-Kalbi: "taw'an": those who were born in Islam; "karhan": those compelled into Islam.

ʿIkrima: "karhan": one whom the [proof] compelled to monotheism, supported by His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: Allah﴾ [43:87], and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say: Allah﴾ [29:61].

Ibn Kaysan: "And to Him submitted," i.e., submitted are whoever is in the heavens and the earth to what He has ordained for them and fashioned them upon, and whatever happens to them; they do not resist Him, whether they dislike that or love it.

﴿And to Him they will be returned﴾ [3:83].

Al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, said: When one of your animals becomes unruly or is skittish, let him recite this verse into its ear.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 75–85 (part 3 of 3):

"Say: We believe in God..." up to His words, "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion..." — the verse was revealed concerning twelve men who apostatized from Islam, left Medina, and joined Mecca as disbelievers. Among them were: al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, brother of al-Hallas ibn Suwayd; Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq al-Ansari; Miqyas ibn Subabah al-Laythi; Abdullah ibn Unays ibn Khatal from the Banu Taym ibn Murrah; Wajwaj ibn al-Aslat; and Abu Amir ibn al-Nu'man. God revealed about them: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾.

And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you. The verse: most exegetes (tafsir) said: this verse was revealed concerning all the Jews. God the Exalted informed that among them there is trustworthiness and treachery. The qintar is an expression for a large amount of wealth, and the dinar is an expression for a small amount of wealth.

If it is said: what is the benefit of this information, when we know that people have always been this way, some trustworthy and some treacherous?

We say: it is a warning from God to the believers not to entrust them with their wealth, or to be deceived by them, because of their permitting the wealth of the believers.

This is like what is related in the report: "Do you refrain from mentioning the wicked person? Mention him with what is in him, so that people may beware of him."

Some of them said: the trustworthiness refers to those among them who embraced Islam, and the treachery refers to those among them who did not embrace Islam.

Muqatil said: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾: Abdullah ibn Salam. A man deposited with him one thousand two hundred ounces of gold, and he returned it to him, so God praised him.

﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾: this refers to Makhdh ibn Azura, because a man from Quraysh deposited a dinar with him and he betrayed him.

In some exegeses: the one who returns the trust in this verse are the Christians, and those who do not return it are the Jews.

Regarding His words ﴿tamanhu﴾ there are two readings. Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli read it as ﴿timinhu﴾ with a kasra on the tා (taʾ), and this is the dialect of Bakr and Tamim. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿ma laka la timinna﴾.

The common reading is ﴿tamanhu﴾ with an alif. The word dinar originally was dannar, and one of the two nuns was replaced by a yaʾ, seeking lightness because of its frequent use. Evidence for this is that you pluralize it as dananir.

Regarding His words ﴿yuaddihi﴾ and its counterparts there are five readings. Abu ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, ʿAsim and Hamza all read them with the hāʾ silent. Abu Jaʿfar and Yaʿqub read it with the hāʾ short and kasra. Salam read it with damma and short. al-Zuhri read it with damma and lengthened. The others read it with kasra and lengthened. As for the one who makes the hāʾ silent, many grammarians criticized him, because jazm (apocopation) does not apply to the hāʾ when the letter before it is moved, and the hāʾ is a pronoun, and pronouns do not take jazm.

Al-Farrāʾ said: this is the view of some Arabs who apply jazm to the hāʾ when the letter before it is moved, so they say: ḍarabtuhu ḍarban shadīdan, just as they silence the mīm of antum and qumtum, though its original is raf.

And he recited:
When he saw there was neither a bed nor a feast, he inclined to a tamarisk on a dune and lay down.

Some said: the silencing of the hāʾ was permitted in these positions because it was placed in the position of jazm, which is the omitted yaʾ. As for the one who reads with a short vowel, he has been satisfied with the damma instead of the waw and with the kasra instead of the yaʾ. Al-Farrāʾ recited:
I am the son of Kilab and the son of Aws, so whoever has a veil covering it, then I am revealed.

And Sibawayh recited:
If he is lean or fat, he will make his eyes closed to himself.

And whoever lengthens the hāʾ does so according to the original, because when the letter was weak it was strengthened by the waw in damma and by the yaʾ in kasra.

Sibawayh said: after the masculine hāʾ comes a waw, just as after the feminine hāʾ comes an alif. And whoever reads the hāʾ with damma does so according to the original, because the original of the hāʾ is damma, like huwa, and humā and hum. And whoever reads with kasra, he says it is because before it is a yaʾ, even if it is omitted, or because what precedes it is kasra.

﴿Except what you constantly stand over﴾: Yahya, Thabit, al-Aʿmash and Talha read it with kasra on the dāl, and the rest with damma.

Whoever reads with damma, it is from dāma, yadūmu, and it is a dialect of al-ʿĀliya. Whoever reads with kasra has two possibilities. Some said: it is also from dāma yadūmu, but on the pattern faʿila, yafʿalu, saying dimta tadūmu like mitta tamūtu. This was said by al-Akhfash. And there is no triliteral verb of the pattern faʿila-yafʿulu (with kasra in the past and damma in the present) from a sound final radical, except fadila, yafdulu, and niʿma, yanʿamu. From a weak verb: mittu, amūtu, and dimtu, adūmu, and these are the dialect of Tamim.

Most scholars said: from karuma, yakrumu, fa'ala, yaf'alu, like khāfa, yakhāfu, and hāba, yahābu.

﴿Standing﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "persistently." Mujahid: "constantly." Saʿid ibn Jubayr: "steadfastly." Qatada: "standing, insisting." al-Suddi: "standing over his head."

Al-ʿUtaybi: "persistently, by insistence." Its origin is that one who demands a thing stands over it, and one who abandons it sits away from it. The indication of His words ﴿a community standing﴾ is: acting by the command of God, not abandoning it.

Abu Rawq: he admits what was given to him, as long as you are standing over his head. If you ask him for it at the time you give it to him, he returns it to you; but if you give him time and delay it, he denies it and takes it away. That is permitting what is forbidden, and treachery.

﴿That is because they say: there is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered﴾: meaning, regarding the Arabs. Its parallel is ﴿He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves﴾. ﴿Blame﴾: sin and fault. Its evidence is His words ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers﴾. This is because the Jews said: there is no fault upon us in withholding the wealth of the Arabs, since God has made it lawful for us, for they are not upon our religion. They used to permit the oppression of those who opposed them in their religion, saying: God did not make for them any sanctity in our Book.

Al-Kalbi: The Jews said: all wealth was ours, and whatever is in the hands of the Arabs of it is ours, and they only oppressed us and seized it from us unjustly, so there is no blame upon us in taking it from them.

Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil: The Jews made contracts with men from the Muslims in the Jahiliyya. When they embraced Islam, they demanded from them the value of their wealth. They said: you have no right against us, and we have no obligation to you; you have abandoned the religion you were upon, and the covenant between us and you has ended. They claimed that they found this in their Book. So God refuted them, saying:
﴿and they speak falsely about God while they know﴾.

In a hadith: when the verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The enemies of God have lied. Everything from the Jahiliyya is under my feet except trust, for it is returned to the righteous and the wicked."

Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani related from Sasaʿa: a man asked Ibn ʿAbbas, saying: "We obtain in raids from the wealth of the people of Medina a chicken or a sheep." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "What do they say?" He said: "They say: there is no harm upon us." He said: "This is like what the People of the Book said: ﴿there is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered﴾. When they pay the jizya (poll tax), your wealth becomes lawful for you only with their willing consent." Then God the Exalted said in refutation of them:

﴿Yes﴾: meaning, it is not as they said. ﴿But whoever fulfills his covenant﴾: that which he covenanted with God in the Torah, of belief in Muhammad and the Quran, and returning trusts.

The pronoun in His words ﴿his covenant﴾ refers to God, the Mighty and Majestic, since He was mentioned in His words ﴿and they speak falsely about God﴾. It is permissible that it refers to ﴿fulfills﴾.

﴿And fears God﴾: from disbelief, treachery and breaking the covenant.

﴿Indeed, God loves the righteous﴾: those who have this description.

From al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he prays and fasts and claims he is a believer: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

From Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is entrusted with a trust and returns it, while he could have not returned it, God will marry him to the wide-eyed houris as many as he wishes."

Al-Hasan from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the prophets, the truthful ones and the martyrs."

Wahb from Hudhayfa, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) related to me two hadiths; I saw one of them while I awaited the other. He related to us: "Trust was sent down into the root of men's hearts, and the Quran was sent down, so learn from the Quran and learn from the source of the Sunna."

Then he related to us about their lifting, saying: "A man sleeps a sleep, and trust is removed from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a blister, like a hot coal you roll on your foot, so you see it swollen and there is nothing in it." Then Hudhayfa took a pebble and rolled it over his shin. He said: "People will then trade with one another, and hardly anyone will return a trust, until it is said: so-and-so is a trustworthy man; and until it is said of a man: how strong he is, how intelligent he is, how witty he is, while there is not in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith. There came upon me a time when I did not care whom I dealt with; if he was a Muslim, his Islam would return him to me; if he was a Jew or Christian, his employer would return him to me. But today, I would not deal with any of you except so-and-so and so-and-so."

It has been said: the perfection of religion is abandoning treachery, and the greatest crime is betraying people.

﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price﴾: they differed regarding the revelation of this verse.

Ikrima said: it was revealed concerning Abu Rafi, Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab and others, leaders of the Jews, who wrote what God had covenanted with them in the Torah regarding Muhammad (ﷺ) and altered it, and wrote with their hands something other than it, and swore that it was from God, so that the bribes and provisions they had from their followers would not escape them.

Al-Kalbi said: some scholars of the Jews, who were in poverty and possessed some share of knowledge of the Torah, were struck by a year of drought. They came to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf seeking a loan from him. Kaʿb asked them: "Do you know that this man is the Messenger of God in your Book?" They said: "Yes. What do you know of him?" He said: "No." They said: "We testify that he is the servant of God and His Messenger." Kaʿb said: "You have lied against me. I want to feed you and clothe you, but God has deprived you of much good."

They said: "It was made to appear similar to us. Wait, until we meet him." He said: "So they went and wrote a description other than his description. Then they came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and concealed it. Then they returned to Kaʿb and said: 'We saw the Messenger of God and came to him, and he is not the description that was described to us.' And they brought out what they had written." Kaʿb was delighted by that, and by their deceit. So God the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what God has sent down of the Book and sell it for a small price﴾, to the end of the verse.

Mansur ibn Abi Wa'il related that he said: Abdullah said: "Whoever swears an oath by which he takes wealth, while he is a liar in it, will meet God the Mighty and Majestic while He is angry with him." So God revealed as confirmation of that: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price﴾, to the end of the verse.

Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said: it was revealed concerning me. There was a dispute between me and a man over a well, and we brought it before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: "Your two witnesses, or his oath." I said: "He will swear, and he does not care." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:
"Whoever swears an oath by which he takes wealth, while he is a liar in it, will meet God the Exalted while He is angry with him." (Bukhari, with the wording "oath that he takes" in place of "oath he takes".)

So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jurayj said: al-Ashʿath ibn Qays and a man disputed before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning land that was in his hand, for which he had been reproached in the Jahiliyya. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do you have proof?" The man said: "No one testifies for me against al-Ashʿath ibn Qays." He said: "Then he swears." Al-Ashʿath stood and said: "I call God and you to witness that my opponent is truthful." So he returned his land to him and added to it a large amount from his own land, fearing that some of his right might remain in his hand; it became for that man's descendants after him.

Bādhān related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: it was revealed concerning Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis al-Kindi, against whom ʿAbdan ibn Ashraʿ sought a ruling. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) decided that he should take the oath. When he was about to swear, this verse was revealed. Imruʾ al-Qays refrained from swearing, admitted the right of ʿAbdan, and handed it over to him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "For you is Paradise because of it."

Mujahid and al-Shaʿbi said: a man displayed his merchandise early in the day. When it was late in the day, a man came and bargained with him. He swore: "By God, he has withheld it earlier in the day for such-and-such, and if not for the evening he would not have sold it for that." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God﴾, i.e., they exchange the covenant of God and the fulfilment of trusts ﴿and their oaths﴾, the false ones, ﴿for a small price﴾.

﴿Those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾: its bliss and its reward. ﴿And God will not speak to them﴾, speech that benefits them and gladdens them. This is what the exegetes said. Al-Mufaddal said: ﴿God will not speak to them﴾: by accepting an argument they could present.

﴿Nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾: meaning, He will not have mercy upon them, nor show compassion to them, nor do good to them, nor speak to them kindly. It is said: "so-and-so looked at so-and-so" and "looked upon him" when he showed mercy to him and did good to him.

The poet said:
So I said: look, how beautiful all the people are, to the sons of Ghullat Sadban, whom longing has wasted away.

From Abu ʿAmr al-Jawni, who said: God never looked upon a thing without having mercy on it. Even if He had decreed to look upon the people of the Fire, He would have had mercy on them; but He decreed that He would not look upon them.

ʿAbdullah ibn Kaʿb related from Abu Umama al-Khazzani that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever seizes the right of a Muslim man by his oath, God has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden Paradise to him." A man said: "Even if it is a small thing?" He said: "Even if it is a twig of arak."

Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Qurashi related from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Umama al-Khazzani, from ʿAbdullah ibn Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, and the perjurous oath (yamin al-ghamus). By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one swears an oath, even if it were on the weight of a mosquito's wing, except that it will be a stain in his heart until the Day of Resurrection."

﴿Nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾:
A man who withheld surplus water on the road, and so denied the traveler; a man who gave allegiance to a man, not giving allegiance except for worldly gain, so if he gave him what he wanted he would fulfil it, and if not he would not fulfil it; and a man who bargained over his merchandise after the afternoon prayer, then swore by God: "He has been given so much for it," and the other believed him and took it.

Al-Harith al-Aʿwar related from ʿAli (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the false oath, for it leaves the dwellings desolate of their people."

Maʿmar related regarding a man from the Banu Tamim, from Abu al-Aswad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The false oath makes the womb barren."

al-ʿAlaʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The false oath promotes the sale of goods and erases the profit."

﴿And indeed among them﴾: meaning, among the People of the Book who were mentioned before, and they are the Jews.

﴿A party﴾: a group. They are: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Abu Yasir, Huyayy, and Sabaʿa ibn ʿAmr the poet.

﴿Distorting﴾: the people of Medina read yulawwuna with the yaʾ dammed, the lam open, and the waw doubled, for intensity. Hamid read yalūna with one waw, on the intention of hamza, then he dropped the hamza and transferred its vowel to the lam. The rest read with two waws and a silent light lam. Their meanings are all the same: ﴿they twist﴾.

﴿Their tongues﴾: by distortion, deliberate and obstinate, which is what they changed of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the verse of stoning. It is said: "He twisted his tongue from such-and-such," meaning he altered it. And "he twisted the thing from what it was" when he changed it to something else. And "he twisted so-and-so from his opinion" when he turned him away from it. From this comes "procrastination by the debtor" (layy al-ghariym). The poet al-Nabigha al-Jaʿdi said:
God twisted the knowledge of the unseen away from its level, and knows what has passed and what came later.

Its parallel is His words: ﴿And if you twist or turn away...﴾, to the end of the verse.

﴿So that you may think﴾: so that you may suppose what they distorted ﴿from the Book﴾: which God sent down.

﴿And it is not from the Book﴾ ... ﴿And they speak falsely about God while they know﴾: that they are liars.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas: the verse was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians together, and those who distorted the Torah and the Gospel, and struck the Book of God, some of it against some, and attached to it what is not from it, so they dropped from it the Hanifite religion. So God the Exalted made their lie clear to the believers.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 75–85 (part 2 of 3):

﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Scripture and the wisdom and prophethood…﴾ (the verse).

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning ʿIsa (peace be upon him), ﴿that Allah should give him the Scripture﴾, meaning he should be given wisdom. It was revealed concerning the Christians of Najran.

Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAta said: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿that Allah should give him the Scripture﴾, meaning the Qur'an. The reason was that Abu Rafi al-Qurazi, from the Jews, and the chief of the Christians of Najran said: "O Muhammad, do you want us to worship you and take you as a lord?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in Allah from worshipping other than Allah, or from commanding the worship of other than Allah. It is not for this that I was sent, nor for this that I was commanded." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan said: It has reached me that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, we greet you as some of us greet one another. Shall we not prostrate to you?" He said: "It is not fitting that anyone be prostrated to besides Allah, but honour your Prophet and recognise the right of those who deserve it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning: it is not befitting for a human being, like His saying ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ [4:92], and His saying ﴿It is not for us to speak of this﴾ [24:16], meaning: it is not befitting.

The people of the meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: this lam is transposed (manqulah), and "an" carries the sense of lam, and the construction of the verse is: "It is not for a human being that he should say that." Similar to His saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾ [19:35], i.e., Allah would not take a son; and His saying ﴿It is not for a prophet to defraud﴾ [3:161], i.e., it is not for a prophet to defraud. "Al-bashar" is the entirety of the children of Adam, with no singular from its own form, like "qawm" (people) and "jaysh" (army); it is used both for the singular and the plural.

﴿that Allah should give him the Scripture and the wisdom and prophethood﴾: meaning understanding and knowledge. It is also said: the rulings from Allah, like His saying: ﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture and the wisdom and prophethood﴾ [6:89].

﴿then he should say to the people﴾: it is in the accusative as a conjunction; Mahbub related from Abu ʿAmr: "thumma yaqulu" with the nominative, as a new sentence.

﴿Be worshippers of me besides Allah﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: this is the dialect of Muzayna, who say "ʿabad" for "ʿabid" (servants).

﴿but rather be﴾: i.e., "but rather he would say: be," so the verb "say" is omitted.

﴿rabbaniyyin﴾ (godly/rabbis): they differed concerning it:
ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: be jurists and scholars.
Mujahid: jurists, but below the rabbis (ahbar). Abu Razin, Qatada and al-Suddi: wise scholars, and this is the narration of ʿAta from Ibn ʿAbbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from him: teaching jurists.
Marrah ibn Sharahil said: ʿAlqama was among the rabbaniyyin who teach people the Qur'an.
Al-Fadl ibn ʿIyad related from ʿAta ibn al-Sa'ib from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: wise and pious.
Ibn Zayd: the rulers of the people and their leaders, some of them devoted and sincere worshippers.
ʿAta: scholars, wise, appointed by Allah over His creation. Abu ʿUbayd: the Arabs did not know the word "rabbaniyyin."
Abu [ʿUbayd]: I heard a learned man say: the rabbani is the one who knows the lawful and the unlawful, the commanding and the forbidding,
and who knows the reports of the community and what was and what will be.
The historian: "Be rabbaniyyin" means: those who submit to their Lord, as if it were "fa'lani" derived from "rububiyya" (lordship).
Some of them said: it was originally "rabbi," then the alif was added for emphasis, as is the Syriac usage, then the nun was added because the alif is silent, as it is said: sanʿani, bahrani, darani.
Al-Mubarrad: the rabbaniyyin are masters of knowledge; its singular is "rabban," who inherits knowledge and trains people, i.e., teaches and reforms them and takes charge of their affairs. The alif and nun are for intensification, as they said: rayyan, ʿatshan, shabʿan, ghawthan, and nuʿsan from "nuʿas" (drowsiness), and wasnan; then the nisba ya was added to it, as is said. A poet said:
"Had I been held in the truth, the narration would have brought me down from it, and my rabbis (ahbari) would have raised me."

ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) gathered all these sayings together and said: he is the one whose knowledge is nurtured by his action.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said on the day Ibn ʿAbbas died: "The rabbani of this community has died."

﴿as you were﴾: its meaning is necessity, i.e., "because you are." Like His saying ﴿and my wife was barren﴾ [19:5], i.e., and my wife; and His saying ﴿how can we speak to one who is in the cradle as a child?﴾ [19:29], i.e., who is in the cradle a child.

﴿you teach the Scripture﴾: As-Sulami, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and the people of Kufa read "tuʿallimuna" with shadda, from "taʿlim" (teaching), and Abu ʿUbayda preferred it. The rest read "taʿlamuna" without shadda, from "ʿilm" (knowledge), and Abu Hatim preferred it. Abu ʿAmr said: its corroboration is ﴿and as you studied﴾ — he did not say "yadrusun." Al-Hasan read "tuʿallimuna" with ta and ʿayn and shadda on the lam, meaning "taʿlamuna." Abu ʿUbayda read "tudrisuna," from "adrasa yadrusu." Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "tudarrisuna," from "tadris" (teaching). The rest: "yadrusuna," from "dars," i.e., they recite; its parallel is in Surat al-Aʿraf: ﴿and they studied what is in it﴾ [7:169].

Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no believer, male or female, free or slave, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has a binding right upon him: that he learn the Qur'an and gain understanding of it." Then he recited this verse: ﴿but rather be rabbaniyyin, as you were teaching the Scripture and as you were studying﴾.

﴿And he does not command you﴾: al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, ʿAsim and Hamza read "wa la yaʾmurakum" with fatha, as a conjunction to His saying "thumma yaqula."
It is also said: it is with the hidden "an," and on this reading it is linked back to "al-bashar." The rest read with damma, as a new sentence, cut off from the first speech; this is supported by the reading of ʿAbdullah and Talha: "wa lan yaʾmurakum." Then they differed about it: most read according to its meaning, "wa la yaʾmurakum" (Allah). Ibn Jurayj said: "wa la yaʾmurakum" (Muhammad, peace be upon him). It is also said: "wa la yaʾmurakum" (the human being).

﴿that you take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾: like the saying of Quraysh and Banu Mulayh when they said: the angels are the daughters of Allah; and the Jews and Christians, when they said about the Messiah and ʿUzayr what they said.

﴿Would he command you to disbelief after you have submitted?﴾: in the form of astonishment and denial, meaning: he would not do this.

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom…﴾: Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "lamma" with a shadda on the mim; Yahya ibn Ri'ab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read with the lam genitive and the mim without shadda.
As for the rest: with fatha on the lam and no shadda on the mim. As for one who reads the lam with fatha and the mim without shadda, al-Akhfash said: it is the lam of initiation, introduced upon "ma" which is the predicate, like the speaker's saying: "Certainly Zayd is better than you." "Ma ataytukum" and what follows it is its relative clause, and its response is in His saying ﴿you shall believe in him﴾. If you wish, make the predicate of "ma" to be "from the Book of Allah." You may say "min" is superfluous, meaning: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom." Then he began: "thumma" meaning: "then there comes to you…" And if you wish, you say: ﴿then, when there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾: the lam is the lam of oath, its sense being: "By Allah, you shall surely believe in him." So it was emphasised at the beginning of the speech with the lam of emphasis, and at the end with the lam of oath.

Al-Farra said: whoever reads with fatha on the lam makes it a superfluous lam, because of His saying: when the oath falls upon a sentence, it makes that conditional act into the form of an act, and makes its response like the response of the oath. The meaning: "Whatever Scripture I have given you, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him," for the lam in His saying "you shall surely believe in him."

Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj said: this is the lam of verification (lam al-tahqiq), introduced upon "ma" of condition, as it is introduced upon "an," and its meaning is: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him." The lam in His saying "you shall surely believe in him" is the response of the condition, like His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away﴾ [17:86], and similar.

Al-Kisa'i said: "la tu'minunna" is connected to the first speech, and the response of the condition is in His saying: ﴿Then whoever turns away after that﴾. Whoever reads with kasra on the lam, it is the lam of annexation (idafa), introduced upon "ma" meaning "that which": "that which I have given you," meaning: the covenant of the prophets was taken for the sake of what is before them of Scripture and wisdom; "then, when there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him," after the covenant, because the taking of the covenant is equivalent to making one swear. It is as we say in speech: "I took your pledge that you would do such and such," as if you had said: "I made you swear that you would do it."

The author of al-Nazm said: whoever reads with kasra on the lam, it has the meaning of "after" (baʿda), i.e., after what I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, like the saying of al-Nabigha:
"I thought the signs of her camp had been effaced, so I recognised them after six years, and this year is the seventh."
I.e., after six years. Whoever doubles the mim, its meaning is "when I gave you" (hina ataytukum), by His saying: ﴿ataytukum﴾.

The people of Kufa read "ataynakum" in the plural of majesty; the others read "ataytukum" in the singular, and this is the preferred reading for agreement with the script, like His saying: ﴿and I am with you﴾ [3:81]. The statement is coherent in the verse on the three modes of its construction: (And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets).

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of this verse. A group said: the covenant was taken from the prophets only that each should confirm the others, and that some should command belief in others; this is the meaning of "confirmation" in the verse, and this is the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Qatada, al-Hasan and al-Suddi, supported by the apparent sense of the verse.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Allah did not send any prophet, from Adam and onward, except that He took from him the covenant concerning Muhammad (ﷺ), and commanded him to take the covenant from his people: ﴿you shall surely believe in him, and surely support him﴾, and that if he were sent while they were alive, they would surely support him.

Others said: the covenant was taken from the People of the Book, among whom the prophets were sent; this is the saying of Mujahid and al-Rabi.

Mujahid said: this is a mixing from the Book, and it is from the reading of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book." They said: do you not see His saying: ﴿then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾? Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent only to the People of the Book, not to the prophets.

Some said: the covenant was taken from the prophets and their nations [that they would surely believe in him]; the prophets are singled out from mention of the nations, because taking the covenant from the leader is an indication that it was taken from the followers. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, and this is closer to the correct view.

Allah said: ﴿Do you acknowledge and accept My covenant on that terms?﴾ — meaning: and do you accept on that My covenant, like His saying: ﴿If you are given this, then take it﴾ [5:41], i.e., accept it; and His saying: ﴿no ransom will be accepted from it﴾, i.e., no ransom will be accepted; and His saying: ﴿He takes the charities﴾, i.e., He accepts them. ﴿They said: We acknowledge.﴾

Allah said: ﴿So bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses﴾ against you and against them.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "fa-ashhadu": meaning "then know." Al-Zajjaj said: "fa-ashhadu," i.e., then make clear, because the witness is the one who identifies the claim of the claimant; and Allah's witness to the prophets is the making clear of the matter of their prophethood through signs and miracles. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: Allah said to the angels: "bear witness against them," so it is a reference to something not mentioned.

﴿Whoever turns away after that﴾ — after the acknowledgment and the testimony — ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾: the sinners, who depart from faith.

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?…﴾ (the verse).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The People of the Book brought their disputes to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), each group claiming that it was closer to his religion. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Both groups are free from the religion of Ibrahim." They became angry and said: "By Allah, we will not accept your judgment nor follow your religion." So Allah revealed: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾

It is the reading of al-Hasan, Humayd, Ya'qub, Salam, Sahl and Safwan with the ya', because of His saying: ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. Abu ʿAmr read "yabghuna" with ya' and "turja'un" with ta', saying: because the first is specific and the second is general, so he differentiated between them for their difference in meaning. The rest read with ta' in both, in address, because of His saying: ﴿whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom﴾.

﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾: "aslama" means submitted and complied; "taw'an" is compliance and following with ease, from their saying: "a horse that is taw' al-'inan," i.e., obedient to the rein. "Karhan" is what is with hardship and the soul's refusal. "Karhan" with damma on the kaf; both are verbal nouns placed in the position of a circumstantial clause, as if He said: "And to Him submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, obedient and unwilling."

They differed concerning His saying "ta'an" and "karhan":
It was narrated that Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning His saying: ﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾, said: "The angels obeyed Him in the heavens, and the Ansar and ʿAbd al-Qays obeyed Him on the earth."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my companions, for my companions embraced Islam out of fear of Allah, and people embraced it out of fear of the sword."

Al-Hasan and al-Mufaddal said: "taw'" is for the people of the heavens specifically; as for the people of the earth, some embraced Islam willingly and some unwillingly.

Ibn ʿAbbas: their worship of Allah, all of them, willingly and unwillingly, and submission to Him.

Al-Rabi, from Abu al-ʿAliya, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾, said: Every child of Adam acknowledged against himself that Allah is my Lord and I am His servant; this is the Islam which, had he remained upon it, would have been [his]; but when he spoke it, it became a proof against him. Then he associated others in worship; this is the one who submitted unwillingly. And among them is one who testified that Allah is my Lord and I am His servant, then made his worship sincere; this is the one who submitted willingly. Al-Dahhak said: this is when the covenant was taken from them and they acknowledged it.

Mujahid: "taw'an" is the shade of the believer, and "karhan" is the shade of the disbeliever, supported by His saying: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ [13:15], and His saying: ﴿whose shadows turn from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah﴾ [16:48].

Al-Sha'bi: it is their seeking refuge in Him when they are in distress, supported by His saying: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [29:65].

Qatada: the believer submits willingly and the disbeliever unwillingly. As for the believer, he submits willingly, so that benefits him and it is accepted from him. As for the disbeliever, he submits unwillingly at the time of calamity and seeing [the punishment], so it is not accepted from him and does not benefit him, supported by His saying: ﴿Their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [40:85].

al-Kalbi: "taw'an": those who were born in Islam; "karhan": those compelled into Islam.

ʿIkrima: "karhan": one whom the [proof] compelled to monotheism, supported by His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: Allah﴾ [43:87], and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say: Allah﴾ [29:61].

Ibn Kaysan: "And to Him submitted," i.e., submitted are whoever is in the heavens and the earth to what He has ordained for them and fashioned them upon, and whatever happens to them; they do not resist Him, whether they dislike that or love it.

﴿And to Him they will be returned﴾ [3:83].

Al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, said: When one of your animals becomes unruly or is skittish, let him recite this verse into its ear.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 75–85 (part 3 of 3):

"Say: We believe in God..." up to His words, "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion..." — the verse was revealed concerning twelve men who apostatized from Islam, left Medina, and joined Mecca as disbelievers. Among them were: al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, brother of al-Hallas ibn Suwayd; Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq al-Ansari; Miqyas ibn Subabah al-Laythi; Abdullah ibn Unays ibn Khatal from the Banu Taym ibn Murrah; Wajwaj ibn al-Aslat; and Abu Amir ibn al-Nu'man. God revealed about them: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾.

And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you. The verse: most exegetes (tafsir) said: this verse was revealed concerning all the Jews. God the Exalted informed that among them there is trustworthiness and treachery. The qintar is an expression for a large amount of wealth, and the dinar is an expression for a small amount of wealth.

If it is said: what is the benefit of this information, when we know that people have always been this way, some trustworthy and some treacherous?

We say: it is a warning from God to the believers not to entrust them with their wealth, or to be deceived by them, because of their permitting the wealth of the believers.

This is like what is related in the report: "Do you refrain from mentioning the wicked person? Mention him with what is in him, so that people may beware of him."

Some of them said: the trustworthiness refers to those among them who embraced Islam, and the treachery refers to those among them who did not embrace Islam.

Muqatil said: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾: Abdullah ibn Salam. A man deposited with him one thousand two hundred ounces of gold, and he returned it to him, so God praised him.

﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾: this refers to Makhdh ibn Azura, because a man from Quraysh deposited a dinar with him and he betrayed him.

In some exegeses: the one who returns the trust in this verse are the Christians, and those who do not return it are the Jews.

Regarding His words ﴿tamanhu﴾ there are two readings. Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli read it as ﴿timinhu﴾ with a kasra on the tා (taʾ), and this is the dialect of Bakr and Tamim. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿ma laka la timinna﴾.

The common reading is ﴿tamanhu﴾ with an alif. The word dinar originally was dannar, and one of the two nuns was replaced by a yaʾ, seeking lightness because of its frequent use. Evidence for this is that you pluralize it as dananir.

Regarding His words ﴿yuaddihi﴾ and its counterparts there are five readings. Abu ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, ʿAsim and Hamza all read them with the hāʾ silent. Abu Jaʿfar and Yaʿqub read it with the hāʾ short and kasra. Salam read it with damma and short. al-Zuhri read it with damma and lengthened. The others read it with kasra and lengthened. As for the one who makes the hāʾ silent, many grammarians criticized him, because jazm (apocopation) does not apply to the hāʾ when the letter before it is moved, and the hāʾ is a pronoun, and pronouns do not take jazm.

Al-Farrāʾ said: this is the view of some Arabs who apply jazm to the hāʾ when the letter before it is moved, so they say: ḍarabtuhu ḍarban shadīdan, just as they silence the mīm of antum and qumtum, though its original is raf.

And he recited:
When he saw there was neither a bed nor a feast, he inclined to a tamarisk on a dune and lay down.

Some said: the silencing of the hāʾ was permitted in these positions because it was placed in the position of jazm, which is the omitted yaʾ. As for the one who reads with a short vowel, he has been satisfied with the damma instead of the waw and with the kasra instead of the yaʾ. Al-Farrāʾ recited:
I am the son of Kilab and the son of Aws, so whoever has a veil covering it, then I am revealed.

And Sibawayh recited:
If he is lean or fat, he will make his eyes closed to himself.

And whoever lengthens the hāʾ does so according to the original, because when the letter was weak it was strengthened by the waw in damma and by the yaʾ in kasra.

Sibawayh said: after the masculine hāʾ comes a waw, just as after the feminine hāʾ comes an alif. And whoever reads the hāʾ with damma does so according to the original, because the original of the hāʾ is damma, like huwa, and humā and hum. And whoever reads with kasra, he says it is because before it is a yaʾ, even if it is omitted, or because what precedes it is kasra.

﴿Except what you constantly stand over﴾: Yahya, Thabit, al-Aʿmash and Talha read it with kasra on the dāl, and the rest with damma.

Whoever reads with damma, it is from dāma, yadūmu, and it is a dialect of al-ʿĀliya. Whoever reads with kasra has two possibilities. Some said: it is also from dāma yadūmu, but on the pattern faʿila, yafʿalu, saying dimta tadūmu like mitta tamūtu. This was said by al-Akhfash. And there is no triliteral verb of the pattern faʿila-yafʿulu (with kasra in the past and damma in the present) from a sound final radical, except fadila, yafdulu, and niʿma, yanʿamu. From a weak verb: mittu, amūtu, and dimtu, adūmu, and these are the dialect of Tamim.

Most scholars said: from karuma, yakrumu, fa'ala, yaf'alu, like khāfa, yakhāfu, and hāba, yahābu.

﴿Standing﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "persistently." Mujahid: "constantly." Saʿid ibn Jubayr: "steadfastly." Qatada: "standing, insisting." al-Suddi: "standing over his head."

Al-ʿUtaybi: "persistently, by insistence." Its origin is that one who demands a thing stands over it, and one who abandons it sits away from it. The indication of His words ﴿a community standing﴾ is: acting by the command of God, not abandoning it.

Abu Rawq: he admits what was given to him, as long as you are standing over his head. If you ask him for it at the time you give it to him, he returns it to you; but if you give him time and delay it, he denies it and takes it away. That is permitting what is forbidden, and treachery.

﴿That is because they say: there is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered﴾: meaning, regarding the Arabs. Its parallel is ﴿He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves﴾. ﴿Blame﴾: sin and fault. Its evidence is His words ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers﴾. This is because the Jews said: there is no fault upon us in withholding the wealth of the Arabs, since God has made it lawful for us, for they are not upon our religion. They used to permit the oppression of those who opposed them in their religion, saying: God did not make for them any sanctity in our Book.

Al-Kalbi: The Jews said: all wealth was ours, and whatever is in the hands of the Arabs of it is ours, and they only oppressed us and seized it from us unjustly, so there is no blame upon us in taking it from them.

Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil: The Jews made contracts with men from the Muslims in the Jahiliyya. When they embraced Islam, they demanded from them the value of their wealth. They said: you have no right against us, and we have no obligation to you; you have abandoned the religion you were upon, and the covenant between us and you has ended. They claimed that they found this in their Book. So God refuted them, saying:
﴿and they speak falsely about God while they know﴾.

In a hadith: when the verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The enemies of God have lied. Everything from the Jahiliyya is under my feet except trust, for it is returned to the righteous and the wicked."

Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani related from Sasaʿa: a man asked Ibn ʿAbbas, saying: "We obtain in raids from the wealth of the people of Medina a chicken or a sheep." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "What do they say?" He said: "They say: there is no harm upon us." He said: "This is like what the People of the Book said: ﴿there is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered﴾. When they pay the jizya (poll tax), your wealth becomes lawful for you only with their willing consent." Then God the Exalted said in refutation of them:

﴿Yes﴾: meaning, it is not as they said. ﴿But whoever fulfills his covenant﴾: that which he covenanted with God in the Torah, of belief in Muhammad and the Quran, and returning trusts.

The pronoun in His words ﴿his covenant﴾ refers to God, the Mighty and Majestic, since He was mentioned in His words ﴿and they speak falsely about God﴾. It is permissible that it refers to ﴿fulfills﴾.

﴿And fears God﴾: from disbelief, treachery and breaking the covenant.

﴿Indeed, God loves the righteous﴾: those who have this description.

From al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he prays and fasts and claims he is a believer: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

From Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is entrusted with a trust and returns it, while he could have not returned it, God will marry him to the wide-eyed houris as many as he wishes."

Al-Hasan from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the prophets, the truthful ones and the martyrs."

Wahb from Hudhayfa, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) related to me two hadiths; I saw one of them while I awaited the other. He related to us: "Trust was sent down into the root of men's hearts, and the Quran was sent down, so learn from the Quran and learn from the source of the Sunna."

Then he related to us about their lifting, saying: "A man sleeps a sleep, and trust is removed from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a blister, like a hot coal you roll on your foot, so you see it swollen and there is nothing in it." Then Hudhayfa took a pebble and rolled it over his shin. He said: "People will then trade with one another, and hardly anyone will return a trust, until it is said: so-and-so is a trustworthy man; and until it is said of a man: how strong he is, how intelligent he is, how witty he is, while there is not in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith. There came upon me a time when I did not care whom I dealt with; if he was a Muslim, his Islam would return him to me; if he was a Jew or Christian, his employer would return him to me. But today, I would not deal with any of you except so-and-so and so-and-so."

It has been said: the perfection of religion is abandoning treachery, and the greatest crime is betraying people.

﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price﴾: they differed regarding the revelation of this verse.

Ikrima said: it was revealed concerning Abu Rafi, Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab and others, leaders of the Jews, who wrote what God had covenanted with them in the Torah regarding Muhammad (ﷺ) and altered it, and wrote with their hands something other than it, and swore that it was from God, so that the bribes and provisions they had from their followers would not escape them.

Al-Kalbi said: some scholars of the Jews, who were in poverty and possessed some share of knowledge of the Torah, were struck by a year of drought. They came to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf seeking a loan from him. Kaʿb asked them: "Do you know that this man is the Messenger of God in your Book?" They said: "Yes. What do you know of him?" He said: "No." They said: "We testify that he is the servant of God and His Messenger." Kaʿb said: "You have lied against me. I want to feed you and clothe you, but God has deprived you of much good."

They said: "It was made to appear similar to us. Wait, until we meet him." He said: "So they went and wrote a description other than his description. Then they came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and concealed it. Then they returned to Kaʿb and said: 'We saw the Messenger of God and came to him, and he is not the description that was described to us.' And they brought out what they had written." Kaʿb was delighted by that, and by their deceit. So God the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what God has sent down of the Book and sell it for a small price﴾, to the end of the verse.

Mansur ibn Abi Wa'il related that he said: Abdullah said: "Whoever swears an oath by which he takes wealth, while he is a liar in it, will meet God the Mighty and Majestic while He is angry with him." So God revealed as confirmation of that: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price﴾, to the end of the verse.

Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said: it was revealed concerning me. There was a dispute between me and a man over a well, and we brought it before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: "Your two witnesses, or his oath." I said: "He will swear, and he does not care." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:
"Whoever swears an oath by which he takes wealth, while he is a liar in it, will meet God the Exalted while He is angry with him." (Bukhari, with the wording "oath that he takes" in place of "oath he takes".)

So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jurayj said: al-Ashʿath ibn Qays and a man disputed before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning land that was in his hand, for which he had been reproached in the Jahiliyya. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do you have proof?" The man said: "No one testifies for me against al-Ashʿath ibn Qays." He said: "Then he swears." Al-Ashʿath stood and said: "I call God and you to witness that my opponent is truthful." So he returned his land to him and added to it a large amount from his own land, fearing that some of his right might remain in his hand; it became for that man's descendants after him.

Bādhān related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: it was revealed concerning Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis al-Kindi, against whom ʿAbdan ibn Ashraʿ sought a ruling. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) decided that he should take the oath. When he was about to swear, this verse was revealed. Imruʾ al-Qays refrained from swearing, admitted the right of ʿAbdan, and handed it over to him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "For you is Paradise because of it."

Mujahid and al-Shaʿbi said: a man displayed his merchandise early in the day. When it was late in the day, a man came and bargained with him. He swore: "By God, he has withheld it earlier in the day for such-and-such, and if not for the evening he would not have sold it for that." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God﴾, i.e., they exchange the covenant of God and the fulfilment of trusts ﴿and their oaths﴾, the false ones, ﴿for a small price﴾.

﴿Those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾: its bliss and its reward. ﴿And God will not speak to them﴾, speech that benefits them and gladdens them. This is what the exegetes said. Al-Mufaddal said: ﴿God will not speak to them﴾: by accepting an argument they could present.

﴿Nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾: meaning, He will not have mercy upon them, nor show compassion to them, nor do good to them, nor speak to them kindly. It is said: "so-and-so looked at so-and-so" and "looked upon him" when he showed mercy to him and did good to him.

The poet said:
So I said: look, how beautiful all the people are, to the sons of Ghullat Sadban, whom longing has wasted away.

From Abu ʿAmr al-Jawni, who said: God never looked upon a thing without having mercy on it. Even if He had decreed to look upon the people of the Fire, He would have had mercy on them; but He decreed that He would not look upon them.

ʿAbdullah ibn Kaʿb related from Abu Umama al-Khazzani that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever seizes the right of a Muslim man by his oath, God has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden Paradise to him." A man said: "Even if it is a small thing?" He said: "Even if it is a twig of arak."

Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Qurashi related from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Umama al-Khazzani, from ʿAbdullah ibn Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, and the perjurous oath (yamin al-ghamus). By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one swears an oath, even if it were on the weight of a mosquito's wing, except that it will be a stain in his heart until the Day of Resurrection."

﴿Nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾:
A man who withheld surplus water on the road, and so denied the traveler; a man who gave allegiance to a man, not giving allegiance except for worldly gain, so if he gave him what he wanted he would fulfil it, and if not he would not fulfil it; and a man who bargained over his merchandise after the afternoon prayer, then swore by God: "He has been given so much for it," and the other believed him and took it.

Al-Harith al-Aʿwar related from ʿAli (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the false oath, for it leaves the dwellings desolate of their people."

Maʿmar related regarding a man from the Banu Tamim, from Abu al-Aswad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The false oath makes the womb barren."

al-ʿAlaʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The false oath promotes the sale of goods and erases the profit."

﴿And indeed among them﴾: meaning, among the People of the Book who were mentioned before, and they are the Jews.

﴿A party﴾: a group. They are: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Abu Yasir, Huyayy, and Sabaʿa ibn ʿAmr the poet.

﴿Distorting﴾: the people of Medina read yulawwuna with the yaʾ dammed, the lam open, and the waw doubled, for intensity. Hamid read yalūna with one waw, on the intention of hamza, then he dropped the hamza and transferred its vowel to the lam. The rest read with two waws and a silent light lam. Their meanings are all the same: ﴿they twist﴾.
