I know of no place on the face of the earth [where it is recorded for one who] has in it the drink of the scholars and the prayer-place of the righteous, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where anyone who touches anything there has it be an expiation of sins, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where, when one makes supplication, the angels say "Amin, amin" for him, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth [.......] [Words illegible in the manuscript.]

except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where whoever looks at the Kaʿbah without circumambulating or praying has recorded for him the worship of a lifetime and the fasting of a lifetime, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth to which all the prophets came [and] to which they went forth, except Makkah. I know of no place where people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, among the prophets, the righteous, the jurists and the worshippers, men and women, as from Makkah; that is, they will be gathered while they are safe. I know of no place on the face of the earth where, every day, the spirit and fragrance of Paradise descend as they descend upon Makkah, may God protect it. (In full in Fada'il Makkah by al-Basri, with variation: 20.)

﴿Blessed﴾: accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾: because it is the qiblah of the believers. ﴿In it are clear signs﴾:

Ibn ʿAbbas recited: "a clear sign" (āyah bayyinah).

﴿The Station of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe﴾ [.......] [A portion fell out of the original manuscript, from verse 97 to verse 102.] ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so that by His favour you became brothers﴾.

[Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Habib related to us from Marthad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Muzani, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUsaylah al-Sunabihi, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I was among those who attended the First Pledge of al-ʿAqabah. We were twelve men, and we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the pledge of women, and that was before fighting was prescribed. [The pledge was] that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and feet, nor disobey him in what is good. "If you fulfil it, then for you is Paradise; and if you fall into any of that..."] [Missing in the manuscript; what is in square brackets is supplemented from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/88.]

"...and if you are punished for it in this world, that is its expiation for him; and if you conceal it until the Day of Resurrection, your affair is with God: if He wills, He will punish you, and if He wills, He will forgive you." He said: That was before fighting was prescribed upon them. When the group departed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent with them Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr ibn Hashim ibn ʿAbd Manaf, and commanded him to recite the Qur'an to them, teach them Islam, and give them understanding of the religion. Mus'ab was called "the reciter" (al-Muqri') in Madinah; he was the first reciter in Madinah. He lodged with As'ad ibn Zurarah.

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to Usayd ibn Hudayr: "Go to these two men who have come to our dwelling to mislead our weak ones, and drive them away. As'ad is my maternal cousin; were it not for that, I would have dealt with you myself." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr were the two chiefs of their people, from the Banu al-Ashhal, and both were polytheists. Usayd ibn Hudayr took his spear and came to Mus'ab and As'ad, who were sitting in an orchard. When As'ad ibn Zurarah saw him, he said to Mus'ab: "This is the chief of his people, and he has come to you, by God. Be sincere toward God concerning him."

Mus'ab said: "If he sits, we will speak to him." So he stood over them, scowling, and said: "What brought you to us? You mislead our weak ones. Leave us alone, if you have any need for yourselves." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter, accept it; and if you dislike it, we will stop what you dislike." He said: "You have been fair." Then he planted his spear and sat with them, and Mus'ab spoke to him about Islam and recited the Qur'an to him.

He said: "By God, we recognised Islam in his face before he spoke, in its brightness and its ease." Then he said: "How excellent and beautiful this is! What do you do when you wish to enter this religion?" They said: "You bathe, purify your clothing, testify to the testimony of truth, and then pray two rakʿahs." So he stood, bathed, purified his clothing, testified to the testimony of truth, then stood and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he said to them: "Behind me is a man who, if he follows you, none of his people will remain behind him. I will send him to you now: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

Then he took his spear and went back to Sa'd and his people, who were sitting in their assembly. When Sa'd ibn Mu'adh saw him approaching, he said: "I swear by God, Usayd has come to you with a face other than the one with which he left you." When he stood before the assembly, Sa'd said to him: "What have you done?" He said: "I spoke with the two men. By God, I saw no harm in them, and I forbade them, but they said: 'We will do nothing except what you like.'"

The Hadith tradition says that the clan of Banu Harithah set out to Asad ibn Zurarah to kill him, because they had learned that he was your maternal cousin, intending to humiliate you. Sa'd rose in anger, hastening toward what he had been told, took the spear from him, and said: "By God, I do not think you have achieved anything." When he saw that the two of them were calm, he realized that Usayd had only wanted to hear from them. So he stood over them, reviling them, and then said to Asad ibn Zurarah: "O Abu Umamah, were it not for the kinship between me and you, you would not have done this to me. You come to our house with what we dislike." He had said to Mus'ab: "The lord of his people has come to you, by God. If he follows you, not one of his people will oppose you." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter and desire it, accept it; and if you dislike it, we have spared you what you dislike." Sa'd said: "You have been fair." Then he planted the spear and sat down. He was presented with Islam and the Qur'an was recited to him. They said: "By God, we recognised Islam in his face before he spoke, in its radiance and its ease." Then he said to them: "What will you do when you have embraced Islam and entered this religion?" They said: "You will wash, purify your garment, bear witness to the truth, then pray two rak'ahs." So he stood, washed, purified his garment, bore witness to the truth, and performed two rak'ahs. Then he took his spear and went purposefully to the assembly of his people, with Usayd ibn Hudayr accompanying him. When his people saw him approaching, they said: "We swear by God, Sa'd has returned to you with a face other than that with which he left you." When he stood before them, he said: "O Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, how do you regard my standing among you?" They said: "You are our lord, the best of us in judgement and the most blessed in counsel." He said: "Then the speech of your men and your women is forbidden to me until you believe in God and His Messenger." So no man or woman in the house of 'Abd al-Ashhal remained at evening except as a Muslim or Muslimah. Asad and Mus'ab returned to the house of Asad ibn Zurarah, and he remained there calling people to Islam, until no house of the Ansar remained except that it had men and women who were Muslims, except for Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, Hatmah, Wa'il and Waqif [and they are the "Awsallah", and they are from Aws ibn Harithah, and that is why] [[Addition from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/90.]] among whom was Abu Qays the poet, and they used to listen to him and obey him. So he held them back from Islam until the Prophet ﷺ emigrated to Madinah, and Badr, Uhud and the Trench passed.

They said: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr returned to Makkah, and with him went seventy men of the Ansar who were Muslims, together with the pilgrims of their people who were polytheists, until they reached Makkah. They arranged with the Messenger of God ﷺ a meeting at the 'Aqabah in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and this was the Second Pledge of 'Aqabah.

Ka'b ibn Malik said, having been present at it: When they had finished the Hajj, and on the night when the Messenger of God ﷺ had appointed for us, and with us was 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, Abu Jabir, we informed him. We concealed our affair from those of our people who were polytheists, and we spoke with him and said: "O Jabir, you are a chief among our chiefs and a noble among our nobles, and we fear that you will be turned away from what you are in, so that we become firewood for the Fire tomorrow." We invited him to Islam, and he embraced Islam. We informed him of the appointment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he attended the 'Aqabah with us, and he was pious. We spent that night in our camps, until when a third of the night had passed we went out to the appointment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, slipping away stealthily like sand-grouse, until we gathered in the ravine at the 'Aqabah, seventy men, and with us two of our women: Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm 'Ammarah, one of the women of Banu al-Najjar, and Asma' bint 'Amr ibn 'Adi, one of the women of Banu Salamah, who was Umm Mani'. We gathered in the ravine awaiting the Messenger of God ﷺ until he came, and with him his uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who on that day was upon the religion of his people, except that he loved to be present at the affair of his nephew and to secure it for him. When we had sat down, the first to speak was al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "O assembly of the Khazraj." The Arabs used to call this tribe of the Ansar, the Khazraj of Khazraj and Aws: "Muhammad is one of us, as you know. We have protected him from our people, from those who share our opinion, and he is in honour among his people and secure in his land. But he has refused except to join you and go to you. If you see that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, and will protect him against whoever opposes him, then you and what you have undertaken; and if you see that you will hand him over and abandon him after going out to you, then leave him now, for he is in honour and security."

He said: We said: "We have heard what you said. Speak, O Messenger of God, and take for yourself and for your Lord whatever you wish."

He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ spoke, recited the Qur'an, called to God, encouraged Islam, and said: "I pledge to you that you will protect me from what you protect your women from."

He said: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur took his hand and said: "By the One who sent you with truth, we will protect you from what we protect our wives from. So pledge to us, O Messenger of God, for we are men of war and men of the armour, which we have inherited from elder to elder."

He said: Then the speech was interrupted, while al-Bara' was speaking to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan said: "O Messenger of God, between us and the people there are ties," meaning the Jews, "and we are about to cut them. Is it possible that if we do this, and then God makes you victorious, you will return to your people and leave us?" The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled, then said: "Rather, blood for blood and destruction for destruction. You are of me and I am of you. I will fight whoever you fight, and make peace with whoever you make peace with."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Bring out to me twelve chiefs from among you, as guarantors over their people for what is in them, as the disciples were guarantors for 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him." [84] [[Al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 1/223.]] So they brought out twelve chiefs: nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws.

'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah said: When the people gathered for the pledge to the Messenger of God ﷺ, al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah al-Ansari said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, do you know what you are pledging to this man? You are pledging to fight the black and the red. If you think that when your wealth is ruined and your nobles killed you will hand him over, then from now on it is, by God, a disgrace in this world and the next. But if you think that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, despite the ruin of wealth and the killing of nobles, then what is our reward for this, O Messenger of God, if we are faithful?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "Extend your hand." He extended his hand and they pledged to him. The first to strike his hand was al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, then the people followed.

He said: When we had pledged to the Messenger of God ﷺ, Satan shouted from the top of the 'Aqabah with the loudest voice I ever heard: "O people of the Jabajib!" [[al-Jabajib here means the dwellings; and in al-Sihah: the jabajibah is the plural of jabajib: a basket of leather used to carry earth, called a "qaffah". See Lisan al-'Arab: 8/291.]] "Do you have a share in Mudhammam? The Sabi'ah with him have gathered to fight you."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "This is, by God, the goatherd of the 'Aqabah. Listen, O enemy of God! By God, I will attend to you." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Return to your camps." Al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah said to him: "By the One who sent you with truth, if you wish, we will fall upon the people of Mina tomorrow with our swords." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "We have not been commanded to that, but return to your camps."

He said: We returned to our resting places and slept upon them until morning. Then the nobles of Quraysh came to us in the morning, and came to our dwellings and said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, we have heard that you have come to our companion here to take him out from among us and pledge to fight us. By God, there is no tribe of the Arabs more hateful to us than that war should break out between us and them through you." He said: Then there arose from there some of our polytheist people, swearing by God that none of this had happened and that they knew nothing of it. They spoke the truth, for they did not know. Some of us looked at others. The people stood up, and among them was al-Harith ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, wearing two new sandals. He said: I said to him a word as though I wished to share it with the people in what they had said: "O Abu Jabir, can you not get a young man of Quraysh like these sandals of mine?" [hmm]

He said: al-Harith heard it, took them off his feet, threw them to me, and said: "By God, you will wear them." Abu Jabir said: "By God, you have angered the young man, so return his sandals to him." He said: I said: "I will not return them." He said: "By God, it is a truce. By God, if he is truthful, I will plunder him."

He said: Then Abu Jabir went back to Madinah, and they had strengthened the covenant. When they reached it, they openly professed Islam there, and that reached Quraysh, who harmed the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to his companions: "God has made for you brothers and a home in which you will be secure." [85] [[In full in Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/88 to 94, and Musnad Ahmad: 3/462.]]

So he commanded them to emigrate to Madinah and to join their brothers, the Ansar. Among those who emigrated was Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, then 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah with his wife Layla bint Abi Khaythamah, then 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh. Then the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ followed one another in succession to Madinah, while the Messenger of God ﷺ remained awaiting permission to emigrate until he was permitted. He came to Madinah, and God gathered the people of Madinah, Aws and Khazraj, through Islam, set right their relations through His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, removed the old enmity from them, and united them. This is His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, O assembly of the Ansar, when you were enemies before Islam, and He joined your hearts, so you became by His favour brothers﴾ — "so you became": you became. Its parallel is His saying in al-Ma'idah: ﴿So he became among the losers﴾ [[al-Ma'idah: 30.]] and His saying: ﴿So he became among the regretful﴾ [[al-Ma'idah: 31.]], and in Ha Mim al-Sajdah: ﴿So you became among the losers﴾ [[Fussilat: 23.]], and in al-Kahf: ﴿Or its water becomes sunk into the earth﴾ [[al-Kahf: 41.]].

﴿By His favour﴾: by the blessing of Islam. ﴿Brothers﴾: in religion and in alliance. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ [[al-Hujurat: 10.]].

From Abu Sa'id, mawla of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Kurayz, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
"Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not undercut one another in trade. Be, O servants of God, brothers. The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, nor forsake him, nor despise him. Piety is here," and he pointed to his chest with his hand, "It is enough evil for a man that he despise his Muslim brother." [86] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/288, 67, 277.]]

From Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it strengthening another," and he interlaced his fingers. [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/123.]]

From al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said to the Prophet ﷺ: "The believers are like one man."

He said: "The believers are like one man: if his head aches, the rest of him responds with fever and sleeplessness." [87] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/277.]]

﴿And you were, O assembly of Aws and Khazraj, on the brink of a pit of the Fire﴾. The rajiz said:
"We dug for the pilgrims a well, with a green growth over its edge."

The meaning of the verse: you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, with nothing between you and falling into it except that you die upon your disbelief. ﴿So He saved you from it﴾ by faith. He said: It reached us that a Bedouin heard Ibn 'Abbas reciting this verse, and said: "By God, He did not save them from it, for he wants to make them fall into it." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Take him away; he is not a jurist." ﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, that you may be guided.﴾

**Al-Tha'labi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 93–103 (Part 1 of 2)**

﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾, and so on.

Abu Rawq and al-Kalbi said: This was when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am upon the religion of Ibrahim." The Jews said: "How can that be, when you eat camel meat and drink its milk?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That was lawful for Ibrahim, and we make it lawful." The Jews said: "Everything we have made unlawful today was unlawful for Nuh and Ibrahim, and it remained so until it reached us." So God the Exalted revealed, refuting them: ﴿All the food made lawful to you today was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾

﴿except what Israel [i.e. Ya'qub], that is Ya'qub, had forbidden to himself before the Torah was sent down﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning that food. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Abu Mijlaz said: it was the veins (ʿuruq). The reason for this was that Ya'qub (peace be upon him) suffered from ʿirq al-nasa (sciatica), and this was the origin of his ailment. This is what Juwaybir and Muqatil related from al-Dahhak: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq had vowed that if God granted him twelve sons and he came to Bayt al-Maqdis in good health, he would slaughter the youngest of them. An angel met him and said: "O Ya'qub, you are a strong man. Are you willing to wrestle?" He wrestled with him, and neither could throw the other. Then the angel pressed him with a squeeze, and ʿirq al-nasa afflicted him because of it. Then he said: "If I wished, I could have thrown you, but I squeezed you with this squeeze because you had vowed that if you came to Bayt al-Maqdis in good health you would slaughter your youngest son. God has made for you a way out through this squeeze." When Ya'qub arrived there, he wanted to slaughter his son, but he forgot the angel's words. The angel came to him and said: "I squeezed you with that squeeze as a way out, and you have fulfilled your vow, so there is no way for you to [harm] your son."

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: Ya'qub (peace be upon him) came from Harran, wishing to go to Bayt al-Maqdis, when he fled from his brother ʿIs, who was a hot-tempered and strong man. He met an angel, and Ya'qub thought he was a thief, so he tried to throw him down. The angel squeezed Ya'qub's thigh and then ascended to heaven while Ya'qub watched him. Ya'qub was then afflicted with ʿirq al-nasa and suffered a severe trial because of it. He could not sleep at night because of the pain, and he would cry out (zuqa'), that is, shout. So Ya'qub (peace be upon him) swore that if God healed him, he would not eat any vein, nor any food containing a vein. He therefore made it unlawful for himself, and his sons began to seek out the veins and remove them from the meat. (Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 18/72.) Abu al-ʿAliyah, ʿAta', Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: what was made unlawful was the flesh of camels and their milk.

Shahr ibn Hawshab related from Ibn ʿAbbas that a group came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, tell us which food Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was sent down?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I call you to witness by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa: Do you know that Ya'qub fell severely ill, and his sickness lasted long upon him? So he vowed to God that if God healed him from his sickness, he would forbid himself the food and drink he loved most. The food he loved most was camel flesh, and the drink he loved most was its milk." (Musnad Ahmad: 1/273, with slight variation.) They said: "O God, yes."

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ʿirq al-nasa afflicted Ya'qub, the physicians prescribed that he avoid camel meat, so Ya'qub made camel meat unlawful for himself. The Jews said: "We have made camel meat unlawful for ourselves because Ya'qub made it unlawful, and God sent down its prohibition in the Torah." So God revealed this verse.

al-Hasan said: Israel made the flesh of the camel unlawful for himself as an act of worship to God the Mighty and Majestic. He then asked his Lord to permit it to him, but God made it unlawful for his offspring. ʿIkrimah said: Israel made unlawful for himself the appendix of the liver, the two kidneys, and the fat, except what is on the back. Layth related from Mujahid, who said: Israel made the flesh of livestock unlawful for himself.

Then the exegetes differed concerning this food that was made unlawful for Israel after the Torah was sent down. al-Suddi said: When God sent down the Torah, He made unlawful for them what they had been making unlawful before it, following their father Ya'qub (peace be upon him). ʿAtiyyah said: It was unlawful for them only because Israel had made it unlawful for them. That was because Israel said, when ʿirq al-nasa afflicted him: "By God, if God heals me from it, none of my sons shall eat it." And it was not unlawful for them in the Torah.

al-Kalbi said: God did not make it unlawful for them in the Torah. Rather, He made it unlawful for them after the Torah because of their wrongdoing and disbelief. Whenever the Children of Israel committed a great sin, God made some good food unlawful for them, or sent upon them a punishment (rijz), which is death. This is His saying: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who became Jews, We made unlawful for them good things that had been lawful for them﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 160), and His saying: ﴿And for those who became Jews We made unlawful every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We made unlawful to them their fat, except what is on their backs or entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That was Our recompense for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾ (Surah al-An'am: 146).

al-Dahhak said: None of that was unlawful for us, and God did not make it unlawful for them in the Torah. Rather, it was something they made unlawful for themselves, following their father, and they attributed its prohibition to God. So God refuted them, saying: ﴿Say, O Muhammad: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, so that it would become clear that it is as he says and not as they claim. They did not bring it. So God said: ﴿Whoever after that fabricates lies against God, those are the wrongdoers﴾ (Surah Al ʿImran: 94).

Anas ibn Sirin related from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said concerning ʿirq al-nasa: "Take the fat tail of a Arabian ram, neither small nor large, and cut it into small pieces. Extract its fat and divide it into three portions, and eat from it each day on an empty stomach." (Musnad Ahmad: 3/219, with slight variation; it is also found in full in the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 4/136.) Anas said: "I prescribed it to more than a hundred people, and God healed them all." (al-Mustadrak ʿala al-Sahihayn: 2/292.)

Shu'bah related that he saw an old man in the time of al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf say to ʿirq al-nasa: "I adjure you by God the Most High: if you do not desist, I will burn you with fire, or I will make you join Musa!" Shu'bah said: "He would say this and then wipe over that place, and he would be cured by God's permission."

﴿Say: God has spoken the truth, so follow the religion of Ibrahim, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists. Indeed, the first House established for mankind...﴾, and so on.

Mujahid said: The Muslims and the Jews boasted to one another. The Jews said: "Bayt al-Maqdis is better and greater than the Kaʿbah, because it is the place of migration of the prophets in the Holy Land." The Muslims said: "Rather, the Kaʿbah is better." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind﴾. Ibn al-Sumayqaʿ recited: "wuḍiʿa" with a fatḥah on the waw and on the ḍad, meaning that God established it. ﴿...is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs: the Station of Ibrahim; and whoever enters it is safe﴾ — and that is not in Bayt al-Maqdis — ﴿and pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by people﴾ — and that is not in Bayt al-Maqdis.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, the first House﴾. Some said: it is the first house that appeared upon the surface of the water when God created the heavens and the earth. God created it two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the earth, and the earth was spread out from beneath it. This is the view of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Others said: it is the first house built in the earth. It is related that ʿAli ibn al-Husayn was asked about the beginning of the Flood, and he said: God the Exalted placed beneath the Throne a house, which is the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Maʿmur) that God mentioned. He said to the angels: "Circumambulate it, and leave the Throne." So the angels circumambulated it and left the Throne, for it was easier for them. Then God commanded the angels who dwell on earth to build for Him a house on earth in its likeness and measure. They built it, and its name is al-Ḍarrah. And God commanded whoever is on earth of His creatures to circumambulate it, just as the people of heaven circumambulate the Frequented House.

It was also said: it is the first house built by Adam on earth. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

al-Dahhak said: The first house established was the one in which blessing was placed, and it is better than the highest Paradise (al-Firdaws).

Sammak related from Khalid ibn ʿArʿarah, who said: A man stood before ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) and said: "Will you not tell me about the House? Is it the first house that was on earth?" He said: "No. Where then were the people of Nuh, ʿAd and Thamud? But it is the first blessed house, a guidance, established for mankind."

It was also said: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind﴾ is the one to which people make pilgrimage for God. This is also related from Ibn ʿAbbas. And it was said: it is the first house made a qiblah for people.

al-Hasan, al-Kalbi and al-Farra' said: its meaning is: indeed, the first mosque and place of worship established for mankind, where God is worshipped. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿That you should settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾ (Surah Yunus: 87), meaning their mosques; and ﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾; and His saying: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned﴾ (Surah al-Nur: 36), meaning the mosques.

Ibrahim al-Taymi related from his father, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked about the first mosque established for mankind. He said: "The Sacred Mosque, then Bayt al-Maqdis." He was asked: "How much time is between them?" He said: "Forty years. Wherever prayer overtakes you, pray there, for that is a mosque." (Musnad Ahmad: 5/167.) This is the meaning of ﴿to the one at Bakkah﴾.

al-Dahhak and al-Mudrij said: it is Makkah. The Arabs interchange the letters bāʾ and mīm; they say sabada raʾsahu and samada (he shaved his head), ightabatat ʿalayhi al-ḥummā and ightamatat (the fever took hold of him), and ḍarbah lāzim and lāzib (a necessary blow).

Ibn Shihab and Damrah ibn Rabiʿah said: Bakkah refers to the mosque and the House, while Makkah refers to the whole Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).

Others said: Makkah is the name of the whole city, while Bakkah is the location of the House and the place of circumambulation. It was called Bakkah because people crowd there (yatabakkūn), that is, they press against one another, one weeping for another (yabki baʿḍuhum baʿḍan). They pray in front of one another and pass in front of one another, and this is not permitted anywhere except Makkah.

The rajaz poet said:

"When the drinker is seized by his intoxication, let him be until he is pressed (yabuk) by his bakkah."
(al-Sihah of al-Jawhari: 4/1573.)

ʿAta' said: A woman passed in front of a man who was praying, while she was circumambulating the House, so he pushed her. Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir said: "She is in Bakkah, where people press upon one another."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr said: It was called Bakkah because it crushes the necks of tyrants (tabukk aʿnaq al-jababirah), that is, it breaks them. No tyrant intended it seeking to harm it without God destroying him. As for Makkah, it was so named because of the scarcity of its water, from the Arab saying makkat al-fasīl ḍarʿ ummihi (the young camel sucked its mother's udder) and imtakkahu, when it sucks out all the milk in it. The poet said:

"It sucked, so no milk remained in its udders."
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/138.)

From al-Husayn, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: I know of no place on the face of the earth today where good deeds are multiplied by a hundred thousand for each one, as in Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where one rakʿah prayed in it is recorded as a hundred thousand rakʿahs, as in Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where whoever gives one dirham in charity has a hundred thousand dirhams recorded for him, as in Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth [where it is recorded for one who] has in it the drink of the scholars and the prayer-place of the righteous, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where anyone who touches anything there has it be an expiation of sins, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where, when one makes supplication, the angels say "Amin, amin" for him, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth [.......] [Words illegible in the manuscript.]

except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where whoever looks at the Kaʿbah without circumambulating or praying has recorded for him the worship of a lifetime and the fasting of a lifetime, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth to which all the prophets came [and] to which they went forth, except Makkah. I know of no place where people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, among the prophets, the righteous, the jurists and the worshippers, men and women, as from Makkah; that is, they will be gathered while they are safe. I know of no place on the face of the earth where, every day, the spirit and fragrance of Paradise descend as they descend upon Makkah, may God protect it. (In full in Fada'il Makkah by al-Basri, with variation: 20.)

﴿Blessed﴾: accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾: because it is the qiblah of the believers. ﴿In it are clear signs﴾:

Ibn ʿAbbas recited: "a clear sign" (āyah bayyinah).

﴿The Station of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe﴾ [.......] [A portion fell out of the original manuscript, from verse 97 to verse 102.] ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so that by His favour you became brothers﴾.

[Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Habib related to us from Marthad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Muzani, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUsaylah al-Sunabihi, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I was among those who attended the First Pledge of al-ʿAqabah. We were twelve men, and we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the pledge of women, and that was before fighting was prescribed. [The pledge was] that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and feet, nor disobey him in what is good. "If you fulfil it, then for you is Paradise; and if you fall into any of that..."] [Missing in the manuscript; what is in square brackets is supplemented from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/88.]

"...and if you are punished for it in this world, that is its expiation for him; and if you conceal it until the Day of Resurrection, your affair is with God: if He wills, He will punish you, and if He wills, He will forgive you." He said: That was before fighting was prescribed upon them. When the group departed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent with them Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr ibn Hashim ibn ʿAbd Manaf, and commanded him to recite the Qur'an to them, teach them Islam, and give them understanding of the religion. Mus'ab was called "the reciter" (al-Muqri') in Madinah; he was the first reciter in Madinah. He lodged with As'ad ibn Zurarah.

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to Usayd ibn Hudayr: "Go to these two men who have come to our dwelling to mislead our weak ones, and drive them away. As'ad is my maternal cousin; were it not for that, I would have dealt with you myself." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr were the two chiefs of their people, from the Banu al-Ashhal, and both were polytheists. Usayd ibn Hudayr took his spear and came to Mus'ab and As'ad, who were sitting in an orchard. When As'ad ibn Zurarah saw him, he said to Mus'ab: "This is the chief of his people, and he has come to you, by God. Be sincere toward God concerning him."

Mus'ab said: "If he sits, we will speak to him." So he stood over them, scowling, and said: "What brought you to us? You mislead our weak ones. Leave us alone, if you have any need for yourselves." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter, accept it; and if you dislike it, we will stop what you dislike." He said: "You have been fair." Then he planted his spear and sat with them, and Mus'ab spoke to him about Islam and recited the Qur'an to him.

He said: "By God, we recognised Islam in his face before he spoke, in its brightness and its ease." Then he said: "How excellent and beautiful this is! What do you do when you wish to enter this religion?" They said: "You bathe, purify your clothing, testify to the testimony of truth, and then pray two rakʿahs." So he stood, bathed, purified his clothing, testified to the testimony of truth, then stood and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he said to them: "Behind me is a man who, if he follows you, none of his people will remain behind him. I will send him to you now: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

Then he took his spear and went back to Sa'd and his people, who were sitting in their assembly. When Sa'd ibn Mu'adh saw him approaching, he said: "I swear by God, Usayd has come to you with a face other than the one with which he left you." When he stood before the assembly, Sa'd said to him: "What have you done?" He said: "I spoke with the two men. By God, I saw no harm in them, and I forbade them, but they said: 'We will do nothing except what you like.'"

The Hadith tradition says that the clan of Banu Harithah set out to Asad ibn Zurarah to kill him, because they had learned that he was your maternal cousin, intending to humiliate you. Sa'd rose in anger, hastening toward what he had been told, took the spear from him, and said: "By God, I do not think you have achieved anything." When he saw that the two of them were calm, he realized that Usayd had only wanted to hear from them. So he stood over them, reviling them, and then said to Asad ibn Zurarah: "O Abu Umamah, were it not for the kinship between me and you, you would not have done this to me. You come to our house with what we dislike." He had said to Mus'ab: "The lord of his people has come to you, by God. If he follows you, not one of his people will oppose you." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter and desire it, accept it; and if you dislike it, we have spared you what you dislike." Sa'd said: "You have been fair." Then he planted the spear and sat down. He was presented with Islam and the Qur'an was recited to him. They said: "By God, we recognised Islam in his face before he spoke, in its radiance and its ease." Then he said to them: "What will you do when you have embraced Islam and entered this religion?" They said: "You will wash, purify your garment, bear witness to the truth, then pray two rak'ahs." So he stood, washed, purified his garment, bore witness to the truth, and performed two rak'ahs. Then he took his spear and went purposefully to the assembly of his people, with Usayd ibn Hudayr accompanying him. When his people saw him approaching, they said: "We swear by God, Sa'd has returned to you with a face other than that with which he left you." When he stood before them, he said: "O Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, how do you regard my standing among you?" They said: "You are our lord, the best of us in judgement and the most blessed in counsel." He said: "Then the speech of your men and your women is forbidden to me until you believe in God and His Messenger." So no man or woman in the house of 'Abd al-Ashhal remained at evening except as a Muslim or Muslimah. Asad and Mus'ab returned to the house of Asad ibn Zurarah, and he remained there calling people to Islam, until no house of the Ansar remained except that it had men and women who were Muslims, except for Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, Hatmah, Wa'il and Waqif [and they are the "Awsallah", and they are from Aws ibn Harithah, and that is why] [[Addition from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/90.]] among whom was Abu Qays the poet, and they used to listen to him and obey him. So he held them back from Islam until the Prophet ﷺ emigrated to Madinah, and Badr, Uhud and the Trench passed.

They said: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr returned to Makkah, and with him went seventy men of the Ansar who were Muslims, together with the pilgrims of their people who were polytheists, until they reached Makkah. They arranged with the Messenger of God ﷺ a meeting at the 'Aqabah in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and this was the Second Pledge of 'Aqabah.

Ka'b ibn Malik said, having been present at it: When they had finished the Hajj, and on the night when the Messenger of God ﷺ had appointed for us, and with us was 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, Abu Jabir, we informed him. We concealed our affair from those of our people who were polytheists, and we spoke with him and said: "O Jabir, you are a chief among our chiefs and a noble among our nobles, and we fear that you will be turned away from what you are in, so that we become firewood for the Fire tomorrow." We invited him to Islam, and he embraced Islam. We informed him of the appointment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he attended the 'Aqabah with us, and he was pious. We spent that night in our camps, until when a third of the night had passed we went out to the appointment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, slipping away stealthily like sand-grouse, until we gathered in the ravine at the 'Aqabah, seventy men, and with us two of our women: Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm 'Ammarah, one of the women of Banu al-Najjar, and Asma' bint 'Amr ibn 'Adi, one of the women of Banu Salamah, who was Umm Mani'. We gathered in the ravine awaiting the Messenger of God ﷺ until he came, and with him his uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who on that day was upon the religion of his people, except that he loved to be present at the affair of his nephew and to secure it for him. When we had sat down, the first to speak was al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "O assembly of the Khazraj." The Arabs used to call this tribe of the Ansar, the Khazraj of Khazraj and Aws: "Muhammad is one of us, as you know. We have protected him from our people, from those who share our opinion, and he is in honour among his people and secure in his land. But he has refused except to join you and go to you. If you see that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, and will protect him against whoever opposes him, then you and what you have undertaken; and if you see that you will hand him over and abandon him after going out to you, then leave him now, for he is in honour and security."

He said: We said: "We have heard what you said. Speak, O Messenger of God, and take for yourself and for your Lord whatever you wish."

He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ spoke, recited the Qur'an, called to God, encouraged Islam, and said: "I pledge to you that you will protect me from what you protect your women from."

He said: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur took his hand and said: "By the One who sent you with truth, we will protect you from what we protect our wives from. So pledge to us, O Messenger of God, for we are men of war and men of the armour, which we have inherited from elder to elder."

He said: Then the speech was interrupted, while al-Bara' was speaking to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan said: "O Messenger of God, between us and the people there are ties," meaning the Jews, "and we are about to cut them. Is it possible that if we do this, and then God makes you victorious, you will return to your people and leave us?" The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled, then said: "Rather, blood for blood and destruction for destruction. You are of me and I am of you. I will fight whoever you fight, and make peace with whoever you make peace with."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Bring out to me twelve chiefs from among you, as guarantors over their people for what is in them, as the disciples were guarantors for 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him." [84] [[Al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 1/223.]] So they brought out twelve chiefs: nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws.

'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah said: When the people gathered for the pledge to the Messenger of God ﷺ, al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah al-Ansari said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, do you know what you are pledging to this man? You are pledging to fight the black and the red. If you think that when your wealth is ruined and your nobles killed you will hand him over, then from now on it is, by God, a disgrace in this world and the next. But if you think that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, despite the ruin of wealth and the killing of nobles, then what is our reward for this, O Messenger of God, if we are faithful?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "Extend your hand." He extended his hand and they pledged to him. The first to strike his hand was al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, then the people followed.

He said: When we had pledged to the Messenger of God ﷺ, Satan shouted from the top of the 'Aqabah with the loudest voice I ever heard: "O people of the Jabajib!" [[al-Jabajib here means the dwellings; and in al-Sihah: the jabajibah is the plural of jabajib: a basket of leather used to carry earth, called a "qaffah". See Lisan al-'Arab: 8/291.]] "Do you have a share in Mudhammam? The Sabi'ah with him have gathered to fight you."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "This is, by God, the goatherd of the 'Aqabah. Listen, O enemy of God! By God, I will attend to you." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Return to your camps." Al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah said to him: "By the One who sent you with truth, if you wish, we will fall upon the people of Mina tomorrow with our swords." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "We have not been commanded to that, but return to your camps."

He said: We returned to our resting places and slept upon them until morning. Then the nobles of Quraysh came to us in the morning, and came to our dwellings and said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, we have heard that you have come to our companion here to take him out from among us and pledge to fight us. By God, there is no tribe of the Arabs more hateful to us than that war should break out between us and them through you." He said: Then there arose from there some of our polytheist people, swearing by God that none of this had happened and that they knew nothing of it. They spoke the truth, for they did not know. Some of us looked at others. The people stood up, and among them was al-Harith ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, wearing two new sandals. He said: I said to him a word as though I wished to share it with the people in what they had said: "O Abu Jabir, can you not get a young man of Quraysh like these sandals of mine?" [hmm]

He said: al-Harith heard it, took them off his feet, threw them to me, and said: "By God, you will wear them." Abu Jabir said: "By God, you have angered the young man, so return his sandals to him." He said: I said: "I will not return them." He said: "By God, it is a truce. By God, if he is truthful, I will plunder him."

He said: Then Abu Jabir went back to Madinah, and they had strengthened the covenant. When they reached it, they openly professed Islam there, and that reached Quraysh, who harmed the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to his companions: "God has made for you brothers and a home in which you will be secure." [85] [[In full in Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/88 to 94, and Musnad Ahmad: 3/462.]]

So he commanded them to emigrate to Madinah and to join their brothers, the Ansar. Among those who emigrated was Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, then 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah with his wife Layla bint Abi Khaythamah, then 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh. Then the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ followed one another in succession to Madinah, while the Messenger of God ﷺ remained awaiting permission to emigrate until he was permitted. He came to Madinah, and God gathered the people of Madinah, Aws and Khazraj, through Islam, set right their relations through His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, removed the old enmity from them, and united them. This is His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, O assembly of the Ansar, when you were enemies before Islam, and He joined your hearts, so you became by His favour brothers﴾ — "so you became": you became. Its parallel is His saying in al-Ma'idah: ﴿So he became among the losers﴾ [[al-Ma'idah: 30.]] and His saying: ﴿So he became among the regretful﴾ [[al-Ma'idah: 31.]], and in Ha Mim al-Sajdah: ﴿So you became among the losers﴾ [[Fussilat: 23.]], and in al-Kahf: ﴿Or its water becomes sunk into the earth﴾ [[al-Kahf: 41.]].

﴿By His favour﴾: by the blessing of Islam. ﴿Brothers﴾: in religion and in alliance. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ [[al-Hujurat: 10.]].

From Abu Sa'id, mawla of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Kurayz, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
"Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not undercut one another in trade. Be, O servants of God, brothers. The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, nor forsake him, nor despise him. Piety is here," and he pointed to his chest with his hand, "It is enough evil for a man that he despise his Muslim brother." [86] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/288, 67, 277.]]

From Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it strengthening another," and he interlaced his fingers. [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/123.]]

From al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said to the Prophet ﷺ: "The believers are like one man."

He said: "The believers are like one man: if his head aches, the rest of him responds with fever and sleeplessness." [87] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/277.]]

﴿And you were, O assembly of Aws and Khazraj, on the brink of a pit of the Fire﴾. The rajiz said:
"We dug for the pilgrims a well, with a green growth over its edge."

The meaning of the verse: you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, with nothing between you and falling into it except that you die upon your disbelief. ﴿So He saved you from it﴾ by faith. He said: It reached us that a Bedouin heard Ibn 'Abbas reciting this verse, and said: "By God, He did not save them from it, for he wants to make them fall into it." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Take him away; he is not a jurist." ﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, that you may be guided.﴾

**Al-Tha'labi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 3, verses 93–103 (Part 1 of 2)**

﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾, and so on.

Abu Rawq and al-Kalbi said: This was when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am upon the religion of Ibrahim." The Jews said: "How can that be, when you eat camel meat and drink its milk?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That was lawful for Ibrahim, and we make it lawful." The Jews said: "Everything we have made unlawful today was unlawful for Nuh and Ibrahim, and it remained so until it reached us." So God the Exalted revealed, refuting them: ﴿All the food made lawful to you today was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾

﴿except what Israel [i.e. Ya'qub], that is Ya'qub, had forbidden to himself before the Torah was sent down﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning that food. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Abu Mijlaz said: it was the veins (ʿuruq). The reason for this was that Ya'qub (peace be upon him) suffered from ʿirq al-nasa (sciatica), and this was the origin of his ailment. This is what Juwaybir and Muqatil related from al-Dahhak: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq had vowed that if God granted him twelve sons and he came to Bayt al-Maqdis in good health, he would slaughter the youngest of them. An angel met him and said: "O Ya'qub, you are a strong man. Are you willing to wrestle?" He wrestled with him, and neither could throw the other. Then the angel pressed him with a squeeze, and ʿirq al-nasa afflicted him because of it. Then he said: "If I wished, I could have thrown you, but I squeezed you with this squeeze because you had vowed that if you came to Bayt al-Maqdis in good health you would slaughter your youngest son. God has made for you a way out through this squeeze." When Ya'qub arrived there, he wanted to slaughter his son, but he forgot the angel's words. The angel came to him and said: "I squeezed you with that squeeze as a way out, and you have fulfilled your vow, so there is no way for you to [harm] your son."

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: Ya'qub (peace be upon him) came from Harran, wishing to go to Bayt al-Maqdis, when he fled from his brother ʿIs, who was a hot-tempered and strong man. He met an angel, and Ya'qub thought he was a thief, so he tried to throw him down. The angel squeezed Ya'qub's thigh and then ascended to heaven while Ya'qub watched him. Ya'qub was then afflicted with ʿirq al-nasa and suffered a severe trial because of it. He could not sleep at night because of the pain, and he would cry out (zuqa'), that is, shout. So Ya'qub (peace be upon him) swore that if God healed him, he would not eat any vein, nor any food containing a vein. He therefore made it unlawful for himself, and his sons began to seek out the veins and remove them from the meat. (Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 18/72.) Abu al-ʿAliyah, ʿAta', Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: what was made unlawful was the flesh of camels and their milk.

Shahr ibn Hawshab related from Ibn ʿAbbas that a group came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, tell us which food Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was sent down?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I call you to witness by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa: Do you know that Ya'qub fell severely ill, and his sickness lasted long upon him? So he vowed to God that if God healed him from his sickness, he would forbid himself the food and drink he loved most. The food he loved most was camel flesh, and the drink he loved most was its milk." (Musnad Ahmad: 1/273, with slight variation.) They said: "O God, yes."

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ʿirq al-nasa afflicted Ya'qub, the physicians prescribed that he avoid camel meat, so Ya'qub made camel meat unlawful for himself. The Jews said: "We have made camel meat unlawful for ourselves because Ya'qub made it unlawful, and God sent down its prohibition in the Torah." So God revealed this verse.

al-Hasan said: Israel made the flesh of the camel unlawful for himself as an act of worship to God the Mighty and Majestic. He then asked his Lord to permit it to him, but God made it unlawful for his offspring. ʿIkrimah said: Israel made unlawful for himself the appendix of the liver, the two kidneys, and the fat, except what is on the back. Layth related from Mujahid, who said: Israel made the flesh of livestock unlawful for himself.

Then the exegetes differed concerning this food that was made unlawful for Israel after the Torah was sent down. al-Suddi said: When God sent down the Torah, He made unlawful for them what they had been making unlawful before it, following their father Ya'qub (peace be upon him). ʿAtiyyah said: It was unlawful for them only because Israel had made it unlawful for them. That was because Israel said, when ʿirq al-nasa afflicted him: "By God, if God heals me from it, none of my sons shall eat it." And it was not unlawful for them in the Torah.

al-Kalbi said: God did not make it unlawful for them in the Torah. Rather, He made it unlawful for them after the Torah because of their wrongdoing and disbelief. Whenever the Children of Israel committed a great sin, God made some good food unlawful for them, or sent upon them a punishment (rijz), which is death. This is His saying: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who became Jews, We made unlawful for them good things that had been lawful for them﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 160), and His saying: ﴿And for those who became Jews We made unlawful every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We made unlawful to them their fat, except what is on their backs or entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That was Our recompense for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾ (Surah al-An'am: 146).

al-Dahhak said: None of that was unlawful for us, and God did not make it unlawful for them in the Torah. Rather, it was something they made unlawful for themselves, following their father, and they attributed its prohibition to God. So God refuted them, saying: ﴿Say, O Muhammad: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, so that it would become clear that it is as he says and not as they claim. They did not bring it. So God said: ﴿Whoever after that fabricates lies against God, those are the wrongdoers﴾ (Surah Al ʿImran: 94).

Anas ibn Sirin related from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said concerning ʿirq al-nasa: "Take the fat tail of a Arabian ram, neither small nor large, and cut it into small pieces. Extract its fat and divide it into three portions, and eat from it each day on an empty stomach." (Musnad Ahmad: 3/219, with slight variation; it is also found in full in the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 4/136.) Anas said: "I prescribed it to more than a hundred people, and God healed them all." (al-Mustadrak ʿala al-Sahihayn: 2/292.)

Shu'bah related that he saw an old man in the time of al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf say to ʿirq al-nasa: "I adjure you by God the Most High: if you do not desist, I will burn you with fire, or I will make you join Musa!" Shu'bah said: "He would say this and then wipe over that place, and he would be cured by God's permission."

﴿Say: God has spoken the truth, so follow the religion of Ibrahim, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists. Indeed, the first House established for mankind...﴾, and so on.

Mujahid said: The Muslims and the Jews boasted to one another. The Jews said: "Bayt al-Maqdis is better and greater than the Kaʿbah, because it is the place of migration of the prophets in the Holy Land." The Muslims said: "Rather, the Kaʿbah is better." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind﴾. Ibn al-Sumayqaʿ recited: "wuḍiʿa" with a fatḥah on the waw and on the ḍad, meaning that God established it. ﴿...is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs: the Station of Ibrahim; and whoever enters it is safe﴾ — and that is not in Bayt al-Maqdis — ﴿and pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by people﴾ — and that is not in Bayt al-Maqdis.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, the first House﴾. Some said: it is the first house that appeared upon the surface of the water when God created the heavens and the earth. God created it two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the earth, and the earth was spread out from beneath it. This is the view of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Others said: it is the first house built in the earth. It is related that ʿAli ibn al-Husayn was asked about the beginning of the Flood, and he said: God the Exalted placed beneath the Throne a house, which is the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Maʿmur) that God mentioned. He said to the angels: "Circumambulate it, and leave the Throne." So the angels circumambulated it and left the Throne, for it was easier for them. Then God commanded the angels who dwell on earth to build for Him a house on earth in its likeness and measure. They built it, and its name is al-Ḍarrah. And God commanded whoever is on earth of His creatures to circumambulate it, just as the people of heaven circumambulate the Frequented House.

It was also said: it is the first house built by Adam on earth. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

al-Dahhak said: The first house established was the one in which blessing was placed, and it is better than the highest Paradise (al-Firdaws).

Sammak related from Khalid ibn ʿArʿarah, who said: A man stood before ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) and said: "Will you not tell me about the House? Is it the first house that was on earth?" He said: "No. Where then were the people of Nuh, ʿAd and Thamud? But it is the first blessed house, a guidance, established for mankind."

It was also said: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind﴾ is the one to which people make pilgrimage for God. This is also related from Ibn ʿAbbas. And it was said: it is the first house made a qiblah for people.

al-Hasan, al-Kalbi and al-Farra' said: its meaning is: indeed, the first mosque and place of worship established for mankind, where God is worshipped. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿That you should settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾ (Surah Yunus: 87), meaning their mosques; and ﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾; and His saying: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned﴾ (Surah al-Nur: 36), meaning the mosques.

Ibrahim al-Taymi related from his father, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked about the first mosque established for mankind. He said: "The Sacred Mosque, then Bayt al-Maqdis." He was asked: "How much time is between them?" He said: "Forty years. Wherever prayer overtakes you, pray there, for that is a mosque." (Musnad Ahmad: 5/167.) This is the meaning of ﴿to the one at Bakkah﴾.

al-Dahhak and al-Mudrij said: it is Makkah. The Arabs interchange the letters bāʾ and mīm; they say sabada raʾsahu and samada (he shaved his head), ightabatat ʿalayhi al-ḥummā and ightamatat (the fever took hold of him), and ḍarbah lāzim and lāzib (a necessary blow).

Ibn Shihab and Damrah ibn Rabiʿah said: Bakkah refers to the mosque and the House, while Makkah refers to the whole Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).

Others said: Makkah is the name of the whole city, while Bakkah is the location of the House and the place of circumambulation. It was called Bakkah because people crowd there (yatabakkūn), that is, they press against one another, one weeping for another (yabki baʿḍuhum baʿḍan). They pray in front of one another and pass in front of one another, and this is not permitted anywhere except Makkah.

The rajaz poet said:

"When the drinker is seized by his intoxication, let him be until he is pressed (yabuk) by his bakkah."
(al-Sihah of al-Jawhari: 4/1573.)

ʿAta' said: A woman passed in front of a man who was praying, while she was circumambulating the House, so he pushed her. Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir said: "She is in Bakkah, where people press upon one another."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr said: It was called Bakkah because it crushes the necks of tyrants (tabukk aʿnaq al-jababirah), that is, it breaks them. No tyrant intended it seeking to harm it without God destroying him. As for Makkah, it was so named because of the scarcity of its water, from the Arab saying makkat al-fasīl ḍarʿ ummihi (the young camel sucked its mother's udder) and imtakkahu, when it sucks out all the milk in it. The poet said:

"It sucked, so no milk remained in its udders."
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/138.)

From al-Husayn, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: I know of no place on the face of the earth today where good deeds are multiplied by a hundred thousand for each one, as in Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where one rakʿah prayed in it is recorded as a hundred thousand rakʿahs, as in Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where whoever gives one dirham in charity has a hundred thousand dirhams recorded for him, as in Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth [where it is recorded for one who] has in it the drink of the scholars and the prayer-place of the righteous, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where anyone who touches anything there has it be an expiation of sins, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where, when one makes supplication, the angels say "Amin, amin" for him, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth [.......] [Words illegible in the manuscript.]

except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth where whoever looks at the Kaʿbah without circumambulating or praying has recorded for him the worship of a lifetime and the fasting of a lifetime, except Makkah. I know of no place on the face of the earth to which all the prophets came [and] to which they went forth, except Makkah. I know of no place where people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, among the prophets, the righteous, the jurists and the worshippers, men and women, as from Makkah; that is, they will be gathered while they are safe. I know of no place on the face of the earth where, every day, the spirit and fragrance of Paradise descend as they descend upon Makkah, may God protect it. (In full in Fada'il Makkah by al-Basri, with variation: 20.)

﴿Blessed﴾: accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾: because it is the qiblah of the believers. ﴿In it are clear signs﴾:

Ibn ʿAbbas recited: "a clear sign" (āyah bayyinah).

﴿The Station of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe﴾ [.......] [A portion fell out of the original manuscript, from verse 97 to verse 102.] ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so that by His favour you became brothers﴾.

[Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Habib related to us from Marthad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Muzani, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUsaylah al-Sunabihi, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I was among those who attended the First Pledge of al-ʿAqabah. We were twelve men, and we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the pledge of women, and that was before fighting was prescribed. [The pledge was] that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and feet, nor disobey him in what is good. "If you fulfil it, then for you is Paradise; and if you fall into any of that..."] [Missing in the manuscript; what is in square brackets is supplemented from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/88.]

"...and if you are punished for it in this world, that is its expiation for him; and if you conceal it until the Day of Resurrection, your affair is with God: if He wills, He will punish you, and if He wills, He will forgive you." He said: That was before fighting was prescribed upon them. When the group departed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent with them Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr ibn Hashim ibn ʿAbd Manaf, and commanded him to recite the Qur'an to them, teach them Islam, and give them understanding of the religion. Mus'ab was called "the reciter" (al-Muqri') in Madinah; he was the first reciter in Madinah. He lodged with As'ad ibn Zurarah.

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to Usayd ibn Hudayr: "Go to these two men who have come to our dwelling to mislead our weak ones, and drive them away. As'ad is my maternal cousin; were it not for that, I would have dealt with you myself." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr were the two chiefs of their people, from the Banu al-Ashhal, and both were polytheists. Usayd ibn Hudayr took his spear and came to Mus'ab and As'ad, who were sitting in an orchard. When As'ad ibn Zurarah saw him, he said to Mus'ab: "This is the chief of his people, and he has come to you, by God. Be sincere toward God concerning him."

Mus'ab said: "If he sits, we will speak to him." So he stood over them, scowling, and said: "What brought you to us? You mislead our weak ones. Leave us alone, if you have any need for yourselves." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter, accept it; and if you dislike it, we will stop what you dislike." He said: "You have been fair." Then he planted his spear and sat with them, and Mus'ab spoke to him about Islam and recited the Qur'an to him.

He said: "By God, we recognised Islam in his face before he spoke, in its brightness and its ease." Then he said: "How excellent and beautiful this is! What do you do when you wish to enter this religion?" They said: "You bathe, purify your clothing, testify to the testimony of truth, and then pray two rakʿahs." So he stood, bathed, purified his clothing, testified to the testimony of truth, then stood and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he said to them: "Behind me is a man who, if he follows you, none of his people will remain behind him. I will send him to you now: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

Then he took his spear and went back to Sa'd and his people, who were sitting in their assembly. When Sa'd ibn Mu'adh saw him approaching, he said: "I swear by God, Usayd has come to you with a face other than the one with which he left you." When he stood before the assembly, Sa'd said to him: "What have you done?" He said: "I spoke with the two men. By God, I saw no harm in them, and I forbade them, but they said: 'We will do nothing except what you like.'"

The Hadith tradition says that the clan of Banu Harithah set out to Asad ibn Zurarah to kill him, because they had learned that he was your maternal cousin, intending to humiliate you. Sa'd rose in anger, hastening toward what he had been told, took the spear from him, and said: "By God, I do not think you have achieved anything." When he saw that the two of them were calm, he realized that Usayd had only wanted to hear from them. So he stood over them, reviling them, and then said to Asad ibn Zurarah: "O Abu Umamah, were it not for the kinship between me and you, you would not have done this to me. You come to our house with what we dislike." He had said to Mus'ab: "The lord of his people has come to you, by God. If he follows you, not one of his people will oppose you." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter and desire it, accept it; and if you dislike it, we have spared you what you dislike." Sa'd said: "You have been fair." Then he planted the spear and sat down. He was presented with Islam and the Qur'an was recited to him. They said: "By God, we recognised Islam in his face before he spoke, in its radiance and its ease." Then he said to them: "What will you do when you have embraced Islam and entered this religion?" They said: "You will wash, purify your garment, bear witness to the truth, then pray two rak'ahs." So he stood, washed, purified his garment, bore witness to the truth, and performed two rak'ahs. Then he took his spear and went purposefully to the assembly of his people, with Usayd ibn Hudayr accompanying him. When his people saw him approaching, they said: "We swear by God, Sa'd has returned to you with a face other than that with which he left you." When he stood before them, he said: "O Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, how do you regard my standing among you?" They said: "You are our lord, the best of us in judgement and the most blessed in counsel." He said: "Then the speech of your men and your women is forbidden to me until you believe in God and His Messenger." So no man or woman in the house of 'Abd al-Ashhal remained at evening except as a Muslim or Muslimah. Asad and Mus'ab returned to the house of Asad ibn Zurarah, and he remained there calling people to Islam, until no house of the Ansar remained except that it had men and women who were Muslims, except for Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, Hatmah, Wa'il and Waqif [and they are the "Awsallah", and they are from Aws ibn Harithah, and that is why] [[Addition from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/90.]] among whom was Abu Qays the poet, and they used to listen to him and obey him. So he held them back from Islam until the Prophet ﷺ emigrated to Madinah, and Badr, Uhud and the Trench passed.

They said: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr returned to Makkah, and with him went seventy men of the Ansar who were Muslims, together with the pilgrims of their people who were polytheists, until they reached Makkah. They arranged with the Messenger of God ﷺ a meeting at the 'Aqabah in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and this was the Second Pledge of 'Aqabah.

Ka'b ibn Malik said, having been present at it: When they had finished the Hajj, and on the night when the Messenger of God ﷺ had appointed for us, and with us was 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, Abu Jabir, we informed him. We concealed our affair from those of our people who were polytheists, and we spoke with him and said: "O Jabir, you are a chief among our chiefs and a noble among our nobles, and we fear that you will be turned away from what you are in, so that we become firewood for the Fire tomorrow." We invited him to Islam, and he embraced Islam. We informed him of the appointment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he attended the 'Aqabah with us, and he was pious. We spent that night in our camps, until when a third of the night had passed we went out to the appointment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, slipping away stealthily like sand-grouse, until we gathered in the ravine at the 'Aqabah, seventy men, and with us two of our women: Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm 'Ammarah, one of the women of Banu al-Najjar, and Asma' bint 'Amr ibn 'Adi, one of the women of Banu Salamah, who was Umm Mani'. We gathered in the ravine awaiting the Messenger of God ﷺ until he came, and with him his uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who on that day was upon the religion of his people, except that he loved to be present at the affair of his nephew and to secure it for him. When we had sat down, the first to speak was al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "O assembly of the Khazraj." The Arabs used to call this tribe of the Ansar, the Khazraj of Khazraj and Aws: "Muhammad is one of us, as you know. We have protected him from our people, from those who share our opinion, and he is in honour among his people and secure in his land. But he has refused except to join you and go to you. If you see that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, and will protect him against whoever opposes him, then you and what you have undertaken; and if you see that you will hand him over and abandon him after going out to you, then leave him now, for he is in honour and security."

He said: We said: "We have heard what you said. Speak, O Messenger of God, and take for yourself and for your Lord whatever you wish."

He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ spoke, recited the Qur'an, called to God, encouraged Islam, and said: "I pledge to you that you will protect me from what you protect your women from."

He said: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur took his hand and said: "By the One who sent you with truth, we will protect you from what we protect our wives from. So pledge to us, O Messenger of God, for we are men of war and men of the armour, which we have inherited from elder to elder."

He said: Then the speech was interrupted, while al-Bara' was speaking to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan said: "O Messenger of God, between us and the people there are ties," meaning the Jews, "and we are about to cut them. Is it possible that if we do this, and then God makes you victorious, you will return to your people and leave us?" The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled, then said: "Rather, blood for blood and destruction for destruction. You are of me and I am of you. I will fight whoever you fight, and make peace with whoever you make peace with."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Bring out to me twelve chiefs from among you, as guarantors over their people for what is in them, as the disciples were guarantors for 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him." [84] [[Al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 1/223.]] So they brought out twelve chiefs: nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws.

'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah said: When the people gathered for the pledge to the Messenger of God ﷺ, al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah al-Ansari said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, do you know what you are pledging to this man? You are pledging to fight the black and the red. If you think that when your wealth is ruined and your nobles killed you will hand him over, then from now on it is, by God, a disgrace in this world and the next. But if you think that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, despite the ruin of wealth and the killing of nobles, then what is our reward for this, O Messenger of God, if we are faithful?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "Extend your hand." He extended his hand and they pledged to him. The first to strike his hand was al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, then the people followed.

He said: When we had pledged to the Messenger of God ﷺ, Satan shouted from the top of the 'Aqabah with the loudest voice I ever heard: "O people of the Jabajib!" [[al-Jabajib here means the dwellings; and in al-Sihah: the jabajibah is the plural of jabajib: a basket of leather used to carry earth, called a "qaffah". See Lisan al-'Arab: 8/291.]] "Do you have a share in Mudhammam? The Sabi'ah with him have gathered to fight you."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "This is, by God, the goatherd of the 'Aqabah. Listen, O enemy of God! By God, I will attend to you." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Return to your camps." Al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah said to him: "By the One who sent you with truth, if you wish, we will fall upon the people of Mina tomorrow with our swords." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "We have not been commanded to that, but return to your camps."

He said: We returned to our resting places and slept upon them until morning. Then the nobles of Quraysh came to us in the morning, and came to our dwellings and said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, we have heard that you have come to our companion here to take him out from among us and pledge to fight us. By God, there is no tribe of the Arabs more hateful to us than that war should break out between us and them through you." He said: Then there arose from there some of our polytheist people, swearing by God that none of this had happened and that they knew nothing of it. They spoke the truth, for they did not know. Some of us looked at others. The people stood up, and among them was al-Harith ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, wearing two new sandals. He said: I said to him a word as though I wished to share it with the people in what they had said: "O Abu Jabir, can you not get a young man of Quraysh like these sandals of mine?" [hmm]

He said: al-Harith heard it, took them off his feet, threw them to me, and said: "By God, you will wear them." Abu Jabir said: "By God, you have angered the young man, so return his sandals to him." He said: I said: "I will not return them." He said: "By God, it is a truce. By God, if he is truthful, I will plunder him."

He said: Then Abu Jabir went back to Madinah, and they had strengthened the covenant. When they reached it, they openly professed Islam there, and that reached Quraysh, who harmed the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to his companions: "God has made for you brothers and a home in which you will be secure." [85] [[In full in Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/88 to 94, and Musnad Ahmad: 3/462.]]

So he commanded them to emigrate to Madinah and to join their brothers, the Ansar. Among those who emigrated was Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, then 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah with his wife Layla bint Abi Khaythamah, then 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh. Then the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ followed one another in succession to Madinah, while the Messenger of God ﷺ remained awaiting permission to emigrate until he was permitted. He came to Madinah, and God gathered the people of Madinah, Aws and Khazraj, through Islam, set right their relations through His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, removed the old enmity from them, and united them. This is His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, O assembly of the Ansar, when you were enemies before Islam, and He joined your hearts, so you became by His favour brothers﴾ — "so you became": you became. Its parallel is His saying in al-Ma'idah: ﴿So he became among the losers﴾ [[al-Ma'idah: 30.]] and His saying: ﴿So he became among the regretful﴾ [[al-Ma'idah: 31.]], and in Ha Mim al-Sajdah: ﴿So you became among the losers﴾ [[Fussilat: 23.]], and in al-Kahf: ﴿Or its water becomes sunk into the earth﴾ [[al-Kahf: 41.]].

﴿By His favour﴾: by the blessing of Islam. ﴿Brothers﴾: in religion and in alliance. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ [[al-Hujurat: 10.]].

From Abu Sa'id, mawla of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Kurayz, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
