The meaning of the verse: the likeness of the expenditures of the disbelievers, in their nullification, their going to waste, and their lack of benefit at the time they need them, after they had hoped for their profit, is like a crop struck by a cold wind or fire which burns it and destroys it, so its owners gain nothing from it after they had hoped for its yield. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ through disbelief, disobedience and withholding the right of Allah.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate friends those other than your own...﴾ [the verse].

From Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate friends those other than your own﴾, he said: «They are the Khawarij» [108] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/179.]].

Ibn 'Abbas said: a man from the Muslims used to associate with some Jewish men because of the kinship, friendship, alliance, neighbourhood and fosterage between them, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them, forbidding them from intimacy with them, out of fear of the trial they might bring upon them. Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning a people among the believers who used to encounter the hypocrites and mix with them, so Allah the Exalted forbade them from that, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate friends those other than your own﴾: allies and confidants from outside the people of your religion.

And al-biṭānah (intimate circle, close confidants): it is a verbal noun placed in the position of a noun, so it is used for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. The poet said:

"Those are my special companions, indeed, and my intimates, and they are my confidants above every near relative."

The reason a man's close friend is called biṭānah is by analogy with the garment that is closest to his belly (biṭn), since he resides close to him in being privy to his secrets and what he conceals from those far away, just as the many relatives of a person are in the position of what covers his body of garments. Then he mentioned the cause of the prohibition against intimacy with them, and made known to them what they harbour of deceit, treachery, oppression and ruin, and so the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿they spare no effort to corrupt you﴾, meaning they do not fall short, nor do they leave off, their covenant and their ability regarding what brings you more than evil and corruption. It is said: "I did not spare him good or evil," meaning I did not fall short in doing that. From this is the saying of Ibn Mas'ud concerning 'Uthman:

"And did not spare good for another it had shown."

And Imru' al-Qays said:

"And a man, so long as the breath of his soul remains, will not attain the extremes of calamities, nor fall short [in seeking them]."

That is, one who falls short in seeking.

al-Khabāl: evil and corruption. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Had they gone out among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47]. ﴿Khabalan﴾ is in the accusative as a second object, because the verb ālā is transitive to two objects. If you wish, it is the verbal noun, meaning "they corrupt you with corruption." If you wish, by removing the preposition, meaning "with corruption," as one says "I hurt him with blows," meaning "with the blow."

﴿They love that you suffer﴾, i.e., they wish for your harm, your evil, your sin and your destruction.

﴿Hatred has already appeared﴾: the reading of the majority uses the feminine ending (tā') because al-baghḍā' is feminine. The meaning of the verse: the signs of enmity have already appeared ﴿from their mouths﴾ through abuse and slander against the Muslims. It is said: through the disclosure of the secrets of the believers to the polytheists. It is also said: it is like His saying: ﴿And you will surely recognise them in the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30].

﴿And what their breasts conceal﴾ of enmity and treachery ﴿is greater﴾, greater. ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you, if you use reason.﴾

From al-Azhar ibn Rashid, who said: Anas ibn Malik used to narrate to his companions, and when he narrated to them a hadith whose meaning they did not understand, they came to al-Hasan to explain it to them. He narrated to them one day and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave Arabic on your rings» [109] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/99.]].

They came to al-Hasan and informed him of that. He said: as for his saying «do not engrave Arabic on your rings», he means: do not engrave Muhammad on your rings. As for his saying «do not seek light from the light of the polytheists», he means: do not consult the polytheists in any of your affairs. And confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate friends those other than your own﴾ [the verse].

'Iyad al-Ash'ari said: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came as a delegation to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: "We have a scribe who is a Christian, with such-and-such a condition." He said: "What is wrong with you, may Allah destroy you? Have you not heard the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate friends those other than your own﴾ [the verse], and His saying: ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 51]? Why did you not take a Hanif?" He said: I said: "His religion is his concern, and my religion is mine, and his writing is mine. I do not honour them when Allah has humiliated them, nor do I raise them when Allah has abased them, nor do I bring them near when Allah has distanced them." [111?] [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/179.]]

﴿Here you are, those who...﴾ "Ha" is an interjection of alerting, "antum" is a pronoun for the addressed masculine plural, "ulā'" is the demonstrative noun of the plural referred to; ﴿you love them﴾ is the predicate concerning them. The meaning of the verse: you, O believers, love these Jews whom I forbade you from being intimate with, for the ties between you of marriage, alliance, fosterage, kinship and neighbourhood, ﴿and they do not love you﴾, because of the difference of religion between you. This is the saying of most of the exegetes. Al-Mufaddal said: the meaning of ﴿you love them﴾ is that you desire Islam for them, which is the best of things, and you do not withhold from them calling them to Paradise; ﴿and they do not love you﴾, for they desire to make you disbelieve, which is destruction. Abu al-'Aliyah and Muqatil said: they are the hypocrites, whom the believers love because of the faith they display, and they do not know what is in their hearts.

Qatadah: regarding this verse, by Allah, the believer does love the hypocrite, inclines towards him and shows him mercy, and if the hypocrite were able to do to the believer what the believer could do to him, he would have destroyed his greenery [108?] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/87.]].

﴿And you believe in the Book, all of it﴾, meaning in all the books; they do not believe in your book. ﴿When they meet you, they say: "We believe." But when they are alone, [with one another], they bite at you with their fingertips﴾, meaning the tips of the fingers, singular anamilah and anamilah, with the mīm vowelled and unvowelled, ﴿out of rage﴾ and fury at what they see of the unity of the believers, the gathering of their word and the goodness of their mutual relations. This is a figurative expression of speech, even if there is no actual biting. The poet said:

"When they see me, may Allah prolong their rage, they bite at the tips of the fingers from rage."

And Abu Talib said:

"And they have made peace with a people niggardly toward us, biting with their fingers in rage behind us."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "Die in your rage."﴾ If it is said: how will they not die, when Allah, if He says to a thing "Be," it is? The answer: the intent is "remain with your rage until death, for your wishes are barred from being fulfilled." Muhammad ibn Jarir said: this statement is in the form of a command, and it is a supplication: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ that he should supplicate against them for destruction through the grief that afflicts them from the rage. Say, O Muhammad: "Perish in your rage" [109?] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 4/89.]]. ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, of good and evil in the hearts. 'Amr ibn Malik narrated from Abu al-Jawza', who said: the people of desires were mentioned, and he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, if my house were filled with monkeys and pigs, it would be more beloved to me than that a man of them should be my neighbour" [110?] [[al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 7/224.]]. He meant a man of desire. And they have entered into this verse: ﴿Here you are, those who love them, and they do not love you﴾, the verse.

﴿If a good thing touches you﴾: Al-Sulami read it with the yā'; the rest with the tā'. It means: if good befalls you, O believers, through your victory over your enemy and booty you obtain from them, and a following of people entering your religion and ease in your livelihood, ﴿it grieves them﴾: it saddens them. ﴿And if an evil befalls you﴾, a calamity through the failure of a detachment of yours, or the killing of an enemy among you, or dissension that arises among you, or an event and a catastrophe, ﴿they rejoice at it.﴾ ﴿And if you are patient﴾ with their harm, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ and fear your Lord, ﴿their plot will not harm you at all.﴾ ﴿It will not diminish you in any way.﴾

The reading of it differed. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read: ﴿lā yaḍirrakum﴾ with a light kasrah on the ḍād. Abu Hatim chose this, and it is said: ḍāra yaḍīru ḍayran, like bā'a yabī'u bay'an, and its evidence in the Qur'an is: ﴿lā ḍayra﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 50]. It is a jussive as the answer of the conditional.

Al-Dahhak read with a ḍammah on the ḍād and a light jussive on the rā', from "ḍāra yaḍūru," and al-Farra' related from al-Kisa'i that he heard some people of al-'Aliyah say: "That does not benefit me, nor does it harm me (lā yaḍūrunī)." The rest read with the ḍammah on the ḍād [and the rā'] [[In the manuscript: the rā' and the ḍād.]] doubled, and he chose it. It is from "ḍarra yaḍurru ḍarran," like "radda yaruddu raddan." On its rā' there are two possibilities:

The first: he intended the jussive, and the original is lā yaḍurrukum; the rā' was assimilated into the rā', the ḍammah of the first rā' was transferred to the ḍād, and the last rā' was given a ḍammah following the nearest vowel to it, which is the ḍād, seeking harmony, as in their saying: "marra yā hādhā."

The second: that "lā" is in the sense of "laysa" and the fā' is implied in it, its estimate: "And if you are patient and fear Allah, then it is not that it harms you." This was said by al-Farra', and he recited:

"If he is not pleased with you until you return me to my territory, I do not think you are content."

﴿Indeed Allah is, of what you do,﴾ — al-A'mash and al-Hasan read with the tā'; the rest with the yā' — ﴿Encompassing,﴾ that is, Knowing.

﴿And [mention] when you left your family in the morning...﴾ [the verse]. The arrangement of the verse: ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all﴾, but Allah the Exalted will help you against them as He helped you at Badr when ﴿you were humiliated﴾; and if you do not show patience in my command and do not fear my prohibition, then there will descend upon you what descended upon you on the day of Uhud, when you opposed the Messenger's command and did not show patience. So remember that day, or tomorrow, among you ﴿He settled the believers﴾.

They differed about the day which Allah the Exalted meant by His saying: ﴿And [mention] when you left your family in the morning﴾. Al-Hasan said: it is the day of Badr. Muqatil said: it is the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). The rest of the exegetes said: it is Uhud, and this is the most established. It is indicated by His saying after it: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾, and this only happened on the day of Uhud.

Mujahid, al-Kalbi and al-Waqidi said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in the morning from the house of 'A'ishah and walked on foot to Uhud, and he began arranging his companions for battle, as though the arrow were straightening them; if he saw a chest protruding, he said: "Fall back." That was because the polytheists had camped at Uhud, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi related from their men, on Wednesday. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of their arrival, he consulted his companions and summoned 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, whom he had never summoned before that, and consulted him. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and most of the Ansar said: "O Messenger of Allah, remain in Medina and do not go out to them. By Allah, we have never gone out from it to an enemy but he struck us, and he has never entered it against us but we struck him. How much more so when you are among us? Leave them, O Messenger of Allah; if they remain, they remain in the worst of places, and if they enter, the men will fight them face to face, and the women and children will pelt them with stones from above. If they return, they will return disappointed as they came."

The Messenger of Allah was pleased with this opinion.

Some of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, let us go out to these dogs; let them not think we have shrunk from them or weakened." Then al-Nu'man ibn Malik al-Ansari came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not deprive me of Paradise, for by Him who sent you with truth, I will surely enter Paradise." He said: "By what?" He said: "By my testifying that there is no god but Allah, and that I do not flee from the battle line." He said: "You have spoken truly." So he was killed that day. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «I saw in my dream cows, and I interpreted them as good. I saw in the notch of my sword a breach, and I interpreted it as defeat. And I saw that I put my hand into a strong coat of mail, and I interpreted it as Medina. So if you see fit to remain in Medina and let them be, then if they remain, they remain in the worst of positions, and if they enter Medina against us, we will fight them in it» [110] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/94–95.]].

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ liked that they should enter upon him in Medina, so that he might fight them in the alleys. But some men among the Muslims who had a share at Badr, and whom Allah honoured with martyrdom at Uhud, said: "Lead us out to our enemies."

They kept at the Messenger of Allah, out of their eagerness to meet the enemy, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went in, put on his armour. When they saw him put on his weapons, they regretted and said: "Evil is what we did, advising the Messenger of Allah while revelation comes to him?" They stood up and apologised to him and said: "Do what you see fit." He ﷺ said: «It is not for a prophet, once he has put on his armour, to take it off until he fights» [111] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/107.]].

The polytheists had camped at Uhud on Wednesday and Thursday. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out after Friday, after he had led his companions in the Friday prayer, and a man of the Ansar died that day, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, then went out to them and arrived at the glen of Uhud on Saturday, the fifteenth of Shawwal in the third year of the Hijrah. What happened in the battle of Uhud happened. That is His saying: ﴿And [mention] when you left your family in the morning, settling the believers﴾. Yahya ibn Thab read (tubawwi) the believers, light, unhamzated, from (abwā yubwī), like (arwā yarwī). The rest read it hamzated and doubled. It is said: bawwa'tu tabwi'atan, and abwaytuhum ibwā'an, when I settled them, and tabawwa'ū when they settled. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿that you two settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾ [Yunus: 87], and He said: ﴿And those who had settled the abode and faith before them﴾.

The doubled form is more eloquent and more well-known, and confirmation of it is His saying: ﴿And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾ [Yunus: 93], and He said: ﴿We will surely settle them in lofty chambers of Paradise﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 58].

Ibn Mas'ud read: tubawwi'u lil-mu'minin.

﴿Positions for fighting﴾, i.e., places and locations. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿in a seat of truth﴾ [al-Qamar: 55], and He said: ﴿that we used to sit therein in positions to listen﴾ [al-Jinn: 9]. Ashhab read: (maqa'ida lil-qitāl). ﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾: to become cowardly, weak, and to lag behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They were the Banu Salamah of the Khazraj and the Banu Harithah of the Aws, and they were the two wings of the army, and that

The Messenger of God ﷺ went out to Uhud with a thousand men. It was also said that they were nine hundred and ninety. Al-Zajjaj said: during the fighting at Uhud the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ numbered three thousand. The Messenger of God ﷺ went out to Uhud, having promised his Companions victory if they remained steadfast. When they reached al-Shawt, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy al-Khazraji withdrew with a third of the people and turned back with three hundred men, saying: "Why should we kill ourselves and our children?" Abu Jabir al-Sulami followed them and said: "I adjure you by God concerning your Prophet and concerning yourselves." ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you." The clans of Banu Salama and Banu Harithah were about to turn back with ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, but God preserved them and they did not turn back; they went on with the Messenger of God ﷺ. God then reminded them of His great favour in preserving them, saying: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart, and God was their Protector and Helper﴾.

Ibn Masʿud recited: "and God is their Protector" (wa-llahu waliyyuhum), because the "two parties" is a plural, like His saying: ﴿These are two adversaries who dispute concerning their Lord﴾ [al-Hajj: 19]. ﴿And upon God let the believers rely﴾.

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: "It does not please us that they should have us as we were about to be; and God has told us that He is our Protector."

﴿And God had already helped you at Badr﴾. Al-Shaʿbi said: Badr was the well of a man called Badr, and it was named after its owner. Al-Waqidi said: I mentioned this view [of al-Shaʿbi – manuscript reads: al-Shafiʿi] to ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar and Muhammad ibn Salih, and they denied it, saying: "Then why was al-Safra named so, and why was al-Jar named so? This is nothing; it is merely the name of the place." He said: I also mentioned that to Yahya ibn al-Nuʿman al-Ghifari, and he said: "I heard our elders of the Banu Ghifar say: it is our water and our dwelling, and no one ever owned it except us, and it and these [places] are not in the lands of Juhayna; it is in the lands of Ghifar." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/99.]

The Messenger of God ﷺ and the polytheists met there, and it was the first battle in which the Prophet of God ﷺ fought. Al-Dahhak said: Badr is a water-place in Mina on the road from Mecca, between Mecca and Medina.

I have given a brief and summary account of the expeditions (maghazi) and raids (sarayaʾ) of the Messenger of God ﷺ, since this is a branch of knowledge whose benefit is great. And success is from God.

Mention of the Expeditions of the Messenger of God ﷺ

The total of the expeditions in which the Messenger of God ﷺ himself took part was twenty-six. The first expedition he undertook was the expedition of Waddan, which is the expedition of al-Abwa'; then the expedition of Buwat toward the direction of Radwa; then the expedition of al-ʿUshayra from the valley of Yanbuʿ; then the first expedition of Badr, to pursue Kurz ibn Jabir; then the great expedition of Badr, in which God killed the chieftains of Quraysh; then the expedition of Banu Sulaym, until he reached al-Kadr, a water belonging to Banu Sulaym; then the expedition of al-Sawiq, pursuing Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, until he reached Qarqarat al-Kadr; then the expedition of Dhi Amr, which was the expedition against Ghatafan toward Najd; then the expedition of Najran, a place in the Hijaz above al-Furʿ; then the expedition of Uhud; then the expedition of al-Asad; then the expedition of Banu al-Nadir; then the expedition of Dhat al-Riqaʿ in Najd; then the last expedition of Badr; then the expedition of Dumat al-Jandal; then the expedition of the Trench (al-Khandaq); then the expedition of Banu Qurayza; then the expedition of Banu Lihyan; then the expedition of Banu Qarada; then the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq of Banu Khuzaʿa, in which he encountered them; then the expedition of Hudaybiyya, in which he did not intend fighting, but the polytheists barred him; then the expedition of Khaybar; then the expedition of the Conquest (al-Fath), the conquest of Mecca; then the expedition of Hunayn, in which he encountered the enemy; then the expedition of al-Taʾif, where he besieged them; then the expedition of Tabuk.

He fought in nine of these expeditions: the great expedition of Badr, which was on Friday, the seventeenth of Ramadan in the second year of the Hijra; Uhud, in Shawwal of the third year; the Trench; Banu Qurayza, in Shawwal of the fourth year; Banu al-Mustaliq; Banu Lihyan, in Shaʿban of the fifth year; Khaybar, in the sixth year; the Conquest, in Ramadan of the eighth year; and Hunayn, in Shawwal of the eighth year. Thus the first expedition in which he himself took part and fought was Badr, and the last was Tabuk.

Mention of the Raids (sarayaʾ) of the Prophet ﷺ

It is related from Muqassam, who said: the raids were thirty-six. They include the expedition of ʿUbayda ibn al-Harith to Hanna from below the pass of al-Murra, which is [a place] of stones [manuscript note: thus in the manuscript]; then the expedition of Hamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib to the seashore on the side of al-Fa'id. Some people place the expedition of Hamza before that of ʿUbayda. Then the expedition of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas to al-Kharrar [al-Kharrar: wells to the left of al-Hujja, near Khumm. Tabaqat al-Kubra: 2/5] in the land of the Hijaz; then the expedition of ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh to Nakhla; the expedition of Zayd ibn Haritha to al-Qardah, a water of Najd; the expedition of Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi to al-Raji', where they encountered [the enemy]; the expedition of Mundhir ibn ʿAmr to the Well of Maʿuna, where they encountered [the enemy]; the expedition of Abu ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrah to Dhu al-Qissa on the Iraq road; the expedition of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab to Turba in the land of Banu ʿAmir; the expedition of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib to Yemen; the expedition of Ghalib ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Kalbi, Kalb of Layth, to al-Kudayd, where they encountered al-Mulawwah; the expedition of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib to Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Saʿd of the people of Fadak; the expedition of Ibn Abi al-ʿAwja' al-Sulami to the land of Banu Sulaym, in which he and all his companions were struck; the expedition of ʿUkkasha ibn Mihsan to al-ʿUmra; the expedition of Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Asad to Qatan, a water of the waters of Banu Asad on the side of Najd, where they encountered [the enemy], and Masʿud ibn ʿUrwa was killed; the expedition of Muhammad ibn Maslama, brother of Banu Harithah, to al-Qurtaʾ, a place of Hawazin; the expedition of Bashir ibn Saʿd ibn Kaʿb ibn Murra to Fadak; the expedition of Bashir ibn Saʿd also to Hayyan, a town in the land of Khaybar; the expedition of Zayd ibn Haritha to al-Jumum in the land of Banu Sulaym; the expedition of Zayd also to Judham in the land of Hasmi, where they encountered [the enemy]; the expedition of Zayd also to a border area on the side of Nakhl on the Iraq road; the expedition of Zayd also to Wadi al-Qura, where he encountered Banu Fazara; the expedition of ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha to Khaybar twice, the first of which was the one in which he captured Bashar [manuscript: apparently "asir"], the Jew; the expedition of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAtik to Hunayn, in which he struck Abu Rafiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq.

The Messenger of God ﷺ had sent Muhammad ibn Maslama and his companions from Uhud and Badr to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, and they killed him. He sent ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays to Khalid ibn Sufyan al-Hudhali, who was at Nakhla, to attack him on behalf of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he killed him. The expedition of the commanders: Zayd ibn Haritha, Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, to Mu'ta in the land of Syria, where they were struck; the expedition of Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr al-Ghifari to Dhat al-Tilah in the land of Syria, where he and all his companions were struck; the expedition of ʿUyayna ibn Hisn ibn Badr al-Fazari against al-ʿAnbar of Banu Tamim; the expedition of Ghalib ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Kalbi, Kalb of Layth, to the land of Banu Murra, in which he struck Mirdas ibn Nahik and an ally of theirs from Juhayna, who was killed by Usama ibn Zayd. He is the one of whom the Prophet ﷺ said to Usama: "Who [will be] for you? Who [will be] for you with 'there is no god but God'?" [112].

The expedition of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs to Dhat al-Salasil in the land of Bali and ʿUdhra; and the expedition of [Abu Qatada] [manuscript: illegible word; what we have written is from al-Maghazi: 2/796] and his companions to Batn Idam before the Conquest, where they encountered [the enemy]; the expedition of al-Khayt to the seashore, under the command of Abu ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrah; and the expedition of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf.

﴿And God had already helped you at Badr when you were humiliated﴾: the plural of dhalil, like ʿazeez and aʿizza, and labib and albba. Here it means fewness of number. ﴿So be mindful of God, that you may be thankful﴾. ﴿When you said to the believers: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should aid you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ They differed concerning this verse. Qatada said: [...] [manuscript: illegible; what we have written is from al-Maghazi: 2/796] on the day of Badr God aided them with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then five thousand. This is shown by His saying: ﴿when you were seeking help from your Lord, and He answered you﴾ [al-Anfal: 9], to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿Yes! If you are patient and mindful of God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will aid you with five thousand angels, marked﴾. The believers were patient on the day of Badr and were mindful of God, so God aided them with five thousand angels as He had promised them. All of this was on the day of Badr. Al-Hasan said: these five thousand angels are a reinforcement for the believers until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: the angels did not fight except on the day of Badr; on other occasions they attend the battle but do not fight, they are only a number and a reinforcement.

ʿUmar ibn Abi Ishaq said: When the day of Uhud came, the Messenger of God ﷺ was left exposed, and Saʿd ibn Malik remained shooting, with a young man who supplied him with arrows. When the arrows ran out, he brought them to him and scattered them, and he said: "Shoot, Abu Ishaq! Shoot, Abu Ishaq!" twice. When the battle was over, he was asked about the man, but he was not known. [al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/70.]

Al-Shaʿbi said: It reached the Messenger of God ﷺ and the Muslims on the day of Badr that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi was reinforcing the polytheists, and this grieved them, so God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Is it not enough for you...﴾ to His saying ﴿marked﴾. When Kurz heard of the defeat, he turned back and did not come to them, and did not reinforce them; God reinforced them also with five thousand, though they had already been reinforced with a thousand.

Others said: God the Exalted only promised the Muslims on the day of Badr that if they were patient in His obedience and mindful of His prohibitions, He would reinforce them in all their wars. They were not patient and were not mindful, except on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), so God the Exalted reinforced them until they besieged Qurayza.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Awfa said: We were besieging Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir for as long as God willed that we should besiege them, but victory was not granted to us, so we returned. The Messenger of God ﷺ asked for water for washing, and while he was washing his head, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you have laid down your weapons, but the angels have not laid down their burdens?" The Messenger of God ﷺ asked for a cloth and wrapped it around his head, without washing it, and then he called out to us, and we rose, weary and exhausted, not minding the march at all, until we came to Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir. On that day God the Exalted reinforced us with three thousand angels, and God granted us a limited victory, and we returned with God's blessing and favour.

Others said: this was on the day of Uhud. God the Mighty and Majestic had promised them reinforcement if they were patient, but they were not patient, so they were not reinforced, not even with a single angel; had they been reinforced, they would not have been defeated. This is the view of ʿIkrima and al-Dahhak. This was on the day of Uhud when Abu Sufyan and his companions withdrew. The reason was that the Messenger of God ﷺ feared the polytheists would enter Medina, so he sent ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) and said: "Go out on the trail of the people and see what they do and what they intend. If they have dismounted from the horses and mounted camels, they intend Mecca; if they ride horses and drive camels, they intend Medina. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if they intend it, I will march against them there and then fight them outright."

ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) said: "I went out on their trail to see what they were doing, and I saw that they had dismounted from the horses, mounted camels, and set off for Mecca. The Messenger of God ﷺ had said: 'Whichever it is, come back and tell me quickly.' When I saw them heading for Mecca, I came back shouting, unable to conceal what I felt of joy. They returned to Mecca and we returned to Medina. God the Exalted then revealed in this regard: ﴿Is it not enough for you that your Lord should aid you...﴾" [Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/207], meaning that they turned back to you and entered Medina.

In the recitation of Ubayy (ألا يكفيكم أن يمدكم ربكم), that is, "Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you," meaning: give you and help you.

Al-Mufaddal said: [everything] [manuscript: "upon"] that was in the sense of strength and assistance is said to be amadda yumiddu imdadan; and everything in the sense of increase is said to be madda yamuddu madda, and from it His saying: ﴿and the sea, after it, [adds to it] seven seas﴾ [Luqman: 27].

Some of them said: madd is for evil and imdad is for good. This is shown by His saying: ﴿and He lets them continue in their rebellion, wandering blindly﴾ [al-Baqara: 15], and His saying: ﴿We shall extend for him the punishment, an extension﴾ [Maryam: 79].

He said of good: ﴿I will reinforce you with a thousand﴾ [al-Anfal: 9], and He said: ﴿your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand﴾, and He said: ﴿and We reinforced you with wealth and sons﴾ [al-Isra: 6].

He said: ﴿Do they reckon that what We reinforce them with of wealth and sons﴾ [al-Muminun: 55]; and He said: ﴿and We reinforced them with fruit﴾ [al-Tur: 22]; and He said: ﴿and He will reinforce you with wealth and sons﴾ [Nuh: 12]; ﴿I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, sent down﴾ [al-Anfal: 9]. Abu Haywaa recited with a kasra on the zay, lightened, meaning "sent down" victory. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Talha ibn Musarrif, ʿUmar ibn Maymun and Ibn ʿAmir read it doubled and with a fatha on the zay, for intensification. Its confirmation is His saying: ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels﴾ [al-Anʿam: 111]. And His saying: ﴿marked﴾. The others read it with a fatha on the zay and lightened. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿Why have the angels not been sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?﴾ [al-Furqan: 21], and His saying: ﴿and He sent down armies you did not see﴾ [al-Tawba: 26]. The explanation of inzal (sending down) is to make a thing go from a height to a low place. Then He said: ﴿Yes!﴾, which confirms the word of God the Exalted and the word of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

﴿If you are patient﴾ against your enemy, ﴿and mindful﴾ of disobeying your Lord.

﴿and they come upon you﴾ from the polytheists, ﴿suddenly, this very moment﴾ [Al ʿImran: 125]. ʿIkrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Rabiʿ, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: "from their direction now," and this is the narration of ʿAtiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas. Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Zadhan said: "from their anger now," for they had been angry on the day of Uhud for the sake of the day of Badr because of what they had suffered. The origin of fawr is intending a thing and taking up its immediate matter; it comes from their saying: the pot boiled (fara al-qidr tafuru fawran wa-fawaran) when it boiled, and ﴿the oven gushed forth﴾ [Hud: 40; al-Muminun: 27]. A poet said:

Their pot boils over us, so it keeps its heat,
and when it boils hot, it cools for us.

﴿with five thousand of the angels, marked﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim and Yaʿqub read it with a kasra on the waw, and Abu Hatim chose this; the rest read it with a fatha, and Abu ʿUbayd chose this. Whoever reads with a kasra means that they marked their horses; whoever reads with a fatha means themselves. The sawma is the sign by which the horseman marks himself in war. They differed about what the marking attributed to the angels in this verse was.

ʿUmayr ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to his companions on the day of Badr: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves with red wool on their caps and their helmets." [al-Musannaf: 8/346; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/196.]

Al-Dahhak and Qatada: [with ʿihn] [ʿihn: wool dyed in various colours] on their forelocks and ears. Mujahid: the tails and manes of their horses were cut short, and their forelocks were marked. Al-Rabiʿ: they were on piebald horses. ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas (may God be pleased with them): they had white turbans, which they let hang between their shoulders. Hisham ibn ʿUrwa al-Kalbi: yellow turbans loose on their shoulders.

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said: al-Zubayr wore a yellow cloak and a yellow turban on the day of Badr, and the angels descended on the day of Badr marked with yellow turbans. [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 10/45.]

Al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir related from his grandfather Abu Usayd, who was a veteran of Badr, who said: "If my sight were restored, and you then went with me to Badr, I would show you the ravine from which the angels emerged in yellow turbans, having let them hang between their shoulders." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/109.] ʿIkrima said: they had the signs of battle. Al-Suddi: the sign of the believers.

﴿And God did not make it﴾, meaning this promise and reinforcement, ﴿except as good news, and that your hearts might be at rest therewith﴾, that your hearts might be calmed by it, so that you would not be dismayed by the multitude of your enemy and the fewness of your number.

﴿And victory is only from God﴾, because might and judgment belong to Him, ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Its parallel is in al-Anfal. Then He said: ﴿and seek help from God and rely upon Him﴾.

﴿That He might cut off a part﴾. The construction of the verse: ﴿And God had already helped you at Badr...﴾ ﴿that He might cut off a part﴾, meaning: that He might destroy a group ﴿of those who disbelieved﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off﴾ [al-Anʿam: 45], meaning destroyed. And in al-Anfal: ﴿and that He might cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Anfal: 7], and in al-Hijr: ﴿that the last remnant of these is cut off at dawn﴾ [al-Hijr: 66]. Al-Suddi: its meaning is to demolish one pillar of the pillars of polytheism by killing and capture; so there were slain from among their chiefs and leaders at Badr seventy, and seventy were taken captive.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 116–129 (part 3 of 6):

Or He will humble them by disappointment, so they will turn back frustrated, having gained nothing of what they were hoping for in terms of victory over you.

Al-Kalbi said: "Or He will humble them" means: or He will defeat them by felling them upon their faces. Al-Mu'arrikh said: "He will disgrace them." Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "He will enrage them." Al-Mubarrad said: "He will grant victory over them." Al-Suddi said: "He will curse them." Abu 'Ubayda said: "He will destroy them." They said: and the people of reflection [see] [[Addition from al-Masir: 2/27.]] that the ta' (ت) in it is a transformation of the dal (د), because the original is yakbidahum, meaning: He will strike them in their livers (akbad) with grief and rage. It is said: grief has burned his liver, and enmity has burned his liver, and the Arabs say of an enemy: "black of liver." Al-A'sha said:

"What I endured in coming to a people, they are enemies and their livers are black."

It is as if the livers, when burned by the intensity of enmity, turned black; and the ta' and the dal interchange, as one says: harrat al-thawb and harradahu, when he tore it. What confirms this interpretation is the reading of Lahiq ibn Humayd: "aw yakbidahum," with a dal.

"You have no part in the affair" (laysa laka min al-amri shay'). The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse.

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: The Prophet ﷺ wished to invoke curses upon those of his companions who turned away from him on the day of Uhud, and 'Uthman was among them. So God, Mighty and Majestic, forbade him from that, and He turned in mercy toward them, and this verse was revealed.

'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: A man from Hudhayl called 'Abdullah ibn Qami'ah wounded the face of the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day of Uhud, so the Messenger of God ﷺ invoked a curse upon him. His death came when God gave power over him to a he-goat which gored him until he died.

'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas split his head and broke his incisor, so he invoked a curse upon him and said: "O God, let him not complete a year before he dies as an unbeliever." He said: The year had not passed over him before he died as an unbeliever, and then God revealed this verse. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/117.]]

Al-Kalbi and al-Rabi' said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day of Uhud, when his face had been wounded and his incisor had been struck out. The Messenger of God ﷺ resolved to curse the polytheists and invoke against them, so God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse, because He knew that many of them would believe.

What indicates this is what Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated from Humayd, from Anas, who said: When the day of Uhud came, the Messenger of God ﷺ was struck on the top of his forehead, his incisor was broken, and his face was wounded. He began wiping the blood from his face, while Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, was washing the blood from his face, and the Messenger of God ﷺ was saying: "How will a people prosper who dye the face of their Prophet with blood while he calls them to their Lord?" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/179.]] So God, exalted, revealed: "You have no part in the affair."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Sha'bi and Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The wrath of God has intensified against the one who bloodied the face of His Prophet," a high group of the Quraysh climbed the mountain, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "[O God, indeed] it is not fitting for them to be above us." 'Umar and a group of the Muhajirun came and drove them down. The Messenger of God ﷺ rose to climb a rock, but he was heavily armored between two coats of mail and could not manage it, so Talhah sat beneath him and he rose until he stood upon it. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Talhah has made Paradise obligatory." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/182.]]

Hind and the women with her stood mutilating the slain of the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, slitting off ears and noses, until Hind made necklaces from them and gave them to Wahshi. She ripped open the liver of Hamzah and chewed it but could not swallow it, so she spat it out. Then she climbed a high rock and shouted:

"We have repaid you for the day of Badr,
and war after war is of fierce flame.
I had no patience for what happened to 'Utbah,
my father, my uncle, my brother, and my son.
You have healed my chest and fulfilled my vow;
Wahshi has healed the thirst of my chest."
[['Uyun al-Athar: 1/424; al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah: 4/42, with variation in the second half of the second line.]]

They said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Hasan said: Hamzah said: "O God, if we meet these people tomorrow, I ask You that they kill me, cut open my belly, and slit my nose and ears, so that You say to me on the Day of Resurrection: 'Why was this done to you?' and I will say: 'For You.'" When the day of Uhud came, he was killed, his belly was cut open, and his ears and nose were slit. A man who heard it said: "As for this one, he has been given in this world what he asked for, and God will give him what he asked for in the Hereafter."

They said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ and the Muslims saw what had been done to their companions of slitting ears and noses and cutting off private parts, they said: "If God grants us victory over them, we will certainly do to them the like of what they did, and we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no Arab has ever inflicted upon anyone." So God, exalted, revealed this verse.

'Ata' said: After Uhud, the Messenger of God ﷺ remained forty days invoking curses upon four of the kings of Kindah: Masrah, Ahmad, Lahy, and their brother al-'Amrdah; and upon a tribe of Hudhayl called the Lahyan; and upon branches of Sulaym, and upon Dhakwan, 'Usayyah and al-Qarah. He would say: "O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/521.]] God answered his supplication, and they suffered drought until they ate their children, and ate dogs, carrion, and burned bones. When the forty days ended, this verse was revealed.

From Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "O God, curse Abu Sufyan; O God, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham; O God, curse Safwan ibn Umayyah." [[Ibid.: 2/93; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/71.]] So God, exalted, revealed: "You have no part in the affair" [[Surah Al 'Imran: 128.]], and they embraced Islam and their Islam was good.

Al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say at the dawn prayer when he raised his head from bowing: "Our Lord, to You be praise. O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," invoking against some hypocrites, so God, exalted, revealed: "You have no part in the affair," and the rest of the verse. [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/35; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/374.]]

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning the well of Ma'unah, where seventy men of the reciters among the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ were killed, whose leader was al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr. The Messenger of God ﷺ had sent them to the well of Ma'unah in Safar of the fourth year of the Hijrah, four months after Uhud, to teach people the Qur'an and knowledge, and they were all killed.

'Amir ibn al-Tufayl: Among them was 'Amir ibn Fuhayrah, freed slave of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. When he was killed, he was lifted up between heaven and earth. The Messenger of God ﷺ was deeply grieved by this and mourned them for a month, and then "You have no part in the affair" was revealed.

Although this verse is general in wording, what is meant by it is particular; its implied sense is: "You have no part in the affair according to your desire." The lam in His saying "laka" (for you) means "ila" (to you), like His saying: "Indeed we heard a caller calling to faith" [[Surah Al 'Imran: 193.]], and His saying: "Praise be to God who guided us to this" [[Surah al-A'raf: 43.]], and similar.

"Or He will turn to them in forgiveness or punish them, for they are wrongdoers" ... "You have no part in the affair," and this is a good reading.

Some of them said: "Or" (aw) here means "until" (hatta), meaning: you have no part in the affair until He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them.

Then He said: "And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth..." to "multiplied manifold."

Abu Ja'far and Shaybah read: "mudda'afah" (with tashdid).

'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning the saying of God, exalted: "O you who believe, do not consume usury, doubled and redoubled" [[Surah Al 'Imran: 130.]]: it is that a man would have a debt owed to him by another man, and when the term came due he demanded it from his debtor, and the debtor said: "Delay me and I will increase your wealth," and they would do so, so God admonished them.

Then He said: "And fear God regarding usury, so that you do not consume it, that perhaps you may prosper." Then He warned them, saying: "And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers." In it is evidence that the Fire is created, refuting the Jahmiyyah, because what is non-existent cannot be prepared. "And obey God and the Messenger, that perhaps you may be shown mercy," so that you may be shown mercy and not be punished. "And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord..." to the end of the verse.

'Ata' said: The Muslims said to the Prophet ﷺ: "The Children of Israel were more honored by God, Mighty and Majestic, than we are, and when they sinned, the expiation of their sins would be written upon the threshold of their doors: 'Cut off your nose, cut off your ear, do such-and-such.'" The Prophet, peace be upon him, was silent, so God, exalted, revealed: "And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord," meaning: race toward the deeds that bring forgiveness.

The people of Medina and Syria omitted the waw from it.

They differed concerning the cause that brings about this forgiveness:

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Hasten to Islam." Abu al-'Aliyah and Abu Rawq: "To emigration." 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face: "To the performance of the obligations." 'Uthman ibn 'Affan: "Sincerity." Anas ibn Malik: "It is the first takbir." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "To the performance of obedience." Yaman: "To the five prayers." al-Dahhak: "To jihad." 'Ikrimah: "To repentance." Muqatil: "To righteous deeds." Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "To following the commands and refraining from the prohibitions." Sahl ibn 'Abdullah: "To the Sunnah." Some of them: "To the congregation and the assemblies."

"And a Garden" — meaning, toward a Garden, "whose breadth is the heavens and the earth" — that is, its breadth is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth, like His saying: "Your creation and your resurrection are only as a single soul" [[Surah Luqman: 28.]], meaning: like the resurrection of a single soul.

The poet said:

"I thought the bellowing of my she-camel was the cry of a ewe,
and it was not, by your life, the cry of a ewe."

He means the voice of a ewe.

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying in Surah al-Hadid: "like the breadth of the heaven and the earth" [[Surah al-Hadid: 21.]], meaning: if they were spread out and joined one to another. The breadth is singled out for emphasis, because the length of anything is generally greater than its breadth. It says: "This is the description of its breadth; how then is its length?" The evidence for this is the saying of al-Zuhri: "Only its breadth is described; as for its length, none knows it but God," like His saying: "Reclining on couches whose linings are of brocade" [[Surah al-Rahman: 54.]], where the lining is described with the goodness of what is known of adornment, since it is known that the outer surfaces are finer and more precious than the linings.

Most of the scholars of meaning said: He did not intend the breadth which is the opposite of length, but rather its vastness and greatness, like the saying of the Arabs: "He is broader than al-Dahna," meaning: wider.

Jarir said:

"Umamah persisted in blaming me, and she did not know
the breadth of al-Samawah, my journeys by day or by morning."

Al-Asma'i recited:

"They carry us across the breadth of the wilderness,
and for us against them is nothing but the sweat of their cheeks."

Another said:

"As if the lands of God, though they are broad,
upon the fearful one who is pursued, his hand is a noose."

By this illustration, He does not mean that it is like the heavens and the earth — no. The meaning is other than that: like the breadth of the seven heavens and the seven earths in your estimation, because those two will necessarily pass away, as in His saying: "abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure" [[Surah Hud: 107.]], because they will necessarily pass away.

Ya'la ibn Murrah said: I met al-Tanukhi, the envoy of Heraclius to the Messenger of God ﷺ at Homs, an elderly man. He said: "I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ with the letter of Heraclius, and he handed the scroll to a man on his left." I said: "Who among your companions is the one who reads?" They said: "Mu'awiyah." Then the letter of my companion (came): "You wrote to me calling me to a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth [prepared for the God-fearing]; then where is the Fire?" The Messenger of God said: "Glory be to God; then where is the night when the day comes?" [113] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/122.]]

Tariq ibn Shihab narrated that some Jews asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab while his companions were present, saying: "Tell us about your saying: 'a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth'; then where is the Fire?" The people hesitated, so 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said: "Tell me: when the night comes, where is the day; and when the day comes, where is the night?" They said: "It is only like that in the Torah."

Anas ibn Malik was asked about Paradise: "Is it on the earth or in the heaven?" He said: "What earth and what heaven could contain Paradise?" It was asked: "Then where is it?" He said: "Above the seven heavens, beneath the Throne."

Qatadah said: They used to hold that Paradise is above the seven heavens, and that Hell is beneath the seven earths.

"Prepared for the God-fearing" (muttaqin). Then He described them, saying: "Those who spend in ease and in hardship" — meaning in hardship and ease, in adversity and prosperity. The first of their character traits is the spending of wealth, and generosity; for this reason:

Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah informed us [Thana Zayd ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz Abu Jabir, thana Jahdar, thana Baqiyyah, thana al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said]: "Paradise is the abode of the generous." [[Musnad al-Shihab: 1/102; al-Mawdu'at by Ibn al-Jawzi: 2/185.]]

al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The generous one is near to God, near to Paradise, near to people, far from the Fire; and the miser is far from God, far from Paradise, far from people, near to the Fire." [114] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 3/231, h. 2027.]]

"In it are clear signs: the station of Ibrahim" — a clear sign, singular: he intended the station of Ibrahim alone, and he said: the imprint of his two feet in the station is a clear sign.

The rest read "ayat" in the plural: they meant the station of Ibrahim, the Black Stone, the Hijr, Zamzam, and the sacred sites; and the mention of the station of Ibrahim has passed in Surah al-Baqarah. "And whoever enters it is safe" — from being attacked within it, because it is a sanctuary, and this is by the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when he said: "My Lord, make this a secure city" [[Surah al-Baqarah: 126.]]. In the pre-Islamic period, whoever entered it and sought refuge there was safe from raids and killing, and Islam did not increase it except in strength.

Abu al-Khuld wrote to Ibn 'Abbas that the first to take refuge in the sanctuary were the small and large fish, fleeing from the flood. It was also said: "whoever enters it" in the year of the 'Umrat al-Qada' with Muhammad ﷺ "is safe," evidenced by His saying: "You will certainly enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in safety" [[Surah al-Fath: 27.]].

The scholars of meaning said: The form of the verse is a report but its meaning is a command; its implied sense is: "Whoever enters it, then make it safe," like His saying: "So there shall be no obscenity, no transgression, and no disputing during the Hajj" [[Surah al-Baqarah: 197.]], meaning: do not be obscene, do not transgress, do not dispute. It was also said: "And whoever enters it" to perform the rite, honoring it, knowing its right, drawing near to God, Mighty and Majestic, "is safe" on the Day of Resurrection. This is like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever's night prayer is abundant, his face is beautified by day," meaning on the day of Resurrection. [[Musnad al-Shihab (Ibn Salamah): 1/252.]] [115]

This is supported by what Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak concerning "And whoever enters it is safe," saying: whoever performs the pilgrimage and enters it is safe from the sins he had committed before that.

Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash narrated from Yahya ibn Ja'dah concerning His saying: "And whoever enters it is safe," that he said: "From the Fire."

Ja'far al-Sadiq (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whoever enters it in purity, as the prophets and saints entered it, is safe from His punishment."

Abu al-Najm al-Qurashi, the Sufi, said: I was circumambulating the House and I said: "O my master, I say: 'And whoever enters it is safe'—safe from what?" I heard someone behind me saying: "Safe from the Fire." I turned around and saw nothing.

What confirms this interpretation is what Aban ibn 'Ayyash narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever dies in either of the two sanctuaries, God will raise him among the safe." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 5/245.]] [116]

It is also narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Al-Hajun and al-Baqi' will be taken by their edges and scattered into Paradise, and they are the cemeteries of Makkah and Madinah." [[Kashf al-Khafa': 1/351.]] [117]

Shaqiq ibn Salamah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood at the pass of the cemetery, and they were not a cemetery at that time, and he said: "God will raise from this place, from this whole sanctuary, seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, each one of them interceding for seventy thousand, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/262, h. 34960.]]

And with it, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd al-'Ammi, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:

"Whoever endures the heat of Makkah for an hour of a day, Hell will be distanced from him by a journey of two hundred years, and Paradise will be brought near to him by a journey of one hundred years." [Kanz al-Ummal: 12/210, no. 34704.] [118]

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It is written in the Torah that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will send seven hundred thousand angels from among the angels brought near, each one holding in his hand a chain of gold, to the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram). He will say to them: "Go to the Sacred House and bind it with these chains, then lead it to the place of gathering (al-mahshar)." They will come to it and bind it with seven hundred thousand chains of gold, then pull it, while an angel calls out: "O Ka'bah of Allah, proceed!" She will say: "I will not proceed until I am given my request." An angel from the atmosphere of the heavens will call out: "Ask, and you will be given." The Ka'bah will say: "O Lord, intercede for me on behalf of my neighbours who were buried around me among the believers." Allah will say: "I have granted you your request." He said: Then the dead of Makkah will be raised from their graves with bright faces, all of them in the state of ihram, and they will gather around the Ka'bah reciting the talbiyah. Then the angels will say: "Proceed, O Ka'bah of Allah," and she will say: "I will not proceed until I am given my request." An angel from the atmosphere of the heavens will call out: "Ask, and you will be given." The Ka'bah will say: "O Lord, Your believing servants who came to me from every deep ravine, disheveled and dusty, who left behind their families, children and loved ones, and set out longing for me as visitors, Muslims, and obedient, until they completed their rites as You commanded them, I ask You to secure them from the Great Terror, to intercede for me on their behalf, and to gather them around me." The angel will call: "Among them are those who committed sins after you and persisted in the major sins until the Fire became due for them." The Ka'bah will say: "I only ask You for intercession for the people of the grave sins." Allah will say: "I have interceded for you on their behalf and granted you your request." A caller from the atmosphere of the heavens will call out: "Whoever visited the Ka'bah, let him withdraw from among the people." They will withdraw, and Allah will gather them around the Sacred House with bright faces, safe from the Fire, circumambulating and reciting the talbiyah. Then an angel from the atmosphere of the heavens will call out: "O Ka'bah of Allah, proceed!" The Ka'bah will say: "Labbayk, labbayk; the good is in Your hands; labbayk, You have no partner, labbayk; indeed the praise and the blessing are Yours, and the dominion; You have no partner." Then they will pull her to the place of gathering. [Ihanat al-Talibin: 2/313-314.]

{Allah has made it a duty upon mankind to make the pilgrimage to the House, for those who are able to make their way there.} ﴿وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا﴾

Ikrimah said: When it was revealed, {Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him} [Surah Al 'Imran: 85], the Jews said: "We are Muslims," so they were commanded to make the pilgrimage if they were Muslims. The lam in His words {lillah} is the lam of obligation and binding, meaning that the pilgrimage to the House has been prescribed and made obligatory upon mankind.

Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ḥijj (حِجُّ) with a kasrah on the ḥa' in this word alone. Ibn Abi Ishaq read every occurrence in the Qur'an with a kasrah, and this is the dialect of the people of Najd. The rest read it with a fatha throughout the Qur'an, and this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. This is the preference of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim; both are eloquent dialects with one meaning.

Al-Hasan al-Ju'fi said: the fatha (ḥajj) is the verbal noun and the kasrah (ḥijj) is the name of the act. Then he said: {those who are able to make their way there}. Know that the conditions for the obligation of the pilgrimage are nine things: maturity (al-bulugh), sanity (al-'aql), Islam, and freedom...

Because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The pen is lifted from three: from the child until he reaches maturity, from the insane until he recovers, and from the sleeper until he wakes." [Musnad Ahmad: 6/100, with variation.] [119]

And because of his saying (ﷺ): "Any child who performs the pilgrimage and then reaches puberty must perform another pilgrimage; and any bedouin who performs the pilgrimage and then migrates must perform another pilgrimage." [120] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 3/140; Nasb al-Rayah: 3/75.]

By "migration" (hijrah) here he means Islam and clearing the road (takhliyat al-tariq), that is, that the road be safe and passable, with no obstacle from an enemy or the like. If it is not passable, the pilgrimage is not obligatory.

The evidence for this: if one is in ihram and an enemy blocks him, he may exit the state of ihram. If it is permissible for him to leave it because of being blocked, then entering it and intending it, while the blockade exists, is all the more fitting. And the possibility of travel: that there be enough time in which the pilgrimage can be performed. If the conditions of the pilgrimage are met, but [....] [an illegible word], and the pilgrim has reached, for example, [al-Karqa] [as it stands in the original], then it is not obligatory upon him, because its conditions came into existence at a time when performing it was impossible; he is like a child who reaches maturity in the middle of the day of fasting, so the fast of that day is not obligatory upon him. It was added: sufficient provision, a mount that conveys him, and physical strength. The opinions of the jurists differ regarding the details of these three conditions.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: ability (al-istita'ah) has two aspects: that he be able in body and have from his wealth what will convey him to the pilgrimage; and the second: that he be disabled in his body (ma'dub, one who is paralysed and cannot move), unable to sit firmly on his mount, yet able to find someone who will perform it on his behalf, whether for a wage or without one. As for the one able by means of wealth, the obligation of the pilgrimage is binding on him by the Sunnah, because of the hadith of the woman of Khath'am. As for the one able by his own body, he is the strong person who suffers no unbearable hardship in sitting on the mount. When he possesses provision and a mount, the obligation of the pilgrimage binds him. If he lacks provision and mount, or one of them, the obligation falls from him. If he is able to walk and is capable of it, and finds provision, or is able to earn provision on the way through a trade such as leatherwork or cupping (hijamah) or the like, then it is recommended for him to perform the pilgrimage on foot, whether man or woman.

Al-Shafi'i said: A man has less excuse than a woman, because he is stronger. This is by way of recommendation, not obligation. As for one who can obtain provision by asking people on the road, I dislike that he perform the pilgrimage, because he becomes a burden upon people. This that I have mentioned, that the existence of provision and mount is a condition for the obligation of the pilgrimage, is the view of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), his son 'Abdullah, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas. Among the Tabi'un: al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and 'Ata'. It is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions, al-Shafi'i, al-Thawri, Ahmad and Ishaq. Their evidence is what was narrated by 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "What is the way (al-sabil) to the pilgrimage?" He said: "Provision and a mount." [121] [al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/56.]

Similarly narrated by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'ishah, Jabir ibn 'Abdullah and Anas ibn Malik.

Al-Harith narrated from 'Ali (may Allah ennoble his face) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever possesses provision and a mount that can carry him to the House of Allah, and does not perform the pilgrimage, then it does not matter whether he dies as a Jew or a Christian, for Allah the Exalted says: {And to Allah is owed from mankind the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make their way there; and whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need of the worlds}." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2/154.] [122]

Ibn 'Umar said: A man stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what makes the pilgrimage obligatory?" He said: "Provision and a mount." He said: "Then what is the pilgrim (al-hajj)?" He said: "[The dishevelled, the unscented]" (al-sha'th al-tafl; al-tafl: one who has abandoned the use of perfume). He said: "Then what is the best pilgrimage?" He said: "The ajj and the thajj" (al-ajj: raising the voice loudly in the talbiyah; al-thajj: sacrificing camels). [al-Musannaf, al-Kufi: 4/535.] [123]

Malik said: If one is able to walk and finds provision and a mount, the pilgrimage is obligatory upon him without disagreement. If he does not find provision and mount but is able to walk, it is considered: if he owns provision, the obligation of the pilgrimage binds him in every case. If he does not own provision but is able to earn his needs on the way, this differs according to the person's condition: if he is one of the people of dignity (al-muruwwat) who does not earn with his own hands, it is not obligatory upon him; if he earns his sustenance through trade or craft, the obligation of the pilgrimage binds him. Likewise, if his habit is to ask people, the obligation binds him. Thus Malik made the pilgrimage obligatory upon one capable of walking when he has no provision or mount. This is the view of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, al-Sha'bi and 'Ikrimah.

Al-Dahhak said: If he is a healthy young man with no property, he must hire himself out for his food or his wages until he completes his pilgrimage. Someone said to him: "Did Allah not charge people to walk to the House?" He said: "If some of them had an inheritance in Makkah, would he leave it? Rather he would go to it even if crawling. Likewise the pilgrimage is obligatory upon him." Those (who hold this view) argued with His words, the Exalted: {And proclaim among the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot} [Surah al-Hajj: 27], meaning on foot.

They said: Because the pilgrimage is one of the bodily acts of worship and one of the individual obligations, it must not be that the provision and mount are conditions for its obligation, like prayer and fasting. Thus, since it is established that the existence of provision and mount is a condition for the obligation of the pilgrimage according to the view of most scholars, it is necessary to explain how the mount and the expenses are to be considered, and that varies with the circumstances of people.

As for the mount: it is that which does not impose severe hardship in riding it. As for expenses: if he has a family and dependents whose maintenance is obligatory upon him, the pilgrimage is not binding on him until he has their maintenance for the duration of his absence for going and returning, because this spending is an obligation with immediacy (ʿala al-fawr), whereas the pilgrimage is an obligation with leeway (ʿala al-tarakhi), and giving precedence to the maintenance of dependents is more fitting and more important.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is sufficient sin for a man to neglect those he provides for." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/160.] [124] If he has no family or dependents, then his travel expenses are necessary. Is his return to be considered or not? On this there are two views among the jurists. Some said: it is not considered, because leaving his homeland does not impose great hardship on him, since he has no family or dependents there; every land is his homeland.

Others said: it is considered, and this is the apparent position of al-Shafi'i's school, for he said in al-Imla': "The pilgrimage is not obligatory on him until he has its expenses going and coming." He stated it absolutely and made no distinction. This is more correct, because a person feels estrangement at separation from his homeland just as he does at separation from his dwelling. Do you not see that if an unmarried person commits fornication he is flogged and exiled from his land, whether or not he has family there? If he has property that yields income, or clothing, furniture and the like, the obligation of the pilgrimage binds him, and he must sell the property, the goods and the wealth and spend them on the pilgrimage. As for the dwelling and the servant...

Al-Shafi'i said in al-Umm: If he has a dwelling and a servant, and his family's maintenance for the duration of his absence, the pilgrimage is obligatory upon him.

The apparent meaning of this is that he considers that the pilgrimage money must exceed the servant and dwelling, because he placed them before his family's maintenance, as if he said: "after all this."

His companions said: He is obliged to sell the dwelling and the servant and buy a dwelling and a servant for his family. As for one who has merchandise with which he trades, whose profit suffices for his own and his dependents' needs on an ongoing basis, and if he spends from the principal of the merchandise its profit is disrupted and no longer suffices for his needs, is he obliged to perform the pilgrimage from the principal of the merchandise or not?

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Surayj said: He is not obliged to do so; the merchandise remains as it is and he does not perform the pilgrimage from its principal, because the pilgrimage is only obligatory upon him from the surplus over his needs.

Others said: Rather he must perform the pilgrimage from the principal of the merchandise, and this is the sound and well-known view held by the majority, because there is no disagreement that if he had property that supplied his income, he would be obliged to sell the principal of that property for the pilgrimage, and likewise the merchandise. The summary is that the obligation of the pilgrimage is tied to what the obligation of zakat al-fitr is tied to: whatever must be sold for zakat al-fitr must be sold for the pilgrimage. This was the discussion of one of the two aspects of ability. As for the other aspect: it is that he be disabled in his body and unable to sit on a mount at all, or be deformed from birth, or be chronically and severely ill with no hope of recovery, or be an elderly, weak old man, yet be able to find someone who will obey him if he commands him to perform the pilgrimage on his behalf. This too is a form of ability, of a certain kind, and it has two aspects:

One: that he be able to have money with which he can hire someone to perform the pilgrimage; in this case the obligation of the pilgrimage binds him. This is the view of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who is related to have said to an elderly man who had not performed the pilgrimage: "Equip a man to perform the pilgrimage on your behalf."

This is the view of al-Shafi'i, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and his companions, 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad ibn al-Mubarak, and Ishaq.

Two: that he be able to find someone who offers obedience and deputyship to perform the pilgrimage on his behalf. This too obligates him to perform the pilgrimage according to al-Shafi'i, Ibn Hanbal and Ibn Rahawayh.

Abu Hanifah said: The pilgrimage is not obligatory upon him by offering of obedience in any case.

Malik said: If he is disabled, the obligation of the pilgrimage falls from him entirely, whether he is able to find someone to perform it with money or without money, or if he is incapable, then the obligation of the pilgrimage does not bind him. If the pilgrimage had been obligatory upon him and then he became disabled and chronically ill, the obligation falls from him. It is not permissible for anyone to perform it on his behalf during his lifetime in any case; rather, if he bequeaths that it be performed on his behalf, it is performed after his death from one-third of his estate, and it is voluntary. He argued with the words of the Exalted: {And that man has nothing but what he strove for} [Surah al-Najm: 39]. He stated that man has nothing except what he strove for; whoever says that someone else's striving benefits him has contradicted the apparent meaning of the verse. And He, Mighty and Majestic, says: {And to Allah is owed from mankind the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make their way there} [Surah Al 'Imran: 97]. This person is not able, because the pilgrimage is the journey to the House by one's own self; and from the standpoint of reasoning, he is unable to perform the pilgrimage himself, so it must not be obligatory upon him to perform it for himself, just as if he were disabled and had no property. Also, every act of worship that cannot be done by proxy when one is able, must not be done by proxy when one is unable, like prayer; the reverse of this is zakat.

The evidence of al-Shafi'i and his companions is what al-Zuhri narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar from Ibn 'Abbas: a woman from Khath'am asked the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the obligation Allah has placed upon His servants regarding the pilgrimage has reached my father as an elderly man who cannot remain steady on the mount. Is it sufficient if I perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Will that benefit him?" He said: "Do you see that if your father had a debt and you paid it, would it not be sufficient?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then the debt owed to Allah is more deserving." [Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah: 4/346.] [125]

So the Prophet (ﷺ) made the pilgrimage obligatory upon him through his daughter's obedience to him and her offering herself to perform it on his behalf. If that is obligatory through a daughter's obedience to him, then it is more fitting that it be obligatory upon him through his ability regarding the money with which he hires someone. As for if money is offered to him without obedience: the correct view is that he is not obliged to accept it and perform the pilgrimage through it on his own behalf, and by offering money to him he does not become able. As for one who has an illness whose cure is hoped for, such as brain fever (al-birsam), severe fever and other such illnesses, it is not permissible for him to have someone perform it on his behalf, because he has not despaired of performing it himself, so it is not performed for him, just like a healthy person; the reverse of this is the disabled person.

Abu Hanifah said: It is permissible for him to perform the pilgrimage on his own behalf; and if someone performs it on his behalf and he recovers, the obligation of the pilgrimage falls from him. And Allah knows best.

{And whoever disbelieves} ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَرَ﴾

Al-Hasan, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata' and al-Dahhak said: it means denying the obligation of the pilgrimage.

Mujahid: whoever performs it, he does not consider it righteousness; and whoever sits back, he does not consider it sinful.

Sufyan narrated from Mansur from him, regarding {And whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day}, which indicates that. Ibn 'Umar narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said, concerning His words {And whoever disbelieves}: "Whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day." [al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/57.]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning the Jews when they said: "The pilgrimage to ... is obligatory." [an illegible word]

Al-Dahhak: When the verse of the pilgrimage was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered the people of all religions and addressed them, saying: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed the pilgrimage upon you, so perform it." A single religious community believed in it, namely the Muslims, while five other communities disbelieved in it and said: "We do not believe in it, nor do we pray towards it, nor do we make the pilgrimage to it." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/29.]

'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: {And whoever disbelieves} refers to the House.

Ibn Zayd: {And whoever disbelieves} refers to these signs which Allah mentioned in His words: {In it are clear signs}.

Al-Suddi said: As for {whoever disbelieves}, it is the one who finds what would allow him to perform the pilgrimage on his behalf, yet does not perform it until he dies; that is his disbelief in it.

Section on the obligation of the pilgrimage

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Pray your five prayers, fast your month, pay the zakat of your wealth, and perform the pilgrimage to the House of your Lord, and you will enter the Paradise of your Lord." [Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah: 4/12, with variation.] [126]

And he (ﷺ) said: "Perform the pilgrimage before you are prevented from performing it, for the House has been demolished twice and will be raised in the third." [Kashf al-Khafa': 1/350.] [127]

Ibn Mas'ud said: Perform the pilgrimage to this House before a tree grows in the desert of which no animal eats without dying. [Kashf al-Khafa': 1/350.]

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sabit narrated from Abu Umamah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is not prevented by an evident need, or a hindering illness, or an unjust ruler, and does not perform the pilgrimage, then let him die, if he wishes, as a Jew, or if he wishes, as a Christian." [Sunan al-Darimi: 2/29.] [128]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 116–129 (part 5 of 6):

It was narrated to us by Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without having performed Hajj, Allah will not accept from him any deed on the Day of Resurrection..." [129].

Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from al-Husayn, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I have considered sending men to the provinces to look into those who possess wealth but have not performed Hajj, and then imposing the jizya (poll tax) upon them."

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while Allah is witness to what you do? Say, "O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses?"﴾ That is, they turn away from the religion of Allah those who believe.

Al-Hasan recited: تَصِدُّونَ (tasiddūna), with a ḍammah on the tā' and a kasrah on the ṣād, and both are dialectal forms: ṣadda and aṣadda, like ṣalla al-laḥm and aṣalla, and khamma and akhamma.

The evidence for the recitation of the majority is His saying: ﴿Did We avert you from the guidance...﴾ [Surah Saba': 32] and His saying: ﴿And they averted you from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 25], and their like.

تَبْغُونَها: you seek it. عِوَجاً: deviation and inclination. The phrase is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the action; its meaning is: "Why do you avert from the way of Allah, seeking for it crookedness?"

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "ʿiwaj" with a kasrah refers to religion, speech and action, while "ʿawaj" with a fatḥah refers to a wall, a barrier and any upright object.

﴿while you are witnesses﴾: In the Torah it is written that the religion of Allah which is not accepted other than it is Islam, and that in it is the description of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture...﴾

Zayd ibn Aslam said: Shas ibn Qays, a Jewish man, who was an old man who had become aged in the pre-Islamic period, great in disbelief, severe in his slander of the Muslims and intense in his envy of them, passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the Aws and the Khazraj in a gathering in which they had come together to converse. He was enraged by what he saw of their unity, their harmony and the goodness of their relations in Islam after the enmity that had existed between them in the pre-Islamic period. He said: "The chiefs of Banu Qaylah have gathered in this land. By Allah, we will have no peace with them when they gather here." So he ordered a young Jewish man who was with him: "Go to them, sit with them, then remind them of the Day of Bu'ath and what was said in it, and recite to them some of the poetry they exchanged concerning it." Bu'ath was a day on which the Aws and the Khazraj fought, and victory in it was for the Aws over the Khazraj. He did so, and the people then spoke, disputed and boasted, until two men from the two clans leapt onto their knees: Aws ibn Qayzi, one of Banu Harithah from the Aws, and Hayyan ibn Sakhr, one of Banu Salamah from the Khazraj. They quarrelled, and one of them said to his companion: "If you wish, I can bring it back now as it was, fresh." Both groups became angry and said: "We have made the weapons our appointment at al-Zahirah, and it is a stony plain (ḥarrah)."
