It is related from Abu Tamim al-Ḥabashani who said: I heard ʿUmar say: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the bird: it goes out hungry in the morning and returns full at evening." [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/30.]] [173]

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb related from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever would like to be the strongest of people, let him rely upon Allah. Whoever would like to be the most honoured of people, let him fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And whoever would like to be the richest of people, let him be more confident in what is in the hand of Allah than in what is in his own hands." [[Musnad al-Shihab: 1/234.]] [174]

ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to recite these two verses:
"Ease your heart, for matters
are by the decree of God,
a self will reach you with what is turned toward it,
and what is decreed for it will not pass you by."
[[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 16/157, no. 44194, with variation.]]

﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you﴾, meaning Allah will aid you against your enemy. ﴿So no one can overcome you﴾ on the day of Badr. ﴿And if He forsakes you﴾, meaning He leaves you and does not help you. Khidhlan (forsaking) is holding back from help, surrendering to destruction and what is hateful. It is said of a cow or a gazelle when it leaves its young and lags behind them: khudhilat, so she is khadhul.

Ṭarafa said:
"A forsaking gazelle that tends the stony grounds in the thicket,
seizing the tips of the berry bushes and grazing."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/254.]]

And someone recited:
"I looked at you with the eye of a young woman
whose companions abandoned her to a child."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/254.]]

Abu ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read ﴿yukhdhilukum﴾ with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the dhāl, meaning: We make you forsaken, and we impose upon you forsaking and abandonment, as you did at Uḥud.

﴿Then who can help you after Him?﴾, meaning after His forsaking. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ ﴿It is not for a prophet to embezzle...﴾ the verse.

ʿIkrima and Muqsim related from Ibn ʿAbbas that this verse was revealed concerning a red cloak that was missing on the day of Badr. Some people said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it."

Juwaybir ibn al-Ḍaḥḥak related from him that when the spoils of Hawazin fell into the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ hand on the day of Ḥunayn, a man embezzled a needle, so Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning the spoils of Uḥud, when the archers left their post and sought the booty, saying: "We fear that the Prophet ﷺ will say: whoever takes anything, it is his, and that the spoils will not be divided as they were not divided on the day of Badr." So they left their post and fell upon the spoils. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Did I not charge you not to leave the post until my command reaches you?" They said: "We left our brothers standing." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, you thought we would embezzle and not divide." [[ʿAwn al-Maʿbud: 11/5.]] [175] Then Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

Some related from al-Ḍaḥḥak from Ibn ʿAbbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out scouts, and they took booty. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it but did not give a share to the scouts. When the scouts returned, they said: "He divided the fay' and did not give us a share." So this verse was revealed.

Qatada said: it was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) when groups of his companions had embezzled.

In some tafsirs it is said: the strong ones pressed him, asking him about the spoils, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿It is not for a prophet to embezzle﴾, meaning he should not give to some people and withhold from others, but rather he must divide equally and not deprive anyone.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: this concerns revelation. The verse says: ﴿It is not for a prophet to embezzle﴾, meaning to conceal anything of the revelation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, out of desire, fear or flattery. That is because they disliked what the Qur'an contained of the faults of their religion and the reviling of their gods, so they asked him to hide that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 156–168 (part 2 of 2):

As for the exegesis: al-Sulami, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and 'Asim read (yaghulla) with a fatha on the ya' and a fatha on the ghayn. This is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas and the choice of Abu 'Ubayda.

The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the ghayn. This is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and the choice of Abu Hatim. Its meaning is that he betrays, and what is meant by it is the community (ummah).

Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the lam in it is shifted (manqulah). The meaning is: "It was not for a Prophet to deceive," and "It was not for Allah, mighty and majestic, to take a son," that is, "It was not for Allah to take a son."

Others said: this is one of the most subtle allusions to them, that [He cleared the honour of] the Prophet ﷺ of deceit, which indicates that deceit is in others. A parallel to this is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, either we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ [Saba': 24]. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Suddi.

Al-Mufaddal said: the meaning is that it was not thought of him, nor was it befitting or suitable for him. Those who adopted this reading relied on the saying of Ibn 'Abbas: "How could it not be for him to deceive, when the Prophet ﷺ was among the prophets who were killed?"

Whoever reads with a damma on the ya' has two meanings:
The first: that it is from ghulul (deceit), meaning: "It was not for the Prophet to deceive," that is, to be betrayed, meaning that his community betrays him.
The other meaning: that it is from al-Ighlal, meaning: "It was not for a prophet to betray, or be attributed to betrayal, or be found a traitor, or be counted among the traitors." So aghalla and ghallala have the same meaning, like His saying: ﴿For they do not deny you﴾ [al-An'am: 33], and His saying: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them a little respite﴾ [al-Tariq: 17].

Al-Mubarrad said: the Arabs say "akfarta al-rajul," meaning: I made the man a disbeliever, attributed disbelief to him, held him to it, found him a disbeliever, and joined him with the disbelievers.

﴿And whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: that thing is shown to him in the Fire, then it is said to him: "Descend and take it." He descends and carries it on his back; when he reaches its place, he falls into the Fire. Then he is commanded to descend to it and bring it out, and he does this repeatedly.

Abu Zur'a related from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day delivering a sermon. He mentioned deceit, magnified it and magnified its matter, and said: "Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck, having a roar, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' I will say: 'I possess nothing for you against Allah; I have already conveyed to you.' Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a sheep on his neck, having a bleat, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' I will say: 'I possess nothing for you against Allah; I have already conveyed to you.' Let me not find any of you coming with gold or silver, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' I will say: 'I possess nothing for you against Allah; I have already conveyed to you.' Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck, having a neigh [al-hamhama: a sound of a horse less than a whinny], saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' I will say: 'I possess nothing for you against Allah; I have already conveyed to you.' Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with cloths on his neck, choking, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' I will say: 'I possess nothing for you against Allah; I have already conveyed to you.'"
[176].

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr who said: There was a man called Kirkira who was in charge of the baggage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He died, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He is in the Fire." They found a cloak he had deceitfully taken.

Al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa from Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man from the Azd called Abu al-Lubayba [in Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/212 (Ibn al-Tabiyya), and in al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/158 (Abu al-Lubtiyya)] to collect the zakat. He came and said: "This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." The Prophet ﷺ stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "What is the matter with the official who is sent, then comes and says: 'This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift'? Why does he not sit in the house of his father or mother and see whether gifts are given to him? By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you will take anything from it except that he will come with it on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck: if it is a camel, it will have a roar; if a cow, it will have a lowing; if a sheep, it will bleat." Then he raised his hands until I saw the whiteness of his armpits, and said: "O Allah, have I not conveyed?"
[177].

From Zayd ibn Khalid: a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ died on the day of Khaybar. They mentioned him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Pray over your companion." The faces of the people changed because of that, and he said: "Your companion has deceived in the way of Allah." So we searched his belongings and found beads of Jewish beads that were not worth two dirhams.

From Abu Hurayra who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Khaybar, and we gained no gold or silver, only clothes and goods. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then headed toward Wadi al-Qura, and a slave called Mid'am had been gifted to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. While Mid'am was unloading the saddle of the Messenger of Allah, an arrow came and killed him. The people said: "Congratulations to him, Paradise!"

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No! By Him in whose hand is my soul, the cloak he took on the day of Khaybar from the spoils, which had not yet been divided, will blaze over him as fire." When the people heard that, a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with one or two thongs, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A thong of fire, or two thongs of fire."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/213] [178].

From 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umayr who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained spoils, he commanded Bilal, who called out among the people, and they brought their spoils, and he gathered and distributed them. Then a man came with a halter of hair and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is from the spoils we had taken." He said: "Did you hear that he called three times?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What prevented you from bringing it?" He made an excuse to him, and he said: "Come with it yourself on the Day of Resurrection, for I will not accept it from you."

From Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Ma'idah who said: I entered the land of the Romans with Maslama, and a man who had deceived was brought, and Salim was asked about him. He said: I heard my father narrate from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "If you find a man has deceived, burn his goods and beat him." He said: We found in his goods a copy of the Qur'an. A man asked Salim about it, and he said: "Sell it and give its price in charity."

From 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) burned the goods of the one who deceived and beat him; and in some narrations, they withheld his share.

From Salih ibn Muhammad who said: We fought with al-Walid ibn Hisham, and with us were Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. A man deceived with some goods, so al-Walid ordered his goods burned, he was paraded around, and his share was not given to him.

﴿Is then one who follows the pleasure of Allah [by abandoning deceit] like one who has returned with wrath from Allah [and deceived], and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination. They are [of] degrees with Allah.﴾ That is, possessors of degrees with Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that those who follow the pleasure of Allah and those who return with wrath from Allah are different in their stations with Allah, the Exalted. For those who follow the pleasure of Allah is honour and great reward, and for those who return with wrath from Allah is humiliation and painful punishment.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favour upon the believers.﴾

Some said: the wording of the verse is general, but its meaning is specific, for there was no tribe of the Arabs but that they had put the necklace of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on [i.e., followed him], and there was no lineage among them except the Banu Taghlib, for Allah purified him from them because of the filth of Christianity in them, since they persisted in it. A clarification of this interpretation is His saying: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2].

Others said: the word "huwa" (He) intends all the believers, and the meaning of His saying "from themselves" is by faith and compassion, not by lineage, as one says: "You are my self (nafsi)." This is indicated by His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128], and so on.

﴿He recites to them His verses and purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom, although they were before that in clear error.﴾ "Before that" refers to before his being sent; and it is in the accusative as an ending point (ghaya).

﴿And when a disaster struck you, although you had struck [the enemy] with twice as much﴾ — at Uhud [i.e., the disaster] — ﴿you said, "From where is this?"﴾ — that is, from where for us is this killing and defeat, while we are Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among us, and revelation descends upon us, while they are polytheists?

Ubayda al-Salmani narrated from 'Ali who said: Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, Allah has disliked what your people did in taking ransom from the captives, and He has commanded you to give them a choice between having their necks struck or taking ransom on condition that an equal number of them be killed." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned that to the people, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are our clans and our brothers. No, we will take their ransom and strengthen ourselves with it against our enemy. Let there be among us a number equal to them; there is nothing in that which we dislike." He said: So seventy men were killed at Uhud, equal to the number of captives at Badr.
[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/222]

So the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾, according to this interpretation, is: by your taking ransom and your choosing killing.

﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿And what struck you on the day the two armies met [at Uhud]﴾ — O assembly of believers — ﴿was by permission of Allah﴾, by His decree, His destiny and His knowledge; ﴿and that He might make evident the believers﴾, that is, that He might distinguish them. It was said: that He might see. It was said: that you might know that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had known what was in them, while you did not know that. ﴿And it was said to them, "Come, fight in the cause of Allah or [at least] defend"﴾, for the sake of Allah's religion and obedience to Him, or defend your families, your city and your sanctuaries.

Al-Suddi, al-Farra' and Abu 'Awn al-Ansari said: that is, increase the numbers of the Muslims and stand guard, even if you do not fight, as that is a repulsion and suppression of the enemy. ﴿They said, "If we had known [there would be] fighting, we would have followed you."﴾ They were 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who turned away from Uhud, and they were three hundred. Allah said: ﴿They were that day nearer to disbelief than to faith﴾, that is, toward disbelief rather than in faith. ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾, for they used to deny faith and conceal disbelief, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made clear their hypocrisy. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.﴾

﴿Those who said of their brothers [in lineage, not religion, and they were one with them] while they sat [back]﴾ — meaning those who sat back from jihad — ﴿"If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed."﴾ Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Then avert from yourselves death, if you should be truthful.﴾ Indeed, caution does not avail against decree.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 169–178 (part 1 of 3):

﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead.﴾ The verse, etc.

Some said: This verse was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr, who numbered fourteen men: eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajirun. Others said: It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud, who numbered seventy men: four from the Muhajirun, Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Uthman ibn Shimas, and Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and the rest were from the Ansar.

Ibn al-Zubayr and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck on the day of Uhud, Allah placed their spirits in the crops of green birds that visit the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, and take shelter in lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they found the goodness of their resting place, their food and their drink, and saw the honour that Allah, exalted is He, had prepared for them, they said: 'Would that our people knew what we are in of bliss and what Allah has done for us, so that they would be eager for jihad and would not shrink from it.' Allah, exalted is He, said: 'I will inform them about you and convey to your brothers.' They rejoiced at this and were glad tidings, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead, but rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for,﴾ up to His saying ﴿the reward of the believers﴾" [179] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/266; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/566, no. 2520.]].

Qatadah and al-Rabi' said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Would that we knew what has become of our brothers who were killed on the day of Uhud," so Allah revealed this verse.

Masruq said: We asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud about this verse, and he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed the spirits of the martyrs of Uhud in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish and take shelter in lamps hanging from the Throne." He said: "Then Allah looked upon them with a look and said: 'Do you desire anything that I may increase for you?' They said: 'Our Lord, do we not roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' Then He looked upon them a second time and said: 'Do you desire anything that I may increase for you?'

They said: 'Our Lord, You have given us nothing except that we would love for You to return us to life, and we would return to the world and fight in Your way, and be killed again for Your sake.' He said: 'No.' They said: 'Then convey our greetings to our Prophet and inform him that we are pleased and that You are pleased with us.' So Allah revealed this verse."

Jabir ibn Abdullah said: My father was killed on the day of Uhud and left behind daughters. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not give you good news, O Jabir?" I said: "Yes, O Prophet of Allah." He said: "When your father was struck at Uhud, Allah brought him back to life and spoke to him directly, saying: 'O servant of Allah, ask me whatever you wish.' He said: 'I ask You to return me to the world so that I may be killed for You a second time.' He said: 'O servant of Allah, I have decreed that I will not return any creature to the world.' He said: 'O Lord, then who will convey to my people what I am in of honour?' Allah, exalted is He, said: 'I will,' and so Allah revealed this verse." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/268.]] [180].

Humayd narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No soul dies having with Allah something good that would make it happy to return to the world and have the world and all in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom; so he wishes to return to the world and be killed once more." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/126.]] [181].

Others said: It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bir Ma'unah, and the cause of that, as narrated by Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar from his father, from al-Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Humayd al-Tawil from Anas ibn Malik, and others of the people of knowledge, is that they said: Abu Bara' Amir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, "Lance-Player" (mula'ib al-asinnah), who was the chief of Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and presented him with a gift. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept it and said: "O Abu Bara', I do not accept a gift from a polytheist; so embrace Islam if you wish me to accept your gift." [182] Then he presented Islam to him, informed him of what he would have in it and what Allah had promised the believers of reward, and recited the Qur'an to him. He did not embrace Islam, nor did he go far away, and said: "O Muhammad, this matter to which you call is good and beautiful. If you were to send some men from your companions to the people of Najd to call them to your matter, I hope they would respond to you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I fear for them from the people of Najd." Abu Bara' said: "I am a protector for them" (i.e., they are under my protection), "so send them to call the people to your matter." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn Amr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men of the best Muslims, among them al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, Haram ibn Milhan, Urwah ibn Asma' ibn al-Salt al-Sulami, Nafi' ibn Waraqa' al-Khuza'i, and Amir ibn Fuhayrah, mawla of Abu Bakr. This was in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijrah, four months after Uhud. They set out until they alighted between Ma'unah, which is a land between the land of Banu Amir and the lava field of Banu Sulaym. When they alighted there, some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?" Haram ibn Milhan said: "I will." He went out with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Amir ibn al-Tufayl, who was in charge of that water. When Haram ibn Milhan came to them, Amir ibn al-Tufayl did not look at the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Haram said: "O people of Bir Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you, and I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger.﴾"

A man from the back of the tent came out to him with a spear and struck him in his side until it came out the other side. He said: "Allah is greater! I have won, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then Amir ibn al-Tufayl called upon Banu Amir against the Muslims, but they refused to answer him in what he called them to, and said: "We will not betray Abu Bara', for he made a covenant and protection for them." So he called upon tribes of Banu Sulaym: Usayyah, Ra'l and Dhakwan, and they answered him. They set out until they surrounded the people and encircled them among their men. When the Muslims saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they were all killed, except Ka'b ibn Zayd, for they left him with a little life in him. He was carried from among the dead and lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench. [[In full in Uyun al-Athar: 2/17.]]

Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damari and a man from the Ansar, of Banu Amr ibn Awf, were herding the camels of the people, and nothing alerted them to the battle lines of their companions except a bird circling over the camp. They said: "By Allah, this bird has some significance," so they approached to look at it, and behold, the people lay in their blood and the horsemen who had struck them were standing. The Ansari said to Amr ibn Umayyah: "What do you think?" He said: "I think we should go back to the Messenger of Allah and inform him of the news." The Ansari said: "But I will not turn my soul away from a place where al-Mundhir ibn Amr was killed," and he fought the people until he was killed. They took Amr ibn Umayyah captive, and when he told them that he was from Mudar, Amir ibn al-Tufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him from a slave, claiming that it was owed upon his mother. Amr ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the news. The Messenger of Allah said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. I was averse to this and fearful of it." [183] This reached Abu Bara', and it grieved him that Amir had breached his protection and what befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of it. Among those killed was Amir ibn Fuhayrah.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Hisham ibn Urwah that Amir ibn al-Tufayl used to say: "Whoever among them was killed, I saw him raised between the sky and the earth until I saw the sky beneath him." They said: "He was Amir ibn Fuhayrah." [[In full in Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/221.]]

They said: Hassan ibn Thabit said, inciting Abu Bara' against Amir ibn al-Tufayl:

A youth of the mother of sons, did it not alarm you,
while you are of the noblest of the people of Najd?
Amir struck you through Abu Bara', to breach his protection,
and a mistake is not like a deliberate act.
Bear this message to Rabi'ah, the one of great deeds:
what has happened in the calamities since I left.
Your father is the father of wars, Abu Bara',
and your maternal uncle is the noble, Hakam ibn Sa'd. [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/221.]]

Ka'b ibn Malik also said about that:

Every face has been scattered in dismay
over the protection that Abu Bara' did not grant.
O sons of the mother of sons, did you not hear
the call of one seeking help along with the women,
and the shout of the one crying for help? Yes, but
you knew that he was true to the encounter.
[[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/221.]]

When Rabi'ah ibn al-Bara' heard the verse of Hassan and the verse of Ka'b ibn Malik, he charged at Amir ibn al-Tufayl and struck him, so that he fell from his horse. He said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. If I die, my blood is for my uncle, and I will pursue it; and if I live, I will consider the matter." Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that Allah revealed concerning the martyrs of Bir Ma'unah a Qur'an: "Convey on our behalf to our people that we have met our Lord; He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him." Then it was abrogated and removed after we had recited it for a time, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead.﴾ The verse, etc.

Some said: The guardians of the martyrs, whenever a blessing or joy befell them, would grieve over the martyrs and say: "We are in blessing and joy while our fathers, sons and brothers are in graves." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this as a comfort to them and as information about the state of their slain: ﴿And do not think﴾, i.e., do not suppose, do not assume. Hisham narrated from the people of Syria: (yahsabanna) with ya'. Al-Hasan and Ibn Amir read: (qutthilu) with doubled ta', and (amwatan) like the death of one who was not killed in the way of Allah. And amwatan is put in the accusative as the second object, because "hasiba" takes two objects; when you say "I considered Zayd," it is not a complete statement until you say "standing" or "sitting." ﴿But they are alive﴾, its meaning: rather they are alive.

Ibn Abi Abla read: ahyā'an in the accusative, meaning: I consider them alive. ﴿with their Lord﴾.

Some said: It means alive in this world in reality [[This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Amr ibn Ubayd, Wasil ibn Ata', al-Jubba'i and al-Rummani; see Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 1/437.]]. It was also said: [in the world]. And it was said: with praise and remembrance, as it was said:

The death of the pious is a life that has no end;
peoples have died while among men they are alive. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/269.]]

It was said: they are alive in that ﴿with their Lord, being provided for﴾, eating and enjoying bliss like the living. It was also said: a reward for a raid is written for them each year, and they share in the merit of every mujahid who exists in this world until the Day of Resurrection, because they initiated the matter of jihad, so the reward of whoever follows their example returns to them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul...﴾ [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 32.]] up to the end of the verse. It was also said: their spirits bow and prostrate every night beneath the Throne until the Day of Resurrection, like the spirits of living believers who spend the night in ablution. And it was said: because the martyr does not decay in the grave and the earth does not consume him.

It is said: four whose bodies do not decay: the Prophets, the scholars, the martyrs and the bearers of the Qur'an.

It was narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah that it reached him that Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, the two Ansar, then of Banu Salamah, had their grave damaged by a flood; they were in one grave, and they were among the martyrs of Uhud, and their grave was on the side of the flood. They dug up their remains to move them from their place, and they found them unchanged, as if they had died only yesterday. One of them had been wounded, and he had placed his hand on his wound when he was buried, and he was buried in that state; his hand was removed from his wound and then released, and it returned as it had been. The time between the day of Uhud and the day they were dug up was forty-six years. It was also said: they were called "alive" because they are not washed, just as the living are not washed.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wrap them in their wounds and their blood; the color is the color of blood and the scent is the scent of musk." [[al-Siyar al-Kabir: 1/232, no. 294.]] [184].

Ubayd ibn Umar said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned back from Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who was slain, and stopped over him and supplicated, then recited: ﴿Among the believers are men who were true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾ [[Surah al-Ahzab: 23.]] up to the end of the verse. Then he (ﷺ) said: "The Messenger of Allah bears witness that these are martyrs before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. So come to them, visit them and greet them, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection without their returning the greeting. ﴿They are provided for﴾ with fruits of Paradise and its gifts." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 10/381, no. 29892.]] [185].

﴿Rejoicing﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) and a detached qualifier (qat') of ﴿they are provided for﴾.

Ibn al-Sumayt'a read: (fariḥīn) with an alif, and both are dialects, like al-fariḥ and al-fārih, al-ḥadhir and al-ḥādhir, al-ṭama' and al-ṭāmi', al-bukhl and al-bākhil.

﴿in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾: of His reward. ﴿And they rejoice﴾: they are glad; its root is from bashrah (skin of the face), because when a person is happy, the trace of joy appears on the skin of his face. ﴿concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾: from their brothers who left them while they were alive in the world, upon their path of faith and jihad, knowing that if they were martyred they would join them and become among the honoured of Allah, exalted is He, in the same state as they had attained; therefore they rejoice.

Al-Suddi said: The martyr is brought a book in which are the names of those of his brothers and family who preceded him, and it is said: "So-and-so preceded you on such a day, and so-and-so on such a day." He rejoices when he comes to them, just as the family of an absent person rejoices at his arrival in the world.

﴿That there is no fear upon them﴾: meaning, that there is no fear upon them ﴿nor shall they grieve.﴾ ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and bounty, and that Allah...﴾: meaning, and that Allah is in the position of the genitive, on the basis of ﴿a blessing from Allah and bounty﴾.

Al-Kisa'i, al-Farra', al-Mufaddal and Muhammad ibn Isa read: (wa-inna Allah) with a kasrah on the alif, as an resumption (istinaf), and their evidence is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and Allah does not waste the reward of the believers."

Al-Kalbi said, with his chain: If the servant meets the enemy in the way of Allah, a gate is opened for him from the sky, and his two wives of the Hur al-Ayn look down upon him. When he advances against the enemy to fight them, they say: "O Allah, grant him success and guidance." When he turns back from the enemy, they say: "O Allah, pardon him and overlook." When he is killed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, boasts of him to the angels, saying to them: "Look at My servant who gave his soul and blood seeking My pleasure." The angels say: "Our Lord, will You not go and help him against those who want to kill him?" He says to them: "Leave My servant alone, for he has stayed awake and toiled in seeking My pleasure; he loved meeting Me, and I loved meeting him." Then his two wives of the Hur al-Ayn descend to him, and Allah commands the angels to come to him from the horizons of the earth, and they embrace him and give him glad tidings of Paradise and honour from Allah, exalted is He. When they have done that, Allah sends to them: "Leave My servant and his wife alone until he rests." His two wives say: "We have been longing for you," and He says to them the same.

From al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said: While Ali ibn Abi Talib was giving a sermon to the people, urging them to jihad, a young man stood up to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the virtue of those who go out to fight in the way of Allah."

He said: "I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his she-camel al-'Adba' as we were returning from a campaign, and I asked him what you have asked me, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When the warriors resolve to go out to fight, Allah, exalted is He, writes for them a quittance from the Fire. When they prepare for their campaign, Allah, exalted is He, boasts of them to the angels. When their families bid them farewell, the walls and houses weep over them, and they come out of their sins as a snake comes out of its skin. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigns to each man of them forty thousand angels who guard him from before him, behind him, on his right and on his left; no good deed he does is left unmultiplied for him, and there is written for him each day the worship of a thousand men who worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for a thousand years, each year three hundred and sixty days, a day equal to the lifespan of the world. When they stand in the presence of their enemy, the knowledge of the people of the world ceases regarding the reward Allah gives them. When they come out against their enemy and the spears are lowered, the arrows are notched, and a man advances against a man, the angels surround them with their wings and pray to Allah for them for victory and steadfastness. A caller calls: "Paradise is under the shadows of the swords!" The blow and the thrust upon the martyr are easier than drinking cold water on a hot day. When the martyr falls from his horse by a thrust or a blow, he does not reach the ground until Allah sends to him his wife from the Hur al-Ayn, who gives him good news of what Allah has prepared for him of honour. When he reaches the ground, the earth says to him: "Welcome, good spirit that came out of a good body. Rejoice, for you have what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 169–178 (part 2 of 3):

God, exalted is He, says: "I am his successor in his family. Whoever pleases them has pleased Me, and whoever angers them has angered Me. God places his spirit in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, eating of its fruits, and they take refuge in lamps of gold suspended beneath the Throne. And to one of them will be given seventy chambers of the Garden of Paradise, the path of each chamber lying between Sana'a and Syria, its light filling what lies between the two horizons. In each chamber there are seventy doors, and on each door seventy leaves of gold, and over each door seventy curtained chambers, and in each chamber seventy tents, and in each tent seventy couches of gold, their legs of pearls and chrysolite, covered with emerald rods, and on each couch forty mattresses, the thickness of each mattress forty cubits, and on each mattress a wife of the large-eyed houris, 'amorous and equal in age'" [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 37.]].

The young man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the 'amorous' (al-'uruba)?" He said: "She is the coquettish, pleasing, desirable one. She has a thousand servant-boys and seventy thousand servant-girls, golden of ornaments and white of faces, upon them crowns of pearls, upon their necks napkins, in their hands cups and ewers. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will come forth from his grave brandishing his sword, his veins gushing with blood, the color the color of blood and the scent the scent of musk, walking in the open ground of the Resurrection.

By He in whose hand is my soul, if the prophets were upon their path, they would dismount for them, because of the radiance they see from them, until they come to tables of jewels and sit upon them. And a man among them will intercede for seventy thousand of his household and neighbors, so that two neighbors dispute which of them is nearer in neighborliness, and they sit with me and with Abraham at the table of eternity, and they gaze upon God every morning and evening" [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/ 444.]].

Makhul narrated from Kathir ibn Murra from Qays al-Judhami, a man who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The martyr is given six qualities at the first drop of his blood: every sin of his is expiated, he sees his seat in Paradise, he is married to the large-eyed houris, he is secured from the Greatest Terror and the punishment of the grave, and he is adorned with the adornment of faith" [[al-Musannaf- al-Kufi-: 4/ 585.]]
[186].

Thabit ibn Aslam al-Bunani narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was on one of his campaigns when a black man came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, I am black, ugly of face, foul of smell, and I have no wealth. If I fight these people until I am killed, where will I be?" He said: "In Paradise." So he charged against them and fought until he was killed. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) came and stood over his head and said: "God has whitened your face, perfumed your scent, and multiplied your wealth." Then he said:
"I have seen his two wives of the large-eyed houris in Paradise vying with one another over a woollen cloak of his, each wanting to enter between him and his cloak" [[al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya- Ibn Kathir-: 4/ 218. With variation.]] [187].

Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The martyr does not feel from being killed in the way of God more than what one of you feels from the pinch of an ant" [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/ 297.]] [188].

And in another hadith: "The bite of an ant is harder on the martyr than the touch of a weapon" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/ 405.]] [189].

And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed God has servants whom He protects from killing, earthquakes and diseases; He lengthens their lives in good works, makes their provision good, gives them life in well-being, and takes their souls in well-being upon their beds, and grants them the dwellings of the martyrs" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/ 426. With variation.]] [190].

"Those who answered God and the Messenger..." the verse. The occasion was that Abu Sufyan and his companions, when they turned away from the Muslims at Uhud and reached al-Rawha, regretted their departure and blamed one another, and said: "You did not kill Muhammad, nor did you take the captive women. You killed them until none remained but the fugitives. Go back and finish them off." This news reached the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he wished to make the enemy depart and to show them his own strength and that of his companions. So he called his companions to set out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan, saying: "Is there not a band that will exert itself for the command of God, pursuing its enemy? For it is more wounding to the enemy and more far-reaching in hearing." A band answered him, despite the wounds and sores that had afflicted them on the day of Uhud. The Messenger of God's crier called out: "None shall go forth in it except those who were present at our battle yesterday." Jabir ibn Abd Allah spoke to him, saying: "O Messenger of God, my father left me in charge of seven younger sisters, and said to me: 'My son, it is not fitting for me or for you to leave these women without a man among them. I would not prefer you over myself in jihad with the Messenger of God ﷺ, so remain behind for your sisters.' So I remained behind for them." The Messenger of God ﷺ gave him permission, and he went out with him. The Messenger of God ﷺ went out only to terrify the enemy, so that it would reach them that he had set out in pursuit of them, and they would think him strong, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them against their enemy so that they would turn back. So the Messenger of God ﷺ went out, and with him Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Abd Allah ibn al-Yaman, and Abu 'Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, with seventy men, until they reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is three miles from Medina.

And from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from A'isha, that she said to Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: "O son of my sister, by God, your father and your grandfather, meaning Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, are among those of whom God said: 'Those who answered God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them.'"

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Abd Allah ibn Kharija ibn Zayd ibn Thabit, from Abu al-Sa'ib: that a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from the Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, who had witnessed Uhud, said: "I and a brother of mine witnessed Uhud, and we returned wounded. When the Messenger of God's caller announced the departure in pursuit of the enemy, we said: 'Let not the expedition with the Messenger of God ﷺ escape us.' By God, we had no mount to ride, and none of us was other than severely wounded. So we went out with the Messenger of God ﷺ. I was less wounded than my brother, and whenever he tired I carried him for a stretch and walked a stretch, until we reached with the Messenger of God ﷺ Hamra' al-Asad. The Messenger of God ﷺ passed by Ma'bad al-Khuza'i at Hamra' al-Asad. Khuza'a, both its Muslims and its unbelievers, were the confidants of the Messenger of God ﷺ in Tihama; their alliance was with him, and they concealed nothing from him that occurred there. Ma'bad was at that time a polytheist. He said: 'O Muhammad, by God, what has befallen you among your companions has grieved us, and we wished that God had spared you from them.' Then he left the Messenger of God ﷺ and met Abu Sufyan and those with him at al-Rawha, who had resolved to return to the Messenger of God ﷺ, saying: 'We have struck most of his companions, their leaders and their nobles. Then we turned back before we had finished them off; we will attack their remnant and finish them.' When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad he said: 'What is behind you, O Ma'bad?'

He said: 'Muhammad has set out with his companions in pursuit of you, with a host the like of which I have never seen. They burn with fury against you, and those who had stayed behind from him have gathered with him, and they regret their conduct. Among them is a rage against you the like of which I have never seen.' He said: 'Woe to you, what are you saying?' He said: 'By God, I do not think you will move until you see the forelocks of the horses.' He said: 'By God, we had resolved to return against them to finish off their remnant.' He said: 'But I, by God, forbid you from that, for what I have seen has moved me to say verses about it.'

He said: 'And what did you say?' He said: 'I said:

My mount nearly broke from the clamor
when the earth flowed with the swift, massed horses.
They were driven by noble lions, not men who flee
at the encounter, nor cowardly fools.
So you wheeled, thinking the earth was tilting
when they heard of a leader not forsaken.
So I said: "Woe to the son of Harb for your meeting
when the valley of Batha roars with the host.
I am a warner to the people of the open country,
and to every man of sense and reason among them,
of the army of Ahmad, whose squadrons are no wild beasts,
and what I have witnessed cannot be described by hearsay."'

He said: So that turned Abu Sufyan and those with him back. A caravan of 'Abd al-Qays passed by him, and he said: 'Where are you headed?' They said: 'We are headed for Medina, to seek provisions.' He said: 'Will you convey to Muhammad a message from me, which I entrust to you, and I will load your camels here with raisins at the market of 'Ukaz if you reach us?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'When you come to him, tell him that we have resolved to march against him and his companions to finish off their remnant.' Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca, and the caravan passed by the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was at Hamra' al-Asad, and they informed him of what Abu Sufyan had said.

The Messenger of God and his companions said: "Hasbuna Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil" (God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs). Then the Messenger of God ﷺ returned to Medina after the third day, having gained favour in the face of Mu'awiya ibn al-Mughira ibn al-'As and Abu Ghurra al-Jumahi.

This is the statement of most of the exegetes.

Mujahid and 'Ikrima said: These verses were revealed concerning the Lesser Battle of Badr. That was because Abu Sufyan said on the day of Uhud, when he wished to turn away: "O Muhammad, our appointment between us and you is the season of the Lesser Badr next year, if you wish." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "That is between us and you, God willing." [[191]] When the following year came, Abu Sufyan went out with the people of Mecca until he halted at Majanna, on the side of al-Zahran. Then God, mighty and majestic, cast terror into his heart before he returned, and he met Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i, who had come as a pilgrim of 'umra. Abu Sufyan said to him: "O Nu'aym, I made an appointment with Muhammad and his companions to meet at the season of the Lesser Badr. This is a year of drought, and only a year in which we graze upon the trees and drink milk will suffice us. It has appeared to me that I should not go out to it, and I dislike that Muhammad should go out and I not go out, which would increase them in boldness. I prefer that the failure come from their side rather than from mine. So go to Medina, discourage them, and inform them that we are in a great host and they have no strength against us. For you I have ten camels, which I will place in your charge through the hand of Suhayl ibn 'Amr, who will guarantee them."

He said: Suhayl came, and Nu'aym said to him: "O Abu Yazid, will you guarantee for me these camels?" He said: "Yes." So Nu'aym set out until he came to Medina, and found the people preparing for the appointment of Abu Sufyan. He said:

"Where are you headed?" They said: "Abu Sufyan has promised us that we would fight at the season of the Lesser Badr."

He said: "What an evil opinion you have held! They came to you in your homes and your dwellings, and none escaped from you except the fugitive, and you wish to go out when they have gathered for you at the season? By God, not one of you will escape." The companions of the Messenger of God disliked going out. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, I will go out even if I am alone" [[192]]. As for the coward, he turned back, but the brave man prepared for battle, and they said: "Hasbuna Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil." So the Messenger of God ﷺ went out with his companions until they reached the Lesser Badr. They kept meeting the polytheists and asking them about Quraysh, and they would say: "They have gathered against you," wishing to terrify the Muslims. The believers would say: "Hasbuna Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil," until they reached Badr. It is a water belonging to the Banu Kinana, and it was the site of a market for them in the pre-Islamic period, to which they gathered every year for eight days. The Messenger of God ﷺ remained at Badr waiting for Abu Sufyan, but Abu Sufyan had turned back from Majanna to Mecca. The people of Mecca called them "the army of the sawiq (barley-gruel)," and said: "You went out only to drink sawiq." The Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions met no polytheist at Badr; they reached the market, which had goods and trade with them, and they sold them and gained a dirham or two, and returned to Medina safe and profiting. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/ 235–236, and Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/ 212.]] This is the meaning of God's words: "Those who answered God and the Messenger."

The position of "alladhina" is in the genitive as an attribute of the believers; its implied sense is: "And that God does not waste the reward of the believers who answer God and the Messenger." The meaning of "istijaba" is answering and obeying, and its parallel is His words: "So let them answer Me" [i.e., let them obey Me]. "After the wound had afflicted them": that is, the wounds and injuries had reached them. Here the statement is complete, then it begins: "For those of them who did good" by obeying the Messenger and answering his call to campaign, "and feared God" by avoiding disobedience to Him and to Him: "a great reward" — abundant reward. "Those to whom the people said..." The position of "alladhina" is also in the genitive, referring back to the first "alladhina." By "the people" is meant Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud according to the view of Mujahid, Muqatil, 'Ikrima and al-Waqidi, and on this interpretation it is of the general term used to mean the particular, as in His words: "Or do they envy the people?" [[Surat al-Nisa': 54.]], meaning Muhammad alone, and His words: "The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind" [[Surat Ghafir: 57.]], meaning men alone.

Ibn Ishaq and a group said: By "the people" is meant the caravan of 'Abd al-Qays, whose story has already passed.

al-Suddi said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions prepared to march to the appointment of Abu Sufyan, the hypocrites came to them and said: "We are your companions who forbade you to go out against them, but you disobeyed us. They have come to you in your homes, fought you and gained the upper hand. If you go to them in their lands, not one of you will return." They said: "Hasbuna Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil."

It is said: "The people" in this verse are the hypocrites.

Abu Ma'shar said: Some men of Hudhayl from the people of Tihama entered Medina, and the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ asked them about Abu Sufyan. They said: "They have gathered great hosts against you, so avoid them." They said: "Hasbuna Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil." Then God, exalted is He, revealed: "Those to whom the people said" — meaning those men of Hudhayl — "Indeed the people" — meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions — "have gathered against you, so fear them," that is, be afraid of them and beware of them, for you have no strength against them. "But it increased them in faith" — meaning in assurance, certainty, strength and boldness.

Mention of some of what has been related in the reports concerning the increase and decrease of faith

Malik narrated from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar, who said: We said: "O Messenger of God, does faith increase and decrease?" He said: "Yes, it increases until its possessor enters Paradise, and decreases until its possessor enters the Fire" [[Bihar al-Anwar: 66/ 209.]] [193].

'Ata': "Indeed your dispute with one of you over the truth is, in this world, more severe than the dispute of the believers with their Lord concerning their brothers who were admitted into the Fire." He said: They will say: "Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us and perform pilgrimage with us, yet You admitted them into the Fire." He said: He will say: "Go and bring out whom you recognize of them." So they will come to them and recognize them by their forms; some of them will have been seized by the Fire up to the middle of their shins, and some up to their ankles. They will bring them out and say: "Our Lord, we have brought out those You commanded us to." Then He will say to them: "Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, and then whoever has in his heart the weight of half a dinar," until He says: "Then whoever has in his heart an atom's weight..." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/ 94.]]

And from Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "While I was asleep, I saw people being shown to me, and they wore shirts, some of which reached the breast and some of which were shorter than that. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was shown to me wearing a shirt which he was dragging." They said: "How did you interpret it, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The religion." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/ 374; Sahih al-Bukhari: 8/ 75.]] [194].

And from Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, from 'Umar (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If the faith of Abu Bakr were weighed against the faith of the people of the earth, or against the faith of this community, it would outweigh them." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/ 493, with slight abridgement.]] [195].

And from Ibn Sabit, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha used to take the hand of a group of his companions and say: "Come, let us believe for a while. Come, let us increase our faith. Come, let us remember God, exalted is He. [Come, let us remember Him by obeying Him, that perhaps He will remember us with His forgiveness]" [[al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 7/ 227; what is between the brackets is from it.]].

And from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Hind, who said: Ali, may God honour his face, said: "Indeed faith begins as a white point in the heart; whenever faith increases, it grows whiter, until the whole heart becomes white. And indeed hypocrisy begins as a black point in the heart; whenever hypocrisy increases, it grows blacker, until the whole heart becomes black. By He in whose hand is my soul, if you were to split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white-hearted, and if you split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black-hearted."

And from 'Umayr ibn Habib ibn Khamasha, who said: "Faith increases and decreases." It was said to him: "And what is its increase and its decrease?" He said: "When we remember our Lord and fear Him, that is its increase; and when we are heedless, forget and become constricted, that is its decrease."

And from Muhammad ibn Talha, from Zubayd, from Zirr, who said: 'Umar used to take hold of a man or two of his companions and say: "Come, let us go and increase our faith."

And from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from his father, from Simak, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, that he used to say to his companions: "Come, let us walk and increase our faith."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 169–178 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Harith ibn 'Umayr reported from Abu al-Darda', who said: Faith (al-iman) increases and decreases.

And 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid reported from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayra, who both said: Faith increases and decreases.

Al-Harith ibn al-Husayn reported from Abu al-Darda', who said: Faith increases and decreases.

Abu Hudhayfa: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: Faith increases and decreases.

Sufyan reported from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, who said: Never does a servant's trustworthiness diminish except that his faith diminishes with it.

And 'Uthman ibn Sa'd al-Darimi said: I asked Muhammad ibn Kathir al-'Abdi about faith, and he said: It is speech and action; it increases and decreases. I said: Did Sufyan say this? He said: Yes, without doubt.

And he said: I asked Abu Hudhayfa Musa ibn Mas'ud about faith, and he said: It is speech and action; it increases and decreases. I said: Did Sufyan say this? He said: Yes.

He said: I asked 'Arim ibn al-Fadl about faith, and he said: It is speech and action; it increases and decreases. I said: Did Hammad ibn Yazid say this? He said: Yes.

He said: I asked Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi about faith, and he said: It is speech, action and intention. I said: Does it increase and decrease? He said: Yes.

He said: I asked Sulayman ibn Harb about faith, and he said: Like that.

He said: I heard Muslim ibn Ibrahim say: Faith is speech and action; it increases and decreases.

He said: I asked 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Madini about faith, and he said: It is speech, action and intention. I said: Does it decrease and increase? He said: Yes, it increases and decreases until nothing of it remains.

He said: I asked 'Amr ibn 'Awn al-Wasiti about faith, and he said: Like that.

He said: I heard Yahya ibn Yahya say: Faith is speech and action, and people differ in their degrees of faith.

He said: I asked Ahmad ibn Yunus about faith. He said: It is action; it increases and decreases.

He said: I asked 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad [al-Tufayl], who was pious, about faith, and he said: It is speech and action; it increases and decreases. So convey this from me.

He said: I asked Abu Bawiyh al-Jili about faith, and he said: Speech and action; it increases and decreases.

He said: I heard Mahbub ibn Musa al-Antaki say: Faith is speech and action; it increases and decreases. Whoever dislikes the exception (al-istithna', saying "if God wills") has erred from the Sunna (the prophetic way). I said: Did Abu Ishaq al-Farari say this? He said: Abu Ishaq would expel from al-Massisa [[al-Massisa: a town in Syria, pronounced without doubling the letter.]] anyone who did not say that faith increases and decreases.

He said: I heard Mahbub ibn Musa say: I heard Yusuf ibn Asbat say: Faith increases and decreases.

He said: I heard al-Husayn ibn 'Umar al-Sijistani say: Faith is speech and action; it increases and decreases.

Al-Hasan said: Wakf ibn al-Jarrah, 'Umar ibn 'Amara, Ibn Abi Barza and Zuhayr ibn Nu'aym used to say: Faith is speech and action; it increases and decreases.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾. That is: He is our sufficiency and our trust. The nun and the alif of (hasbuna) are in the genitive case by virtue of the construction, as when you say: "Hasb Zayd dirham" (the sufficiency of Zayd is a dirham), because hasb is a noun, although it has the sense of a verb; do you not see the dammah on the second letter?

The poet said:
"So you fill our house with curds and butter,
and your sufficiency of wealth is a full belly and a drink."
[[al-Sihah: 5/2138; Taj al-'Arus: 5/392.]]

And (ni'ma al-wakil): the one to whom affairs are entrusted; (fa'il) here has the sense of (maf'ul).

Al-Waqidi said: (ni'ma al-wakil) means "the preventer." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Then if We willed, We would surely take away what We have revealed to you; then you would find for yourself no advocate against Us in that matter﴾ [[Surat al-Isra': 86.]], that is, no preventer; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants, over them you have no authority; and your Lord is sufficient as a Disposer﴾ [[Surat al-Isra': 65.]].

From Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The last thing that Abraham (peace be upon him) said when he was thrown into the fire was: ﴿God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾." [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/154; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/6.]] [196]

And from 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) judged between two men, and the one against whom judgment was passed said: ﴿God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God praises the shrewd and blames the helpless. When a matter overcomes you, say: ﴿God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 18/54; Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/86.]] [197]

﴿So they returned﴾: they went back and came back. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿So that they may recognize it when they return to their families﴾ [[Surat Yusuf: 62.]], that is, they returned.

﴿With a blessing from God﴾: with well-being, as they met no enemy and their wounds healed. ﴿And grace﴾: with profit and trade, which is what they gained from the market, so they profited. ﴿No harm touched them﴾: neither killing nor wounding touched them, nor did any evil, hurt or harm reach them. ﴿And they followed the pleasure of God﴾: in obedience to God and His Messenger. This is because they said: "Would this count as a raid?" So God gave them the reward of a raid and was pleased with them. ﴿And God is possessor of great grace﴾.

﴿It is only Satan who frightens you﴾: that is, the one who said to you: ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them﴾, is an act of Satan, who placed (the fear) in their mouths, so they frighten them and make them cowardly toward them. ﴿He frightens his allies﴾: that is, he frightens you with his allies, meaning the allies of Iblis, so that he frightens the believers with the disbelievers.

Al-Suddi said: He magnifies his allies in your hearts so that you fear them. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿To warn of a severe punishment﴾ [[Surat al-Kahf: 2.]], that is, with a punishment; and His saying: ﴿To warn of the Day of Meeting﴾ [[Surat Ghafir: 15.]], and ﴿That you may warn of the Day of Gathering﴾ [[Surat al-Shura: 7.]], that is, with the Day of Gathering he frightens people, his allies. It is like the saying of the speaker: "He gives dirhams and clothes garments," meaning he gives people dirhams and clothes people in garments. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: (yukhawwif al-nas awliya'ahu) (he frightens people with his allies).

Yahya ibn al-Yaman narrated from Talha, from 'Ata', that he used to recite: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾.

Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi Wadah narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn Khuzayma told us: In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "He frightens you with his allies."

﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ in abandoning My command, ﴿if you are believers﴾, affirming My promise; for I guarantee you victory and triumph. ﴿And let them not grieve you﴾.

Nafi' recited (yahzunuka) with a dammah on the yaʼ and a kasrah on the zay, and likewise every occurrence of this verb in the Qur'an, except the one in al-Anbiya': ﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾ [[Surat al-Anbiya': 103.]], where he read it with a fatha on the yaʼ and a dammah on the zay. Abu Ja'far was of the opposite view. Ibn Muhaysin recited all of them with a dammah on the yaʼ and a kasrah on the zay. The rest read all of them with a fatha and a dammah on the zay. Both are the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, and both are dialects: hazana yahzunu and ahzana yahzunu, but the elevated, eloquent usage is hazana yahzunu and ahznatuhu (he grieved and I grieved him). The poet said:
"My companions have passed, and the abodes have grieved me."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/285.]]

﴿Those who race to disbelief﴾.

The common readers recite it this way. Talha ibn Musarrif recited: (yusri'un) (they hasten).

Al-Dahhak said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh. Others said: They are the hypocrites who race to disbelief by supporting the disbelievers.

﴿Indeed, they will not harm God at all﴾ by their hastening into disbelief and their support of its people. ﴿God intends not to give them a share in the Hereafter﴾: a portion in the reward of the Hereafter. For this reason He forsook them until they hastened into disbelief. ﴿And for them is a great punishment.﴾ In this verse is a refutation of the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination).

﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith﴾: they replaced faith with disbelief. ﴿Will not harm God at all﴾, for they only harm themselves. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think﴾.

The reading of Hamza and Abu Bahtariyya: with the ta' (tahsabanna, "let them not think" addressed to the Prophet).

The rest read it with the ya' (yahsabanna, "let them not think"). Whoever reads with the ya', then (alladhina) is in the nominative case as the subject; its implied meaning is: "And let not the disbelievers think that Our granting them respite is good for them."

Whoever reads with the ta', al-Farra' said: it is repeated in meaning: "Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve... and do not think that We only grant them respite," because when you make the verb of thinking govern (alladhina), (innama) cannot follow it. It is like His saying: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?﴾ [[Surat Muhammad: 18.]], meaning: do they await anything but that it come upon them suddenly. It was also said: the position of (innama) is in the accusative as a substitute for (alladhina).

As the poet said:
"The death of Qays was not the death of one man,
but the building of a people that collapsed."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/44; al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 8/35.]]

Here (halak) is in the nominative as a substitute for the first (the one before it).

Al-Imla' is delay, postponement, lengthening of life and extending the term. Among its uses is His saying: ﴿And leave me alone for a long time﴾ [[Surat Maryam: 46.]], that is, for a long period. It is said: "I lived a long time," meaning I was given respite for a time. Its origin is from al-mulawa and al-mala', which mean the age (al-dahr).

The poet said:
"And I have seen myself a hunter of the beautiful, given long respite, as if above me is a sky."
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 3/125.]]

And al-malawan are the night and the day.

Tamim ibn Muqbil said:
"O abodes of the tribe at al-Sab'an, may the wearing away pass over them."
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 8/150.]]

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, We grant them respite only that they may increase in sin; and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ This verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh.

Muqatil said: 'Ata' said: concerning Qurayza and al-Nadir.

From 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, that a man said: "O Messenger of God, who among people is best?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are good." He said: "Then who among people is worst?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are evil." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/40.]] [198]

Ibn Mas'ud said: No soul, righteous or wicked, but death is for it. As for the wicked, they find rest and others find rest from them. He recited: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is good for them...﴾ the verse. As for the righteous, he recited: ﴿A provision from the presence of God; and what is with God is better for the righteous﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 169–178 (part 1 of 3):

﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead.﴾ The verse, etc.

Some said: This verse was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr, who numbered fourteen men: eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajirun. Others said: It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud, who numbered seventy men: four from the Muhajirun, Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Uthman ibn Shimas, and Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and the rest were from the Ansar.

Ibn al-Zubayr and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck on the day of Uhud, Allah placed their spirits in the crops of green birds that visit the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, and take shelter in lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they found the goodness of their resting place, their food and their drink, and saw the honour that Allah, exalted is He, had prepared for them, they said: 'Would that our people knew what we are in of bliss and what Allah has done for us, so that they would be eager for jihad and would not shrink from it.' Allah, exalted is He, said: 'I will inform them about you and convey to your brothers.' They rejoiced at this and were glad tidings, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead, but rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for,﴾ up to His saying ﴿the reward of the believers﴾" [179] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/266; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/566, no. 2520.]].

Qatadah and al-Rabi' said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Would that we knew what has become of our brothers who were killed on the day of Uhud," so Allah revealed this verse.

Masruq said: We asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud about this verse, and he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed the spirits of the martyrs of Uhud in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish and take shelter in lamps hanging from the Throne." He said: "Then Allah looked upon them with a look and said: 'Do you desire anything that I may increase for you?' They said: 'Our Lord, do we not roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' Then He looked upon them a second time and said: 'Do you desire anything that I may increase for you?'

They said: 'Our Lord, You have given us nothing except that we would love for You to return us to life, and we would return to the world and fight in Your way, and be killed again for Your sake.' He said: 'No.' They said: 'Then convey our greetings to our Prophet and inform him that we are pleased and that You are pleased with us.' So Allah revealed this verse."

Jabir ibn Abdullah said: My father was killed on the day of Uhud and left behind daughters. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not give you good news, O Jabir?" I said: "Yes, O Prophet of Allah." He said: "When your father was struck at Uhud, Allah brought him back to life and spoke to him directly, saying: 'O servant of Allah, ask me whatever you wish.' He said: 'I ask You to return me to the world so that I may be killed for You a second time.' He said: 'O servant of Allah, I have decreed that I will not return any creature to the world.' He said: 'O Lord, then who will convey to my people what I am in of honour?' Allah, exalted is He, said: 'I will,' and so Allah revealed this verse." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/268.]] [180].

Humayd narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No soul dies having with Allah something good that would make it happy to return to the world and have the world and all in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom; so he wishes to return to the world and be killed once more." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/126.]] [181].

Others said: It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bir Ma'unah, and the cause of that, as narrated by Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar from his father, from al-Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Humayd al-Tawil from Anas ibn Malik, and others of the people of knowledge, is that they said: Abu Bara' Amir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, "Lance-Player" (mula'ib al-asinnah), who was the chief of Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and presented him with a gift. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept it and said: "O Abu Bara', I do not accept a gift from a polytheist; so embrace Islam if you wish me to accept your gift." [182] Then he presented Islam to him, informed him of what he would have in it and what Allah had promised the believers of reward, and recited the Qur'an to him. He did not embrace Islam, nor did he go far away, and said: "O Muhammad, this matter to which you call is good and beautiful. If you were to send some men from your companions to the people of Najd to call them to your matter, I hope they would respond to you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I fear for them from the people of Najd." Abu Bara' said: "I am a protector for them" (i.e., they are under my protection), "so send them to call the people to your matter." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn Amr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men of the best Muslims, among them al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, Haram ibn Milhan, Urwah ibn Asma' ibn al-Salt al-Sulami, Nafi' ibn Waraqa' al-Khuza'i, and Amir ibn Fuhayrah, mawla of Abu Bakr. This was in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijrah, four months after Uhud. They set out until they alighted between Ma'unah, which is a land between the land of Banu Amir and the lava field of Banu Sulaym. When they alighted there, some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?" Haram ibn Milhan said: "I will." He went out with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Amir ibn al-Tufayl, who was in charge of that water. When Haram ibn Milhan came to them, Amir ibn al-Tufayl did not look at the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Haram said: "O people of Bir Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you, and I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger.﴾"

A man from the back of the tent came out to him with a spear and struck him in his side until it came out the other side. He said: "Allah is greater! I have won, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then Amir ibn al-Tufayl called upon Banu Amir against the Muslims, but they refused to answer him in what he called them to, and said: "We will not betray Abu Bara', for he made a covenant and protection for them." So he called upon tribes of Banu Sulaym: Usayyah, Ra'l and Dhakwan, and they answered him. They set out until they surrounded the people and encircled them among their men. When the Muslims saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they were all killed, except Ka'b ibn Zayd, for they left him with a little life in him. He was carried from among the dead and lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench. [[In full in Uyun al-Athar: 2/17.]]

Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damari and a man from the Ansar, of Banu Amr ibn Awf, were herding the camels of the people, and nothing alerted them to the battle lines of their companions except a bird circling over the camp. They said: "By Allah, this bird has some significance," so they approached to look at it, and behold, the people lay in their blood and the horsemen who had struck them were standing. The Ansari said to Amr ibn Umayyah: "What do you think?" He said: "I think we should go back to the Messenger of Allah and inform him of the news." The Ansari said: "But I will not turn my soul away from a place where al-Mundhir ibn Amr was killed," and he fought the people until he was killed. They took Amr ibn Umayyah captive, and when he told them that he was from Mudar, Amir ibn al-Tufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him from a slave, claiming that it was owed upon his mother. Amr ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the news. The Messenger of Allah said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. I was averse to this and fearful of it." [183] This reached Abu Bara', and it grieved him that Amir had breached his protection and what befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of it. Among those killed was Amir ibn Fuhayrah.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Hisham ibn Urwah that Amir ibn al-Tufayl used to say: "Whoever among them was killed, I saw him raised between the sky and the earth until I saw the sky beneath him." They said: "He was Amir ibn Fuhayrah." [[In full in Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/221.]]

They said: Hassan ibn Thabit said, inciting Abu Bara' against Amir ibn al-Tufayl:

A youth of the mother of sons, did it not alarm you,
while you are of the noblest of the people of Najd?
Amir struck you through Abu Bara', to breach his protection,
and a mistake is not like a deliberate act.
Bear this message to Rabi'ah, the one of great deeds:
what has happened in the calamities since I left.
Your father is the father of wars, Abu Bara',
and your maternal uncle is the noble, Hakam ibn Sa'd. [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/221.]]

Ka'b ibn Malik also said about that:

Every face has been scattered in dismay
over the protection that Abu Bara' did not grant.
O sons of the mother of sons, did you not hear
the call of one seeking help along with the women,
and the shout of the one crying for help? Yes, but
you knew that he was true to the encounter.
[[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/221.]]

When Rabi'ah ibn al-Bara' heard the verse of Hassan and the verse of Ka'b ibn Malik, he charged at Amir ibn al-Tufayl and struck him, so that he fell from his horse. He said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. If I die, my blood is for my uncle, and I will pursue it; and if I live, I will consider the matter." Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that Allah revealed concerning the martyrs of Bir Ma'unah a Qur'an: "Convey on our behalf to our people that we have met our Lord; He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him." Then it was abrogated and removed after we had recited it for a time, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead.﴾ The verse, etc.

Some said: The guardians of the martyrs, whenever a blessing or joy befell them, would grieve over the martyrs and say: "We are in blessing and joy while our fathers, sons and brothers are in graves." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this as a comfort to them and as information about the state of their slain: ﴿And do not think﴾, i.e., do not suppose, do not assume. Hisham narrated from the people of Syria: (yahsabanna) with ya'. Al-Hasan and Ibn Amir read: (qutthilu) with doubled ta', and (amwatan) like the death of one who was not killed in the way of Allah. And amwatan is put in the accusative as the second object, because "hasiba" takes two objects; when you say "I considered Zayd," it is not a complete statement until you say "standing" or "sitting." ﴿But they are alive﴾, its meaning: rather they are alive.

Ibn Abi Abla read: ahyā'an in the accusative, meaning: I consider them alive. ﴿with their Lord﴾.

Some said: It means alive in this world in reality [[This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Amr ibn Ubayd, Wasil ibn Ata', al-Jubba'i and al-Rummani; see Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 1/437.]]. It was also said: [in the world]. And it was said: with praise and remembrance, as it was said:
