ʿAmr ibn Mūsā narrated from Qatādah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most severe verse in the Qur'an upon the jinn is ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [211]," the verse.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: "What signs did Mūsā bring you?" They said: "His staff and his white hand, to the beholders." They asked the Christians: "How was ʿĪsā among you?" They said: "He used to heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life." Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Ask your Lord to make Ṣafā gold for us." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ the verse, then described them, saying:

﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides.﴾

ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Nakhaʿī and Qatādah said: This refers to prayer: one prays standing; if he cannot, sitting; if he cannot, on his side. It is ease and lightening from Allah.

The rest of the exegetes said: It means the remembrance of Allah, mentioning their constancy in it, since a person rarely is free of one of these three states. Its parallel is His saying in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

From Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to frolic in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase the remembrance of Allah." [Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah 7/72.] [212]

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, is the knowledge of faith, freedom from hypocrisy, a fortress against Satan, and a protection from the fires." [Mentioned by Quṭb al-Dīn al-Rawandī in Lubb al-Lubāb, as in Mustadrak al-Wasā'il 5/285 no. 5868.] [213]

Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā (ʿalayhi al-salām): "O Mūsā, keep Me in mind, and do not forget My remembrance in any state. Let your concern be My remembrance, for indeed the path is to Me."

﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: that they have a Creator, powerful and wise, a Manager.

Ḥammād narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū al-Ṣalt, from Abū Hurayrah: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey to the seventh heaven, there was a wind, smoke and voices. He said: "I said: 'What is this, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'These are the devils, who are burned, so that the children of Ādam do not reflect upon the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and were it not for that, they would have seen wonders.'"

Ibn ʿAwr used to say: Reflection removes heedlessness and brings fear of Allah into the heart, as water brings forth crops and plants. Hearts were never polished by anything like sorrows, nor illuminated by anything like reflection. It is related that Sufyān al-Thawrī prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqām, then raised his head to the sky, and when he saw the stars he fainted. Sufyān used to pass blood in his urine from the length of his grief and reflection.

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was lying on his bed, he raised his head, looked at the stars and the sky, and said: 'I bear witness that I have a Lord and Creator. O Allah, forgive me.' So Allah looked at him and forgave him." [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/314.] [214]

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ said: It reached me that a worshipper among the Children of Israel worshipped for thirty years, and whenever a man among them worshipped for thirty years, a cloud would shade him. But he saw nothing, so he complained of that to his father. He said to him: "O my son, reflect: have you committed any sin since you began your worship?" He said: "No, and I do not know that I ever intended one in thirty years." He said: "O my son, one remains; if you are saved from it, I hope it will shade you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Have you ever raised your gaze to the sky and then lowered it without reflection?" He said: "Many times." He said: "From here you were brought." ﴿You did not create this in vain﴾ — he referred to the word "creation," and had it referred to the heavens and the earth, it would have said: "this is vain, purposeless, frivolous; rather, You created it for a great matter."

The accusative of "al-bāṭil" is in two ways: one, by removing the preposition, meaning "for the vain" and "with the vain"; the other, as the second object.

﴿Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ "Disgraced" means: humiliated.

Al-Mufaḍḍal said: destroyed; and he recited:
"May God disgrace from the cross His servants, and those who wear the caps of monks."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/316.]

It was also said: exposed. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿and do not disgrace me regarding my guest﴾ [Hūd 11:78].

Those who hold the doctrine of threat used this verse as a shield, saying: Allah has informed that He does not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him; then He said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced," so it is necessary that everyone who enters the Fire is not a believer and does not come out of it.

The people of interpretation differed concerning this verse:

Qatādah narrated from Anas concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire."

al-Thawrī narrated from a man, from Ibn al-Musayyab concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "This is specific to whoever does not come out of it."

Abū Hilāl al-Rājī narrated from Qatādah concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him": "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire, and we do not say as the Ḥarūrīyah said; Anas ibn Mālik related this to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'A people will come out of the Fire.'" [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 9/102, with slight variation.] [215]

Some of them said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire" means whoever abides in it; and whoever does not abide in it, You have disgraced him with punishment, destruction and humiliation. ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said: "Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh came to us on ʿUmrah; I and ʿAṭāʾ met him and I said to him: 'Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him.'" He said: "And what is its disgracing when He burns him with the Fire? Indeed, below that is a disgrace."

The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: "Khizy" (disgrace) may mean shame; it is said: "khaziya yakhzā, khazāyah," when he felt shame. Dhū al-Rummah said:
"A shame overtook him at his jawl,
from the side of the rope, mixed with it was anger."
[Lisān al-ʿArab 14/227.]

al-Quṭāmī said regarding the bull and the dogs:
"Harjan and the charge of a man of valor,
the disgrace of free women is that he be a coward."
[Gharīb al-Ḥadīth 4/36; Lisān al-ʿArab 14/227.]

That is, he feels shame. So the disgrace of the believers is shame, and the disgrace of the disbelievers is humiliation and eternal abiding in the Fire.

﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed.﴾ — meaning Muḥammad (ﷺ), who calls to faith, that is, to faith, like His saying: ﴿they would have returned to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-Anʿām 6:28].

It was also said: the lām is in the sense of "ajl" (for).

Qatādah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed you about the believers among mankind, how they spoke, and about the believers among the jinn, how they spoke. As for the believing jinn, they said: ﴿Indeed, we heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct﴾ [al-Jinn 72:1–2]. As for the believing humans, they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith... so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous﴾, that is, among the company of the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, upon the tongues of Your messengers, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yūsuf 12:82].

al-Aʿmash read "rusulika" with light pronunciation.

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — do not punish us, do not destroy us, do not expose us, do not humiliate us. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise.﴾

It is said: What is the sense of their saying "Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers," when they knew and claimed that Allah does not break the promise? The answer: its wording is supplication, but its meaning is report. Its estimated sense: "And forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous," and "do not disgrace us," and "grant us what You promised us upon the tongues of Your messengers of grace, mercy, reward and blessing." It was also said its meaning is: "Make us among those to whom You give what You promised upon the tongues of Your messengers, and who deserve Your reward," because they were not certain of their deserving this honor, so they asked Him to make them deserving of it. And if the people had testified this for themselves, they would have purified themselves, and that is not a characteristic of the righteous.

Some of them said: They only asked their Lord to hasten what He promised them of victory over the enemies and the exaltation of the religion, because it is a narration about the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We know that You do not break Your promise of victory and triumph over the disbelievers, but we have no patience with Your judgment, so hasten their disgrace and grant us victory over them."

Thābit al-Bunānī narrated from Anas ibn Mālik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for a deed, He fulfills His promise; and whoever is threatened with punishment for a deed, He has the choice concerning it." [Ta'wīl Mukhtalif al-Ḥadīth of Ibn Qutaybah: 91; Musnad Abī Ya'lā 9/66.] [216]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 187–195 (part 2 of 2):

It is narrated from al-Asma'i who said: I heard Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' say: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd asked me: "Does God break His promise?" I said: "No." He said: "Then does God break His threat?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Why?" I said: "Because breaking a promise is a sign of regret, while breaking a threat is a display of generosity." Then he composed:

*The cousin does not fear my assault as long as I live,*
*nor do I hide from the fear of one who threatens.*
*Indeed, whether I threaten him or promise him,*
*I break my threat and I fulfill my promise.*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/318; al-Sihah: 1/46.]

It is narrated from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to recite ten verses from the end of Surat Al 'Imran every night.

It is narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…﴾ to its end in one night, it is recorded for him as the reward of standing in prayer for a night."

﴿So their Lord responded to them.﴾

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated from al-Hasan who said: "They kept saying, 'Our Lord, our Lord,' until their Lord responded to them."

It is also narrated from al-Sadiq (Ja'far al-Sadiq) that he said: "Whoever is struck by a matter and says five times, 'Our Lord,' God will save him from what he fears and give him what he wants." It was asked of him: "And how is that?" He said: "Recite, if you wish, ﴿Those who remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides…﴾ up to His saying ﴿the appointment.﴾"

Regarding the occasion of revelation:

Mujahid said: Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of God, I hear God mention men in the emigration (hijrah) but He does not mention women at all." So God revealed this verse.

He (Mujahid) said: The Ansar said: "She was the first woman (zaʿīnah, a woman traveling on a litter) to come to us."

﴿That I﴾: meaning "that I" or "because I," in the accusative by removal of the preposition (naṣb bi-naz' al-khafḍ, i.e., the preposition is dropped and the word is put in the accusative).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read ﴿إني﴾ (*inni*) with a kasra on the alif, as if he had implied a verb of saying, or treated the response as a statement.

﴿I will not waste the work of any worker among you﴾, O believers, ﴿whether male or female, you are of one another﴾: I will not nullify or cancel the deed of any doer.

Al-Kalbi said: This means in religion, support, and allegiance. It was also said: the reward of all of you is equal. And it was said: all of you are from Adam and Eve.

Al-Dahhak said: "Your men are like your women in obedience, and your women are like your men in obedience." A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another.﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 71.]

﴿So those who emigrated, and were expelled from their homes, and were harmed in My way﴾: meaning in My obedience. They are the emigrants whom the polytheists expelled from Mecca and harmed, ﴿and fought and were killed.﴾

Muharib ibn Dithar read ﴿وَقَتَلوا﴾ (*wa-qatalū*, with a fatha on the qaf).

It is narrated from Yazid ibn Hazim who said: "I heard 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz read: *wa-qutilū wa-qutilū*." He meant that they were killed, and those who killed them were killed by the polytheists.

Abu Raja', al-Hasan, and Talha read ﴿وقاتلوا وقتّلوا﴾ with shadda on the second verb. Al-Hasan said: this means they were cut to pieces in the battle.

'Asim, Abu 'Ubayd, and the people of Medina read ﴿وَقاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا﴾, meaning that they fought and then were killed.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read ﴿وقتلوا وقاتلوا﴾, and this has two interpretations:
One: "and those among them who remained fought," as the Arabs say, "We killed the Banu Tamim," though only some of them were killed.
The other: with *qad* implied, meaning "and they were killed, having fought."

A poet said:
*He feigned youthfulness, though old age had overtaken him.*

﴿Surely I will remove from them their misdeeds and surely I will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from God.﴾ Al-Kisa'i said: the word ﴿thawāban﴾ (as a reward) is in the accusative as a circumstantial/detached term (qaṭʿ). Al-Mubarrad said: it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and its meaning is "I will surely reward them."

﴿And with God is the best of rewards.﴾

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn 'Amr who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "On the Day of Resurrection, God, Mighty and Majestic, will call for Paradise and bring its adornments and splendor, and say: 'Where are My servants who fought in the way of God, who were harmed in My way, and who struggled in My way? Enter Paradise.' They will enter it without reckoning or punishment. Then the angels will come, prostrating and saying: 'Our Lord, we glorify You night and day and sanctify You; who are these whom You have preferred over us?' God, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'These are My servants who were harmed in My way.' Then the angels will enter upon them, saying: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you endured; how excellent is the final abode.﴾"

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/286.] [217]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 187–195 (part 1 of 2):

And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, [saying]: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it" — concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr and the people of Makkah read it with the yāʾ in both places, and Abū ʿUbayd preferred this reading.

The rest read it with the tāʾ, and Abū Ḥātim preferred this. Whoever reads with the tāʾ, it is on the assumption of an implied verb of speech, meaning: "He said, 'You shall make it clear'." Its evidence is His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom..."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:81]. Whoever reads with the yāʾ, it is based on His saying: ﴿they threw it behind their backs﴾, meaning they cast it aside, neglected it, and abandoned acting upon it.

﴿And sold it for a small price﴾, meaning the food they ate, ﴿and evil is what they bought﴾.

Qatādah said: "This is the covenant of Allah taken from the people of Makkah: whoever knows something should teach it. Beware of concealing knowledge, for it is a ruin."

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: "It is not lawful for a scholar to remain silent about his knowledge, nor for an ignorant person to remain silent about his ignorance. Allah said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book...﴾ the verse, and He said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [al-Naḥl 16:43]."

Thābit ibn al-Bunānī, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayrah, that he said: "Were it not for what Allah took from the People of the Book, I would not have related anything to you," then he recited this verse: ﴿And when Allah took...﴾.

Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever conceals knowledge from its people will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire."

And from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmārah, who said: "I came to al-Zuhrī after he had given up narrating hadith, and I placed myself at his door and said: 'If you see fit, would you narrate to me?' He said: 'Do you not know that I have given up narrating hadith?' I said: 'Either you narrate to me, or I narrate to you.' He said: 'Narrate to me.' So I said: 'al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to me from Najm al-Jazzār, who said: I heard ʿAlī (ʿalayhi al-salām) say: "Allah did not take a covenant from the people of ignorance to learn until He took a covenant from the people of knowledge to teach."'" He said: 'Then narrate to me forty hadiths.'" [Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān 2/467.]

﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they were given...﴾ — "do not think" with the yāʾ is read by Ḥumayd ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū ʿAmr, while others read it with the tāʾ. Whoever reads it with the yāʾ, its meaning is: "let not those who rejoice think they have a means of escape from the punishment." Whoever reads it with the tāʾ, its meaning is: "Do not think, O Muḥammad, that those who rejoice are safe from the punishment," and its complement is in the bāʾ.

His saying "do not think" with the tāʾ and the fatḥah on the bāʾ is an emphatic repetition.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿĪsā read "lā taḥsabunna" with the tāʾ and a ḍammah on the bāʾ, meaning Muḥammad and his companions.

Muḥammad, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur read with the yāʾ and a ḍammah on the bāʾ, as a report about those who rejoice, meaning: "let them not think themselves [safe]." They differed concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse.

ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that some hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Messenger of Allah, if you went out to fight, we would fight with you." So when he (ﷺ) went out, they stayed behind him and rejoiced in their sitting "against the Messenger of Allah." When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned, they made excuses to him, and he accepted their excuses, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done.

Mālik ibn Anas narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, that he and Zayd ibn Thābit were with Marwān, who was then the governor of Madīnah. Marwān said to Rāfiʿ: "About what was this verse revealed: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they were given...﴾?" Rāfiʿ said: "It was revealed about some hypocrites who, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a journey, would stay behind from him." Marwān denied this and said: "What is this?" Rāfiʿ became distressed by this and said to Zayd ibn Thābit: "I ask you by Allah, do you know what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said?" Zayd said: "Yes." So they both left Marwān's presence, and Zayd said to Rāfiʿ, joking with him: "Will you not be praised for what I testified to on your behalf?" Rāfiʿ said: "And what is this? Shall I praise you for testifying to the truth?" Zayd said: "Yes, Allah has praised the people of truth for the truth."

ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed about Finḥāṣ, Ashyaʿ and their like among the rabbis, who rejoiced at misleading the people, and at the people's attributing knowledge to them, and their saying that they were scholars when they were not people of knowledge; they did not guide anyone to guidance or good.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī said: They are the Jews of Madīnah who wrote to the Jews of Yemen, Syria and the far regions: "Muḥammad is not a messenger, so hold firm to your religion." Their word then united upon disbelief in Muḥammad and the Qur'an, and they rejoiced at that and said: "Praise be to Allah who has united our word; we are upon the religion of Ibrāhīm, and we are the first people of knowledge." But they were not so.

Mujāhid: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at people's admiration of their altering of the Book and their striving at it.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at what Allah gave Ibrāhīm, while they are innocent of that.

Ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf that Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam said to his freedman: "O Abū Rāfiʿ, go to Ibn ʿAbbās and say to him: 'If every one of us rejoices at what he was given and loves to be praised for what he did not do, we will all surely be punished.'" Ibn ʿAbbās said: "What is it to you with this verse? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only summoned the Jews and asked them about something, and they concealed it from him and told him something else, showing him that they had told him what he had asked about. They therefore sought praise from him for that and rejoiced at their concealment, so this verse was revealed."

Qatādah and Muqātil: The Jews of Khaybar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We recognize you and affirm you, and we are upon your opinion, and we are a shield for you," but that was not in their hearts. When they left his presence, the Muslims said to them: "What did you do?" They said: "We recognized him and affirmed him." The Muslims said to them: "You have done well, so do likewise." They praised them and invoked blessings upon them, so Allah revealed this verse concerning them.

Shuʿbah narrated from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: It was revealed about some Jews who equipped an army against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spent on them. Ibrāhīm recited it as "bimā ūtū" with a madd, meaning "they were given."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read "ūtū," meaning "they were given."

Allah said: ﴿Do not think them safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾

From ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, who said: I entered with Ibn ʿUmar upon ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and Ibn ʿUmar said: "Tell us of the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah." She wept and prolonged it, then said: "Everything about the Messenger of Allah was wondrous. He came to me on my night, entered under my covering until his skin touched my skin, then said: 'O ʿĀʾishah, will you permit me to worship my Lord, mighty and majestic?' I said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I love your nearness and I love what pleases you; I have permitted you.' So he (ʿalayhi al-ṣalāh wa-al-salām) rose to a waterskin in the house and performed ablution, not pouring much water. Then he stood to pray and recited from the Qur'an and began to weep until the tears reached his lap. Then he raised his hand and kept weeping until I saw the tears had wet the ground. Then Bilāl came to him with the dawn prayer and saw him weeping, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you weep when Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?' He said: 'O Bilāl, shall I not be a grateful servant?' Then he said: 'And why should I not weep, when Allah has revealed to me tonight: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾' — the verse. Then he said: 'Woe to whoever recites it and does not reflect upon it.'" [al-Durr al-Manthūr 2/111.] [210]

From Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with them both, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he rose at night would use the miswāk, then look at the sky, then say: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ up to His saying ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾

ʿAmr ibn Mūsā narrated from Qatādah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most severe verse in the Qur'an upon the jinn is ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [211]," the verse.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: "What signs did Mūsā bring you?" They said: "His staff and his white hand, to the beholders." They asked the Christians: "How was ʿĪsā among you?" They said: "He used to heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life." Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Ask your Lord to make Ṣafā gold for us." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ the verse, then described them, saying:

﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides.﴾

ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Nakhaʿī and Qatādah said: This refers to prayer: one prays standing; if he cannot, sitting; if he cannot, on his side. It is ease and lightening from Allah.

The rest of the exegetes said: It means the remembrance of Allah, mentioning their constancy in it, since a person rarely is free of one of these three states. Its parallel is His saying in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

From Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to frolic in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase the remembrance of Allah." [Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah 7/72.] [212]

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, is the knowledge of faith, freedom from hypocrisy, a fortress against Satan, and a protection from the fires." [Mentioned by Quṭb al-Dīn al-Rawandī in Lubb al-Lubāb, as in Mustadrak al-Wasā'il 5/285 no. 5868.] [213]

Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā (ʿalayhi al-salām): "O Mūsā, keep Me in mind, and do not forget My remembrance in any state. Let your concern be My remembrance, for indeed the path is to Me."

﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: that they have a Creator, powerful and wise, a Manager.

Ḥammād narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū al-Ṣalt, from Abū Hurayrah: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey to the seventh heaven, there was a wind, smoke and voices. He said: "I said: 'What is this, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'These are the devils, who are burned, so that the children of Ādam do not reflect upon the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and were it not for that, they would have seen wonders.'"

Ibn ʿAwr used to say: Reflection removes heedlessness and brings fear of Allah into the heart, as water brings forth crops and plants. Hearts were never polished by anything like sorrows, nor illuminated by anything like reflection. It is related that Sufyān al-Thawrī prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqām, then raised his head to the sky, and when he saw the stars he fainted. Sufyān used to pass blood in his urine from the length of his grief and reflection.

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was lying on his bed, he raised his head, looked at the stars and the sky, and said: 'I bear witness that I have a Lord and Creator. O Allah, forgive me.' So Allah looked at him and forgave him." [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/314.] [214]

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ said: It reached me that a worshipper among the Children of Israel worshipped for thirty years, and whenever a man among them worshipped for thirty years, a cloud would shade him. But he saw nothing, so he complained of that to his father. He said to him: "O my son, reflect: have you committed any sin since you began your worship?" He said: "No, and I do not know that I ever intended one in thirty years." He said: "O my son, one remains; if you are saved from it, I hope it will shade you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Have you ever raised your gaze to the sky and then lowered it without reflection?" He said: "Many times." He said: "From here you were brought." ﴿You did not create this in vain﴾ — he referred to the word "creation," and had it referred to the heavens and the earth, it would have said: "this is vain, purposeless, frivolous; rather, You created it for a great matter."

The accusative of "al-bāṭil" is in two ways: one, by removing the preposition, meaning "for the vain" and "with the vain"; the other, as the second object.

﴿Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ "Disgraced" means: humiliated.

Al-Mufaḍḍal said: destroyed; and he recited:
"May God disgrace from the cross His servants, and those who wear the caps of monks."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/316.]

It was also said: exposed. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿and do not disgrace me regarding my guest﴾ [Hūd 11:78].

Those who hold the doctrine of threat used this verse as a shield, saying: Allah has informed that He does not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him; then He said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced," so it is necessary that everyone who enters the Fire is not a believer and does not come out of it.

The people of interpretation differed concerning this verse:

Qatādah narrated from Anas concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire."

al-Thawrī narrated from a man, from Ibn al-Musayyab concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "This is specific to whoever does not come out of it."

Abū Hilāl al-Rājī narrated from Qatādah concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him": "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire, and we do not say as the Ḥarūrīyah said; Anas ibn Mālik related this to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'A people will come out of the Fire.'" [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 9/102, with slight variation.] [215]

Some of them said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire" means whoever abides in it; and whoever does not abide in it, You have disgraced him with punishment, destruction and humiliation. ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said: "Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh came to us on ʿUmrah; I and ʿAṭāʾ met him and I said to him: 'Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him.'" He said: "And what is its disgracing when He burns him with the Fire? Indeed, below that is a disgrace."

The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: "Khizy" (disgrace) may mean shame; it is said: "khaziya yakhzā, khazāyah," when he felt shame. Dhū al-Rummah said:
"A shame overtook him at his jawl,
from the side of the rope, mixed with it was anger."
[Lisān al-ʿArab 14/227.]

al-Quṭāmī said regarding the bull and the dogs:
"Harjan and the charge of a man of valor,
the disgrace of free women is that he be a coward."
[Gharīb al-Ḥadīth 4/36; Lisān al-ʿArab 14/227.]

That is, he feels shame. So the disgrace of the believers is shame, and the disgrace of the disbelievers is humiliation and eternal abiding in the Fire.

﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed.﴾ — meaning Muḥammad (ﷺ), who calls to faith, that is, to faith, like His saying: ﴿they would have returned to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-Anʿām 6:28].

It was also said: the lām is in the sense of "ajl" (for).

Qatādah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed you about the believers among mankind, how they spoke, and about the believers among the jinn, how they spoke. As for the believing jinn, they said: ﴿Indeed, we heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct﴾ [al-Jinn 72:1–2]. As for the believing humans, they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith... so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous﴾, that is, among the company of the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, upon the tongues of Your messengers, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yūsuf 12:82].

al-Aʿmash read "rusulika" with light pronunciation.

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — do not punish us, do not destroy us, do not expose us, do not humiliate us. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise.﴾

It is said: What is the sense of their saying "Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers," when they knew and claimed that Allah does not break the promise? The answer: its wording is supplication, but its meaning is report. Its estimated sense: "And forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous," and "do not disgrace us," and "grant us what You promised us upon the tongues of Your messengers of grace, mercy, reward and blessing." It was also said its meaning is: "Make us among those to whom You give what You promised upon the tongues of Your messengers, and who deserve Your reward," because they were not certain of their deserving this honor, so they asked Him to make them deserving of it. And if the people had testified this for themselves, they would have purified themselves, and that is not a characteristic of the righteous.

Some of them said: They only asked their Lord to hasten what He promised them of victory over the enemies and the exaltation of the religion, because it is a narration about the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We know that You do not break Your promise of victory and triumph over the disbelievers, but we have no patience with Your judgment, so hasten their disgrace and grant us victory over them."

Thābit al-Bunānī narrated from Anas ibn Mālik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for a deed, He fulfills His promise; and whoever is threatened with punishment for a deed, He has the choice concerning it." [Ta'wīl Mukhtalif al-Ḥadīth of Ibn Qutaybah: 91; Musnad Abī Ya'lā 9/66.] [216]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 187–195 (part 2 of 2):

It is narrated from al-Asma'i who said: I heard Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' say: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd asked me: "Does God break His promise?" I said: "No." He said: "Then does God break His threat?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Why?" I said: "Because breaking a promise is a sign of regret, while breaking a threat is a display of generosity." Then he composed:

*The cousin does not fear my assault as long as I live,*
*nor do I hide from the fear of one who threatens.*
*Indeed, whether I threaten him or promise him,*
*I break my threat and I fulfill my promise.*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/318; al-Sihah: 1/46.]

It is narrated from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to recite ten verses from the end of Surat Al 'Imran every night.

It is narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…﴾ to its end in one night, it is recorded for him as the reward of standing in prayer for a night."

﴿So their Lord responded to them.﴾

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated from al-Hasan who said: "They kept saying, 'Our Lord, our Lord,' until their Lord responded to them."

It is also narrated from al-Sadiq (Ja'far al-Sadiq) that he said: "Whoever is struck by a matter and says five times, 'Our Lord,' God will save him from what he fears and give him what he wants." It was asked of him: "And how is that?" He said: "Recite, if you wish, ﴿Those who remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides…﴾ up to His saying ﴿the appointment.﴾"

Regarding the occasion of revelation:

Mujahid said: Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of God, I hear God mention men in the emigration (hijrah) but He does not mention women at all." So God revealed this verse.

He (Mujahid) said: The Ansar said: "She was the first woman (zaʿīnah, a woman traveling on a litter) to come to us."

﴿That I﴾: meaning "that I" or "because I," in the accusative by removal of the preposition (naṣb bi-naz' al-khafḍ, i.e., the preposition is dropped and the word is put in the accusative).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read ﴿إني﴾ (*inni*) with a kasra on the alif, as if he had implied a verb of saying, or treated the response as a statement.

﴿I will not waste the work of any worker among you﴾, O believers, ﴿whether male or female, you are of one another﴾: I will not nullify or cancel the deed of any doer.

Al-Kalbi said: This means in religion, support, and allegiance. It was also said: the reward of all of you is equal. And it was said: all of you are from Adam and Eve.

Al-Dahhak said: "Your men are like your women in obedience, and your women are like your men in obedience." A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another.﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 71.]

﴿So those who emigrated, and were expelled from their homes, and were harmed in My way﴾: meaning in My obedience. They are the emigrants whom the polytheists expelled from Mecca and harmed, ﴿and fought and were killed.﴾

Muharib ibn Dithar read ﴿وَقَتَلوا﴾ (*wa-qatalū*, with a fatha on the qaf).

It is narrated from Yazid ibn Hazim who said: "I heard 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz read: *wa-qutilū wa-qutilū*." He meant that they were killed, and those who killed them were killed by the polytheists.

Abu Raja', al-Hasan, and Talha read ﴿وقاتلوا وقتّلوا﴾ with shadda on the second verb. Al-Hasan said: this means they were cut to pieces in the battle.

'Asim, Abu 'Ubayd, and the people of Medina read ﴿وَقاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا﴾, meaning that they fought and then were killed.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read ﴿وقتلوا وقاتلوا﴾, and this has two interpretations:
One: "and those among them who remained fought," as the Arabs say, "We killed the Banu Tamim," though only some of them were killed.
The other: with *qad* implied, meaning "and they were killed, having fought."

A poet said:
*He feigned youthfulness, though old age had overtaken him.*

﴿Surely I will remove from them their misdeeds and surely I will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from God.﴾ Al-Kisa'i said: the word ﴿thawāban﴾ (as a reward) is in the accusative as a circumstantial/detached term (qaṭʿ). Al-Mubarrad said: it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and its meaning is "I will surely reward them."

﴿And with God is the best of rewards.﴾

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn 'Amr who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "On the Day of Resurrection, God, Mighty and Majestic, will call for Paradise and bring its adornments and splendor, and say: 'Where are My servants who fought in the way of God, who were harmed in My way, and who struggled in My way? Enter Paradise.' They will enter it without reckoning or punishment. Then the angels will come, prostrating and saying: 'Our Lord, we glorify You night and day and sanctify You; who are these whom You have preferred over us?' God, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'These are My servants who were harmed in My way.' Then the angels will enter upon them, saying: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you endured; how excellent is the final abode.﴾"

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/286.] [217]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 187–195 (part 1 of 2):

And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, [saying]: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it" — concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr and the people of Makkah read it with the yāʾ in both places, and Abū ʿUbayd preferred this reading.

The rest read it with the tāʾ, and Abū Ḥātim preferred this. Whoever reads with the tāʾ, it is on the assumption of an implied verb of speech, meaning: "He said, 'You shall make it clear'." Its evidence is His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom..."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:81]. Whoever reads with the yāʾ, it is based on His saying: ﴿they threw it behind their backs﴾, meaning they cast it aside, neglected it, and abandoned acting upon it.

﴿And sold it for a small price﴾, meaning the food they ate, ﴿and evil is what they bought﴾.

Qatādah said: "This is the covenant of Allah taken from the people of Makkah: whoever knows something should teach it. Beware of concealing knowledge, for it is a ruin."

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: "It is not lawful for a scholar to remain silent about his knowledge, nor for an ignorant person to remain silent about his ignorance. Allah said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book...﴾ the verse, and He said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [al-Naḥl 16:43]."

Thābit ibn al-Bunānī, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayrah, that he said: "Were it not for what Allah took from the People of the Book, I would not have related anything to you," then he recited this verse: ﴿And when Allah took...﴾.

Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever conceals knowledge from its people will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire."

And from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmārah, who said: "I came to al-Zuhrī after he had given up narrating hadith, and I placed myself at his door and said: 'If you see fit, would you narrate to me?' He said: 'Do you not know that I have given up narrating hadith?' I said: 'Either you narrate to me, or I narrate to you.' He said: 'Narrate to me.' So I said: 'al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to me from Najm al-Jazzār, who said: I heard ʿAlī (ʿalayhi al-salām) say: "Allah did not take a covenant from the people of ignorance to learn until He took a covenant from the people of knowledge to teach."'" He said: 'Then narrate to me forty hadiths.'" [Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān 2/467.]

﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they were given...﴾ — "do not think" with the yāʾ is read by Ḥumayd ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū ʿAmr, while others read it with the tāʾ. Whoever reads it with the yāʾ, its meaning is: "let not those who rejoice think they have a means of escape from the punishment." Whoever reads it with the tāʾ, its meaning is: "Do not think, O Muḥammad, that those who rejoice are safe from the punishment," and its complement is in the bāʾ.

His saying "do not think" with the tāʾ and the fatḥah on the bāʾ is an emphatic repetition.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿĪsā read "lā taḥsabunna" with the tāʾ and a ḍammah on the bāʾ, meaning Muḥammad and his companions.

Muḥammad, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur read with the yāʾ and a ḍammah on the bāʾ, as a report about those who rejoice, meaning: "let them not think themselves [safe]." They differed concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse.

ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that some hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Messenger of Allah, if you went out to fight, we would fight with you." So when he (ﷺ) went out, they stayed behind him and rejoiced in their sitting "against the Messenger of Allah." When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned, they made excuses to him, and he accepted their excuses, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done.

Mālik ibn Anas narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, that he and Zayd ibn Thābit were with Marwān, who was then the governor of Madīnah. Marwān said to Rāfiʿ: "About what was this verse revealed: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they were given...﴾?" Rāfiʿ said: "It was revealed about some hypocrites who, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a journey, would stay behind from him." Marwān denied this and said: "What is this?" Rāfiʿ became distressed by this and said to Zayd ibn Thābit: "I ask you by Allah, do you know what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said?" Zayd said: "Yes." So they both left Marwān's presence, and Zayd said to Rāfiʿ, joking with him: "Will you not be praised for what I testified to on your behalf?" Rāfiʿ said: "And what is this? Shall I praise you for testifying to the truth?" Zayd said: "Yes, Allah has praised the people of truth for the truth."

ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed about Finḥāṣ, Ashyaʿ and their like among the rabbis, who rejoiced at misleading the people, and at the people's attributing knowledge to them, and their saying that they were scholars when they were not people of knowledge; they did not guide anyone to guidance or good.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī said: They are the Jews of Madīnah who wrote to the Jews of Yemen, Syria and the far regions: "Muḥammad is not a messenger, so hold firm to your religion." Their word then united upon disbelief in Muḥammad and the Qur'an, and they rejoiced at that and said: "Praise be to Allah who has united our word; we are upon the religion of Ibrāhīm, and we are the first people of knowledge." But they were not so.

Mujāhid: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at people's admiration of their altering of the Book and their striving at it.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at what Allah gave Ibrāhīm, while they are innocent of that.

Ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf that Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam said to his freedman: "O Abū Rāfiʿ, go to Ibn ʿAbbās and say to him: 'If every one of us rejoices at what he was given and loves to be praised for what he did not do, we will all surely be punished.'" Ibn ʿAbbās said: "What is it to you with this verse? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only summoned the Jews and asked them about something, and they concealed it from him and told him something else, showing him that they had told him what he had asked about. They therefore sought praise from him for that and rejoiced at their concealment, so this verse was revealed."

Qatādah and Muqātil: The Jews of Khaybar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We recognize you and affirm you, and we are upon your opinion, and we are a shield for you," but that was not in their hearts. When they left his presence, the Muslims said to them: "What did you do?" They said: "We recognized him and affirmed him." The Muslims said to them: "You have done well, so do likewise." They praised them and invoked blessings upon them, so Allah revealed this verse concerning them.

Shuʿbah narrated from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: It was revealed about some Jews who equipped an army against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spent on them. Ibrāhīm recited it as "bimā ūtū" with a madd, meaning "they were given."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read "ūtū," meaning "they were given."

Allah said: ﴿Do not think them safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾

From ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, who said: I entered with Ibn ʿUmar upon ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and Ibn ʿUmar said: "Tell us of the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah." She wept and prolonged it, then said: "Everything about the Messenger of Allah was wondrous. He came to me on my night, entered under my covering until his skin touched my skin, then said: 'O ʿĀʾishah, will you permit me to worship my Lord, mighty and majestic?' I said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I love your nearness and I love what pleases you; I have permitted you.' So he (ʿalayhi al-ṣalāh wa-al-salām) rose to a waterskin in the house and performed ablution, not pouring much water. Then he stood to pray and recited from the Qur'an and began to weep until the tears reached his lap. Then he raised his hand and kept weeping until I saw the tears had wet the ground. Then Bilāl came to him with the dawn prayer and saw him weeping, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you weep when Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?' He said: 'O Bilāl, shall I not be a grateful servant?' Then he said: 'And why should I not weep, when Allah has revealed to me tonight: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾' — the verse. Then he said: 'Woe to whoever recites it and does not reflect upon it.'" [al-Durr al-Manthūr 2/111.] [210]

From Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with them both, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he rose at night would use the miswāk, then look at the sky, then say: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ up to His saying ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾

ʿAmr ibn Mūsā narrated from Qatādah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most severe verse in the Qur'an upon the jinn is ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [211]," the verse.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: "What signs did Mūsā bring you?" They said: "His staff and his white hand, to the beholders." They asked the Christians: "How was ʿĪsā among you?" They said: "He used to heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life." Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Ask your Lord to make Ṣafā gold for us." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ the verse, then described them, saying:

﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides.﴾

ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Nakhaʿī and Qatādah said: This refers to prayer: one prays standing; if he cannot, sitting; if he cannot, on his side. It is ease and lightening from Allah.

The rest of the exegetes said: It means the remembrance of Allah, mentioning their constancy in it, since a person rarely is free of one of these three states. Its parallel is His saying in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

From Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to frolic in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase the remembrance of Allah." [Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah 7/72.] [212]

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, is the knowledge of faith, freedom from hypocrisy, a fortress against Satan, and a protection from the fires." [Mentioned by Quṭb al-Dīn al-Rawandī in Lubb al-Lubāb, as in Mustadrak al-Wasā'il 5/285 no. 5868.] [213]

Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā (ʿalayhi al-salām): "O Mūsā, keep Me in mind, and do not forget My remembrance in any state. Let your concern be My remembrance, for indeed the path is to Me."

﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: that they have a Creator, powerful and wise, a Manager.

Ḥammād narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū al-Ṣalt, from Abū Hurayrah: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey to the seventh heaven, there was a wind, smoke and voices. He said: "I said: 'What is this, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'These are the devils, who are burned, so that the children of Ādam do not reflect upon the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and were it not for that, they would have seen wonders.'"

Ibn ʿAwr used to say: Reflection removes heedlessness and brings fear of Allah into the heart, as water brings forth crops and plants. Hearts were never polished by anything like sorrows, nor illuminated by anything like reflection. It is related that Sufyān al-Thawrī prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqām, then raised his head to the sky, and when he saw the stars he fainted. Sufyān used to pass blood in his urine from the length of his grief and reflection.

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was lying on his bed, he raised his head, looked at the stars and the sky, and said: 'I bear witness that I have a Lord and Creator. O Allah, forgive me.' So Allah looked at him and forgave him." [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/314.] [214]

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ said: It reached me that a worshipper among the Children of Israel worshipped for thirty years, and whenever a man among them worshipped for thirty years, a cloud would shade him. But he saw nothing, so he complained of that to his father. He said to him: "O my son, reflect: have you committed any sin since you began your worship?" He said: "No, and I do not know that I ever intended one in thirty years." He said: "O my son, one remains; if you are saved from it, I hope it will shade you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Have you ever raised your gaze to the sky and then lowered it without reflection?" He said: "Many times." He said: "From here you were brought." ﴿You did not create this in vain﴾ — he referred to the word "creation," and had it referred to the heavens and the earth, it would have said: "this is vain, purposeless, frivolous; rather, You created it for a great matter."

The accusative of "al-bāṭil" is in two ways: one, by removing the preposition, meaning "for the vain" and "with the vain"; the other, as the second object.

﴿Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ "Disgraced" means: humiliated.

Al-Mufaḍḍal said: destroyed; and he recited:
"May God disgrace from the cross His servants, and those who wear the caps of monks."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/316.]

It was also said: exposed. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿and do not disgrace me regarding my guest﴾ [Hūd 11:78].

Those who hold the doctrine of threat used this verse as a shield, saying: Allah has informed that He does not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him; then He said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced," so it is necessary that everyone who enters the Fire is not a believer and does not come out of it.

The people of interpretation differed concerning this verse:

Qatādah narrated from Anas concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire."

al-Thawrī narrated from a man, from Ibn al-Musayyab concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "This is specific to whoever does not come out of it."

Abū Hilāl al-Rājī narrated from Qatādah concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him": "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire, and we do not say as the Ḥarūrīyah said; Anas ibn Mālik related this to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'A people will come out of the Fire.'" [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 9/102, with slight variation.] [215]

Some of them said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire" means whoever abides in it; and whoever does not abide in it, You have disgraced him with punishment, destruction and humiliation. ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said: "Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh came to us on ʿUmrah; I and ʿAṭāʾ met him and I said to him: 'Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him.'" He said: "And what is its disgracing when He burns him with the Fire? Indeed, below that is a disgrace."

The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: "Khizy" (disgrace) may mean shame; it is said: "khaziya yakhzā, khazāyah," when he felt shame. Dhū al-Rummah said:
"A shame overtook him at his jawl,
from the side of the rope, mixed with it was anger."
[Lisān al-ʿArab 14/227.]

al-Quṭāmī said regarding the bull and the dogs:
"Harjan and the charge of a man of valor,
the disgrace of free women is that he be a coward."
[Gharīb al-Ḥadīth 4/36; Lisān al-ʿArab 14/227.]

That is, he feels shame. So the disgrace of the believers is shame, and the disgrace of the disbelievers is humiliation and eternal abiding in the Fire.

﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed.﴾ — meaning Muḥammad (ﷺ), who calls to faith, that is, to faith, like His saying: ﴿they would have returned to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-Anʿām 6:28].

It was also said: the lām is in the sense of "ajl" (for).

Qatādah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed you about the believers among mankind, how they spoke, and about the believers among the jinn, how they spoke. As for the believing jinn, they said: ﴿Indeed, we heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct﴾ [al-Jinn 72:1–2]. As for the believing humans, they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith... so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous﴾, that is, among the company of the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, upon the tongues of Your messengers, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yūsuf 12:82].

al-Aʿmash read "rusulika" with light pronunciation.

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — do not punish us, do not destroy us, do not expose us, do not humiliate us. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise.﴾

It is said: What is the sense of their saying "Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers," when they knew and claimed that Allah does not break the promise? The answer: its wording is supplication, but its meaning is report. Its estimated sense: "And forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous," and "do not disgrace us," and "grant us what You promised us upon the tongues of Your messengers of grace, mercy, reward and blessing." It was also said its meaning is: "Make us among those to whom You give what You promised upon the tongues of Your messengers, and who deserve Your reward," because they were not certain of their deserving this honor, so they asked Him to make them deserving of it. And if the people had testified this for themselves, they would have purified themselves, and that is not a characteristic of the righteous.

Some of them said: They only asked their Lord to hasten what He promised them of victory over the enemies and the exaltation of the religion, because it is a narration about the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We know that You do not break Your promise of victory and triumph over the disbelievers, but we have no patience with Your judgment, so hasten their disgrace and grant us victory over them."

Thābit al-Bunānī narrated from Anas ibn Mālik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for a deed, He fulfills His promise; and whoever is threatened with punishment for a deed, He has the choice concerning it." [Ta'wīl Mukhtalif al-Ḥadīth of Ibn Qutaybah: 91; Musnad Abī Ya'lā 9/66.] [216]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verses 187–195 (part 2 of 2):

It is narrated from al-Asma'i who said: I heard Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' say: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd asked me: "Does God break His promise?" I said: "No." He said: "Then does God break His threat?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Why?" I said: "Because breaking a promise is a sign of regret, while breaking a threat is a display of generosity." Then he composed:

*The cousin does not fear my assault as long as I live,*
*nor do I hide from the fear of one who threatens.*
*Indeed, whether I threaten him or promise him,*
*I break my threat and I fulfill my promise.*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/318; al-Sihah: 1/46.]

It is narrated from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to recite ten verses from the end of Surat Al 'Imran every night.

It is narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…﴾ to its end in one night, it is recorded for him as the reward of standing in prayer for a night."

﴿So their Lord responded to them.﴾

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated from al-Hasan who said: "They kept saying, 'Our Lord, our Lord,' until their Lord responded to them."

It is also narrated from al-Sadiq (Ja'far al-Sadiq) that he said: "Whoever is struck by a matter and says five times, 'Our Lord,' God will save him from what he fears and give him what he wants." It was asked of him: "And how is that?" He said: "Recite, if you wish, ﴿Those who remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides…﴾ up to His saying ﴿the appointment.﴾"

Regarding the occasion of revelation:

Mujahid said: Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of God, I hear God mention men in the emigration (hijrah) but He does not mention women at all." So God revealed this verse.

He (Mujahid) said: The Ansar said: "She was the first woman (zaʿīnah, a woman traveling on a litter) to come to us."

﴿That I﴾: meaning "that I" or "because I," in the accusative by removal of the preposition (naṣb bi-naz' al-khafḍ, i.e., the preposition is dropped and the word is put in the accusative).

'Isa ibn 'Umar read ﴿إني﴾ (*inni*) with a kasra on the alif, as if he had implied a verb of saying, or treated the response as a statement.

﴿I will not waste the work of any worker among you﴾, O believers, ﴿whether male or female, you are of one another﴾: I will not nullify or cancel the deed of any doer.

Al-Kalbi said: This means in religion, support, and allegiance. It was also said: the reward of all of you is equal. And it was said: all of you are from Adam and Eve.

Al-Dahhak said: "Your men are like your women in obedience, and your women are like your men in obedience." A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another.﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 71.]

﴿So those who emigrated, and were expelled from their homes, and were harmed in My way﴾: meaning in My obedience. They are the emigrants whom the polytheists expelled from Mecca and harmed, ﴿and fought and were killed.﴾

Muharib ibn Dithar read ﴿وَقَتَلوا﴾ (*wa-qatalū*, with a fatha on the qaf).

It is narrated from Yazid ibn Hazim who said: "I heard 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz read: *wa-qutilū wa-qutilū*." He meant that they were killed, and those who killed them were killed by the polytheists.

Abu Raja', al-Hasan, and Talha read ﴿وقاتلوا وقتّلوا﴾ with shadda on the second verb. Al-Hasan said: this means they were cut to pieces in the battle.

'Asim, Abu 'Ubayd, and the people of Medina read ﴿وَقاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا﴾, meaning that they fought and then were killed.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read ﴿وقتلوا وقاتلوا﴾, and this has two interpretations:
One: "and those among them who remained fought," as the Arabs say, "We killed the Banu Tamim," though only some of them were killed.
The other: with *qad* implied, meaning "and they were killed, having fought."

A poet said:
*He feigned youthfulness, though old age had overtaken him.*

﴿Surely I will remove from them their misdeeds and surely I will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from God.﴾ Al-Kisa'i said: the word ﴿thawāban﴾ (as a reward) is in the accusative as a circumstantial/detached term (qaṭʿ). Al-Mubarrad said: it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and its meaning is "I will surely reward them."

﴿And with God is the best of rewards.﴾

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn 'Amr who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "On the Day of Resurrection, God, Mighty and Majestic, will call for Paradise and bring its adornments and splendor, and say: 'Where are My servants who fought in the way of God, who were harmed in My way, and who struggled in My way? Enter Paradise.' They will enter it without reckoning or punishment. Then the angels will come, prostrating and saying: 'Our Lord, we glorify You night and day and sanctify You; who are these whom You have preferred over us?' God, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'These are My servants who were harmed in My way.' Then the angels will enter upon them, saying: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you endured; how excellent is the final abode.﴾"

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 4/286.] [217]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 3, verse 187–195 (part 1 of 2):

And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, [saying]: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it" — concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr and the people of Makkah read it with the yāʾ in both places, and Abū ʿUbayd preferred this reading.

The rest read it with the tāʾ, and Abū Ḥātim preferred this. Whoever reads with the tāʾ, it is on the assumption of an implied verb of speech, meaning: "He said, 'You shall make it clear'." Its evidence is His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom..."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:81]. Whoever reads with the yāʾ, it is based on His saying: ﴿they threw it behind their backs﴾, meaning they cast it aside, neglected it, and abandoned acting upon it.

﴿And sold it for a small price﴾, meaning the food they ate, ﴿and evil is what they bought﴾.

Qatādah said: "This is the covenant of Allah taken from the people of Makkah: whoever knows something should teach it. Beware of concealing knowledge, for it is a ruin."

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: "It is not lawful for a scholar to remain silent about his knowledge, nor for an ignorant person to remain silent about his ignorance. Allah said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book...﴾ the verse, and He said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [al-Naḥl 16:43]."

Thābit ibn al-Bunānī, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayrah, that he said: "Were it not for what Allah took from the People of the Book, I would not have related anything to you," then he recited this verse: ﴿And when Allah took...﴾.

Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever conceals knowledge from its people will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire."

And from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmārah, who said: "I came to al-Zuhrī after he had given up narrating hadith, and I placed myself at his door and said: 'If you see fit, would you narrate to me?' He said: 'Do you not know that I have given up narrating hadith?' I said: 'Either you narrate to me, or I narrate to you.' He said: 'Narrate to me.' So I said: 'al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to me from Najm al-Jazzār, who said: I heard ʿAlī (ʿalayhi al-salām) say: "Allah did not take a covenant from the people of ignorance to learn until He took a covenant from the people of knowledge to teach."'" He said: 'Then narrate to me forty hadiths.'" [Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān 2/467.]

﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they were given...﴾ — "do not think" with the yāʾ is read by Ḥumayd ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū ʿAmr, while others read it with the tāʾ. Whoever reads it with the yāʾ, its meaning is: "let not those who rejoice think they have a means of escape from the punishment." Whoever reads it with the tāʾ, its meaning is: "Do not think, O Muḥammad, that those who rejoice are safe from the punishment," and its complement is in the bāʾ.

His saying "do not think" with the tāʾ and the fatḥah on the bāʾ is an emphatic repetition.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿĪsā read "lā taḥsabunna" with the tāʾ and a ḍammah on the bāʾ, meaning Muḥammad and his companions.

Muḥammad, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur read with the yāʾ and a ḍammah on the bāʾ, as a report about those who rejoice, meaning: "let them not think themselves [safe]." They differed concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse.

ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that some hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Messenger of Allah, if you went out to fight, we would fight with you." So when he (ﷺ) went out, they stayed behind him and rejoiced in their sitting "against the Messenger of Allah." When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned, they made excuses to him, and he accepted their excuses, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done.

Mālik ibn Anas narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, that he and Zayd ibn Thābit were with Marwān, who was then the governor of Madīnah. Marwān said to Rāfiʿ: "About what was this verse revealed: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they were given...﴾?" Rāfiʿ said: "It was revealed about some hypocrites who, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a journey, would stay behind from him." Marwān denied this and said: "What is this?" Rāfiʿ became distressed by this and said to Zayd ibn Thābit: "I ask you by Allah, do you know what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said?" Zayd said: "Yes." So they both left Marwān's presence, and Zayd said to Rāfiʿ, joking with him: "Will you not be praised for what I testified to on your behalf?" Rāfiʿ said: "And what is this? Shall I praise you for testifying to the truth?" Zayd said: "Yes, Allah has praised the people of truth for the truth."

ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed about Finḥāṣ, Ashyaʿ and their like among the rabbis, who rejoiced at misleading the people, and at the people's attributing knowledge to them, and their saying that they were scholars when they were not people of knowledge; they did not guide anyone to guidance or good.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī said: They are the Jews of Madīnah who wrote to the Jews of Yemen, Syria and the far regions: "Muḥammad is not a messenger, so hold firm to your religion." Their word then united upon disbelief in Muḥammad and the Qur'an, and they rejoiced at that and said: "Praise be to Allah who has united our word; we are upon the religion of Ibrāhīm, and we are the first people of knowledge." But they were not so.

Mujāhid: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at people's admiration of their altering of the Book and their striving at it.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at what Allah gave Ibrāhīm, while they are innocent of that.

Ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf that Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam said to his freedman: "O Abū Rāfiʿ, go to Ibn ʿAbbās and say to him: 'If every one of us rejoices at what he was given and loves to be praised for what he did not do, we will all surely be punished.'" Ibn ʿAbbās said: "What is it to you with this verse? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only summoned the Jews and asked them about something, and they concealed it from him and told him something else, showing him that they had told him what he had asked about. They therefore sought praise from him for that and rejoiced at their concealment, so this verse was revealed."

Qatādah and Muqātil: The Jews of Khaybar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We recognize you and affirm you, and we are upon your opinion, and we are a shield for you," but that was not in their hearts. When they left his presence, the Muslims said to them: "What did you do?" They said: "We recognized him and affirmed him." The Muslims said to them: "You have done well, so do likewise." They praised them and invoked blessings upon them, so Allah revealed this verse concerning them.

Shuʿbah narrated from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: It was revealed about some Jews who equipped an army against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spent on them. Ibrāhīm recited it as "bimā ūtū" with a madd, meaning "they were given."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read "ūtū," meaning "they were given."

Allah said: ﴿Do not think them safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾

From ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, who said: I entered with Ibn ʿUmar upon ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and Ibn ʿUmar said: "Tell us of the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah." She wept and prolonged it, then said: "Everything about the Messenger of Allah was wondrous. He came to me on my night, entered under my covering until his skin touched my skin, then said: 'O ʿĀʾishah, will you permit me to worship my Lord, mighty and majestic?' I said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I love your nearness and I love what pleases you; I have permitted you.' So he (ʿalayhi al-ṣalāh wa-al-salām) rose to a waterskin in the house and performed ablution, not pouring much water. Then he stood to pray and recited from the Qur'an and began to weep until the tears reached his lap. Then he raised his hand and kept weeping until I saw the tears had wet the ground. Then Bilāl came to him with the dawn prayer and saw him weeping, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you weep when Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?' He said: 'O Bilāl, shall I not be a grateful servant?' Then he said: 'And why should I not weep, when Allah has revealed to me tonight: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾' — the verse. Then he said: 'Woe to whoever recites it and does not reflect upon it.'" [al-Durr al-Manthūr 2/111.] [210]

From Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with them both, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he rose at night would use the miswāk, then look at the sky, then say: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ up to His saying ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾

ʿAmr ibn Mūsā narrated from Qatādah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most severe verse in the Qur'an upon the jinn is ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [211]," the verse.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: "What signs did Mūsā bring you?" They said: "His staff and his white hand, to the beholders." They asked the Christians: "How was ʿĪsā among you?" They said: "He used to heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life." Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Ask your Lord to make Ṣafā gold for us." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ the verse, then described them, saying:

﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides.﴾

ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Nakhaʿī and Qatādah said: This refers to prayer: one prays standing; if he cannot, sitting; if he cannot, on his side. It is ease and lightening from Allah.

The rest of the exegetes said: It means the remembrance of Allah, mentioning their constancy in it, since a person rarely is free of one of these three states. Its parallel is His saying in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

From Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to frolic in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase the remembrance of Allah." [Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah 7/72.] [212]

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, is the knowledge of faith, freedom from hypocrisy, a fortress against Satan, and a protection from the fires." [Mentioned by Quṭb al-Dīn al-Rawandī in Lubb al-Lubāb, as in Mustadrak al-Wasā'il 5/285 no. 5868.] [213]

Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā (ʿalayhi al-salām): "O Mūsā, keep Me in mind, and do not forget My remembrance in any state. Let your concern be My remembrance, for indeed the path is to Me."

﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: that they have a Creator, powerful and wise, a Manager.

Ḥammād narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū al-Ṣalt, from Abū Hurayrah: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey to the seventh heaven, there was a wind, smoke and voices. He said: "I said: 'What is this, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'These are the devils, who are burned, so that the children of Ādam do not reflect upon the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and were it not for that, they would have seen wonders.'"

Ibn ʿAwr used to say: Reflection removes heedlessness and brings fear of Allah into the heart, as water brings forth crops and plants. Hearts were never polished by anything like sorrows, nor illuminated by anything like reflection. It is related that Sufyān al-Thawrī prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqām, then raised his head to the sky, and when he saw the stars he fainted. Sufyān used to pass blood in his urine from the length of his grief and reflection.

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was lying on his bed, he raised his head, looked at the stars and the sky, and said: 'I bear witness that I have a Lord and Creator. O Allah, forgive me.' So Allah looked at him and forgave him." [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/314.] [214]

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ said: It reached me that a worshipper among the Children of Israel worshipped for thirty years, and whenever a man among them worshipped for thirty years, a cloud would shade him. But he saw nothing, so he complained of that to his father. He said to him: "O my son, reflect: have you committed any sin since you began your worship?" He said: "No, and I do not know that I ever intended one in thirty years." He said: "O my son, one remains; if you are saved from it, I hope it will shade you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Have you ever raised your gaze to the sky and then lowered it without reflection?" He said: "Many times." He said: "From here you were brought." ﴿You did not create this in vain﴾ — he referred to the word "creation," and had it referred to the heavens and the earth, it would have said: "this is vain, purposeless, frivolous; rather, You created it for a great matter."

The accusative of "al-bāṭil" is in two ways: one, by removing the preposition, meaning "for the vain" and "with the vain"; the other, as the second object.

﴿Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ "Disgraced" means: humiliated.

Al-Mufaḍḍal said: destroyed; and he recited:
"May God disgrace from the cross His servants, and those who wear the caps of monks."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī 4/316.]

It was also said: exposed. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿and do not disgrace me regarding my guest﴾ [Hūd 11:78].

Those who hold the doctrine of threat used this verse as a shield, saying: Allah has informed that He does not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him; then He said: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced," so it is necessary that everyone who enters the Fire is not a believer and does not come out of it.

The people of interpretation differed concerning this verse:

Qatādah narrated from Anas concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "You mean whoever You make abide in the Fire."

al-Thawrī narrated from a man, from Ibn al-Musayyab concerning His saying: "Indeed, whoever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him," he said: "This is specific to whoever does not come out of it."
